1.name: Dun Morogh

77.name: Anvilmar
77.description: Nestled beneath the snow-covered peaks of Dun Morogh, Anvilmar is a humble dwarven settlement where the traditions of stone and steel endure against the bitter mountain cold. Anvilmar is renowned as one of Dun Morogh's centers of blacksmithing, where skilled dwarven smiths forge durable arms and armor with unmatched dedication to their craft. Its reputation reaches far beyond the settlement itself: Brann Bronzebeard's mithril mail was forged in Anvilmar, and the sturdy armor has saved his life on countless occasions during his perilous expeditions across Azeroth. Surrounded by rugged cliffs and winding paths carved into the frozen landscape, this secluded outpost offers a welcome refuge from the unforgiving wilderness. Smoke rises from sturdy stone chimneys, mingling with the crisp mountain air, while the distant ring of hammers against metal echoes through the settlement, a familiar reminder of the dwarves' enduring craftsmanship and industrious spirit. Here, travelers may find a moment of respite, exchanging stories with local craftsmen, resting their weary feet by a fire, or seeking guidance from those who know the surrounding wilderness well.

131.name: Kharanos
131.description: Kharanos is the largest town in Dun Morogh after Ironforge itself, a bustling dwarven settlement tucked into a snowy hollow along the main road that winds from Coldridge Valley up toward the gates of the capital. Steep-roofed stone and timber houses huddle together behind a sturdy wall that keeps wolves and worse at bay, their chimneys trailing smoke into the frigid air. At its heart stands the famed Thunderbrew Distillery, whose ales are praised across Khaz Modan, alongside a busy smithy whose forge glows day and night. For all its homely charm, Kharanos is also a frontier garrison: Ironforge mountaineers patrol its roads with long rifles, keeping watch over the Frostmane trolls entrenched on Shimmer Ridge to the northwest and the savage wendigo dwelling in the caves to the southwest. Young dwarven and gnomish recruits trained at Anvilmar come here to take their next steps, and hunters, traders, and travelers mingle by warm hearths, trading news, tall tales, and plenty of beer.

132.name: Coldridge Valley
132.description: Coldridge Valley is a sheltered, snow-filled vale in the far southwestern corner of Dun Morogh, ringed by steep, icy cliffs and reachable from the wider land only through the tunnel of Coldridge Pass. Within the valley lies Anvilmar, an old dwarven enclave of smiths and soldiers where young dwarves and gnomes are trained before they are sent out into the world. Tall pines bend beneath heavy snow, frozen streams wind across the valley floor, and wolves, boars, and wild beasts roam the drifts. The peace of the valley is far from complete: Rockjaw troggs have burrowed into the surrounding hills and the pass, and Frostmane trolls keep a camp at the valley's edge, so the dwarves of Anvilmar stand constant watch. For many a dwarf, these cold slopes and the ring of Anvilmar's hammers are the first memories of home.

133.name: Gnomeregan
133.description: In the snowy foothills of western Dun Morogh lie the entrance and surface works of Gnomeregan, once the gleaming capital of the gnomes and a marvel of engineering carved deep into the mountains. Built with the help of their dwarven allies, the city withstood even the orcish Horde during the Second War behind its impenetrable iron gates. Yet in recent years it fell from within: troggs burrowed up from the depths and overran its lower halls, and in a desperate attempt to destroy them, the gnomes vented the city's toxic, radioactive waste. The troggs survived, but most of the gnomish people perished, and those who escaped fled to Ironforge, where High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque leads his exiled people and dreams of reclaiming their home. Today the area around the city's entrance is a grim, polluted place of rusting machinery, abandoned workshops, and tainted snow, haunted by irradiated troggs and the mad, mutated leper gnomes. Rumor holds that the High Tinker's former advisor, Mekgineer Sicco Thermaplugg, betrayed his people and now rules the ruined city's depths as its self-proclaimed overlord.

134.name: Gol'Bolar Quarry
134.description: Gol'Bolar Quarry is a sprawling dwarven dig site in southeastern Dun Morogh, carved into the rocky flanks of the mountains near the road leading east toward Loch Modan. For generations, dwarven miners hewed stone and ore here for the forges of Ironforge, but the quarry and its mine have been overrun by Rockjaw troggs, crude, savage creatures that swarm through the excavations and tunnels. A small camp of miners and mountaineers clings to the edge of the site, where tents, supply crates, and campfires stand against the cold while the dwarves strive to hold back the troggs and protect what remains of their work. The ring of pickaxes has largely given way to the clash of steel, and the dwarves who keep vigil here dream of the day when the quarry can be reclaimed.

135.name: Frostmane Hold
135.description: Frostmane Hold is the stronghold of the Frostmane tribe of ice trolls, nestled among the cold, rocky heights of western Dun Morogh, south of the entrance to Gnomeregan. A cluster of crude huts and hide tents guards the mouth of a dark, winding cave system that serves as the heart of the tribe's domain, and troll headhunters and hideskinners keep a fierce watch over its approaches. The Frostmane regard these snowy mountains as their ancestral lands, claimed long before the dwarves made Dun Morogh their home, and they have grown bolder while Ironforge's forces are distracted by troggs and Dark Iron dwarves. Bones, skulls, and totems mark the trolls' territory, and few dwarves venture near without good reason and a ready weapon. For the people of Kharanos, the hold is a constant reminder that their homeland is still contested.

136.name: The Grizzled Den
136.description: The Grizzled Den is a large, winding cave system in the snowy hills southwest of Kharanos, home to a pack of savage wendigo, the great shaggy beasts of the frozen mountains. The wendigo are fierce and territorial, able to exhale freezing breath and quick to band together against anyone who enters their lair. Their thick, white manes are prized among the dwarves of Dun Morogh for warmth and comfort, and the bravest hunters venture into the cold, echoing tunnels in search of them, though many return wounded or not at all. Veins of copper glint in the cavern walls, and the bones of unlucky intruders lie scattered across the icy floor. The local dwarves keep a wary eye on the den, mindful of how close it lies to their town.

137.name: Brewnall Village
137.description: Brewnall Village is a small dwarven hamlet on the shores of frozen Iceflow Lake in Chill Breeze Valley, in the western reaches of Dun Morogh near the gnomish city of Gnomeregan. It is home to the Barleybrew family and other devoted brewers, who tirelessly experiment with new recipes in pursuit of the perfect ale, and it is said that its people produce some of the finest beers in all of Khaz Modan. A few cozy stone houses, stacks of barrels, and the scent of hops and malt give the village a warm, cheerful character despite the biting cold. Life here is not without danger, however; wolves prowl the lake's islands, and the troubles spilling out of nearby Gnomeregan are never far away. The villagers are brewers and connoisseurs first, but like all dwarves, they will readily take up axe and rifle to defend their homes and their precious casks.

138.name: Misty Pine Refuge
138.description: Misty Pine Refuge is a modest wooden lodge standing among the tall, snow-laden pines of central Dun Morogh, along the road between Kharanos and the outposts leading toward Loch Modan. The building serves as an outpost of the Argent Dawn, the order devoted to fighting the Scourge and the plague of undeath. While most of the order's forces battle the undead in the distant Plaguelands, a lone agent keeps the refuge in order, studying the plague and offering shelter and counsel to those passing through. The morning mists that drift between the pines give the refuge its name, and its warm hearth is a welcome sight for travelers on the cold mountain road.

189.name: Steelgrill's Depot
189.description: Steelgrill's Depot is a small settlement of dwarven miners and engineers just east of Kharanos, a solid stone complex of workshops and wooden awnings where machines are built, repaired, and maintained. Half-finished siege engines and the rusting hulks of broken war machines lie scattered in the snow around the depot, a testament to the dwarven love of mechanical might and the long years of war. The air rings with hammering and the hiss of steam, and gnomish tinkerers often work side by side with their dwarven hosts, especially since the fall of Gnomeregan sent many gnomes seeking new places to ply their craft. The depot is a gathering place for engineers, miners, and those fascinated by machinery, and the mountaineers stationed nearby keep a close eye on the troggs and wild beasts that occasionally stray too close.

211.name: Iceflow Lake
211.description: Iceflow Lake is a frozen lake in western Dun Morogh, lying within Chill Breeze Valley close to Brewnall Village and the snowy foothills of Gnomeregan. The high altitude and bitter cold keep its surface locked in thick ice for most of the year, though the dwarves of Brewnall keep a hole open to draw fresh water and to fish the cold depths below. A pair of wooded islands rises from the center of the lake, the domain of a large pack of ravenous wolves that sensible travelers give a wide berth. Snow-covered pines line the shores, and on still days the frozen expanse gleams beneath the pale mountain sun.

212.name: Helm's Bed Lake
212.description: Helm's Bed Lake is a small mountain lake in southeastern Dun Morogh, near the passes that lead toward Loch Modan. Its waters have mostly frozen over, though a hole in the ice is always kept clear to provide access to fresh water. Crossing the ice is generally safe, but the surrounding shores are a different matter: hungry wildlife roams the snowy hills, stray troggs wander up from the nearby quarry, and Dark Iron dwarves have seized an abandoned dwarven compound just south of the lake, attacking anyone who strays too close. The stark, wind-swept landscape of rock, ice, and pine makes Helm's Bed Lake a lonely and dangerous place, especially when night falls over the mountains.

716.name: Ironband's Compound
716.description: Ironband's Compound is a fortified dwarven homestead south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh, once owned by a dwarven family but now abandoned by its rightful inhabitants. It has been seized by a band of Dark Iron dwarves, the ancient enemies of Ironforge, who use it as a base of operations deep within Bronzebeard lands and readily assault anyone who wanders too close. The presence of Dark Iron agents so near to Ironforge is a source of great concern for the dwarven authorities, rekindling memories of the bitter War of the Three Hammers. Smoke from their fires rises above the snowy hills, and the mountaineers of Dun Morogh regard the compound as hostile territory.

800.name: Coldridge Pass
800.description: Coldridge Pass is a tunnel carved through the mountains linking Coldridge Valley with the rest of Dun Morogh, the vital route by which young dwarven recruits trained at Anvilmar travel on toward Kharanos and Ironforge. The passage is dark, cold, and echoing, its rough stone walls lit by only a few torches. In recent times, Rockjaw troggs have infested the tunnel, ambushing those who attempt to pass, and travelers must either dash through at full speed or fight their way past the snarling creatures. Beyond the tunnel, the road opens onto the snowy slopes of central Dun Morogh.

801.name: Chill Breeze Valley
801.description: Chill Breeze Valley is a T-shaped valley in western Dun Morogh, stretching between the gnomish city of Gnomeregan to the west and the town of Kharanos to the east. The east-west branch of the valley carries the main road and is frequently traveled, passing the brewing hamlet of Brewnall Village and the frozen expanse of Iceflow Lake. The north-south branch, however, sees far fewer travelers, for ominous signs mark its snows: large bloodstains and torn animal carcasses betray the presence of ferocious beasts, and a fearsome wendigo is said to lurk in one of its caves. Cold winds sweep constantly through the valley, giving it its name, and the snowy slopes are dotted with dark pines and grey rock.

802.name: Shimmer Ridge
802.description: Shimmer Ridge is a high, rocky ridge in northern Dun Morogh, rising west of the great gates of Ironforge. It has been claimed by the Frostmane ice trolls, who dwell in two fortified camps connected by a rickety bridge spanning a gap in the ridge. The trolls cultivate shimmerweed, a strange, glimmering plant that grows on the cold slopes, and keep tamed crag boars among their huts. The ridge looms uncomfortably close to both Kharanos and the dwarven capital, and the trolls' presence is a constant source of tension for the mountaineers of Ironforge. From its heights, the snowy expanse of central Dun Morogh stretches out below.

803.name: Amberstill Ranch
803.description: Amberstill Ranch is a dwarven ranch off the road leading east toward Loch Modan, north of Gol'Bolar Quarry in Dun Morogh. It is run by the Amberstill family, renowned breeders of the sturdy mountain rams that serve as the traditional mounts of the dwarves of Ironforge. The ranch's stables and paddocks are well kept despite the harsh climate, and the rams graze on the hardy grasses that push up through the snow. Snowshoe rabbits hop through the surrounding drifts, while wolves and wendigo in the nearby hills sometimes threaten the herds. For dwarves, a well-bred ram from Amberstill is a source of great pride, and the ranch is a familiar stop for those traveling between Ironforge and the eastern passes.

804.name: The Tundrid Hills
804.description: The Tundrid Hills are a range of snowy, rolling hills in south-central Dun Morogh, stretching west of Gol'Bolar Quarry and south of the main road through Kharanos. The hills are home to many species of hostile wildlife, including wolves, bears, and boars, and few venture there without a weapon at hand. Some bold travelers use the hills as a shortcut between Coldridge Valley and eastern Dun Morogh, but this route is far more dangerous than the road that passes through Kharanos. Snow-laden pines dot the slopes, and the wind howls endlessly over the barren crests.

805.name: South Gate Pass
805.description: South Gate Pass is a mountain pass in eastern Dun Morogh that links the high, snowy uplands of the dwarven homeland with the lower mountains and green valleys of Loch Modan to the east. It is the closest route to the dwarven town of Thelsamar, and a steady stream of travelers, merchants, and soldiers passes along its road. A great dwarven gate and the guard station of South Gate Outpost stand watch over the pass, ensuring that no enemy can easily enter the heart of Khaz Modan. Snow lies thick on the steep rock walls on either side, and the wind whistles through the narrow defile.

806.name: South Gate Outpost
806.description: South Gate Outpost is a dwarven guard station set in the middle of South Gate Pass, watching over the road between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. The mountaineers stationed here have cleared out most of the dangerous wildlife from the surrounding slopes and keep the road safe for travelers heading to and from the town of Thelsamar. Sturdy stone walls, watchtowers, and warm fires make the outpost a welcome resting place for weary travelers, and its garrison is proud of the order it keeps. Snow blankets the pass, and the dwarves here are well accustomed to the bitter mountain cold.

807.name: North Gate Pass
807.description: North Gate Pass is a mountain pass in northeastern Dun Morogh, linking the snowy highlands of the dwarven homeland with Loch Modan to the east. It is the favored route for travelers bound for the Wetlands, since it lies closest to the descent from the loch toward the northern marshes. A massive dwarven gate and the guard station of North Gate Outpost protect the pass, a reminder of how fiercely the dwarves guard the approaches to their homeland. The steep, rocky walls of the pass are covered in snow and ice, and the cold wind rarely stops blowing.

808.name: North Gate Outpost
808.description: North Gate Outpost is the northeasternmost dwarven settlement in Dun Morogh, a guard station in the middle of North Gate Pass that watches over the road to Loch Modan. The mountaineers stationed here are kept busy defending the outpost from encroaching wildlife, as bears, wolves, and other ferocious beasts roam the surrounding mountains, and some of the dwarves who ventured into the wilderness to hunt them have never returned. Despite the dangers, the outpost's sturdy walls and watchtowers provide a measure of safety for travelers, and its garrison remains vigilant against any threat to the passes.

809.name: Gates of Ironforge
809.description: The Gates of Ironforge are the great entrance to the dwarven capital, carved into the face of the mighty mountain at the heart of Dun Morogh. A broad, winding ramp climbs from the snowy valley below toward the massive gates, and a colossal statue of Modimus Anvilmar, the legendary first king of the Ironforge dwarves, gazes out over the land. The gates are visible from far across Dun Morogh, a symbol of dwarven strength and endurance, and Ironforge guards stand constant watch over the approach. Travelers, merchants, soldiers, and adventurers of the Alliance pass through these gates in an endless stream, while warm air and the glow of the city's great forges spill out into the frigid mountain wind.

2102.name: Thunderbrew Distillery
2102.description: The Thunderbrew Distillery is the beloved inn and tavern at the heart of Kharanos, owned by the Thunderbrew family of brewers, whose ales are known far and wide as some of the finest in Khaz Modan. Its sturdy stone walls and warm hearth offer a welcome refuge from the biting cold of Dun Morogh, and its common room is always lively with dwarves and gnomes swapping stories over foaming tankards. The distillery is much more than a place to drink: it serves as an inn for weary travelers and a meeting place where seasoned warriors, priests, and spellcasters pass on their wisdom to the young dwarves and gnomes of the region. The smell of roasting meat and fresh brew fills the air, and the sound of laughter and song rarely fades, even late into the night.

1.description: Dun Morogh is a rugged, snowbound land nestled among the towering peaks of Khaz Modan, where winter reigns supreme. Vast stretches of white snow blanket the rocky hills, frozen lakes glisten beneath pale sunlight, and dense pine forests stand silent beneath heavy drifts. The air is sharp with frost, carrying the scent of evergreen, woodsmoke, and freshly forged iron from the dwarven settlements scattered throughout the region. Despite its harsh climate, Dun Morogh is far from lifeless. The sturdy dwarves of Ironforge have carved their homes into the heart of the mountains, their forges burning bright against the endless cold. The center of dwarven culture and ingenuity, Dun Morogh holds the capital of Ironforge. The region is snow-swept and forested, with gray, craggy mountains and slinking wolves.

3.name: Badlands

337.name: Apocryphan's Rest
337.description: Apocryphan's Rest is the name given to the enormous skeleton of a long-dead dragon that lies fallen in the Badlands, south of Kargath. Its massive ribs and skull rise from the cracked earth like the ruins of some ancient structure, bleached white by the relentless sun. No one knows for certain which dragon it was or how it died, but the bones have become a landmark for travelers crossing the wasteland. A flock of hungry vultures circles above and roosts among the bones, waiting for the next unfortunate creature to succumb to the heat.

338.name: Angor Fortress
338.description: Angor Fortress is a grim stone stronghold in the northern Badlands, just south of Uldaman, held by the Dark Iron dwarves. It serves as their main base of operations in the region, from which they organize their excavations and their efforts to plunder the ancient titan vault for the benefit of their master, the Firelord Ragnaros. It is said that an emissary of Ragnaros himself resides within its walls. The fortress is heavily guarded, its dark walls bristling with weapons, and few who are not Dark Irons approach it and live. Smoke rises from its forges, and the heat of the Badlands seems even more oppressive in its shadow.

339.name: Lethlor Ravine
339.description: Lethlor Ravine is a wide, craggy valley in the eastern Badlands, a desolate stretch of red rock and scorched earth that has become a nesting ground for the black dragonflight. Whelps scurry among the rocks, and black drakes patrol the skies above, attacking any who intrude upon their domain. Strange crystalline obelisks rise from the floor of the ravine, their purpose unknown. The ravine is one of the most dangerous places in the Badlands, and even the hardiest prospectors and ogres steer clear of it.

340.name: Kargath
340.description: Kargath is a small, functional Horde fortress hidden in the northwestern corner of the Badlands, built into the rocky cliffs near the passage into the Searing Gorge. It began as the last remnant of the old Horde forces that met defeat in Khaz Modan after the Second War; abandoned by their ogre allies, the orcs had little hope of survival until Thrall's New Horde sent aid and reinforcements. Thrall made the outpost permanent and named it after the former Shattered Hand chieftain, Kargath Bladefist. From here, the Kargath Expeditionary Force explores the wasteland, which has revealed rich mineral and gem deposits as well as the ruins of Uldaman. The orcs have also cut a narrow pass into the Searing Gorge in hopes of reaching Blackrock Mountain, inadvertently unleashing the Dark Iron dwarves upon the region once more. Kargath is a vital link between the northern and southern Horde holdings in the Eastern Kingdoms, and its wind riders connect it with distant outposts.

341.name: Camp Kosh
341.description: Camp Kosh is the northernmost of the four camps of the Dustbelcher ogres in the Badlands, a crude collection of tents and cauldrons near the trade routes leading to Kargath and the Searing Gorge. The ogres here prey on the supply caravans that must cross the barren land, and the camp is littered with the remains of plundered wagons and goods. The Dustbelchers are primitive and brutal, and their leader roams between the camps, keeping the tribe in line.

342.name: Camp Boff
342.description: Camp Boff is a small camp of the Dustbelcher ogres in the southeastern Badlands, one of four such camps scattered across the wasteland. It consists of little more than a cauldron, a cart, and a tent, guarded by a few ogres. Despite its modest size, the camp is a danger to travelers, for the Dustbelchers are brutal and quick to attack anyone who wanders into their territory.

343.name: Camp Wurg
343.description: Camp Wurg is one of the four camps of the Dustbelcher ogres in the Badlands, located in the dusty northwestern flats known as the Dustbowl. Crude tents, cooking fires, and piles of bones mark the ogres' territory, and the Dustbelchers who dwell here attack any travelers who stray too close. The ogres are primitive and violent, having abandoned their former orcish allies after the Second War to claim the Badlands for themselves.

344.name: Camp Cagg
344.description: Camp Cagg is one of the four camps of the Dustbelcher ogres in the Badlands, located in the southwestern part of the wasteland. Like the other camps, it is a crude settlement of tents, cauldrons, and piles of plunder, guarded by brutish ogres who attack anyone who wanders into their territory. The Dustbelchers are a constant danger to the caravans and travelers crossing the Badlands, and a small band of dwarves is said to be dedicated to hunting them down.

345.name: Agmond's End
345.description: Agmond's End is an abandoned dwarven dig site in the south-central Badlands, named for the dwarven prospector who met an unfortunate end there at the hands of the troggs that have infested the site. Like so many excavations in Khaz Modan, the dig uncovered more than its workers bargained for, and the troggs now swarm among the abandoned tents, tools, and half-excavated ruins. A lone explorer is said to camp nearby, studying the mysteries of the Badlands. The site is a grim reminder of the dangers faced by those who seek the secrets of the titans.

346.name: Hammertoe's Digsite
346.description: Hammertoe's Digsite is a dwarven excavation in the northern Badlands, near the ruins of Uldaman. It was recently abandoned by its dwarven crew and has since been taken over by a gang of Dark Iron dwarves, presumably part of the same force that has moved into Uldaman. The Dark Irons now dig through the site for their own purposes, and the scaffolds, tents, and mining equipment left behind by the original crew have been put to use by the new occupants. The dwarves of Ironforge view the loss of the site with bitterness.

347.name: Dustbelch Grotto
347.description: Dustbelch Grotto is a large ogre camp built around a cave in the southwestern Badlands, the main home of the Dustbelcher ogres. The grotto is filled with crude dwellings, cooking fires, and piles of bones and plunder, and the ogres who dwell here are brutal and territorial. After the Second War, the Dustbelchers abandoned their orcish allies and claimed the Badlands as their own, and they remain a constant danger to travelers and prospectors alike.

1517.name: Uldaman
1517.description: Uldaman is an ancient titan vault buried deep within the mountains of the northern Badlands, one of the few known titan cities in the world. Dwarven excavations recently penetrated the forgotten complex, revealing vast halls of carved stone, colossal statues, and mysterious machinery, but they also released the titans' first failed creations: the troggs. Legends say the titans shaped the troggs from stone, and when they deemed the experiment a failure, they locked them away and tried again, resulting in the creation of the dwarven race. The secrets of the dwarves' creation are said to be recorded on the fabled Discs of Norgannon, which lie at the very bottom of the city, guarded by giant constructs of living stone. The Stonevault troggs now infest the outer halls, and the Dark Iron dwarves have launched incursions into the vault, hoping to claim its treasures for Ragnaros. Rumors even suggest that the dwarves' stone-skinned ancestors, the earthen, still dwell in the city's hidden depths. For the Explorers' League, Uldaman is one of the most important discoveries in dwarven history.

1877.name: Valley of Fangs
1877.description: The Valley of Fangs is a small valley in the central Badlands, nestled between two massive stone formations that rise like great teeth from the cracked earth, giving the valley its name. A small camp of wanderers and traders can be found here, a rare spot of relative safety in the wasteland. Travel through the valley is hazardous, however, for it is home to wolves and cougars that prowl among the rocks. The valley offers some shelter from the relentless sun and wind, and it is a common stopping point for those crossing the Badlands.

1878.name: The Dustbowl
1878.description: The Dustbowl is a large expanse of dusty flatland in the northwestern Badlands, stretching between Kargath and the Valley of Fangs. It is home to a variety of creatures that have adapted to the harsh conditions, including coyotes, buzzards, and living rock elementals. A few hardy plants manage to survive on the arid ground, such as cacti and scattered, gnarled trees. Dust storms frequently sweep across the flats, reducing visibility and making travel difficult. The Dustbowl also contains one of the camps of the Dustbelcher ogres.

1879.name: Mirage Flats
1879.description: The Mirage Flats are a stretch of barren, sun-baked flatland in the southern Badlands, east of Dustbelch Grotto. The intense heat rising from the cracked earth creates shimmering mirages on the horizon, which have led many a weary traveler astray in search of water that is not there. Coyotes roam the flats in packs, and little else lives here. The flats are a desolate and disorienting place, where the line between land and sky seems to blur in the haze.

1897.name: The Maker's Terrace
1897.description: The Maker's Terrace is a large excavation site just outside the entrance to Uldaman in the northern Badlands, where dwarven prospectors first uncovered the ancient titan vault. Great stone steps, carved pillars, and colossal statues have been unearthed from the rock, hinting at the grandeur of the city below. The terrace is now patrolled by Dark Iron dwarves, who have taken over the excavation and guard the entrance to Uldaman. For travelers entering the Badlands from Loch Modan, the terrace is often the first sight of the ancient secrets buried beneath the wasteland.

1898.name: Dustwind Gulch
1898.description: Dustwind Gulch is a narrow, windswept gulch in the eastern Badlands, lying to the west of Lethlor Ravine. Strong winds funnel through the gulch, whipping up clouds of dust and sand that sting the eyes and obscure the path ahead. The rocky walls of the gulch offer little shelter, and the area is home to scorpids, vultures, and other creatures adapted to the harsh conditions. Travelers passing through toward the eastern canyons must also watch for the black dragonkin that venture out from the ravine beyond.

3.description: The Badlands are a harsh, sun-scorched wasteland in southern Khaz Modan, lying south of Loch Modan and east of the Searing Gorge. It is a cracked desert of dry red earth, scattered boulders, mesas, and winding canyons, enclosed by jagged mountains. Water is scarce, the heat is relentless by day, and dust storms sweep across the barren flats, where only the hardiest creatures survive: coyotes, cougars, buzzards, scorpids, and basilisks, along with living elementals of rock and dust. The region is a place of ancient secrets. In its northern reaches lies Uldaman, an immense titan vault recently unearthed by dwarven excavations, which holds clues to the origins of the dwarves themselves. The dig released the Stonevault troggs from millennia of slumber, and they slaughtered the explorers and now viciously defend the ruins. Ironforge prospectors and the Explorers' League still search the land for titan artifacts, while the Dark Iron dwarves hold a fortress and excavations of their own in the north, seeking the vault's treasures for their fiery master, Ragnaros. Dustbelcher ogres roam the land from their camps, black dragons nest in the eastern canyons, and in the northwest the Horde holds the small fortress of Kargath, built from the remnants of the old Horde forces and reinforced by Thrall's New Horde. During the Second War, orcish forces marched through these lands on their way to Grim Batol. The Badlands are a dangerous, lawless place, where every faction seeks to claim the riches buried beneath the dust.

4.name: Blasted Lands

72.name: The Dark Portal
72.description: The Dark Portal is the great gateway between Azeroth and Draenor, standing in a vast crater in the southeastern Blasted Lands. It was created by the corrupted Guardian Medivh and the warlocks of the Shadow Council, allowing the orcish Horde to invade Azeroth and begin the First War. After the Second War, the Alliance captured the portal and the Archmage Khadgar attempted to close it, and later the heroes of the Alliance Expedition sealed it from the other side as Draenor was torn apart. For twenty years it lay dormant, until the demon lord Kazzak reopened it, and now its green, swirling energies once again lead to Outland. The massive stone gateway, flanked by colossal statues, is guarded by the armies of both the Alliance and the Horde, whose encampments stand at its foot. Soldiers, adventurers, and supplies pass through it in an endless stream, bound for the battles in the shattered world beyond.

73.name: The Tainted Scar
73.description: The Tainted Scar is a large expanse in the southwestern Blasted Lands, shrouded in a thick, vile mist that chokes mortals foolish enough to venture close. It serves as the domain of many of the remaining forces of the Burning Legion that stayed on Azeroth after the Third War, who wait in the poison fog for their masters' return. Demons dwell here and pervert the already tainted land with their energies, and the ground is cracked and scorched. Few who enter the Scar return, and the mages of Nethergarde regard it as the most dangerous place in the region.

1437.name: Dreadmaul Hold
1437.description: Dreadmaul Hold is the main stronghold of the Dreadmaul ogres in the northwestern Blasted Lands, built on the ruins of the old orcish town of Rockard, which the Horde established during the First War. The ogres, who came through the Dark Portal from Draenor alongside the orcs, remained in the Blasted Lands and took over the town, and they now launch regular attacks against Nethergarde Keep. The hold is a crude, brutal place of ogre huts and fortifications, and venturing into it alone is extremely dangerous.

1438.name: Nethergarde Keep
1438.description: Nethergarde Keep is a heavily defended fortress on a high bluff in the northern Blasted Lands, standing along the only road into the region. It was built after the Second War at the behest of the Archmage Khadgar to ensure that there would be no further invasions from Draenor, funded by the kingdoms of the Alliance of Lordaeron and constructed by Stormwind's stonemasons. After Khadgar led the Alliance Expedition through the portal, the mages of Dalaran kept Nethergarde in operation, studying the effects of the portal's energies on the land. When Dalaran was destroyed during the Third War, the keep came to depend on the support of Stormwind. Its garrison of some three hundred dour mages, soldiers, and dwarven miners fights daily against the demons and ogres of the region, and since the reopening of the Dark Portal, the keep has become the main hub of Alliance activity between Stormwind and Outland. Its keepers are grim and uptight, but they are the only friendly faces for many miles.

1439.name: Dreadmaul Post
1439.description: Dreadmaul Post is an outpost of the Dreadmaul ogres in the Blasted Lands, near the road leading toward the Dark Portal. The ogres, who came to Azeroth from Draenor alongside the orcs, remained close to the portal and maintain a strong presence in the area. Their camp is a crude collection of huts and campfires, and they attack any travelers who come near. Occasionally, a lost draenei can be found wandering the nearby territory.

1440.name: Serpent's Coil
1440.description: Serpent's Coil is a winding cave system in the eastern Blasted Lands, within sight of Nethergarde Keep. It has been occupied by a cult of evil worshippers devoted to dark powers, among them many high elves who have turned to shadow, and they conduct their foul rituals deep within the caves. Several burnt-out orcish structures from the Second War stand near the entrance, remnants of the days when the Horde held these lands. The mages of Nethergarde keep a wary eye on the caves and the cultists within.

1441.name: Altar of Storms
1441.description: The Altar of Storms in the Blasted Lands is one of the few remaining altars from the Second War, when orc warlocks of the Horde created such structures to channel demonic energies into their ogre allies and turn them into ogre magi. The altar stands cracked and scarred in the red wastes, but its dark energies still linger, and it has become a gathering place for servants of the Burning Legion and other dark powers. The air around it crackles with fel magic, and the ground is scorched and lifeless.

1457.name: Garrison Armory
1457.description: The Garrison Armory is a vital Alliance mining outpost near Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands, where dwarven and human miners toil to extract precious ores and minerals from the red earth. The resources gathered here are shipped to Stormwind in exchange for the supplies Nethergarde depends on to survive. The armory is guarded by the soldiers of the keep, for the ogres and demons of the region are a constant threat. The mine's tunnels glitter with veins of ore, and the sound of picks echoes through the passages.

2517.name: Rise of the Defiler
2517.description: The Rise of the Defiler is a craggy range of mountains near the middle of the Blasted Lands, its jagged peaks rising from the red wasteland like broken teeth. It is said to be the home of a great and terrible demon, a remnant of the Burning Legion who lurks among the rocks. The mountains are barren and scorched, and the air around them is heavy with fel energy. Few dare to approach the Rise, and those who do rarely return.

4.description: The Blasted Lands are a scorched, barren desert of red clay in the southeastern Eastern Kingdoms, south of the Swamp of Sorrows. Once the southern part of the dark fens called the Black Morass, the land was twisted and transformed by the chaotic magic that accompanied the creation and destruction of the Dark Portal, through which the orcish Horde first entered Azeroth. The original tan color of the rocks has been transmuted into an unearthly crimson, lightning strikes the land frequently, and nothing fertile grows. The days are dry and hot, the nights bitterly cold, and the mountains block any moisture from the north. Hardy creatures such as basilisks, scorpids, hyenas, and vultures have colonized the area, mutated by the land's tainted energies. The Dark Portal still stands in a great crater in the southeast, and since it was reopened by the demon lord Kazzak, it once again leads to Outland, the shattered remains of the orcs' homeworld, Draenor. Armies of both the Alliance and the Horde now stand guard at its foot, and travelers of every race pass through it on their way to the war in Outland. Nethergarde Keep, a fortress of dour mages and soldiers established after the Second War by the Archmage Khadgar, watches over the region from the north. The land is also home to the brutal Dreadmaul ogres, who came through the portal from Draenor, and to remnants of the Burning Legion lurking in the poisonous mists of the Tainted Scar.

8.name: Swamp of Sorrows

74.name: Pool of Tears
74.description: The Pool of Tears is the largest and deepest bog in the Swamp of Sorrows, the place where the green Dragon Aspect Ysera drowned the Temple of Atal'Hakkar beneath the waters after learning of the evil plans of the Atal'ai priests. Its waters are deep and less murky than the rest of the swamp, and the ruins of the sunken temple rise from its center, overgrown with vines. Scattered Atal'ai ruins surround the shores, and the waters are home to ravenous fish. Green dragonkin keep watch over the pool, for Ysera has warned of a lurking terror within the temple.

75.name: Stonard
75.description: Stonard is the lone Horde town in the Swamp of Sorrows, a fortified orcish outpost built on a rise just off the swamp's only road. Originally established during the First War as a base for the invasion of the human Kingdom of Azeroth, it was abandoned after the Second War, but was rebuilt by Thrall's New Horde. Protected by high wooden walls and guarded by sentries at every gate, it is populated mostly by orc warriors and shamans, and its weaponsmiths are known for their fine work. Stonard is a center of operations for those who seek to enter the sunken temple and is the closest Horde outpost to the Dark Portal in the Blasted Lands. Wind riders connect it with other Horde holdings, and regular patrols keep watch over the surrounding swamp.

76.name: Fallow Sanctuary
76.description: The Fallow Sanctuary is a village in the northern Swamp of Sorrows, within sight of the Redridge Mountains, inhabited by a tribe of draenei Lost Ones. These draenei were stranded on Azeroth when the Dark Portal was destroyed, and they have been driven mad by homesickness and the separation from their world, turning feral and hostile to all outsiders. They have managed to make a life for themselves in the swamp, growing water-loving crops and hunting the local beasts, and they send spies and assassins against the orcs of Stonard. The sanctuary is a sad and dangerous place, a reminder of the tragic fate of the draenei who were lost.

116.name: Misty Valley
116.description: Misty Valley is a valley in the northwestern corner of the Swamp of Sorrows, close to the road leading in from Deadwind Pass. As its name suggests, the valley is perpetually shrouded in mist, and its boggy ground is home to tangled horrors and swampwalkers, living elementals of mud and vines. At the far end of the valley lies a cave said to be the lair of a powerful mire lord. The valley is a gloomy, unsettling place, where the mist hides many dangers.

300.name: Misty Reed Strand
300.description: The Misty Reed Strand is the gloomy coastline of the Swamp of Sorrows, a long stretch of beach where the swamp meets the sea. There is little along the strand but driftwood, debris, reeds, and the creatures that dwell there: crocolisks, crabs, and murlocs. The mist that rolls in from the sea gives the coast its name and makes it a dreary, desolate place. The sound of the waves and the cries of seabirds are the only sounds that break the silence.

657.name: The Harborage
657.description: The Harborage is a small village in the northern Swamp of Sorrows, home to a group of draenei and Broken who managed to stay sane after being stranded on Azeroth. Unlike their kin in the Fallow Sanctuary, they have resisted the madness that consumed the Lost Ones, and they struggle to survive in the harsh swamp. They are willing to deal with both the Horde and the Alliance, and visitors from Outland have come to study their condition and seek a cure. The Harborage is a humble place of simple huts, a fragile refuge of sanity in a land of sorrow.

1777.name: Itharius's Cave
1777.description: Itharius's Cave is a cave in the far southwestern corner of the Swamp of Sorrows, the home of a mysterious hermit who has taken it upon himself to watch over a brood of green dragon whelps. The whelps play in the area outside the cave, and the hermit guards them as they grow. The cave is a peaceful place, surrounded by lush vegetation, and the whelps grow safely under their guardian's watchful eye.

1778.name: Sorrowmurk
1778.description: The Sorrowmurk is the area of the Swamp of Sorrows just east of the Pool of Tears and the sunken temple, a region of deep bogs and dense vegetation. It is crawling with green dragonspawn of Ysera's flight, who guard the approaches to the temple, and a large green drake patrols the area. Venturing into the Sorrowmurk is extremely hazardous, for the dragonkin attack any who intrude. The murk is dark and oppressive, the air thick with mist and the hum of insects.

1780.name: Splinterspear Junction
1780.description: Splinterspear Junction is the place where the main road through the Swamp of Sorrows splits. The northern branch leads past the Harborage to the Fallow Sanctuary, while the southern branch leads to Stonard and the path to the Blasted Lands. The junction is regularly patrolled by Horde guards from Stonard, and travelers are advised to keep their eyes open. The road here rises only inches above the murky water, painstakingly built to allow travel through the swamp.

1797.name: Stagalbog
1797.description: Stagalbog is a region of deep, stagnant bogs in the eastern Swamp of Sorrows, south of the Pool of Tears. Its waters are black and murky, its trees draped with moss, and the air is thick with the stench of decay. Crocolisks, bog beasts, and other creatures lurk in the bog, and a large cave nearby is home to a tribe of murlocs. The Stagalbog is one of the most inhospitable areas of the swamp.

1798.name: The Shifting Mire
1798.description: The Shifting Mire is the central bulk of the Swamp of Sorrows, west of the Pool of Tears, a vast expanse of bogs, pools, and reeds where the ground seems to shift and sink underfoot. The mire is home to young crocolisks, giant spiders, swamp jaguars, and wandering Lost Ones, and travelers must take care not to become stuck in the sucking mud. The mist hangs low over the water, and the weeping willows droop over the dark pools.

1817.name: Stagalbog Cave
1817.description: Stagalbog Cave is a large cave in the Stagalbog in the eastern Swamp of Sorrows, home to many murlocs of the Marsh tribe and their leader, a murloc oracle. The cave is damp and dark, its floor covered with shallow pools, and the gurgling cries of murlocs echo through its passages. The murlocs are hostile to outsiders and attack any who enter their lair.

1978.name: Misty Reed Post
1978.description: Misty Reed Post is a small Horde outpost of Stonard, lying between the Stagalbog and the southern Misty Reed Strand. It consists of a few tents and a campfire, guarded by a handful of orc warriors, hunters, and shamans who keep watch over the coast and the murlocs that dwell there. The post is isolated and humble, and its defenders dream of the day it will be expanded into a proper fortification.

2403.name: The Forbidding Sea
2403.description: The waters of the Forbidding Sea wash the eastern coast of the Swamp of Sorrows, rolling in grey and misty onto the Misty Reed Strand. The sea seeps into the fens through the estuary, making the swamp's waters brackish and leaving salt deposits on the rocks and logs. The waters are cold and rough, often shrouded in fog, and few ships venture near this desolate coast. Murlocs and crocolisks dwell in the shallows, and the cries of seabirds echo over the waves.

8.description: The Swamp of Sorrows is a stagnant, mist-shrouded marshland in the southeastern Eastern Kingdoms, lying east of Deadwind Pass, north of the Blasted Lands, and bordered by the sea to the east. It is a land of sucking bogs, weeping willows, and murky pools, where the brackish water seeping in from the ocean leaves salt deposits encrusting fallen logs and rocks. The air is humid and heavy, the rain frequent, and crocolisks, jaguars, giant spiders, and hulking bog beasts lurk in the reeds. The swamp was once the northern part of a vast swampland called the Black Morass. After the fall of the Gurubashi Empire, the renegade Atal'ai priests fled here and built a great temple to the blood god Hakkar; the green Dragon Aspect Ysera drowned it beneath the largest bog, and her dragonspawn still guard the sunken ruins. During the First War, the orcish Horde built settlements here, among them Stonard, which has since been rebuilt by Thrall's Horde and is now the only true town in the swamp. When the Dark Portal was destroyed during the Second War, the southern part of the Morass was blasted into the barren Blasted Lands, and some draenei were stranded on Azeroth; most of them were driven mad and became the hostile Lost Ones, while a small group of Broken exiles remained sane. Murlocs inhabit the coast, and the green dragonflight patrols the east.

10.name: Duskwood

42.name: Darkshire
42.description: Darkshire is a once-quaint woodland village in eastern Duskwood, now the last refuge of the region's people against the darkness that has swallowed the forest. Formerly known as Grand Hamlet, it was destroyed by the orcs in the First War and rebuilt, only to be engulfed later by the curse that turned southern Elwynn into Duskwood. Today it numbers some thirty-five hundred souls, many of them refugees from the abandoned town of Raven Hill. The town is governed by an elected mayor, and its militia, the Night Watch, patrols the roads and strikes against the undead and worgen that plague the land. Stormwind has all but abandoned Darkshire, leaving its people to defend themselves, and they have become a jumpy, suspicious lot, though desperate for any aid against the evil that surrounds them. Lanterns burn day and night along its streets, and the town's walls offer the only true safety in Duskwood.

93.name: Vul'Gol Ogre Mound
93.description: The Vul'Gol Ogre Mound is a small basin in southern Duskwood, just southwest of where the main road splits and runs south into Stranglethorn Vale. It has been completely overrun by the Splinter Fist ogres, who have moved into the region from the east and built crude huts and campfires among the trees. The ogres are brutal and numerous, and debris and plunder from their raids lie scattered around the mound. Travelers on the southern road give the area a wide berth.

94.name: Raven Hill
94.description: Raven Hill is an abandoned town in western Duskwood, north of Addle's Stead and south of the great Raven Hill Cemetery. Once it took pride in honoring the dead and was home to a mortuary school that graduated the finest embalmers in Azeroth. But when the darkness fell, the dead rose from their graves, and the townsfolk, unable to bear fighting their own loved ones, fled east to Darkshire. Even the Defias Brotherhood, who tried to make camp in the empty town, could not withstand the constant attacks of the undead. Today Raven Hill is a ghost town of crumbling houses and silent streets, where only a few desperate souls remain, and the Black Riders are said to haunt its outskirts.

121.name: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery
121.description: The Tranquil Gardens Cemetery lies just southeast of Darkshire in Duskwood, the town's graveyard and the site of a ruined chapel. Once a peaceful resting place, it is now anything but tranquil, for the dead have risen from their graves, and skeletons and ghouls wander among the tombstones. The undead here are weaker than those found elsewhere in Duskwood, and the Night Watch works to keep them from spilling into the town. The broken chapel and leaning gravestones, shrouded in mist, give the cemetery an eerie, melancholy air.

241.name: The Rotting Orchard
241.description: The Rotting Orchard is an abandoned orchard in southern Duskwood, east of the Yorgen Farmstead and west of the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. It was once a bright orchard laden with apples, pears, and peaches, but now the trees are gnarled and the fruit lies fallen and rotting on the ground, filling the air with a sickly sweet stench. The orchard has become a haunt of ravenous worgen, who prowl among the twisted trees and attack anyone who comes near. The nearby mine of Roland's Doom is said to be their lair.

242.name: Brightwood Grove
242.description: Brightwood Grove was once a pleasant, sunny field in the midst of the forest just west of Darkshire, but since the gloom of permanent night settled over Duskwood, its name serves only to recall a happier time. The few buildings that stood at the edge of the grove lie in ruins, and worgen prowl the dark fields, erecting crude camps and attacking anyone who comes too close. The Night Watch regularly sends hunters to thin their numbers. A few stubborn souls still live near the grove, clinging to their homes despite the danger.

243.name: Forlorn Rowe
243.description: Forlorn Rowe is a dark hill in northwestern Duskwood, on the northern edge of Raven Hill Cemetery, cloaked in an ominous darkness even deeper than the rest of the forest. Upon the hill stands a gloomy house, said to be the lair of a powerful necromancer who commands the undead of the region through foul magic. The air around the hill is cold and still, and the undead that wander the slopes make it one of the most dangerous places in Duskwood. Few who climb the hill return.

244.name: The Whipple Estate
244.description: The Whipple Estate is an abandoned family house in Duskwood, once the home of the Whipple family, standing among the dark, gnarled trees of the cursed forest. Like so many homes in the region, it was deserted when the eternal twilight fell over the land, and its owners fled or met a grim fate. The house now stands silent and decaying, its windows dark, its garden overgrown, and its rooms filled with dust and cobwebs. The people of Darkshire avoid the place, and some claim that strange noises can be heard from within on moonless nights. It is a lonely reminder of the ordinary lives that were swept away by the darkness of Duskwood.

245.name: The Yorgen Farmstead
245.description: The Yorgen Farmstead is an abandoned farm in southern Duskwood, once the home of a farming family who met a terrible fate when the darkness fell. The farmstead is now in the hands of the Defias Brotherhood, whose stealthy assassins lurk in the shadows of the barn and the overgrown fields. The farmhouse is dark and empty, and the locals say that something terrible happened here, though few speak of it openly. Travelers are warned to stay alert when passing nearby.

492.name: Raven Hill Cemetery
492.description: Raven Hill Cemetery is a sprawling graveyard north of the abandoned town of Raven Hill in western Duskwood, one of the largest burial grounds in the Kingdom of Stormwind. It holds the graves of the many people killed by wild beasts and undead since the darkness fell, as well as the ancient tombs of the town's honored dead. Now the cemetery is crawling with scores of undead, as well as massive spiders and gangs of grave robbers who loot the tombs. Beneath it lie the Dawning Wood Catacombs, home to the most powerful undead in the region, and the dark hill of Forlorn Rowe looms at its northwestern corner. A fearsome undead warrior is said to patrol the grounds, and few dare to walk among the graves after dark.

536.name: Addle's Stead
536.description: Addle's Stead is an abandoned farmstead in southwestern Duskwood, south of Raven Hill and west of the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. Like many farms in the region, it was deserted when the darkness crept into Duskwood, and it has since been taken over by agents of the Defias Brotherhood, who creep through the fields, hide in the barn, and lurk in the small farmhouse. The fields are overgrown and the buildings decaying, and the bandits use the farm as a hideout for their schemes.

576.name: Beggar's Haunt
576.description: Beggar's Haunt is a ruined stone tower in northeastern Duskwood, east of Manor Mistmantle and north of the road leading into Deadwind Pass. It serves as a discreet outpost for agents of the Forsaken, who keep watch over the region and conduct their own studies of the curse that has fallen over the forest. A twisting path leads from the tower to a small pool and waterfall, near which rests an unmarked grave flanked by two great statues. The tower is a lonely and ominous place, and the people of Darkshire regard its occupants with deep suspicion.

799.name: The Darkened Bank
799.description: The Darkened Bank stretches along the northern edge of Duskwood, following the river that separates the cursed forest from Elwynn. It runs from the western edge of Duskwood east to the bridge connecting to the Redridge Mountains. The riverbank is shrouded in mist and shadow, and the trees lean over the dark water. Spiders, wolves, and other creatures roam the area, and a small camp of refugees has been set up at its western end. Across the river, the bright forests of Elwynn are a painful reminder of what Duskwood once was.

856.name: Twilight Grove
856.description: Twilight Grove lies in the heart of Duskwood, within the crater of an ancient, long-dead volcano. Unlike the rest of the cursed forest, the grove is bathed in a peaceful, eternal twilight, and it has a surprisingly night elven feel, with lush vegetation and a moonwell. At its center stands one of the great trees that serve as portals to the Emerald Dream, watched over by the green dragonflight of the Dreaming Aspect Ysera. The influence of the sleeping druids can be felt throughout the grove, and the air is still and dreamlike. Yet whispers of a growing corruption within the Dream have reached even here, and a sense of unease lingers beneath the tranquility.

1097.name: The Hushed Bank
1097.description: The Hushed Bank is the stretch of western Duskwood along the river that separates the forest from Westfall, running south from where the borders of Westfall, Elwynn, and Duskwood meet toward Stranglethorn Vale. A covered bridge connects Duskwood with Westfall here. The bank is eerily quiet, as its name suggests, and the dark waters flow silently past the gnarled trees. Spiders and wolves inhabit the area, and a small camp of refugees can be found at its northern end.

1098.name: Manor Mistmantle
1098.description: Manor Mistmantle is the ancestral home of the Mistmantle family, standing in northeastern Duskwood, north of Darkshire and west of Beggar's Haunt. Once a fine estate, it has fallen into ruin and decay, its grounds rotten and overrun by ghoulish undead. A dark tale of tragedy surrounds the family, and the people of Darkshire avoid speaking of it. The only sign of life on the property is a single flower that still blooms in the overgrown garden. The manor is a gloomy, haunted place, and few venture near it.

2098.name: Dawning Wood Catacombs
2098.description: The Dawning Wood Catacombs lie beneath Raven Hill Cemetery in western Duskwood, a twisting network of tombs and burial chambers that are home to the most powerful undead in the region. Swarms of ghouls and skeletons lurk in the darkness, guarding the tombs of their former brethren, and the stench of decay fills the air. The catacombs have two separate entrances, one leading into a den of diseased ghouls and the other into a hall of skeletal warriors. Few who enter alone return.

2161.name: Roland's Doom
2161.description: Roland's Doom is an abandoned mine in southern Duskwood, near the Rotting Orchard. It is said that the mine was where the darkness first took hold, and that a team of men who entered it in search of its source were torn apart by worgen. Whoever Roland was, he apparently died here, and his name has become a grim byword. Today the mine is infested by worgen, who use it as a lair, and the area around it is one of the most dangerous in Duskwood. The entrance is dark and silent, and the howls of the wolf-men echo from its depths.

10.description: Duskwood is a dark, cursed forest lying south of Elwynn Forest, east of Westfall, west of Deadwind Pass, and north of the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Once the southern reaches of Elwynn, a bright and beautiful woodland with two prosperous towns, it has been swallowed by an unnatural, eternal twilight. Black fog hangs among gnarled, twisted trees, the sun never fully breaks through the gloom, and the air is cold and heavy with the smell of rot and damp earth. The origin of the darkness is shrouded in rumor: some blame the evil leaking from the haunted tower of Karazhan in nearby Deadwind Pass, others speak of an ancient artifact and the savage worgen that appeared alongside the curse. Whatever its cause, the land is now plagued by the walking dead, who rise from the graveyards, by ferocious worgen that roam the woods and abandoned farmsteads, by giant spiders, and by the sinister Black Riders said to ride out of the night. Ogres have moved in from the east, and Defias bandits lurk in the deserted farms. Technically part of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Duskwood has been largely abandoned by the crown, and its stubborn, suspicious people huddle in the town of Darkshire, defended by their own militia, the Night Watch. In the heart of the forest, a sheltered grove around one of the great trees of the druids remains bathed in a strange, peaceful twilight, a portal to the Emerald Dream watched over by the green dragonflight.

11.name: Wetlands

118.name: Whelgar's Excavation Site
118.description: Whelgar's Excavation Site lies east of Menethil Harbor and southwest of Dun Modr in the Wetlands, a dwarven dig site carved into the rocky hills in search of ancient relics and fossils. Once a peaceful place of study, it has been overrun by mottled raptors, which nest among the excavations and attack anyone who comes near. The remaining dwarves of the expedition have retreated to a ridge overlooking the site, where they cling to their camp and their research. Scaffolding, tools, and half-uncovered bones of ancient creatures litter the dig, and the cries of raptors echo across the damp hills.

150.name: Menethil Harbor
150.description: Menethil Harbor is a fortified port town on the western coast of the Wetlands, built by dwarves and humans on an island in Baradin Bay and named after the royal house of Lordaeron. Established after the Third War as the main sea link between Khaz Modan and the kingdoms of the Alliance, it is the only stable Alliance presence in this wild region, a small but well-defended town of over ten thousand souls. Ships sail from its docks to Theramore Isle in Kalimdor and to Valgarde in Northrend, and gryphons connect it with Ironforge and other Alliance holdings. The imposing Menethil Keep dominates the town, and the Deepwater Tavern offers warmth and ale to sailors and travelers. Life here is hard: murlocs from the nearby marshes and the Dragonmaw orcs to the east are a constant threat, and the townsfolk are known to be braver and sterner than most. The air smells of salt, tar, and fish, and the cries of gulls mingle with the creak of ships at anchor.

205.name: Dun Modr
205.description: Dun Modr is a fortified dwarven town on the road just south of the Thandol Span in the northern Wetlands, near the ruins of an ancient dwarven city that once stretched across both sides of the channel. It has always been of great strategic importance: during the Second War, the orcs used it as a staging area until a force of warriors from Stromgarde laid siege to it and drove them back toward Dun Algaz. In recent times, while the Alliance armies were called away to distant battles, the Dark Iron dwarves seized Dun Modr and damaged the Thandol Span. Now the Dark Irons claim the fallen town as their own and attack anything that enters their territory, and the dwarves of Ironforge struggle to hold the remaining bridge and retake the town.

298.name: Baradin Bay
298.description: Baradin Bay is a broad portion of the Great Sea off the western coast of the central Eastern Kingdoms, washing the northwestern shores of the Wetlands north of Menethil Harbor and stretching toward the coasts of Hillsbrad and southern Lordaeron. Its name is believed to derive from the island fortress of Tol Barad, which lies out in its waters. The bay is grey and often shrouded in mist, its cold waters churned by the winds that sweep in from the sea. Ships bound to and from Menethil Harbor ply its waters, and murlocs dwell in hovels along its marshy shores. The wrecks of the Kul Tiran Lost Fleet lie off its coast, a grim reminder of the Second War.

299.name: Menethil Bay
299.description: Menethil Bay is the stretch of the Great Sea surrounding Menethil Harbor on the western coast of the Wetlands. Its waters are the gateway to the harbor, and ships from Kalimdor and Northrend sail through it to reach the docks. The bay and its marshy shores are crawling with crocolisks of all sizes, which are often hunted for their fine leather and pose a danger to careless travelers and fishermen. Grey skies, salty winds, and frequent mists give the bay a bleak, desolate beauty, and the lights of Menethil Keep serve as a beacon for incoming ships.

309.name: Ironbeard's Tomb
309.description: Ironbeard's Tomb is an ancient dwarven crypt just west of the road to Dun Modr in the north-central Wetlands, the burial place of the Ironbeard clan. Once a solemn and sacred site, it has been defiled by oozes of black, crimson, and monstrous varieties, which have crept into its halls and fill them with foul, corrosive slime. None who wish to lay their dead to rest come here any longer, and the tomb has fallen into decay, its stone carvings worn and its entrances choked with moss and filth. Its fate is yet another sign of how far the dwarves' former holdings in the Wetlands have fallen.

836.name: Dun Algaz
836.description: On the Wetlands side, Dun Algaz is the mountain pass leading south from the marshes into Loch Modan and the dwarven heartland. The tunnels pass through the ruins of an ancient dwarven stronghold, which became the Horde's last hold in Khaz Modan during the Second War. Today the old outpost in the middle of the pass has been overrun by orcs of the Dragonmaw clan, forcing the dwarven mountaineers to fall back to the upper tunnel near Loch Modan. The road through the pass remains the main route between Menethil Harbor and the dwarven lands, but it is dangerous to travel, and the dark, echoing tunnels are best crossed quickly and with weapons ready.

881.name: Thandol Span
881.description: On the Wetlands side, the Thandol Span rises from the misty northern hills of the marshland and stretches across the deep sea channel toward the Arathi Highlands. The great dwarven bridge has been badly damaged, first by the Scourge during the Third War and more recently by the Dark Iron dwarves, who all but destroyed one of its bridges and seized the nearby town of Dun Modr. Dwarven forces fight to hold the remaining bridge, and the guard posts along its length are tense and watchful. The roar of the waves crashing against the bridge's massive pillars far below fills the air, and the wind carries cold sea spray across the stone.

1016.name: Direforge Hill
1016.description: Direforge Hill is a rocky hill in the northeastern Wetlands, just southeast of Dun Modr, where Dark Iron dwarves have established several small camps. From here, the Dark Irons support their occupation of Dun Modr and their attacks on the Thandol Span, and their sorcerers and soldiers are a constant danger to anyone traveling the road nearby. Smoke from their forges and campfires rises above the hill, and the area is marked by crude fortifications, weapons racks, and the banners of the Dark Iron clan.

1017.name: Raptor Ridge
1017.description: Raptor Ridge is a rocky ridge in the eastern Wetlands, just northwest of the Dragonmaw Gates and the road leading up to Grim Batol. Raptors lair here in great numbers, and the ridge also features a cavern where a fierce raptor matriarch guards her brood. The beasts are aggressive and territorial, and their cries ring out across the damp hills. Few travelers venture onto the ridge willingly, and those who must pass near do so with great caution.

1018.name: Black Channel Marsh
1018.description: Black Channel Marsh is a stretch of murky bogland in the southwestern Wetlands, crossed by the road leading to Menethil Harbor. The dark, slow-moving waters and thick reeds give it its name, and the marsh holds numerous raptor lairs. Some of the hungrier beasts wander dangerously close to the road, and travelers are advised to stay alert. Mist hangs low over the water, and the air is heavy with the smell of rot and wet earth.

1020.name: Mosshide Fen
1020.description: Mosshide Fen is a region of marshland in the eastern Wetlands, near the tunnels of Dun Algaz, which has fallen under the control of the Mosshide tribe of gnolls. Several of their crude camps dot the soggy landscape, and the gnolls, led by a vicious chieftain, prey on anyone who wanders through their territory. The fen is a damp, foul-smelling place of mud, reeds, and stagnant pools, and its proximity to the road through Dun Algaz makes it a constant threat to travelers heading to and from Loch Modan.

1021.name: Thelgen Rock
1021.description: Thelgen Rock is a rocky outcrop in the southern Wetlands, best known for the extensive cavern that stretches deep beneath it into the mountains of Khaz Modan. The caves and their surroundings are crawling with poisonous spiders, which spin thick webs throughout the tunnels and prey on anything that strays inside. The cavern also holds deposits of rare ores, which draw miners willing to brave the danger. The dark, twisting passages are notoriously confusing, and it is said that even seasoned cartographers have lost their way within.

1022.name: Bluegill Marsh
1022.description: Bluegill Marsh is a stretch of marshland on the western coast of the Wetlands, north of Menethil Harbor, home to several camps of the Bluegill murlocs. The murlocs dwell in crude huts along the shore and in the shallow waters, and they travel in groups, making them dangerous to lone travelers. Led by a particularly ferocious murloc, they raid nearby settlements and steal whatever they can carry. The marsh is a wet, reedy place where the gurgling cries of murlocs mingle with the sound of the waves.

1023.name: Saltspray Glen
1023.description: Saltspray Glen is a small glen in the northwestern Wetlands, bordered by Bluegill Marsh to the south, Ironbeard's Tomb to the east, and Baradin Bay to the north and west. It takes its name from the ease with which strong winds off the bay drive seawater inland, coating the grasses and trees with salt. Like much of the Wetlands, the glen is crawling with raptors that nest among its rocks and thickets, and the area is wild and dangerous despite its proximity to the sea.

1024.name: Sundown Marsh
1024.description: Sundown Marsh is the deepest and most remote part of the Wetlands, a vast tangle of bogs, pools, and reed beds where the mists rarely lift. In the midst of the swamp stands a small stone dwelling with a windmill, home to a pair of eccentric traders who sell the odd things they find in the marsh to those brave enough to visit. The surrounding swampland is full of aggressive crocolisks, gnolls, raptors, bog beasts, and oozes, which discourage most travelers from approaching. The marsh is eerily beautiful at sunset, when the fading light turns the mists golden, but it is a dangerous place to be caught after dark.

1025.name: The Green Belt
1025.description: The Green Belt is an area of the eastern Wetlands where trees and shrubs grow especially thick and swamp flowers bloom all year round, a lush oasis in the otherwise grey marshland. It is said that a solitary guardian of nature dwells here, and where he treads, plants spring to life and blossoms flourish. The Green Belt is also home to crocolisks, bog beasts, and oozes, and its dense vegetation can conceal many dangers. The scent of flowers and wet earth fills the air, and the area has a peaceful, almost enchanted quality that sets it apart from the rest of the Wetlands.

1036.name: Angerfang Encampment
1036.description: The Angerfang Encampment, located in the southern hills of the Wetlands, is home to the remnants of the Dragonmaw clan of orcs. After the Second War, when the red dragons they had enslaved broke free and turned on them, the surviving Dragonmaw fled to the mountains and established this camp as their new base of operations. Led by the son of the infamous Nekros Skullcrusher, who once held the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza captive, the Dragonmaw remain loyal to the old ways of the Horde and reject Thrall's leadership. They use the encampment as a rallying point for raids against Menethil Harbor and the surrounding lands, and its crude palisades, war banners, and bone-strewn grounds make it one of the most dangerous places in the region.

1037.name: Grim Batol
1037.description: Grim Batol is a legendary mountain fortress in the eastern Wetlands, its great walls and spires reaching toward the steel-grey sky, though the bulk of the stronghold lies deep underground. Founded by the Wildhammer dwarves after the War of the Three Hammers, it was attacked by the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud, whose death within its halls left an evil taint that forced the Wildhammers to abandon it for Aerie Peak. During the Second War, the Dragonmaw orcs seized the fortress and used it to hold the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza captive, breeding her children as war mounts for the Horde until she was freed and took her vengeance on her captors. Today a flight of red dragons commands Grim Batol, guarding its desolate halls and letting no one near. The ruins of the orcish caravans that tried to flee the fortress can still be seen scattered along the road leading to its gates.

1038.name: Dragonmaw Gates
1038.description: The Dragonmaw Gates are a series of grandiose stone gates blocking the winding mountain path that leads up to Grim Batol in the eastern Wetlands. Built in ages past, they now stand as the outer defenses of the ancient fortress, guarded by dragonkin of the red dragonflight and powerful drakes who attack any who approach. The road beyond climbs through desolate, rocky slopes toward the fortress itself, and the shattered remains of orcish wagons and siege engines from the Second War still litter the way. Few who are not invited by the dragons dare to pass through the gates.

1039.name: The Lost Fleet
1039.description: The Lost Fleet is the sunken remnant of the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, which lies in the shallow waters of Baradin Bay off the northern coast of Bluegill Marsh. Under the command of Derek Proudmoore, son of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, the fleet was destroyed by the Dragonmaw clan and their dragons during the Second War. The wrecked hulls of the ships still jut from the water, and it is said that the fleet is cursed, for the drowned crew have risen as restless undead who continue to haunt the wreckage. Sailors avoid the area, and the eerie silence of the wrecks is broken only by the creak of rotting timbers and the lapping of waves.

2103.name: Menethil Keep
2103.description: Menethil Keep is the stone fortress that dominates the port town of Menethil Harbor, rising above the docks and houses as the seat of the town's military command. The keep houses the commander of the Menethil militia and serves as the heart of the town's defense against the Dragonmaw orcs and the other threats of the Wetlands. Its thick walls, banners, and watchful guards give it an air of strength and order, and its towers offer a view across Baradin Bay and the misty marshes beyond. The keep is also a reminder of the town's ties to the old kingdoms of the Alliance, for its stern architecture recalls the fortresses of Lordaeron.

2104.name: Deepwater Tavern
2104.description: The Deepwater Tavern is the main tavern of Menethil Harbor, a lively, crowded establishment where sailors, soldiers, dwarves, and travelers gather to drink, eat, and swap stories. Its wooden walls are hung with nets, anchors, and other reminders of the sea, and the air is thick with the smell of ale, smoke, and salt. The tavern is known for its boisterous atmosphere and the bar brawls that frequently break out among its patrons, but it is also a welcome refuge from the cold, damp marshes outside. Many a journey to Kalimdor or Northrend begins with a final drink at the Deepwater.

2365.name: The Great Sea
2365.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the western coast of the Wetlands, stretching out beyond Baradin Bay and Menethil Harbor toward the open ocean. Grey waves roll in from the west, often under heavy skies and drifting mists, and the cold winds carry the smell of salt far inland. Ships bound for Theramore in Kalimdor and Valgarde in Northrend sail out across these waters from Menethil Harbor, while murlocs and crocolisks lurk along the marshy shoreline. The sunken wrecks of the Kul Tiran Lost Fleet rest in the shallows nearby, a grim reminder of the battles once fought along this coast.

2402.name: The Forbidding Sea
2402.description: In the far north of the Wetlands, beneath the cliffs and the great Thandol Span, a narrow channel of cold, deep seawater cuts between Khaz Modan and the Arathi Highlands, leading east toward the Forbidding Sea. The waters are rough and treacherous, churned by strong currents and winds, and broken sections of the damaged bridge lie beneath the waves, some visible at low tide. Few ships venture into the channel, and the roar of the surf against the bridge's massive pillars echoes off the surrounding cliffs.

11.description: The Wetlands are a vast, cold marshland in northern Khaz Modan, stretching below the Stonewrought Dam between the mountains of the dwarven homeland and the sea. Bordered by mountains on three sides and open to Baradin Bay in the west, the region is laced with small rivers, ponds, bogs, and reed-choked channels. Mists cloak the ground, the overcast sky turns the land a uniform grey, and rain falls often, keeping the air damp and chill. Once part of the ancient dwarven kingdom, the Wetlands later came under the Wildhammer clan after the War of the Three Hammers, and many dwarven strongholds were built here. War has since reduced most of them to rubble: the Horde ravaged the land in the Second War, when the Dragonmaw clan held the fortress of Grim Batol and used the captive red Dragonqueen Alexstrasza to breed war mounts, and the Scourge brought further devastation in the Third War. Today the Wetlands are wild and untamed. The port town of Menethil Harbor on the western coast is the main Alliance presence, a vital link by sea between Khaz Modan, Kalimdor, and Northrend. Elsewhere, the remnants of the Dragonmaw orcs lurk in the southern hills, Dark Iron dwarves hold Dun Modr and threaten the Thandol Span, gnolls and murlocs roam the marshes, raptors and crocolisks hunt the bogs, and the red dragonflight jealously guards Grim Batol. The region serves as a buffer between the dwarven lands and the troubled kingdoms of Lordaeron to the north.

12.name: Elwynn Forest

9.name: Northshire Valley
9.description: Northshire Valley is a pristine, sheltered valley in the foothills of northern Elwynn Forest, home to Northshire Abbey and its vineyards. Surrounded by steep, forested mountains, it can be entered only through a pass to the south guarded by thick stone walls, and the Northshire River flows through it on its way to Crystal Lake. The valley is a place of green meadows, tall trees, and the peaceful sound of the abbey bells, where young recruits of the Stormwind army and the clergy of the Holy Light begin their training. Yet even here the peace is troubled: wolves driven from Duskwood prowl the woods in growing numbers, kobolds have infested the nearby mine, and Defias bandits have seized the vineyards. The guards of the abbey work hard to keep order in this cherished corner of the kingdom.

18.name: Crystal Lake
18.description: Crystal Lake is a clear, sparkling lake just east of Goldshire in Elwynn Forest, fed by the waters of the Northshire River. Its shores are lined with grass and tall trees, and on calm days its surface mirrors the sky like polished glass. The lake is a pleasant sight for travelers on the road between Goldshire and the eastern farms, but it is not without danger: murlocs have settled along its banks and in its waters, and they attack unwary fishermen and passersby. The locals tell strange tales about the lake, including stories of odd objects fished up from its depths, and few care to linger by its shores after dark.

23.name: Northshire River
23.description: The Northshire River flows from the mountains north of Elwynn Forest through Northshire Valley, past the abbey and its vineyards, and finally empties into Crystal Lake east of Goldshire. Its clear, cold waters rush over smooth stones and small waterfalls, and the riverbanks are lined with tall grass, wildflowers, and shady trees. The river provides fresh water for the abbey and the surrounding farms, and its gentle murmur is one of the most familiar sounds of the valley. Wolves and other wild animals often come to drink along its banks.

24.name: Northshire Abbey
