24.description: Northshire Abbey is the home of the Brotherhood of Northshire, an order of clerics devoted to the Holy Light, standing in the sheltered Northshire Valley in the foothills of Elwynn Forest. Its great stone halls, library, and hall of arms make it both a place of worship and a center for training the young defenders of the kingdom. Before the First War, the abbey was home to the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, whose leader, Archbishop Alonsus Faol, aided Stormwind's armies against the Horde; the abbey was destroyed in the orcish onslaught, and during the Second War its ruins served as the headquarters of the Twilight's Hammer clan. After the Alliance reclaimed Elwynn, the abbey was rebuilt, and today it serves as a recruiting and training ground for the Stormwind army, where warriors, priests, mages, and paladins take their first steps. A small graveyard rests to the east of the abbey, and its bells ring out across the peaceful valley.

34.name: Echo Ridge Mine
34.description: Echo Ridge Mine is a small mine in the northwestern part of Northshire Valley in Elwynn Forest, carved into the forested ridge that gives it its name. It was worked by local miners until it was overrun by a clan of kobolds, who drove the workers out and now dig through its tunnels by the light of candles stuck to their heads. The kobolds pose little threat to the abbey itself, but the guards fear their foothold in the valley will only grow if they are ignored. The sound of picks and the squeaky chatter of kobolds echo from the mine's dark entrance.

54.name: Jasperlode Mine
54.description: Jasperlode Mine is one of the key mining sites in Elwynn Forest, located along the road east of Goldshire, which once provided Stormwind with valuable ore and stone needed in the wars. Lately it has been overrun by kobolds, and with the kingdom's soldiers tied up on distant fronts, Stormwind lacks the manpower to drive the vermin out. The kobolds themselves are not safe in the deepest recesses of the mine, however, for a colony of mine spiders has made its nest there, preying on the hapless kobolds. The mine's tunnels are dark, damp, and dangerous, and the miners who once worked them now wait for the day they can return.

56.name: Heroes' Vigil
56.description: Heroes' Vigil is the heart of the island in the middle of Stone Cairn Lake in eastern Elwynn Forest, where a ring of stones surrounds a monument known as the Stone of Remembrance. The monument commemorates those who died when the orcs sacked Goldshire and the surrounding lands during the First War, and it was once a place of quiet pilgrimage for the people of Elwynn. In recent times, however, the island has fallen into the hands of Defias bandits and their renegade wizards, who have desecrated the peace of the memorial. The ancient stones still stand in silent vigil, a solemn reminder of the kingdom's darkest days.

57.name: Fargodeep Mine
57.description: Fargodeep Mine is an old gold mine located south of Goldshire in Elwynn Forest, near the Stonefield and Maclure farms. Once a source of wealth for the region, it has been abandoned by its miners and overrun by kobolds, who scurry through its tunnels collecting candles and gold dust. Rumor has it that the kobolds may be working in league with the Defias Brotherhood, gathering gold from the mines for the bandits. The entrance is dark and littered with abandoned carts and tools, and the deeper tunnels are a maze of narrow passages and underground chambers.

59.name: Northshire Vineyards
59.description: The Northshire Vineyards lie just northeast of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest, rows of grapevines climbing the gentle hillsides of the valley. For years they were the pride of the abbey and produced fine wines for Stormwind, but they have been taken over by agents of the Defias Brotherhood, who have driven out the workers and use the vineyards as a base for raiding the local farmers and merchants. The bandits lurk among the vines, wearing their distinctive red bandanas, and the vineyard workers can only watch helplessly as their harvest is stolen. The occupation is a bitter sign of how far the Defias' influence has spread.

60.name: Forest's Edge
60.description: Forest's Edge is a wide stretch of woodland in southwestern Elwynn Forest, bordering the dry fields of Westfall and the shadowed forests of Duskwood across the river. It lies between Mirror Lake Orchard, the Nazferiti River, and the small river along the Westfall border. A tribe of Riverpaw gnolls has set up camps in the woods here, led by a notoriously vicious chieftain, and they pose a growing threat to the farms and roads of western Elwynn. The soldiers of the nearby Westbrook Garrison patrol the area to keep the gnolls in check. Boars and other wild animals roam the trees, and copper veins can be found along the riverbanks.

61.name: Thunder Falls
61.description: Thunder Falls is a picturesque waterfall in western Elwynn Forest, where a river plunges from a rocky plateau into Mirror Lake below. Fed by waters cascading from the mountains to the north, it is an unusual double-sided waterfall, and the roar of the falling water can be heard from far away. A steep path near the falls leads up to the plateau above, where Defias bandits have set up a small camp, taking advantage of the secluded location. The falls are a place of natural beauty, spoiled only by the presence of the outlaws.

62.name: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch
62.description: The Brackwell Pumpkin Patch is a farmstead in southeastern Elwynn Forest, whose fields of plump orange pumpkins were once a common sight along the road. It has been taken over by the Defias Brotherhood, whose agents now patrol its two buildings and use it as a hideout. A large, prize-winning boar roams the pumpkin patch along with its companion, and the beast has become notorious among the local farmers for raiding their crops. The farm is a dangerous place for unwary travelers, and its rightful owners have long since fled.

63.name: The Stonefield Farm
63.description: The Stonefield Farm is a homestead in southern Elwynn Forest, south of Goldshire, owned by the Stonefield family. The farm is known for its fields and livestock, and for the bitter feud between the Stonefields and their neighbors, the Maclures, whose vineyards lie just across the way. The two families have long despised each other, though rumors say that a child from each family has fallen in love, which may one day bring the feuding clans together. The farm's matriarch is well known in the area, and the farm offers a warm meal and a kind word to travelers who stop by.

64.name: The Maclure Vineyards
64.description: The Maclure Vineyards are a family-owned vineyard in southern Elwynn Forest, south of Goldshire, belonging to the Maclure family. Rows of grapevines cover the gentle slopes around the family's farmhouse, and the Maclures take great pride in their wine. The family is locked in a bitter rivalry with their neighbors, the Stonefields, a feud so old that few remember how it began. Wild boars roam the vineyards and the surrounding fields in large numbers, often trampling the vines and eating the crops.

86.name: Stone Cairn Lake
86.description: Stone Cairn Lake is a ring-shaped lake in northeastern Elwynn Forest, its waters encircling a large island crowned by Heroes' Vigil, the stone monument commemorating those who fell during the First War. For years the lake was a peaceful place of pilgrimage, but it has recently fallen into the hands of Defias bandits and renegade wizards who have settled on the island. A tribe of murlocs has also raised crude huts along the southern banks, and wolves and bears roam the surrounding woods. The hills near the lake are rich in copper, and miners still brave the dangers to work the veins.

87.name: Goldshire
87.description: Goldshire is a bustling village at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest, one of the oldest and most important settlements of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Roads lead from it northwest to Stormwind City, northeast to Northshire Abbey, west to Westfall, and east to Redridge, making it a vital center of trade where travelers, merchants, soldiers, and priests stop on their journeys. At its heart stands the Lion's Pride Inn, one of the most respectable alehouses in Azeroth, famous for its warm hearth and lively company. Home to about seven thousand souls, mostly farmers, miners, and traders, Goldshire is led by an elected marshal and protected by the Stormwind guard. During the First War, the village was destroyed by the Horde, but it has since been rebuilt and has returned to its former glory. Today it also shelters many refugees from Westfall who have fled the Defias Brotherhood, and its guards keep watch against the bandits, kobolds, gnolls, and murlocs that threaten the surrounding countryside.

88.name: Eastvale Logging Camp
88.description: The Eastvale Logging Camp lies in the far east of Elwynn Forest, in the shadow of the Redridge Mountains, north of the main road. Its lumberjacks work tirelessly to fill the constant orders for timber flowing in from Stormwind and beyond, and the camp is a busy place of sawmills, stacked logs, and the ring of axes. Because it lies in wilder country, the camp is troubled by wolves and bears, which chase off workers and threaten to delay deliveries, and the Stormwind guard has been forced to step in. The camp also has stables where fine horses are bred and sold, for the riders of Elwynn are proud of their steeds.

89.name: Mirror Lake Orchard
89.description: Mirror Lake Orchard lies in western Elwynn Forest, on the southern banks of Mirror Lake. Its fruit trees once produced fresh apples and pears for the people of the region, but the orchard has been taken over by Defias bandits, who have stripped the trees bare and claimed the nearby cottage as their own. Whoever lived here is long gone, another victim of the growing banditry in the region. The orchard is still a pretty place, with its neat rows of trees and the glittering lake beyond, but travelers are wise to pass it by with care.

91.name: Tower of Azora
91.description: The Tower of Azora is a small mage tower in eastern Elwynn Forest, east of Goldshire and northwest of the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. It is the home of an archmage who presides over a staff of gnomish servants, and it is a place of magical study and enchantment. The tower's master is locked in a long-standing rivalry with the sorcerer of the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains, and the two towers are said to spy on each other through magical means. The tower's magical aura is known to have strange effects on its surroundings, and the servants occasionally have to deal with animated objects and oddly mutated creatures.

92.name: Mirror Lake
92.description: Mirror Lake is a small, beautiful lake in western Elwynn Forest, fed by the waters of Thunder Falls cascading from the plateau above. The lake earns its name from the way it shines brightly in the afternoon sun, reflecting the trees and sky like a polished mirror. It would be an ideal spot for swimming or fishing, but the Defias bandits who infest the nearby orchard and the plateau above make such pursuits hazardous. The mages of Stormwind have shown some interest in the lake's waters, suspecting that they may hold unusual magical properties.

120.name: Westbrook Garrison
120.description: Westbrook Garrison is a fortified outpost of the Stormwind guard on the western edge of Elwynn Forest, near the border with Westfall, considered by many to be the last bastion of order heading west from Stormwind. Its soldiers patrol the borderlands against the Riverpaw gnolls lurking in the woods to the south and the Defias bandits slipping in from the lawless fields of Westfall. The Stormwind guard often uses the garrison as a testing ground for newly initiated knights, and the soldiers and mercenaries stationed here are known as a loud, brawling bunch, eager for tales from the road, a good mug of ale, and a good fight. Wanted posters on the garrison's walls name the most notorious threats to the region.

797.name: Jerod's Landing
797.description: Jerod's Landing is a boat landing on the Elwynn Forest bank of the Nazferiti River, in the southeastern part of the forest near the border of Duskwood. Once a quiet place where boats and barges were loaded with goods, it has been taken over by the Defias Brotherhood, who use it to smuggle stolen goods from Redridge to their hideouts in Westfall. The area around the landing is crawling with Defias rogues and bandits, making it hazardous to cross. The river flows lazily past the dock, and the dark forests of Duskwood loom on the far bank.

798.name: Ridgepoint Tower
798.description: Ridgepoint Tower is a stone guard tower in eastern Elwynn Forest, one of several built after the Second War to defend the human lands against their enemies. It stands on a rise near the border of the Redridge Mountains and Duskwood, keeping watch for gnolls and orcs from Redridge, undead from the shadowed woods to the south, and Defias bandits from nearby camps. The tower's garrison is small but vigilant, and its beacon can be seen from across the eastern forest.

12.description: Elwynn Forest is the green heartland of the Kingdom of Stormwind, a gentle land of tall oaks and pines, rolling meadows, clear lakes, and rushing rivers lying south of the capital. Its climate is mild and temperate, with warm summers, soft rains, and golden autumns, and its people are hardy, hard-working farmers, loggers, miners, and fishermen whose harvests feed the great city to the north. Elwynn is dotted with farmsteads, vineyards, and orchards, and at its center lies the bustling village of Goldshire, while Northshire Abbey, home of the clerics of the Holy Light, rests in a sheltered valley to the north. The forest has known great suffering: during the First War, the orcish Horde overran Elwynn, razed its forests, and destroyed Goldshire and Northshire before sacking Stormwind itself. When the humans reclaimed their homeland after the Second War, rebuilding came at a heavy cost, and the high taxes and unpaid labor that followed gave rise to the Defias Brotherhood, a band of outlaws born from the disgruntled stonemasons who rebuilt the capital. Today Elwynn is peaceful by the standards of a troubled world, yet its tranquility is fragile. Defias bandits have seized farms, orchards, and landings, kobolds infest the mines, gnolls camp along the western border, murlocs haunt the lakes, and wolves and bears roam the deeper woods. The Stormwind guard patrols the roads, but the army is stretched thin by wars far beyond the kingdom's borders. Broken orcish catapults, slowly rotting among the trees, remain the only reminders of the Horde's occupation.

14.name: Durotar

362.name: Razor Hill
362.description: Razor Hill is an orcish town built at a crossroads in central Durotar, where the roads from Orgrimmar, the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village, and the Barrens meet. Its wooden buildings and spiked palisades surround the great Razor Hill Barracks, the town's most prominent structure, and some three thousand orcs live here. The town's guards keep watch against the Burning Blade cultists, the Kul Tiran marines of nearby Tiragarde Keep, and the quilboar who raid from the west. Shortly after the Third War, Razor Hill was the site of a planned summit with Kul Tiras that turned out to be an ambush, foiled by the hero Rexxar.

363.name: Valley of Trials
363.description: The Valley of Trials is a sheltered valley in southern Durotar, where young orcs and trolls begin their journey as recruits of the Horde, safe from the dangers beyond its tall walls. Within its red cliffs, they face their first challenges against scorpids and boars, while orc peons gather lumber from the few trees that grow there. The Den, a cave carved into the cliff at the center of the valley, serves as the home of their teachers. Recently, demons have crept into caves in the northern part of the valley, suggesting that cultists of the Burning Blade may have gained a foothold there.

364.name: The Den
364.description: The Den is a small cave carved into the cliff at the center of the Valley of Trials in southern Durotar, equipped with the basic comforts of living. It is the home and workplace of the recruiters and teachers who guide young orcs and trolls through their first trials, and the place where new recruits report back as they complete their tasks. The Den is a humble but welcoming place, the first home of many a Horde warrior.

365.name: Burning Blade Coven
365.description: The Burning Blade Coven is a cave in the dusty red mountains that form the northern border of the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Imps and other lesser demons have spilled out from its mouth, causing mischief in the valley, and it is said that members of the Burning Blade, a demon-worshipping cult of orc warlocks, lurk within the abandoned caverns. The coven is a grim reminder that not all orcs have turned away from the demonic magic that once enslaved their people.

366.name: Kolkar Crag
366.description: Kolkar Crag is a craggy gorge on the southernmost shores of Durotar, where a band of Kolkar centaurs has taken up residence. The Kolkar have plotted against the orcs ever since they arrived on Kalimdor, and from this crag they plan to attack the towns of Durotar and even the gates of Orgrimmar. A mighty centaur warlord from Desolace is said to lead them. The crag is rocky and barren, and the centaurs' tents and fires dot its floor.

367.name: Sen'jin Village
367.description: Sen'jin Village is the home of the Darkspear tribe of jungle trolls on the southern coast of Durotar, a village of some two thousand trolls built of wood and thatch among the palm trees. After the Darkspear were driven from the nearby Echo Isles by the treachery of one of their own, their leader Vol'jin founded the village and named it after his father, Sen'jin, who fell saving his people from murlocs long ago. Vol'jin now resides in Orgrimmar as an advisor to Thrall, while others see to the village's needs. The trolls keep a close watch on the Echo Isles, waiting for the day they can reclaim them.

368.name: Echo Isles
368.description: The Echo Isles are a handful of small, jungle-covered islands off the southeastern coast of Durotar, once the home of the Darkspear trolls. The trolls were driven from the islands by the Kul Tiran fleet during the Third War, and when they returned, one of their own, the witch doctor Zalazane, betrayed them, using dark voodoo to enslave his people as mindless thralls and forcing the survivors to flee again to the mainland. The isles are now held by Zalazane and his enslaved trolls, and the Darkspear make constant attempts from Sen'jin Village to reclaim their home.

369.name: Thunder Ridge
369.description: Thunder Ridge is a breathtaking gorge in northwestern Durotar, southwest of Orgrimmar, untamed by any civilized race. Great thunder lizards dominate the landscape, giving the ridge its name, and tallstriders roam its fringes. The presence of the lizards helps hide a camp of the Burning Blade, led by a goblin warlock. Shortly after the founding of Durotar, the hero Rexxar discovered that human loggers here were driving the lizards mad.

370.name: Drygulch Ravine
370.description: Drygulch Ravine is a twisting canyon in western Durotar, home to Dustwind harpies who have taken to banditry, stealing supplies from caravans and hoarding them on their high cliffs. The ravine's many twists and folds make it easy for raiders to hide from Horde patrols. Its walls are red and dry, and the cries of the harpies echo through the canyon.

371.name: Dustwind Cave
371.description: Dustwind Cave is a cave atop the cliffs of Razorwind Canyon in Durotar, just northeast of Razor Hill. It has become a haven for exiled members of the Burning Blade, the demon-worshipping cult of orc warlocks, who hide here from the Horde. The cave is dark and filled with the signs of their foul rituals.

372.name: Tiragarde Keep
372.description: Tiragarde Keep is a gleaming white stone fortress on the eastern coast of Durotar, distinctly out of place among the crimson rocks of the orcish homeland. It was built by Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras when he brought his fleet to Kalimdor to destroy the orcs, in violation of the peace forged by Thrall and Jaina Proudmoore. Although the admiral was slain at Theramore, his loyal Kul Tiran marines and sailors still hold the damaged keep and are filled with contempt for the Horde. The fortress is a constant thorn in the side of Durotar.

373.name: Scuttle Coast
373.description: The Scuttle Coast is the stretch of the eastern coast of Durotar southeast of Razor Hill, near Tiragarde Keep. The shore is littered with the wrecks of Kul Tiran ships, smashed upon the rocks during the battles between the orcs and Admiral Proudmoore's fleet, and the orcs still salvage pieces of the ships' cargo. Crabs and makrura scuttle along the beach, and the waves crash against the broken hulls.

374.name: Bladefist Bay
374.description: Bladefist Bay is the stretch of the Great Sea off the northeastern coast of Durotar and the southern coast of Azshara, near Skull Rock. It is named after Kargath Bladefist, the legendary chieftain of the Shattered Hand clan. The bay's waters are blue and calm, and its rocky shores are home to crabs and seabirds.

375.name: Deadeye Shore
375.description: Deadeye Shore is a stretch of the eastern coast of Durotar, directly east of Drygulch Ravine. It is named after Kilrogg Deadeye, the legendary chieftain of the Bleeding Hollow clan, for Thrall has named many places in the new orcish homeland after the fallen heroes of the Horde. The shore is rocky and windswept, and the waves of the Great Sea break against its cliffs.

393.name: Darkspear Strand
393.description: The Darkspear Strand is the stretch of beach on the southern coast of Durotar where the Darkspear trolls landed when they fled the Echo Isles. Just beyond the strand lies Sen'jin Village, founded by Vol'jin after the flight. From the beach, the Echo Isles can be seen across the water, a constant reminder of the home the trolls lost.

410.name: Razorwind Canyon
410.description: Razorwind Canyon is a canyon in central Durotar, the nesting ground of the Dustwind harpies. The aggressive harpies are numerous throughout the canyon, guarding their nests and eggs, and they can quickly overwhelm unwary travelers. The canyon's walls are steep and red, and the wind howls through it constantly.

638.name: Hidden Path
638.description: The Hidden Path is a secret route through the mountains bordering the Valley of Trials in Durotar, known to those who follow the path of the shaman. It leads to the mystical Spirit Rock, and from its highest point there is a fine view of the Barrens. The path is narrow and winding, and few know of its existence.

639.name: Spirit Rock
639.description: Spirit Rock is a place sacred to the shamans of the Horde, located in the hills high above the Valley of Trials in Durotar and reached by the Hidden Path. Young shamans come here to commune with the spirits of the earth. The rock offers a peaceful, wind-swept retreat with a view of the surrounding lands.

640.name: Shrine of the Dormant Flame
640.description: The Shrine of the Dormant Flame is a place most holy to the shamans of the Horde, reached by a secret path that spirals around the tallest mountain northwest of the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Young shamans climb here to commune with the spirits of fire. The summit offers a fantastic view of the region, but the narrow path and the cliffs make the climb perilous.

814.name: Southfury River
814.description: On the side of Durotar, the Southfury River forms the western border of the orcish homeland, separating it from the Barrens. The wide, swift-flowing river is patrolled by crocolisks, and a bridge near Far Watch Post connects Durotar with the Barrens. Its banks are lined with reeds, and the red cliffs of Durotar rise above its eastern shore.

816.name: Razormane Grounds
816.description: The Razormane Grounds are an area in central Durotar that forms the front line of the battle between the Horde and the Razormane quilboar, who seek to expand from the Barrens into the orcish homeland. The bones of dead animals stripped of their flesh litter the ground, and thorny brambles burst from the red mountains above. For every quilboar cut down, two more seem to emerge from the thickets.

817.name: Skull Rock
817.description: Skull Rock is a cave in northeastern Durotar, one of several holdouts of the Burning Blade, the demon-worshipping cult of orc warlocks who reject Thrall's new Horde. The cave is dark and dangerous, filled with cultists and their demons, and its entrance is marked by a great rock shaped like a skull.

1296.name: Rocktusk Farm
1296.description: Rocktusk Farm is a pig farm in Durotar, just outside the gates of Orgrimmar. Its owners feel fairly safe so close to the capital, and they raise their swine to provide food for the Horde. The farm is a simple place of pens, a farmhouse, and grunting pigs.

1297.name: Jaggedswine Farm
1297.description: Jaggedswine Farm is one of several pig farms in Durotar, close to the zeppelin tower and Orgrimmar. It has a house, a large pig pen, and a pond, and its swine provide food for the Horde. The farm appears quiet, its owner perhaps away on business in the city.

2320.name: The Great Sea
2320.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the eastern and southern coasts of Durotar, rolling onto red rocky shores and sandy beaches. The coast is littered with the wrecks of Kul Tiran ships from the battles of the Third War, and the Echo Isles lie off the southern shore. Crabs, makrura, and murlocs dwell along the coast, and the sea breeze tempers the heat of the land.

2337.name: Razor Hill Barracks
2337.description: The Razor Hill Barracks is the most prominent building in the town of Razor Hill in central Durotar, a large orcish fortress of wood and stone that serves as the town's military headquarters. Here warriors, shamans, priests, and other trained folk teach young members of the Horde, and the town's defenders plan their patrols against the Burning Blade and the Kul Tirans. The barracks is one of the largest structures in Durotar outside Orgrimmar.

2979.name: Tor'kren Farm
2979.description: Tor'kren Farm is a small pig farm in northwestern Durotar, near Thunder Ridge. It has not seen as much profit as other farms in the area, and its future is uncertain since the farmer's son went to hunt crocolisks at the Southfury River. The farm is humble and quiet, surrounded by the dry red hills of Durotar.

14.description: Durotar is a land of red, sun-baked earth, rugged canyons, and rocky hills on the eastern coast of Kalimdor, bordered by the Southfury River and the Barrens to the west, the ruined coast of Azshara to the north, and the sea to the east and south. Its dry, cracked soil, sparse vegetation, and harsh heat recall Draenor, the lost homeland of the orcs, who see a harsh beauty in it. When Thrall led the orcs and the Darkspear trolls to Kalimdor after the Third War, he claimed this land as the new orcish homeland, driving out the quilboar who had long dwelt here, and named it Durotar in honor of his father, Durotan. At its northern edge he founded the great city of Orgrimmar, named after the former warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. Today Durotar is the heart of the Horde, a tribal chiefdom ruled by Warchief Thrall and home to orcs, trolls, tauren, and others, with the town of Razor Hill at its central crossroads and the troll village of Sen'jin on its southern coast. Young orcs and trolls prove themselves in the Valley of Trials. Though the land is largely at peace, dangers remain: quilboar raid from the west, Kolkar centaurs lurk in the southern crags, harpies nest in the canyons, the demon-worshipping cultists of the Burning Blade hide in caves, and a Kul Tiran fortress still stands on the eastern coast. Scorpids, boars, raptors, thunder lizards, crocolisks, and makrura roam the wilds.

15.name: Dustwallow Marsh

403.name: Shady Rest Inn
403.description: The Shady Rest Inn was a human-built inn near the border between Dustwallow Marsh and the Barrens, once a welcome sight for weary travelers on the Gold Road. Built beside a deep natural well, it was famous for its soft beds, warm meals, and cold drinks, and a small village grew up around it. Now it lies in burned ruins, and who set it ablaze remains a subject of rumor and suspicion. The charred remains stand as a grim reminder of the tensions in the marsh.

496.name: Brackenwall Village
496.description: Brackenwall Village is a Horde outpost in northwestern Dustwallow Marsh, built and populated mainly by the Stonemaul ogres, who were driven from their original village by the black dragonflight. The Stonemaul have been allies of the Horde since the hero Rexxar defeated their brutal chieftain and took command of the tribe, and they are now led by a powerful overlord. The village is a rough collection of huts and palisades, and it is the oldest Horde presence in the marsh.

497.name: Swamplight Manor
497.description: Swamplight Manor is a small house on Witch Hill in Dustwallow Marsh, the home of an eccentric cook famous for his swamp-inspired cuisine. A small garden surrounds the house, and its owner is always on the lookout for exotic ingredients.

498.name: Bloodfen Burrow
498.description: Bloodfen Burrow is a cave in western Dustwallow Marsh where a large number of Bloodfen raptors nest. The remnants of a ruined settlement can be seen just outside the cave, torn apart by the ravenous beasts.

499.name: Darkmist Cavern
499.description: Darkmist Cavern is a small mine in northwestern Dustwallow Marsh that has become completely overrun with enormous Darkmist spiders. The locals cannot agree whether the spiders were named after the cavern or the other way around.

501.name: Beezil's Wreck
501.description: Beezil's Wreck is a crashed goblin zeppelin in the deepest parts of Dustwallow Marsh, east of Tabetha's Farm. The zeppelin was carrying a shipment of supplies south when it went down, and its wreckage lies half-sunk in the swamp. The pilot is nowhere to be found.

502.name: Witch Hill
502.description: Witch Hill is an area in Dustwallow Marsh on the way to Theramore, home to Swamplight Manor and several camps of the Mirefin murlocs. It is said to be haunted by a demon. The tauren tell of a murloc witch who dwells on a hill that is, in truth, a giant turtle, and whose oracle speaks only truth.

503.name: Sentry Point
503.description: Sentry Point is a watchtower built by the people of Theramore on the mainland of Dustwallow Marsh, just across the bridge from the island citadel. As its name suggests, it watches the comings and goings on the road to Theramore.

504.name: North Point Tower
504.description: North Point Tower is a watchtower built by the people of Theramore in northern Dustwallow Marsh, near a well-traveled stretch of road. It is staffed by a sizable contingent of Theramore soldiers, who keep watch over the road and the surrounding marsh.

506.name: Lost Point
506.description: Lost Point is a run-down, decrepit tower built by the humans of Theramore in western Dustwallow Marsh, the westernmost of their watchtowers. It has been abandoned by its garrison and is now inhabited by deserters from Theramore, who have their own reasons for leaving.

507.name: Bluefen
507.description: Bluefen is an area of Dustwallow Marsh near the border with the Barrens, once the site of a village known for a plant that the locals boiled to produce bright blue dyes. Now it is overrun with spiders, birds, raptors, and crocolisks, and infiltrators of various loyalties have been spotted here.

508.name: Stonemaul Ruins
508.description: The Stonemaul Ruins are the former home of the Stonemaul ogres in southern Dustwallow Marsh, within the Dragonmurk. The village was destroyed by the black dragonflight, and its surviving ogres fled north to found Brackenwall Village. The ruins are now infested with black dragonspawn, and the Stonemaul have sworn revenge.

509.name: The Den of Flame
509.description: The Den of Flame is an area in southern Dustwallow Marsh, just west of the Stonemaul Ruins, completely overrun by dragonkin of the black dragonflight. Its architecture suggests that it was once built by the Stonemaul ogres. The air is hot and smoky.

510.name: The Dragonmurk
510.description: The Dragonmurk is a section of southern Dustwallow Marsh where whelps and dragonspawn of the black dragonflight are numerous. Only a few abandoned huts remain of a tauren outpost that once stood here, its inhabitants fled or consumed when the black dragons claimed the land. Travelers tell tales of unfortunates abducted and tortured by the dragons.

511.name: Wyrmbog
511.description: The Wyrmbog is the southernmost area of Dustwallow Marsh, named for the black drakes and whelps that lurk among its shadowed rocks and slither across its waters. It is the domain of the black dragonflight, and it is said that the great black dragon Onyxia makes her lair in a cave here, together with her many children. Travelers who skirt its edges often come into conflict with the dragonkin.

512.name: Blackhoof Village
512.description: Blackhoof Village is a village of the renegade Grimtotem tauren in northern Dustwallow Marsh. The Grimtotem hold captives here, and the village is said to hold secrets about the burning of the Shady Rest Inn. The tauren here are hostile to outsiders.

513.name: Theramore Isle
513.description: Theramore Isle is a fortified island city off the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, founded by Lady Jaina Proudmoore after the Third War as a refuge for the humans who followed her to Kalimdor. It is the great bastion of the Alliance on the continent, with gleaming white walls, a harbor, and the citadel where Jaina resides. Ships sail from its docks to Menethil Harbor, and gryphons connect it with other Alliance holdings. Jaina has long sought peace with the Horde, but Theramore's presence does not extend far beyond its walls, and its garrison has recently suffered from desertions.

514.name: Foothold Citadel
514.description: Foothold Citadel is the military stronghold within Theramore Isle, the heart of the city's defenses and the seat of its military commanders. Soldiers, officers, and merchants fill its halls, and from here the defense of Theramore and its outposts is coordinated. The citadel's white walls rise above the harbor.

516.name: Dustwallow Bay
516.description: Dustwallow Bay is the stretch of the Great Sea off the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, west of Theramore Isle. Ships sail across it to and from Theramore's harbor, and its waters are home to sea turtles and other sea creatures. A famous fisherman makes his home on a small island off the bay.

517.name: Tidefury Cove
517.description: Tidefury Cove is a cove at the end of Dustwallow Bay, south of Theramore Isle, dotted with small islands and reefs that make it perilous for ships. Two ships lie broken upon its shallows, now roamed by makrura. During the Third War, the Horde decimated part of Admiral Proudmoore's fleet in these waters. A renowned fisherman has made his home on one of the cove's islets.

518.name: Dreadmurk Shore
518.description: The Dreadmurk Shore is the coastline and islands of Dustwallow Marsh between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold. It is heavily infested by the Mirefin murlocs, and sea turtles and other creatures inhabit the waters. A group of shipwrecked bandits has set up camp on the beach and nearby islands.

2079.name: Alcaz Island
2079.description: Alcaz Island is a large island off the northeastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, covered in tropical vegetation unlike the rest of the region. Once a human settlement, it has been taken over by naga and hydras, who seem to be guarding something. The island's old village has an underground tunnel system, and rumors speak of a prison hidden beneath it. A strange gnome is said to have arrived there with his flying machine.

2158.name: Emberstrife's Den
2158.description: Emberstrife's Den is a large cave in the Wyrmbog region of southern Dustwallow Marsh, the lair of a mighty black drake who tests young dragonkin of the black dragonflight. The cave is hot and filled with the smell of brimstone.

2302.name: The Quagmire
2302.description: The Quagmire is a large section of marshland in central Dustwallow Marsh, stretching from Lost Point in the west to Dustwallow Bay in the east, and from Brackenwall Village in the north to the Dragonmurk in the south. It is inhabited by crocolisks, Grimtotem tauren, spiders, and oozes, and its sucking mud and treacherous bogs make travel difficult.

2318.name: The Great Sea
2318.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, mixing with the brackish waters of the swamp and surrounding the island citadel of Theramore. Ships sail these waters to and from Theramore's harbor, and reefs and islands dot the coast. Murlocs, naga, and hydras dwell in the waters near the shore.

4010.name: Mudsprocket
4010.description: Mudsprocket is a goblin town in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh, a neutral haven open to all races and factions. Built of wood and scrap on stilts above the mud, it has an inn, a flight master, and merchants, and it has become a gathering place for adventurers exploring the southern marsh. The goblins here are tied to the Steamwheedle Cartel.

4046.name: Direhorn Post
4046.description: Direhorn Post is a camp of hostile Grimtotem tauren in the Quagmire of Dustwallow Marsh, north of Tabetha's Farm. The Grimtotem here are suspected of dark dealings, and they attack anyone who comes near.

4047.name: Nat's Landing
4047.description: Nat's Landing is a small fishing spot on an islet in Dustwallow Bay, the home of a renowned fisherman. It features a tent, fish racks, rods and reels, and a small rickety dock from which he fishes. It is a peaceful, quiet place, a welcome refuge from the dangers of the marsh.

4049.name: Tabetha's Farm
4049.description: Tabetha's Farm is a small hut with a garden in the murkiest part of the Quagmire in Dustwallow Marsh, home to a reclusive sorceress and her apprentices. A small dock serves those who navigate the swamp by boat. The farm is a curious island of order amid the wild marsh.

15.description: Dustwallow Marsh is a vast, ancient swamp on the eastern coast of central Kalimdor, lying southeast of the Barrens and north of Thousand Needles. Once a high plain filled with herds grazing on tall grasses, it was smashed down into a sunken valley by the Great Sundering, and the water table welled up to create the great marsh that exists today. It is a hot, fetid land fed by underground springs, eternally wet and muddy, where mosquitoes buzz in the air, trees dip their fronds into stagnant pools, and narrow banks of slippery mud separate algae-choked channels. Raptors, spiders, crocolisks, and murlocs lurk everywhere, and in the south the black dragonflight has made its lair in the Wyrmbog, where the great black dragon Onyxia, daughter of Deathwing, is said to dwell. After the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore led her people here and founded the city of Theramore on an island off the eastern coast, which remains a great bastion of the Alliance on Kalimdor. In the northwest, the Stonemaul ogres, allies of the Horde, have opened their village of Brackenwall to the Horde. It was here that Admiral Daelin Proudmoore met his end, a conflict that broke the fragile peace between the Alliance and the Horde. Today, covert skirmishes between the two continue despite the official truce, the renegade Grimtotem tauren lurk in the marsh, and the goblin town of Mudsprocket offers neutral ground to all.

16.name: Azshara

878.name: Southfury River
878.description: On the side of Azshara, the Southfury River forms the western border of the region, separating it from the ancient forest of Ashenvale. The river is wide and swift, and a bridge near Talrendis Point connects the two lands. Its eastern bank is lined with the autumn-tinged trees of Azshara.

1216.name: Timbermaw Hold
1216.description: This part of Timbermaw Hold lies in the western mountains of Azshara, where the tunnels of the Timbermaw furbolgs emerge from the hills. The Timbermaw, one of the last tribes of uncorrupted furbolgs, have extended their holdings into Azshara, with settlements stretching south from Ursolan to Bear's Head. The furbolgs are wary of strangers but loyal to their friends.

1219.name: Legash Encampment
1219.description: The Legash Encampment is a satyr camp in northern Azshara, east of Ursolan, occupied by the Legashi satyrs. The satyrs dwell among the ruins of the ancient night elven civilization, performing dark rituals and attacking anyone who comes near.

1220.name: Thalassian Base Camp
1220.description: The Thalassian Base Camp is a hill in northern Azshara containing several small camps of hostile blood elves. They are on an expedition to plunder the ancient magical secrets of Azshara, and they are said to have betrayed those who funded them. It is rumored that they seek to summon demons using ancient night elven tomes. The camp is guarded by blood elf magi and soldiers.

1221.name: Ruins of Eldarath
1221.description: The Ruins of Eldarath are the remains of an ancient night elven city in central Azshara, once one of the most beautiful cities of the Kaldorei. The Great Sundering caused most of the city to crumble into the sea, and only a cluster of ruins clings to the eastern cliffs, while about half of the city lies deep underwater. The ruins are now claimed by the Spitelash naga, led by a powerful warlord, who repel all treasure hunters and explorers.

1222.name: Hetaera's Clutch
1222.description: Hetaera's Clutch is a large underwater temple in the Bay of Storms, off the coast of Azshara, populated by hydras. It is said that a great hydra matriarch swims the waters nearby, guarding her brood. The temple's ancient stone is overgrown with coral and seaweed.

1223.name: Temple of Zin-Malor
1223.description: The Temple of Zin-Malor is an ancient temple in the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara, once a prominent night elven temple devoted to the moon goddess Elune. Its design is strikingly similar to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The temple is now occupied by the Spitelash naga, whose warlord dwells within in a place of honor, and an ancient crystal of great power is said to have once rested here.

1224.name: Bear's Head
1224.description: Bear's Head is a remote area by the southeastern edge of the mountains of Azshara, named after the villages of Timbermaw furbolgs that dot the landscape, outposts of the Timbermaw Hold to the north. On a cliff nearby stands a tower that houses an eccentric archmage and his apprentices, among them high elves. The area is quiet and secluded.

1225.name: Ursolan
1225.description: Ursolan is an area in western Azshara just east of Timbermaw Hold, characterized by a deep scar running through its middle, perhaps a remnant of the implosion of the Well of Eternity. It is the site of an extensive settlement of Timbermaw furbolgs, and it is named after Ursol, the bear demigod revered by the furbolgs. The settlement is peaceful and well defended.

1226.name: Temple of Arkkoran
1226.description: The Temple of Arkkoran is an ancient temple on the northeastern shores of Azshara, once a temple of Elune, now the home of a colossal sea giant revered by his kind as a god of the sea. The temple is guarded by murlocs and makrura, and the surrounding shore is watched by hydras and sea giants. The temple's design recalls the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.

1227.name: Bay of Storms
1227.description: The Bay of Storms is a large bay off the eastern coast of Azshara, its waters frequently churned by storms. Its depths hide the underwater temple of the hydras, while islands and reefs dot its surface. Sea giants, naga, murlocs, and makrura roam its shores, and the ruins of the ancient night elven civilization line the coast.

1228.name: The Shattered Strand
1228.description: The Shattered Strand is a coastal area of Azshara lining the northern side of the Bay of Storms. It is densely populated by hydras, sea giants, makrura, and murlocs, and it is the site of the Temple of Arkkoran and the Tower of Eldara. The shore is rocky and broken, a reminder of the Sundering that shattered the land.

1229.name: Tower of Eldara
1229.description: The Tower of Eldara is an ancient night elven tower on the very tip of land northeast of the Bay of Storms in Azshara, once part of the extensive civilization that stretched across the region. The tower stands closed and abandoned, and the beaches around it are patrolled by murlocs, makrura, and hydras. It is a lonely sentinel overlooking the sea.

1230.name: Jagged Reef
1230.description: The Jagged Reef is the northern coast of Azshara, a stretch of sandy beaches broken up by jutting rocks and small inlets. Traveling along the shore is hazardous due to the treacherous rocks and shallows beneath the surface, and murlocs, hydras, and makrura inhabit the area.

1231.name: Southridge Beach
1231.description: Southridge Beach is a beach in central Azshara lining the western and southern edges of the Bay of Storms. It is heavily inhabited by naga, as well as makrura, hydras, murlocs, and the occasional sea giant, and countless ruins of the ancient city of Eldarath dot the sand.

1232.name: Ravencrest Monument
1232.description: The Ravencrest Monument is a huge statue in Azshara raised in honor of Lord Kur'talos Ravencrest, who led the night elven resistance against the Burning Legion after the fall of Zin-Azshari, fighting beside the young Tyrande Whisperwind and the brothers Malfurion and Illidan Stormrage. The statue now lies in ruins; only its broken legs still stand, and the rest presumably lies beneath the waves. The ruins are inhabited by naga.

1233.name: Forlorn Ridge
1233.description: The Forlorn Ridge is a huge, long-dead volcano in southwestern Azshara, dominating the surrounding landscape. Its crater is mysterious and largely unexplored, and both the Alliance and the Horde have built fortifications on its slopes. The ridge is barren and windswept.

1234.name: Lake Mennar
1234.description: Lake Mennar is a lake in Azshara surrounded by blue dragonspawn of the blue dragonflight, one of the few places outside Northrend and Winterspring where the blue dragons dwell. The lake itself is free from danger and offers solace and refreshment to those brave enough to pass the dragonkin. Ancient ruins of Zin-Azshari lie nearby.

1235.name: Shadowsong Shrine
1235.description: Shadowsong Shrine is a ruin-covered hill in western Azshara, haunted by the ghosts of the Highborne, who roam the surrounding landscape seeking to destroy all living intruders. The shrine shares its name with Jarod Shadowsong, a commander of the resistance during the War of the Ancients, and his sister Maiev, the famous warden. It may honor their deeds or mark the site of their ancestral home.

1236.name: Haldarr Encampment
1236.description: The Haldarr Encampment is a satyr camp in western Azshara, northeast of Shadowsong Shrine and south of Valormok, densely populated by the Haldarr satyrs. The satyrs perform dark rituals among their tents and attack anyone who comes near.

1237.name: Valormok
1237.description: Valormok is a small orcish outpost in western Azshara, built against the mountains north of the Haldarr Encampment. It is fairly unprotected and bare, for the Horde has little interest in this hostile land, and its warriors live through difficult times, having lost many of their comrades to the treachery of blood elf explorers. A wind rider master connects it with Orgrimmar.

1256.name: The Ruined Reaches
1256.description: The Ruined Reaches form the southern coast of Azshara near the border with Durotar, stretches of beach and cliffs broken up by inlets and dotted with ancient ruins and shipwrecks. Travel along the reaches is hazardous due to the treacherous shallows and the murlocs, hydras, and makrura that inhabit them. A gnomish building on a hill above the shore is home to a pair of engineers.

2321.name: The Great Sea
2321.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the eastern and northern coasts of Azshara, where a labyrinth of coral reefs and jagged rocks makes sea travel nearly impossible. Beneath the waves lie the drowned ruins of the ancient city of Zin-Azshari, and many believe that the naga and darker things dwell in the depths. Storms frequently sweep in from the sea, and the waves crash against the cliffs.

2497.name: Bitter Reaches
2497.description: The Bitter Reaches are the northeastern region of Azshara, a rugged land of hills and cliffs densely populated by hippogryphs, oozes, and chimaeras. Along the northern edge, mighty mountain giants have displaced most of the wildlife. The reaches are wild and windswept, and few travelers venture here.

3137.name: Talrendis Point
3137.description: Talrendis Point is a very small night elf outpost in southwestern Azshara, near the bridge to Ashenvale. It is a frontier camp offering only the barest of necessities, populated mostly by night elves, and it watches over the cursed land and the satyrs that dwell in it. A hippogryph roost connects it with other night elf holdings.

3138.name: Rethress Sanctum
3138.description: Rethress Sanctum is a ruined shrine on the southern coast of Azshara, southwest of the Ravencrest Monument. It is uninhabited, visited only by stray murlocs and makrura, and its broken stones are slowly being reclaimed by the sea.

3140.name: Scalebeard's Cave
3140.description: Scalebeard's Cave is a cave on a tiny island in the western part of the Bay of Storms off Azshara, said to be the home of a great sea turtle who spends much of its time hunting in the open sea. The cave is damp and quiet.

16.description: Azshara is a beautiful but cursed coastal land in northeastern Kalimdor, lying east of Ashenvale, south of Winterspring, and north of Durotar. It is cloaked in eternal autumn, its trees tinged in brilliant oranges and reds, and great cliffs and white sandy beaches line the sea. Ten thousand years ago, this land was part of the great night elven capital of Zin-Azshari, the seat of Queen Azshara, before the War of the Ancients and the Great Sundering tore the land apart and the sea thundered in, drowning much of the city. The surviving night elves named the shattered region after their queen, who was driven mad by demonic influence, and they consider it cursed. Ruins of the ancient city perch on the cliffs and lie among the coral beneath the waves, and many tales are told of what lurks in the depths: some say Queen Azshara was transformed into a hideous sea creature and rules the naga, others that demons still slumber beneath the sea. Today the land is haunted by the ghosts of the Highborne and infested with satyrs, naga, and blue dragons, while the friendly Timbermaw furbolgs hold the mountains in the west and sea giants roam the eastern shores. The Horde and the Alliance maintain small outposts at Valormok and Talrendis Point, and storms frequently sweep in from the sea. A labyrinth of coral reefs makes sea travel along the coast nearly impossible.

17.name: The Barrens

359.name: Bael Modan
359.description: Bael Modan is a dwarven excavation and fortified settlement in the southern Barrens, its name meaning the red mountain in the dwarven tongue. The largest Alliance stronghold in the Barrens, it is marked by sturdy stone walls and guard towers blocking the mouth of a cavern, behind which lies the largest dwarven archaeological dig in Kalimdor, where the dwarves have uncovered significant titan ruins. The dig has angered the local tauren, whose tribe was driven from its lands by the excavation, and the dwarves of Bael Modan keep a close watch on all visitors.

378.name: Camp Taurajo
378.description: Camp Taurajo is a tauren outpost in the southern Barrens, near the mountain pass leading to Mulgore, along the Gold Road south of the Crossroads. It has an inn, merchants, and a wind rider master, and its tauren defend it against the encroaching quilboar, often holding captured quilboar prisoners. The camp's tents and totems stand on the dry plains, a link between Mulgore and the rest of the Horde.

379.name: Far Watch Post
379.description: Far Watch Post is a small Horde outpost just west of the bridge between Durotar and the Barrens, made up of a watchtower and an orc burrow guarded by orc warriors. It protects the approach to Durotar from the Alliance, the centaurs, and the quilboar of the Barrens. A riding wolf pen lies nearby, though it holds more chickens than wolves.

380.name: The Crossroads
380.description: The Crossroads is the largest Horde town in the Barrens, built at the crossing of the Gold Road, which runs north to south, and the road from Ratchet in the east to the Stonetalon Mountains in the west. Its wooden palisades, watchtowers, and buildings surround an inn, merchants, and a wind rider roost that connects it with nearly every Horde outpost in Kalimdor. The Crossroads is a busy place, full of travelers, warriors, and caravans, and its guards keep constant watch against the centaurs, quilboar, and the Alliance forces that strike from the north and east.

381.name: Boulder Lode Mine
381.description: Boulder Lode Mine is a mine in the northeastern corner of the Barrens, east of the Sludge Fen, operated by the goblins of the Venture Company. Venture Co. enforcers and overseers infest both the mine and the nearby fort and tower, and they guard their operations jealously.

382.name: The Sludge Fen
382.description: The Sludge Fen is an oil field in the northeastern corner of the Barrens, occupied by the goblins of the Venture Company for their oil refining projects. The goblins have built a large oil platform and machinery that pollute the land and water, and they defend their operations fiercely. The air is thick with smoke and the smell of oil.

383.name: The Dry Hills
383.description: The Dry Hills are the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains in the far northwestern corner of the Barrens. Despite their name, they are one of the greener areas of the Barrens, for seeds from nearby Ashenvale have been carried on the wind over the crags. Witchwing harpies nest here and raid caravans on the northern Gold Road, while zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors roam the hills.

384.name: Dreadmist Peak
384.description: Dreadmist Peak is a mountain northwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens, probably an ancient volcano, its slopes resembling solidified lava flows. As one climbs to the top, the air becomes red and foggy, and at the summit dwell cultists of the Burning Blade, who guard a demonic artifact in the Dreadmist Den. The peak is a sinister place, shrouded in crimson mist.

385.name: Northwatch Hold
385.description: Northwatch Hold is a massive Alliance naval fortress on the coast between the Barrens and Dustwallow Marsh, built by the forces of Theramore to block the coastal approaches to their city from the north. It has massive walls and gates, watchtowers, and barracks, and it is garrisoned by Theramore marines and guards. The fortress is a symbol of the Alliance's presence on Kalimdor, and the Horde regards it as a provocation.

386.name: The Forgotten Pools
386.description: The Forgotten Pools are the northernmost of the oases in the Barrens, north of the western road out of the Crossroads. Like many of these verdant pools, they are patrolled by Kolkar centaurs, and turtles and other wildlife come to drink from their waters. The pools are a welcome sight of green in the dry savanna.

387.name: Lushwater Oasis
387.description: Lushwater Oasis is an oasis just south of the Crossroads in the Barrens, perhaps the most important of the oases for it hides the entrance to the Wailing Caverns, a network of caves corrupted by the nightmares of a druid. Kolkar centaurs stalk between the trees, hunting the wild beasts that come to drink, and strange, mutated fish are said to swim in its waters.

388.name: The Stagnant Oasis
388.description: The Stagnant Oasis is an oasis between the Merchant Coast and the Gold Road in the Barrens. Kolkar centaurs camp on its fringes, and weakened, solitary kodos wander its shores. Its waters are murky and still, and strange fish are said to swim within.

390.name: Field of Giants
390.description: The Field of Giants is a vast plain covering much of the southern Barrens, between Camp Taurajo and the entrance to Dustwallow Marsh. Hundreds of termite mounds, some towering more than sixty feet tall, rise from the plains, their misshapen forms resembling giants. Thunder lizards, kodos, and lions roam the land, and the centaurs consider the field a holy place. Recently, silithid hives have appeared here, the northernmost in all Kalimdor, a cause of great concern.

391.name: The Merchant Coast
391.description: The Merchant Coast is the stretch of the Barrens that forms the coastline of the Great Sea, home to the goblin port of Ratchet and the Alliance fortress of Northwatch Hold, with Fray Island just offshore. It takes its name from the lucrative trade that passes through Ratchet. The coast is sandy and warm, and ships sail along it constantly.

392.name: Ratchet
392.description: Ratchet is a bustling goblin port town on the coast of the Barrens, run by the Steamwheedle Cartel and open to all races and factions. Its streets sprawl in every direction, its architecture follows no common vision, and it is a city of trade and entertainment where almost anything can be bought, and plenty of things no one wants are on sale. Ships sail from its docks to Booty Bay, and pirates are welcome in its waters. The town is overseen by the goblin Gazlowe, and its goblin bruisers keep the peace. Ratchet is a lively, noisy, and colorful place.

401.name: The Tidus Stair
401.description: The Tidus Stair is an interesting rock formation on the coast of the Barrens, a half-day's travel south of Ratchet: several terraces form a giant set of ancient stone stairs that descend from the beach and vanish beneath the waves. Local legend says that they lead down to a night elven city that fell into the sea after the collapse of the Well of Eternity, but no diver has ever found the bottom. Tauren druids sometimes sit here and commune with the spirits of the water.

458.name: Gold Road
458.description: The Gold Road is an ancient highway that once ran the breadth of Kalimdor, and its northern section runs through the Barrens from the Mor'shan Rampart in the north to the bridge connecting the northern and southern halves of the region. It is named for the trade caravans that travel regularly along it, from Ratchet in the south to Nighthaven in the north. The road is the lifeline of the Barrens, though centaurs and quilboar often raid the caravans.

720.name: Fray Island
720.description: Fray Island is a small, arid island off the eastern coast of the Barrens, south of Ratchet, where warriors of all races and creeds meet to train and test their skill in combat. It is overseen by a renowned weapon master. The island is a place of honor and challenge, where the clang of steel rings out day and night.

815.name: Southfury River
815.description: On the side of the Barrens, the Southfury River forms the eastern border of the region, separating it from Durotar. The wide river is patrolled by crocolisks, and a bridge near Far Watch Post connects the Barrens with the orcish homeland. The river flows south toward the sea, emptying near Ratchet in a great waterfall.

1156.name: Southern Barrens
1156.description: The Southern Barrens are the lands on the southern side of the Barrens, beyond the bridge that divides the region, stretching south toward the cliffs of Thousand Needles. It is a land of dry plains, termite mounds, and thorny brambles, home to the tauren of Camp Taurajo, the dwarves of Bael Modan, the quilboar of Razorfen, and roaming herds of kodos and thunder lizards.

1157.name: Southern Gold Road
1157.description: The Southern Gold Road is the southern section of the ancient highway running through the Barrens, from the bridge connecting the northern and southern halves of the region to the Great Lift at the border with Thousand Needles. Traders and travelers from as far as Gadgetzan and Auberdine use it, and Camp Taurajo stands along its course.

1316.name: Razorfen Downs
1316.description: Razorfen Downs is the ancestral burial ground of the quilboar, nestled among huge brambles at the southern edge of the Barrens, near the cliffs of Thousand Needles. Its entrance is said to be made from the maw of Agamaggan, the boar demigod revered by the quilboar. In recent times, the Scourge has taken an interest in the Downs, and it is said that necromancers and undead have allied with some of the quilboar. The thorny mounds are dark and foreboding.

1599.name: Mor'shan Base Camp
1599.description: Mor'shan Base Camp is a sizable Horde village in the northern Barrens, just south of the border with Ashenvale. It is home to the families of many orc warriors fighting for the Warsong clan in the forest to the north, and it serves as the staging ground for the Warsong Outriders in their war against the Silverwing Sentinels. The camp is a busy place of tents, barracks, and warriors preparing for battle.

1697.name: Raptor Grounds
1697.description: The Raptor Grounds are a small valley in the southern Barrens, west of Northwatch Hold, densely populated by the Sunscale raptors. These raptors are unusual among their kind, showing an unnatural intelligence and even building crude huts and tools. Their attraction to shiny objects has led them to steal many items from nearby settlements.

1698.name: Bramblescar
1698.description: Bramblescar is a thorny area in the Barrens, home to a tribe of Razormane quilboar. They are at war with the Bristleback quilboar of Agama'gor across the road, and they attack anyone who wanders close to their lair. The area is covered with enormous thorny brambles.

1699.name: Thorn Hill
1699.description: Thorn Hill is a sizable hill on the north face of a mountain between the Crossroads and Durotar, populated by a large number of quilboar. The quilboar have been raiding Horde caravans in the region, and they are led by a cunning raider. The hill is covered with thorny brambles.

1700.name: Agama'gor
1700.description: Agama'gor is a large settlement of Bristleback quilboar in the southern Barrens, just north of the road leading west from Camp Taurajo. The quilboar are at war with the Razormane tribe of Bramblescar across the road, and they are hostile to all outsiders. Their settlement is built among great thorny brambles.

1701.name: Blackthorn Ridge
1701.description: Blackthorn Ridge is a thorny valley in the southern Barrens, just north of the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul, populated primarily by Razorfen quilboar. A wise orc shaman dwells on the ridge above, and below her camp lies a pool of remarkably pure water.

1702.name: Honor's Stand
1702.description: Honor's Stand is a Horde outpost guarding the west road between the Crossroads and Sun Rock Retreat, consisting of a number of burrows, some badly damaged. It has been the site of many great battles between the Horde and its enemies, and the orcs stationed here are proud of its illustrious history, though they are now beset by attacks from Kolkar centaurs.

1703.name: The Mor'shan Rampart
1703.description: The Mor'shan Rampart is a defensive wall at the northern end of the Gold Road in the Barrens, built to withstand the push of night elf forces into the Barrens from Ashenvale. It is guarded by Horde warriors, and it serves as a staging point for raids into the forest. A damaged section of the wall lies unguarded to the east.

1704.name: Grol'dom Farm
1704.description: Grol'dom Farm is one of the many orcish pig farms that have sprung up since the founding of Orgrimmar, located in the northern Barrens. It is home to an orc farmer and his family, and it is a peaceful place of pens and simple buildings amid the dry plains.

1717.name: Razorfen Kraul
1717.description: Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral home of the quilboar, a vast labyrinth of giant thorny vines at the southwestern edge of the Barrens. Legends say that where the demigod Agamaggan fell, his blood gave rise to great masses of thorny vines, and the quilboar revere the largest cluster, the Razorfen, as his resting place. The quilboar defend it fiercely, and their shamans and warriors dwell within its twisting passages.

1718.name: The Great Lift
1718.description: The Great Lift is a massive elevator carved into the cliffs at the southern edge of the Barrens, connecting the high savanna with the canyon floor of Thousand Needles far below. Built and operated with goblin ingenuity, its platforms rise and fall along the cliff face, carrying travelers and goods between the two regions. Guards watch over the lift at both ends, and the view from the top over the needle-like spires of the canyon is breathtaking.

2138.name: Dreadmist Den
2138.description: Dreadmist Den is a cave on Dreadmist Peak in the Barrens, held by cultists of the Burning Blade. It is said to contain a demonic artifact of great value to the cult. The den is perpetually shrouded in a dark red mist that cloaks the demon worshippers in eternal twilight.

2157.name: Bael'dun Keep
2157.description: Bael'dun Keep is a dwarven fortress overlooking the Bael Modan dig site in the southern Barrens. It is held by a force of dwarves led by a cunning general, who guard the excavation and are hostile to the Horde. The keep is built of sturdy stone, with walls and towers bristling with rifles and cannons.

2319.name: The Great Sea
2319.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the eastern coast of the Barrens along the Merchant Coast, where ships sail to and from the bustling goblin port of Ratchet. Fray Island lies offshore, and ancient stairs descend from the beach into the depths. The sea is warm and blue, and the waterfall of the Southfury River pours into it nearby.

2757.name: Shrine of the Fallen Warrior
2757.description: The Shrine of the Fallen Warrior is a small monument on a hill southwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens, raised in honor of a fallen hero who once set foot on his native soil here. It is said that part of his essence resides at the shrine, and that a mystical blessing is given to those who honor him. The shrine is quiet and solemn, a place of remembrance amid the dry plains.

17.description: The Barrens are a vast, arid savanna in central Kalimdor, stretching west of Durotar from the forests of Ashenvale in the north to the cliffs of Thousand Needles in the south. It is a hot, dry land of yellow grass, scattered thorny trees, rocky hills, and dusty plains, with a few lush oases in the north and a stretch of coastline to the east. Before the Great Sundering, great night elven cities stood here, and the ancient Gold Road, a highway built long ago, still runs the length of the region, carrying caravans between Ratchet and the northern lands. The Barrens are largely controlled by the Horde, whose town of the Crossroads is its main hub, with the tauren outpost of Camp Taurajo in the south. The land is far from tamed, however: Kolkar centaur warbands and Razormane and Bristleback quilboar raid caravans and settlements, harpies nest in the hills, the goblins of the Venture Company drill for oil in the northeast, demon cultists of the Burning Blade hide on Dreadmist Peak, and silithid hives have appeared in the south. The goblin port of Ratchet on the coast is a neutral haven for all, while the Alliance holds the naval fortress of Northwatch Hold and the dwarven excavation of Bael Modan. Zhevras, kodos, plainstriders, lions, raptors, and thunder lizards roam the plains, and the land is rich in ruins and buried treasures.

25.name: Blackrock Mountain
25.description: Blackrock Mountain is a towering, still-active volcano rising between the Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes, one of the most dangerous and storied places in all of Azeroth. It was born at the end of the War of the Three Hammers, when the Dark Iron sorcerer-thane Thaurissan summoned the Firelord Ragnaros from his prison beneath the earth; the explosion shattered a great swath of the Redridge Mountains and raised the mountain from the ruins. Ragnaros enslaved the Dark Iron clan, who carved a vast underground city in the depths of the volcano, while the above-ground citadel came to be known as Blackrock Spire. During the Second War, the Blackrock clan of orcs made the spire the headquarters of the Horde, and the mountain saw one of the fiercest battles of that war. Today it is bitterly contested between two great powers: Ragnaros and his Dark Iron servants, golems, and fire elementals, who rule the depths and the molten core of the mountain, and the black dragon Nefarian, who commands the remnants of the Blackrock orcs, trolls, ogres, and his own monstrous dragonkin from the heights of the spire. Within, a vast chamber of molten rock is spanned by great chains and platforms, connecting the various halls of the mountain. The heat is intense, the air thick with smoke and sulfur, and the constant rumble of the volcano is a reminder of the power that slumbers within. It is fortunate for the rest of the world that the two rivals spend most of their strength fighting each other.

28.name: Western Plaguelands

190.name: Hearthglen
190.description: Hearthglen is a fortified town in the northern Western Plaguelands, once the seat of regional government for this part of Lordaeron, ruled from Mardenholde Keep by the paladin Tirion Fordring until he was exiled for treason for defending an orc. At the start of the Third War, Prince Arthas and Uther the Lightbringer defended the town against the undead, and it survived the plague. Today Hearthglen is held by the Scarlet Crusade, who have made it their second most important bastion, garrisoned by some three thousand zealous soldiers and priests. Its walls and towers are relatively untouched by the plague, and its fanatical defenders attack the undead and outsiders alike.

192.name: Northridge Lumber Camp
192.description: The Northridge Lumber Camp is a lumber mill in the northern Western Plaguelands, near Hearthglen, operated by the Scarlet Crusade. The Crusade relies on the camp for timber to build and repair its fortifications and siege engines, and it is guarded by Scarlet soldiers and workers. The surrounding forest, though tainted by the plague, still provides wood. The camp is a busy place of sawmills and stacked logs, and the Crusade's enemies would dearly love to disrupt its supply.

193.name: Ruins of Andorhal
193.description: The Ruins of Andorhal are what remains of the town of Andorhal in the center of the Western Plaguelands, once the center of grain distribution for Lordaeron's northern provinces. It was here that Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned infected the grain with the plague of undeath, and it was here that Arthas slew his former mentor, Uther the Lightbringer. Today the town is the largest Scourge stronghold in the Western Plaguelands, ruled by a powerful lich and infested with ghouls, skeletons, banshees, and abominations. Its crumbling houses and silos stand amid ash and rubble, and the undead patrol its streets endlessly.

195.name: School of Necromancy
195.description: The School of Necromancy, known as the Scholomance, lies hidden beneath the ruined House of Barov on the island of Caer Darrow in Darrowmere Lake. Once the opulent residence of the wealthy Barov family, it became a school for necromancers of the Cult of the Damned when the Barovs made a pact with Kel'Thuzad to preserve their fortune beyond death. Here the cult trained its acolytes, experimented with the plague on the family's servants, and created the first abominations. Today the Scholomance is a vile academy of the Scourge, where necromancers study the dark arts under a sinister headmaster, and the undead Barovs still haunt its halls.

196.name: Uther's Tomb
196.description: Uther's Tomb is a great monument on Sorrow Hill in the Western Plaguelands, the resting place of Uther the Lightbringer, the first paladin and founder of the Order of the Silver Hand. Uther was slain near Andorhal by his former student, Prince Arthas, who had become a death knight of the Lich King, and his body was recovered by his surviving followers and buried here. A statue shows him in a heroic pose, with a tome of the Light in one hand and his warhammer in the other. The tomb is consecrated ground, one of the few bastions of the Light in this dying land, and the spirit of Uther is said to still watch over those who come to honor him.

197.name: Sorrow Hill
197.description: Sorrow Hill is a large cemetery south of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands, where the people of the town and the surrounding lands once buried their dead. When the plague struck and the Scourge attacked, the number of graves skyrocketed, and hastily dug, poorly marked graves still cover the hillside; eventually, the survivors stopped burying their dead and burned them in a mass grave instead, fearing they would rise. On the summit stands the tomb of Uther the Lightbringer. The plague cauldrons nearby have caused the dead of Sorrow Hill to rise, and skeletal soldiers and ghouls now stand guard over their own graves.

198.name: The Weeping Cave
198.description: The Weeping Cave is a damp cave in the northeastern Western Plaguelands, just west of the Thondroril River. It is filled with bog beasts and oozes, creatures that have thrived in the polluted waters and tainted soil of the Plaguelands. Water drips constantly from the cave's ceiling, giving it its name, and the air within is thick and foul.

199.name: Felstone Field
199.description: Felstone Field is a farmstead in the northwestern Western Plaguelands that was once a life-sustaining farm. It has been overrun by the Scourge, who placed a great plague cauldron in the middle of the field, constantly spewing disease-filled vapors into the air. Skeletal warriors, sorcerers, and ghouls guard the cauldron, and Scarlet Crusaders also roam the area, attacking both the undead and outsiders. The fields are blighted and barren, and the farmhouse is said to still shelter a lone survivor.

200.name: Dalson's Tears
200.description: Dalson's Tears is an abandoned farm in the middle of the Western Plaguelands, once known as Dalson's Orchard. The Scourge has taken it over and placed a great plague cauldron in the middle of the field, spewing disease-filled vapors into the air. The unfortunate members of the family that lived here still wander the farm in undeath, and the farmhouse and outbuildings bear signs of the tragedy that befell them. The orchard's trees are withered and dead.

201.name: Gahrron's Withering
201.description: Gahrron's Withering is an abandoned farmstead at the eastern end of the Western Plaguelands, once known as Gahrron's Quickening. The Scourge has taken it over and placed a great plague cauldron in the middle of the field, spewing disease-filled vapors into the air. It is haunted by wailing spirits and wraiths, and it is one of the most dangerous of the cauldron fields. The land around it is blighted and barren.

202.name: The Writhing Haunt
202.description: The Writhing Haunt is a former farm in the central Western Plaguelands, just east of the Ruins of Andorhal. Once a life-sustaining farm, it has been overrun by the Scourge, who placed a great plague cauldron in the middle of the field. Ghouls and zombies guard the cauldron, and the farmhouse is said to shelter a desperate survivor in hiding. The fields are grey and barren, and the air is thick with the cauldron's poisonous vapors.

203.name: Mardenholde Keep
203.description: Mardenholde Keep is the fortress within the town of Hearthglen in the Western Plaguelands, now the headquarters of the Scarlet Crusade in the region. Before the Third War, it was the seat of Lord Tirion Fordring, governor of the region, and a bustling center of commerce that never fell to the orcs during the Second War. Today it is held by the Scarlet Crusade, led by the son of Tirion Fordring, and it is heavily guarded by Scarlet soldiers. Its halls are grand but cold, and its original image as a bastion of hope has long since faded.

813.name: The Bulwark
813.description: On the side of the Western Plaguelands, the Bulwark marks the western edge of the blighted lands, where the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn have raised barricades and watchtowers against the armies of the Scourge. The yellowish plague mist that hangs over the Plaguelands drifts up against the fortifications, and the undead constantly test the defenders. Beyond the Bulwark to the west lies Tirisfal Glades, the homeland of the Forsaken.

2297.name: Darrowmere Lake
2297.description: On the side of the Western Plaguelands, Darrowmere Lake stretches across the southeastern part of the region, one of the largest lakes in the Eastern Kingdoms. At its center lies the island of Caer Darrow, with its ruined town and the dark House of Barov, beneath which lies the Scholomance. The lake was once beautiful and full of life, but the filth of the Scourge now pollutes its waters, and dead fish wash up on its shores. On its eastern side, a breeze from the Hinterlands thins the plague mist, and traces of blue sky can sometimes be seen.

2298.name: Caer Darrow
2298.description: Caer Darrow is a ruined town and keep on an island in the middle of Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. The keep is among the oldest human monuments in the world, dating back to the days of the Empire of Arathor, and the island was once home to a sacred runestone of the high elves, which the Horde shattered during the Second War to build its Altars of Storms. After the war, the wealthy Barov family ruled the island, but they made a pact with Kel'Thuzad, and their manor became the Scholomance. Disease ravaged the island, and none survived; the spirits of its inhabitants still wander the ruins, seeking justice for the wrongs committed there. Today the town is abandoned and haunted, and the undead guard the approaches to the school.

2620.name: Thondroril River
2620.description: On the side of the Western Plaguelands, the Thondroril River forms the natural boundary between the western and eastern halves of the Plaguelands, flowing south from the northern mountains into Darrowmere Lake. Its waters are dark and polluted, and its banks are home to maggots, plague-ridden bears, giant spiders, bats, and snapping turtles. Ruined farmhouses stand along its shores, and the plague mist hangs low over the water.

3197.name: Chillwind Camp
3197.description: Chillwind Camp is a small Alliance encampment in the southern Western Plaguelands, at the entrance to the blighted lands from Chillwind Point in the Alterac Mountains. It is maintained by a small contingent of the Argent Dawn, who have made it the last bastion of safety for Alliance travelers entering the Plaguelands. With few troops of their own, the Dawn relies on volunteers and mercenaries to strike against the Scourge at Andorhal and the plague cauldrons. The camp is a modest collection of tents and a ruined house, and gryphons connect it to Ironforge and Southshore.

28.description: The Western Plaguelands are a blighted land in northern Lordaeron, lying between Tirisfal Glades to the west, the Eastern Plaguelands to the east, and the Alterac Mountains to the south.
