Once a beautiful forested farmland, the eastern belt of Tirisfal stretching toward Darrowmere Lake, it was the breadbasket of the kingdom's northern provinces: Hearthglen was the seat of regional government, and Andorhal the center of grain distribution. It was here that the necromancer Kel'Thuzad and his Cult of the Damned infected Andorhal's grain with the plague of undeath and set up great plague cauldrons on the region's largest farms, dooming the kingdom. Today the land is grey, sick, and noxious: a smoky grey mist hangs in the air, the trees pulse with tumor-like growths and their needles have turned a sickly brown, and the creatures that remain are blighted and ferocious. Countless undead infest the ruins of Andorhal, the cauldron fields, and the graveyards, and the Scourge trains new necromancers in the Scholomance on the island of Caer Darrow. The fanatical Scarlet Crusade holds Hearthglen in the north, the Argent Dawn and the Alliance maintain Chillwind Camp in the south, and the Forsaken stand guard at the Bulwark in the west. Near Andorhal rises the tomb of Uther the Lightbringer, the first paladin, one of the few places of peace in this dying land. Despite everything, the land still struggles to resist the plague, and it is in somewhat better condition than its eastern counterpart.

33.name: Stranglethorn Vale

7.name: Blackwater Cove
7.description: Blackwater Cove is the sheltered lagoon on the southern cape of Stranglethorn Vale, enclosed by steep cliffs and home to the bustling port of Booty Bay. Long ago, the humans of Stormwind established a small port here in an attempt to forge trade routes through the jungle, but they were overwhelmed by the jungle trolls and driven back to their homeland. In their wake came the goblins and the pirates of the Blackwater Raiders, who built the town that now clings to the cliffs above the turquoise water. Ships of every flag and loyalty anchor in the cove, and the waters are busy with boats, fishermen, and the occasional shark.

19.name: Zul'Gurub
19.description: Zul'Gurub is the ancient capital of the Gurubashi Empire, a vast troll city of stone temples, ziggurats, and altars nestled in a valley in northeastern Stranglethorn Vale. More than a thousand years ago, the Atal'ai priests called forth the avatar of the blood god Hakkar the Soulflayer, tearing the empire apart in a terrible civil war. Now the Atal'ai have succeeded in summoning Hakkar into the heart of the ruins, and reports confirm the presence of the dreaded Soulflayer in the city. The trolls of the land sent a contingent of high priests, champions of the primal gods, to stop him, but they fell under his sway and now feed his power. The city's walls are overgrown with vines, its temples stained with blood, and a dark, oppressive power radiates from within. The Zandalari trolls, who regard the Gurubashi as their kin, have come to oppose Hakkar's return.

35.name: Booty Bay
35.description: Booty Bay is a large, bustling port town carved into the cliffs surrounding the beautiful blue lagoon of Blackwater Cove on the southern tip of Stranglethorn Vale. The town is entered through the bleached-white jaws of a giant shark skull, and its wooden houses, docks, and walkways cling to the cliffs in tiers above the water. Run by the Blackwater Raiders, a band of pirates closely tied to the goblin Steamwheedle Cartel, and ruled by Baron Revilgaz, the port offers its services to anyone who can pay, regardless of their loyalties, and its goblin bruisers enforce the peace with brutal efficiency. The famous Salty Sailor Tavern is one of the most popular establishments in Azeroth, and ships sail from the docks to Ratchet in Kalimdor. The town is a place of trade, adventure, and intrigue, filled with sailors, merchants, hunters, and rogues of every race. Its greatest enemy is the Bloodsail Buccaneers, a rival band of pirates who wage a bitter war against the Blackwater Raiders.

37.name: Lake Nazferiti
37.description: Lake Nazferiti is a large lake in northern Stranglethorn Vale, west of Zul'Gurub, one of the largest lakes in the Eastern Kingdoms. Far from the pleasant waters of the northern lakes, it is thick with slime, insects, and weeds, and its murky depths teem with small, ravenous fish with teeth as sharp as blades and with crocolisks that lurk among the reeds. The Nazferiti River flows through the lake on its long journey from the mountains of Redridge, and the goblins of the Venture Company have established a large base of operations on its shores, including an oil platform that pollutes its waters.

43.name: Wild Shore
43.description: The Wild Shore is the southernmost coastline of the Eastern Kingdoms, a rugged stretch of beaches, rocky coves, and small islands around the southern cape of Stranglethorn Vale. It is the home of the Bloodsail Buccaneers, whose fleet of three ships lies anchored among the islands, and whose camps dot the shore. The pirates use the coast as a base for their raids against Booty Bay and passing ships. The waves crash against the rocks, the palm trees sway in the sea breeze, and the beaches are littered with driftwood and the bottles that wash ashore.

99.name: Rebel Camp
99.description: The Rebel Camp is a fortified encampment in the northernmost part of Stranglethorn Vale, just west of the road leading south from Duskwood. It is home to soldiers who once served under the renegade Colonel Kurzen but rebelled against him, and they are now determined to overthrow their former commander and end his reign of terror in the jungle. The camp is a rough, practical place of tents, palisades, and watchtowers, and its soldiers work alongside the Alliance, which maintains a gryphon roost here. The soldiers are hardened by years in the jungle, and they keep a constant watch for Kurzen's men and the dangers of the wilds.

100.name: Nesingwary's Expedition
100.description: Nesingwary's Expedition is a hunting camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, just below the river north of Lake Nazferiti. It was established by the renowned dwarven big-game hunter Hemet Nesingwary, who came to Stranglethorn to hunt the jungle's wild beasts; after the Dark Portal was reopened, he left the camp in the hands of his associates and traveled to Outland in search of more dangerous game. The camp is a cheerful collection of tents, trophies, and campfires, where hunters gather to swap stories and compare their kills. It welcomes hunters of all races, and its residents are always eager to see the jungle's tigers, panthers, and raptors thinned out.

101.name: Kurzen's Compound
101.description: Kurzen's Compound is a fortified encampment in northern Stranglethorn Vale, east of the Rebel Camp, the base of the renegade Colonel Kurzen and his jungle fighters. Kurzen was once an officer of Stormwind sent to the jungle, but he turned rogue, and his men now attack Alliance and Horde alike. Behind the compound lies a cave known as the Stockpile, where the fighters keep their weapons and supplies. The compound is surrounded by wooden walls and watchtowers, and its soldiers are hardened, ruthless, and loyal to their commander. The rebels of the nearby camp are locked in a deadly conflict with Kurzen's forces.

102.name: Ruins of Zul'Kunda
102.description: The Ruins of Zul'Kunda are vast ancient troll ruins in northern Stranglethorn Vale, reached by a path leading east from the Zuuldaia Ruins. Once a great city of the Gurubashi Empire, it is now the stronghold of the Bloodscalp tribe, whose leaders dwell among the crumbling temples and stone altars. The ruins are overgrown with vines and jungle plants, and the Bloodscalp trolls guard them fiercely against any intruders. Skulls and totems mark the tribe's territory, and the sound of drums echoes through the jungle at night.

103.name: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe
103.description: The Ruins of Zul'Mamwe are ancient Gurubashi ruins in eastern Stranglethorn Vale, south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, surrounded by mountains on all sides except the north. They are inhabited by the Skullsplitter trolls, the second great troll tribe of Stranglethorn, who are fierce, solitary warriors led by a cruel chieftain. The ruins are a maze of crumbling stone, overgrown courtyards, and broken statues, and the Skullsplitters guard them jealously. Their war with the Bloodscalps is ancient and bitter.

104.name: The Vile Reef
104.description: The Vile Reef is a colorful coral reef off the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale, near Grom'gol Base Camp. Beneath its waters lie sunken troll ruins, possibly the remains of an ancient city lost long ago, now inhabited by murlocs who have made their homes among the broken stone. Giant clams are scattered among the corals, rumored to hold precious pearls, and floating wreckage can be found along the coast. The reef is beautiful to behold, with its vibrant corals and schools of fish, but the murlocs and sharks make it dangerous to explore.

105.name: Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound
105.description: The Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound is a stronghold of the Mosh'Ogg ogres in northeastern Stranglethorn Vale, just south of Zul'Gurub. The ogres have built crude huts and fortifications around a large cave, and their leader, a powerful ogre mage, is said to hold a mysterious relic deep within. The Mosh'Ogg are brutal and numerous, and they raid supply caravans and attack travelers throughout the eastern jungle. The mound is a foul-smelling place littered with bones and plunder.

106.name: The Stockpile
106.description: The Stockpile is a cave at the back of Kurzen's Compound in northern Stranglethorn Vale, where the renegade Colonel Kurzen and his jungle fighters store their weapons, equipment, and supplies. The cave is heavily guarded by Kurzen's most loyal soldiers, and its passages are filled with crates, weapon racks, and makeshift barracks. It is the heart of Kurzen's operations, and the rebels of the nearby camp would dearly love to see it destroyed.

117.name: Grom'gol Base Camp
117.description: Grom'gol Base Camp is a fortified Horde outpost on the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale, north of Booty Bay, named in honor of the orc hero Grom Hellscream. It is heavily defended by high palisades and watchtowers to guard against the jungle trolls, naga, and Alliance forces who threaten it from the jungle and the coast. Zeppelins connect the camp with Orgrimmar and the Undercity, and wind riders fly to other Horde holdings, making it a vital link in the Horde's network. The camp is a busy place of orc warriors, troll scouts, and travelers, and its proximity to Booty Bay makes it a gateway to the southern jungle.

122.name: Zuuldaia Ruins
122.description: The Zuuldaia Ruins are ancient troll ruins on the northern part of the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale. A large number of Bloodscalp trolls inhabit the ruins, guarding the crumbling stone temples and statues against outsiders. From here, a path leads east to the great ruins of Zul'Kunda, the heart of Bloodscalp territory. The ruins are overgrown with jungle plants, and the sea breeze carries the smell of salt and smoke from the trolls' fires.

123.name: Bal'lal Ruins
123.description: The Bal'lal Ruins are ancient troll ruins near the northwestern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, north of Grom'gol Base Camp and on the shore of the Vile Reef. A band of Bloodscalp trolls resides in what is left of the ruins, guarding the broken stone platforms and statues. The ruins overlook the sea and the colorful reef below, and the trolls' fires can be seen from far along the coast.

125.name: Kal'ai Ruins
125.description: The Kal'ai Ruins are a collection of ancient troll ruins in Stranglethorn Vale, now partially submerged beneath the waters of a river. The Murkgill tribe of murlocs has made its home among the flooded stones, building crude huts and attacking anyone who wanders near. The ruins are overgrown with water plants and moss, and the half-sunken statues gaze out from the water like forgotten sentinels.

126.name: Tkashi Ruins
126.description: The Tkashi Ruins are ancient troll ruins in northwestern Stranglethorn Vale, inhabited by the Bloodscalp trolls. The tribe guards the crumbling stone structures fiercely, and their warriors, mystics, and headhunters patrol the area. The ruins are surrounded by dense jungle, and skulls and totems mark the edges of the trolls' territory.

127.name: Balia'mah Ruins
127.description: The Balia'mah Ruins are ancient troll ruins in Stranglethorn Vale, east of Grom'gol Base Camp on the eastern side of the river. They are inhabited by the Skullsplitter trolls, who guard the crumbling stone temples and statues. The ruins are surrounded by thick jungle, and the Skullsplitters are quick to attack any intruders.

128.name: Ziata'jai Ruins
128.description: The Ziata'jai Ruins are ancient troll ruins in eastern Stranglethorn Vale, southwest of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, inhabited by the Skullsplitter trolls. The ruins include great stone platforms and broken temples overgrown with vines, and the Skullsplitters have made them one of their strongholds. The tribe's warriors and witch doctors guard the ruins jealously against outsiders.

129.name: Mizjah Ruins
129.description: The Mizjah Ruins are ancient troll ruins southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale, now inhabited by Mosh'Ogg ogres rather than trolls. The ogres use the ruins as a base for ambushing the supply caravans traveling between Grom'gol and Stonard. The crumbling stone structures are littered with plunder and bones, and the ogres' crude huts stand among the ancient walls.

297.name: Jaguero Isle
297.description: Jaguero Isle is a jungle-covered island off the southeastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, populated by panthers and gorillas. It is said that an enormous ape rules the island as its king, and that he keeps a captive in his lair. The island is wild and untamed, its beaches lined with palm trees and its interior thick with jungle. Few visit the island, and those who do must contend with its fierce inhabitants.

301.name: The Savage Coast
301.description: The Savage Coast is the long coastline of northern Stranglethorn Vale, stretching from the border of Westfall south past the Vile Reef to Grom'gol Base Camp. Its sandy beaches and rocky shores are inhabited by crocolisks, basilisks, and other creatures, and several troll settlements and ruins line the coast. The jungle comes right down to the shore in many places, and the sea breeze carries the cries of birds and the distant drums of the trolls.

302.name: The Crystal Shore
302.description: The Crystal Shore is a coastline in southwestern Stranglethorn Vale, where clear, sparkling waters wash onto sandy beaches beneath the jungle. The shore takes its name from the crystal-clear water, through which colorful fish and coral can be seen. Naga and murlocs prowl the area, and the Bloodsail Buccaneers have camps along the nearby coast. The beauty of the shore belies the dangers that lurk in the jungle and the waters.

310.name: Crystalvein Mine
310.description: Crystalvein Mine is a mine in southern Stranglethorn Vale, near the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe, known for the strange crystals that grow within its tunnels. The native basilisks eat these crystals, which give them their hardened, stony skin, and the mine is infested with the creatures. The goblins of the Venture Company have moved into the area hoping to harvest the crystals, but the basilisks have made it impossible so far. Outside the mine, crystallized statues of trolls and humans stand as grim reminders of the basilisks' petrifying gaze.

311.name: Ruins of Aboraz
311.description: The Ruins of Aboraz are ancient troll ruins on the southeastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, now the home of an outcast troll witch doctor who commands an army of ghouls, naga, and enthralled trolls. The ruins are a dark and sinister place, filled with the undead and the witch doctor's minions, and strange rituals are performed among the crumbling stones. Even the other trolls of Stranglethorn avoid the area, and travelers are warned to stay away.

312.name: Janeiro's Point
312.description: Janeiro's Point is a small island just outside the entrance to Booty Bay, upon which stands a giant statue of Baron Revilgaz, built as a beacon to all travelers approaching the port. The statue towers over the waves, its outstretched arm pointing toward the bay. Recently, a malevolent sea giant has taken up residence on the island, making it a dangerous place to visit. The island is battered by the waves and winds of the open sea.

477.name: Ruins of Jubuwal
477.description: The Ruins of Jubuwal are ancient troll ruins just east of the Gurubashi Arena in southern Stranglethorn Vale, along the main road that runs the length of the jungle. They are inhabited by the ghouls, naga, and troll minions of an outcast witch doctor, who has made the ruins part of his dark domain. The ruins are dangerous to travelers on the road, and the undead that wander among the stones are a grim sight.

1577.name: The Cape of Stranglethorn
1577.description: The Cape of Stranglethorn is the southern part of Stranglethorn Vale, the rugged peninsula south of the Gurubashi Arena that forms the southernmost tip of the Eastern Kingdoms. It is a land of dense jungle, rocky coasts, and hidden coves, home to the port of Booty Bay, the camps of the Bloodsail Buccaneers, gorilla-infested valleys, and ancient troll ruins. The air is hot and humid, the sea breeze carries the smell of salt and tropical flowers, and the sounds of the jungle never cease. The cape is a place of trade and piracy, adventure and danger.

1578.name: Southern Savage Coast
1578.description: The Southern Savage Coast is the stretch of the Great Sea around the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms, washing the southwestern coast of Stranglethorn Vale near Booty Bay. The waters are warm and clear, but they are also home to sharks, naga, and the ships of the Bloodsail Buccaneers. Vessels sailing to and from Booty Bay must navigate these waters carefully, for the pirates prey on the unwary. The waves crash against the rocky cliffs and sandy beaches of the coast.

1737.name: Mistvale Valley
1737.description: Mistvale Valley is a valley in southern Stranglethorn Vale, perpetually shrouded in mist and home to the great Mistvale gorillas. The gorillas are powerful and territorial, and they attack anyone who intrudes on their domain. The valley is lush and green, filled with towering trees and hanging vines, and the mist gives it a mysterious, otherworldly feel. A hidden cave on the valley's northern side is said to be the home of a troll witch doctor.

1738.name: Nek'mani Wellspring
1738.description: The Nek'mani Wellspring is a holy spring high on the bluffs near the western coast of southern Stranglethorn Vale. Its waters are said to be divine, and every race in Azeroth claims that the spring was blessed for its people, making it the subject of great debate among religious and mystical scholars. The spring is guarded by naga explorers, who have claimed the area for their own mysterious purposes. The spring's fountain is surrounded by ancient stone, and its waters shimmer with a faint light.

1739.name: Bloodsail Compound
1739.description: The Bloodsail Compound is a camp of the Bloodsail Buccaneers on the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale, in the central part of the jungle. The pirates use the compound as a base for their raids against Booty Bay and passing ships, and it is filled with tents, crates of stolen goods, and armed buccaneers. The Bloodsails are ruthless and violent, and they attack anyone who comes near their camp.

1740.name: Venture Co. Base Camp
1740.description: The Venture Co. Base Camp is the main base of operations for the goblins of the Venture Company in northern Stranglethorn Vale, on the shores of Lake Nazferiti. The goblins are here to strip the jungle of its resources, logging its trees and mining its crystals, and their camp is a noisy, smoky place of machines, shredders, and workers. Adjacent to the camp is the company's operations center, an oil platform on the lake. The Venture Company is ruthless in its pursuit of profit, and it has made many enemies among the jungle's inhabitants.

1741.name: Gurubashi Arena
1741.description: The Gurubashi Arena is an ancient gladiatorial stadium in the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale, north of Booty Bay, a relic of the mighty Gurubashi Empire. Although it stands partly in ruins, games are still held within its walls, and fighters of every race come to test their skill, while others are captured and sold to the arena by the troll tribes. Gambling on the fights is common, and fortunes, and lives, are won and lost on the outcome. Pirates and goblins use the arena for their own entertainment, and the area around it is one of the few places in Stranglethorn where visitors are not immediately captured or killed, though it is far from friendly. Goblin merchants sell weapons and supplies to the fighters and spectators.

1742.name: Spirit Den
1742.description: The Spirit Den is a hidden cave on the northern side of Mistvale Valley in southern Stranglethorn Vale, said to be the home of a troll witch doctor who knows the secrets of the jungle's many ailments. The cave is dark and filled with strange herbs, totems, and bubbling cauldrons, and the air is thick with the smell of incense and smoke. The witch doctor welcomes those who seek his help, for a price.

1757.name: The Crimson Veil
1757.description: The Crimson Veil is one of the three ships of the Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored among the islands of the Wild Shore in southern Stranglethorn Vale, lying between the other two vessels. The ship is crewed by ruthless pirates who use it as a base for their raids against Booty Bay and passing merchant ships. Its decks are crowded with cannons, rigging, and armed buccaneers, and its crimson sails are a feared sight along the southern coasts.

1758.name: The Riptide
1758.description: The Riptide is the westernmost of the three ships of the Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored among the islands of the Wild Shore in southern Stranglethorn Vale. Crewed by ruthless pirates, it serves as one of the bases for the Bloodsails' raids against Booty Bay and passing ships. The ship is heavily armed, and its crew attacks anyone who comes near.

1759.name: The Damsel's Luck
1759.description: The Damsel's Luck is the easternmost of the three ships of the Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored among the islands of the Wild Shore in southern Stranglethorn Vale. Like its sister ships, it is crewed by ruthless pirates who raid Booty Bay and passing vessels. Its decks are filled with plunder, cannons, and armed buccaneers.

1760.name: Venture Co. Operations Center
1760.description: The Venture Co. Operations Center is a goblin oil platform built on Lake Nazferiti in northern Stranglethorn Vale, adjacent to the Venture Company's base camp. The platform is a noisy, smoky structure of metal and wood, filled with mechanics, geologists, and workers who drill for oil and pollute the lake's waters. The goblins guard the platform jealously, for it is a key part of their operations in the jungle.

2177.name: Battle Ring
2177.description: The Battle Ring is the fighting floor at the center of the Gurubashi Arena in southern Stranglethorn Vale, where gladiators and adventurers battle for glory, gold, and survival. The ring is surrounded by the crumbling stone stands of the ancient Gurubashi stadium, where spectators watch and gamble on the outcome. The pirates of the region regularly toss chests of treasure into the ring, and the bloody free-for-all that follows is a favorite entertainment. Anyone who steps into the ring must be ready to fight anyone else who enters.

2338.name: South Seas
2338.description: The South Seas surround the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms and stretch toward the southern coasts of Kalimdor, washing the shores of the Cape of Stranglethorn and the port of Booty Bay. The waters are warm and often calm, but they are also home to sharks, naga, and pirates, and they hide many islands and secrets. Somewhere far to the south lies the goblin island of Kezan. Ships sail these waters on their way between Booty Bay and Ratchet, and sailors tell many tales of the dangers and wonders of the southern seas.

2339.name: The Great Sea
2339.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale, stretching from the Vile Reef past Grom'gol Base Camp toward the open ocean. The sea is warm and blue, and its coral reefs and sunken ruins are home to murlocs, sharks, and colorful fish. Ships sail these waters on their way to and from Booty Bay and the northern ports, and the wreckage of unlucky vessels can be found along the coast.

3357.name: Yojamba Isle
3357.description: Yojamba Isle is a small island off the northwestern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, near the border with Westfall, home to an encampment of the Zandalar trolls. The Zandalari, ancient and wise trolls who regard all troll tribes as their kin, have come to Stranglethorn to oppose the return of the blood god Hakkar in Zul'Gurub, and they seek the help of brave adventurers in their struggle. The island is dotted with tents, altars, and the Zandalari's distinctive totems, and an air of solemn purpose hangs over the camp. The Zandalari welcome all who would aid them, regardless of race or faction.

33.description: Stranglethorn Vale is a vast, steaming jungle stretching across the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms, south of Duskwood and bordered by the sea on three sides. It is a land of towering trees, tangled vines, thorny undergrowth, and rushing rivers, where the air is hot, humid, and alive with the calls of birds and beasts. Tigers, panthers, raptors, gorillas, crocolisks, and giant spiders hunt in the shadows, and the eponymous strangle-thorns make travel slow and dangerous. For millennia, Stranglethorn was the heart of the Gurubashi Empire of the jungle trolls, ruled from the great city of Zul'Gurub. More than a thousand years ago, the Atal'ai priests summoned the avatar of the blood god Hakkar the Soulflayer, and the empire collapsed in a bloody civil war; its cities fell into ruin, and the surviving tribes became bitter enemies. Today the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter trolls dwell among the crumbling ruins, determined to purge their ancient lands of outsiders, while the Gurubashi in Zul'Gurub have once again fallen under the sway of Hakkar, and the Zandalari trolls have come to oppose him. Many outsiders have come to the jungle: the humans of Stormwind once tried to forge trade routes here and failed, goblins of the Venture Company mine and log the land, renegade soldiers and rebels fight in the north, ogres hold mounds in the east, naga lurk along the coasts, and the Bloodsail Buccaneers wage war on the Blackwater Raiders of Booty Bay, the bustling neutral port on the southern cape. The Horde maintains Grom'gol Base Camp on the western coast, and famous hunters come from far and wide to test their skill against the jungle's beasts.

36.name: Alterac Mountains

277.name: The Foothill Caverns
277.description: The Foothill Caverns are a network of caves in the hills between the Alterac Mountains and the Hillsbrad Foothills, inhabited by ferocious yetis. Only the most courageous hunters dare to cross paths with these fearsome creatures, and it is said that even the famous explorer Brann Bronzebeard once tracked a yeti here for days before slaying it. The caves are cold and dark, their floors littered with bones.

278.name: Lordamere Internment Camp
278.description: The Lordamere Internment Camp is a camp on a hill overlooking the Dalaran Crater in the western Alterac Mountains, defended by the forces of Dalaran. Originally one of the internment camps built after the Second War, it is now used by the Kirin Tor to hold their own prisoners and to guard the approaches to the crater. The camp is surrounded by wooden palisades and watchtowers, and its guards are wary of the Forsaken and other intruders.

279.name: Dalaran Crater
279.description: The Dalaran Crater is a vast crater on the western shore of Lordamere Lake in the Alterac Mountains, where the magical city of Dalaran once stood. Dalaran was destroyed by the demon lord Archimonde during the Third War, and the Kirin Tor rebuilt it beneath a great violet dome. Recently, the mages lifted the entire city from the ground and flew it north to Northrend to confront the Blue Dragonflight and the Lich King, leaving behind a gaping crater surrounded by the fading remains of the dome and a purplish haze. Glowing ley lines can be seen at the bottom of the crater. A few Kirin Tor mages and their elemental servants remain to guard the site.

280.name: Strahnbrad
280.description: Strahnbrad is a ghost town in the northern foothills of the Alterac Mountains, occupied by the Syndicate. Before the Third War, it was raided by Blackrock orcs, and Prince Arthas and the paladin Uther the Lightbringer came to its defense. The town survived the plague of undeath but fell years later to the Syndicate when the protection of Lordaeron's army vanished. Now it serves as a base of operations for the Syndicate's efforts throughout Hillsbrad and Arathi. Its houses stand empty and decaying, and Syndicate rogues and thugs patrol the streets.

281.name: Ruins of Alterac
281.description: The Ruins of Alterac are the remains of Alterac City, the former capital of the kingdom of Alterac, lying in the snowy heart of the Alterac Mountains. After the kingdom was destroyed by the Alliance for its betrayal during the Second War, most of the population abandoned their homes, and now the Crushridge ogres have taken over the ruins. Of the former capital, only the mighty keep remains relatively intact, looming over the broken walls and snow-covered streets. The Syndicate dreams of reclaiming the city, but the ogres hold it firmly.

282.name: Crushridge Hold
282.description: Crushridge Hold is a cave near the Ruins of Alterac in the Alterac Mountains, housing a large number of Crushridge ogres. The cave is dark and foul-smelling, littered with bones and plunder, and the ogres within attack anyone who comes near. It is one of the main strongholds of the Crushridge clan in the mountains.

283.name: Slaughter Hollow
283.description: Slaughter Hollow is an ogre mound deep in the Alterac Mountains, home to the Crushridge ogres. The hollow lives up to its grim name, for the ogres are brutal and violent, and the remains of their victims are scattered around their crude huts. The surrounding mountains are cold and snowy, and the ogres' fires can be seen from afar.

284.name: The Uplands
284.description: The Uplands are a high plateau in the northern Alterac Mountains, once the breadbasket of the kingdom of Alterac. After the destruction of the kingdom, the Uplands fell under the control of the Syndicate, who still hold them today, and the exiled nobles of Alterac use them as a base for their schemes. The farmlands are cold and windswept, and rare herbs grow among the rocks.

1339.name: Lordamere Lake
1339.description: On the Alterac side, the cold, grey waters of Lordamere Lake stretch west from the Misty Shore toward the distant shores of Silverpine Forest and the ruins of Lordaeron's capital. The great crater of Dalaran lies on the lake's eastern shore, and the dark keep of Fenris Isle can be seen in the distance. Mist often hangs over the water, and turtles and murlocs dwell along the shores.

1357.name: Gallows' Corner
1357.description: Gallows' Corner is a crossroads in the Alterac Mountains, close to the Ruins of Alterac, marked by a ruined tower and a grim gallows. The area is held by Crushridge ogres, who patrol the roads around the tower and attack travelers. The crossroads lives up to its sinister name, and few linger here.

1677.name: Gavin's Naze
1677.description: Gavin's Naze is a hill in the southern Alterac Mountains, overlooking the Hillsbrad Foothills. Mountain lions inhabit the area, including one of unusual coloring that hunters speak of with interest. The naze offers a sweeping view of the green hills and fields below.

1678.name: Sofera's Naze
1678.description: Sofera's Naze is a hill in the southern Alterac Mountains overlooking Tarren Mill, where the Syndicate has pitched a small camp. From here, the Syndicate's agents keep watch over the Forsaken town and the roads of Hillsbrad. The camp is a collection of tents and campfires, guarded by Syndicate thugs.

1679.name: Corrahn's Dagger
1679.description: Corrahn's Dagger is a hill in the southern Alterac Mountains overlooking Hillsbrad, where the Syndicate has established a small camp. Its rogues and mercenaries watch the roads below and prey on travelers. The hill takes its name from its sharp, dagger-like shape.

1680.name: The Headland
1680.description: The Headland is a hill jutting out over the Hillsbrad Foothills in the southern Alterac Mountains, covered with mountain lions. It is the site of one of the entrances to Alterac Valley, where the dwarves of the Stormpike Expedition and their allies come and go. The hill offers a commanding view of the surrounding lands.

1681.name: Misty Shore
1681.description: The Misty Shore is a stretch of shoreline along Lordamere Lake in the western Alterac Mountains, running from Dandred's Fold to the Dalaran Crater. As its name suggests, it is often shrouded in mist rising from the lake, and it is home to a large population of turtles. From the shore, the Dawning Isles and the eerie silhouette of Fenris Keep can be seen in the distance. A few zealots of the Scarlet Crusade are known to wander the area.

1682.name: Dandred's Fold
1682.description: Dandred's Fold is a small area on the shores of Lordamere Lake in the Alterac Mountains, where a fine mansion stands, said to be the residence of the scion of the Perenolde family, the leader of the Syndicate. Despite its charming appearance, the area is crawling with Syndicate rogues and mercenaries, quick to put a dagger in the back of anyone who does not share their affiliation. The mansion is a symbol of the exiled nobility's ambitions to reclaim their lost kingdom.

1683.name: Growless Cave
1683.description: Growless Cave is a cave in the Alterac Mountains, home to yetis. Within the cave burns a ceremonial pyre, created long ago by a would-be necromancer as part of a dark ritual. It is said that burning meat upon the flame can lure a powerful yeti from its lair. The cave is cold and dark, and the yetis within are fierce and territorial.

1684.name: Chillwind Point
1684.description: Chillwind Point is a small rise on the far eastern edge of the Alterac Mountains, dominated by an ancient troll ruin and named for the chill winds that sweep through the nearby ravine from the Western Plaguelands to the north. The point lies close to Chillwind Camp, an Alliance outpost just inside the Plaguelands, and it was once part of the Kingdom of Lordaeron. A solitary wise hermit is said to dwell here, watching the winds.

2839.name: Alterac Valley
2839.description: Alterac Valley is a secluded, snow-covered valley deep in the heart of the Alterac Mountains, long the home of the Frostwolf clan of orcs. Before the First War, the warlock Gul'dan exiled the Frostwolves here for refusing to drink the blood of the demon Mannoroth, and they eked out a living in the valley's southern reaches until Thrall united the Horde. Now led by the blind shaman Drek'Thar, the Frostwolves chose to remain in their ancestral home. In recent times, the dwarves of the Stormpike Expedition arrived in the northern valley in search of resources and ancient relics, sparking a bitter war with the Frostwolves. The two forces, led by General Vanndar Stormpike and Drek'Thar, battle endlessly for control of the valley, and both sides call upon allies from the Alliance and the Horde to aid them.

3486.name: Ravenholdt Manor
3486.description: Ravenholdt Manor is a secluded estate hidden among the peaks of the Alterac Mountains, reachable only by a winding mountain path through a hidden cave northwest of Durnholde Keep. It is said to be the headquarters of Ravenholdt, a secretive league of assassins and thieves whose members come from many races and loyalties. The manor is a fine building with courtyards and training grounds, but it is guarded closely, and only those who know its secrets are welcome. Few outside the shadows even know it exists.

36.description: The Alterac Mountains are a massive range of snow-capped peaks rising north of the Hillsbrad Foothills, stretching between Lordamere Lake in the west and the borders of the Western Plaguelands and the Hinterlands in the east. They were once the seat of the human kingdom of Alterac, ruled from Alterac City by the Perenolde family. During the Second War, Lord Perenolde betrayed the Alliance and allied with the Horde, and after the war the Alliance destroyed the kingdom and exiled its nobles. The exiles formed the Syndicate, a criminal organization that now seeks to reclaim the mountains and the surrounding lands. The ruins of Alterac City have been taken over by the Crushridge ogres, and the Syndicate holds the farmlands of the Uplands and several camps on the hills overlooking Hillsbrad. On the western shore of Lordamere Lake lies the great crater where the magical city of Dalaran once stood, before it lifted from the ground and flew north to Northrend, leaving only a fading dome and a few Kirin Tor mages behind. In a hidden valley deep in the mountains, the Frostwolf orcs, exiled here long ago by the warlock Gul'dan, battle the dwarves of the Stormpike Expedition for control of Alterac Valley. The mountains are cold and snowy at their heights, home to yetis, mountain lions, and ogres, and the secretive Ravenholdt Manor hides somewhere among their peaks.

38.name: Loch Modan

142.name: Ironband's Excavation Site
142.description: Ironband's Excavation Site is an extensive dwarven dig site in southeastern Loch Modan, south of the loch and southwest of the Farstrider Lodge. The dwarves of Ironforge dug deep into the hills here in search of relics and clues to their ancient past, but their excavations awakened something they had not expected: troggs of a particularly large and volatile breed, which swarmed up from below and overran the site. Once known by the name of an earlier prospector whose crew was driven off by the troggs, the dig has since passed into the hands of another dwarven prospector who struggles to keep the work going. Scaffolds, carts, and half-excavated ruins are scattered across the site, and the guttural cries of the troggs echo through the hills, a reminder of the dangers that lie buried beneath Khaz Modan.

143.name: Mo'grosh Stronghold
143.description: Mo'grosh Stronghold is a set of caves and rocky heights in northeastern Loch Modan, occupied by a powerful band of ogres. Brutes, enforcers, and shamans dwell within, and their raids make them a serious threat to the dwarves of the region. Crumbling ruins scattered across the area suggest that the stronghold was once a troll settlement, though whether the ogres drove the trolls out or simply moved into abandoned ruins long after the trolls departed is unknown. The caves are dark, foul-smelling, and littered with bones, and the dwarven mountaineers of Loch Modan regard the stronghold as one of the most dangerous places in the region.

144.name: Thelsamar
144.description: Thelsamar is a dwarven town on the western side of Loch Modan, the heart of dwarven life in the region and a welcome sight for travelers making their way between Ironforge, the Wetlands, and the southern lands. A road runs just west of the town, leading north to Dun Algaz and the Wetlands and west to the passes into Dun Morogh. Its sturdy stone houses, forge, and the cozy Stoutlager Inn cluster among the green hills near the shore of the loch, and gryphon riders come and go from its roost. The people of Thelsamar are fishermen, miners, and hunters, but they are also well acquainted with danger: troggs lurk in the valleys to the south, bears roam the hills, and the mountaineers stationed here are kept busy protecting the town and the roads.

145.name: Algaz Gate
145.description: Algaz Gate is the fortified dwarven gate in the northwestern corner of Loch Modan that guards the tunnels of Dun Algaz, the mountain pass leading north to the Wetlands. Dun Algaz was once a great dwarven stronghold, and during the Second War it served as the Horde's last bastion in the region after the orcs were driven from Dun Modr. Long ago, the gate made Loch Modan one of the most peaceful places in the Eastern Kingdoms, for few enemies could penetrate the mountains around it. Today it remains the main thoroughfare between the dwarven lands and the Wetlands, but the road beyond is no longer safe, and the mountaineers stationed here watch the tunnels warily.

146.name: Stonewrought Dam
146.description: The Stonewrought Dam is a colossal wall of stone stretching across the northern edge of Loch Modan, one of the greatest wonders of dwarven engineering in the world. It traps the snowmelt flowing from Ironforge Mountain, more than doubling the size of the loch, while the lands below it to the north have been drained into the marshy Wetlands. A road runs across the top of the dam, and waterfalls cascade from its spillways into the valleys below. The dam is of vital importance to the dwarves, and it has recently drawn the attention of the Dark Iron dwarves, whose threats have forced the engineers of Ironforge to tighten security. Dwarven engineers and guards keep a constant watch over the great structure, aware of the catastrophe its failure would bring.

147.name: The Farstrider Lodge
147.description: The Farstrider Lodge is a hunting lodge in the eastern hills of Loch Modan, built in the graceful style of the high elves, with tall arched windows and sweeping roofs that stand out among the rugged dwarven lands. It is a gathering place for hunters, trappers, and rangers, and its halls are decorated with trophies of the many beasts that roam the region. The lodge is run by a grizzled dwarf of Ironforge, and its inhabitants are now mostly dwarves and humans, though a high elf of the Farstriders, the rangers sworn to defend Quel'Thalas, still resides there. The surrounding hills are rich with game, including bears, boars, and mountain buzzards, and the lodge offers a warm hearth to those who brave the wilds of eastern Loch Modan.

149.name: Silver Stream Mine
149.description: Silver Stream Mine is a mine in northern Loch Modan, east of Algaz Station and southwest of the Stonewrought Dam. For generations it has been a bountiful source of silver for the dwarves of Ironforge, its tunnels running deep into the mountainside. In recent times, however, the mine has been completely taken over by aggressive Tunnel Rat kobolds, who seek its riches for themselves and drive off anyone who dares to enter. Abandoned mine carts and tools lie scattered at the entrance, and the dim light of the kobolds' candles flickers in the depths of the tunnels.

556.name: The Loch
556.description: The loch at the heart of Loch Modan is a vast expanse of cold, clear water held in place by the Stonewrought Dam, one of the largest freshwater lakes in the world. Its waters teem with fish, drawing fishermen from Thelsamar as well as bears and other predators to its shores, and crocolisks lurk among the reeds. Three large islands rise from the lake; the northernmost bears ruins from the Second War, while the others are rocky and barren, haunted by troggs and wild beasts. Broken catapults and ballistae from the war still lie on the islands and beneath the waves, mute evidence of the region's bloody history. Mists frequently drift across the surface, and the grey mountains surrounding the lake are reflected in its still waters on calm days.

837.name: Dun Algaz
837.description: Dun Algaz is a tunneled mountain pass leading north from Loch Modan to the Wetlands, guarded at its southern end by the dwarven gate of Algaz. It was once a great dwarven stronghold, and during the Second War it became the Horde's last hold in the region after the orcs were driven from Dun Modr. The derelict fortress still serves as the main thoroughfare between the dwarven lands and the Wetlands, but it is no longer safe: orcs of the Dragonmaw clan have overrun the old outpost in the middle of the pass, forcing the dwarven mountaineers to fall back to the upper tunnel. Travelers passing through Dun Algaz must be either strong or swift, and the dwarves of Loch Modan regard the pass with growing concern.

838.name: North Gate Pass
838.description: On the Loch Modan side, North Gate Pass descends from the snowy heights of Dun Morogh into the green, misty hills of the loch country, passing through a massive dwarven gate guarded by Ironforge mountaineers. It is the route most often taken by those heading from Ironforge toward Algaz Station, Dun Algaz, and the Wetlands beyond. As travelers emerge from the pass, the bitter cold of the highlands gives way to cooler, damper air, and the snow-covered rock gives way to pine and birch forests. The dwarves guard the gate closely, for it is one of the few passages into the heart of their homeland.

839.name: South Gate Pass
839.description: On the Loch Modan side, South Gate Pass descends from the frozen highlands of Dun Morogh into the green hills of the loch country, passing through a great dwarven gate watched over by Ironforge mountaineers. It is the closest route to the town of Thelsamar, and a steady stream of travelers, merchants, and soldiers passes along its road. Beyond the pass lies the verdant Valley of Kings, with its towering statues of ancient dwarven kings, and the road continues east toward the heart of Loch Modan. The change in climate is striking: the snow of Dun Morogh fades into the cool, misty air and lush grass of the lowlands.

923.name: Stonesplinter Valley
923.description: Stonesplinter Valley is a valley carved among the mountains in southwestern Loch Modan, east of the Valley of Kings. Once a pristine and peaceful place, it is now crawling with hostile Stonesplinter troggs, who have built crude camps among the rocks and dug into the caves of the hillsides. The troggs, unearthed by dwarven excavations, are savage and numerous, and they strike at any travelers who stray too close. The dwarves of Thelsamar regard the valley as enemy territory and wage a constant struggle to keep the troggs from spreading further into Loch Modan.

924.name: Valley of Kings
924.description: The Valley of Kings is a verdant valley in the southwestern corner of Loch Modan, through which the road from South Gate Pass passes on its way into the loch country. The valley is dominated by two great statues of the dwarven kings Madoran Bronzebeard and Khardros Wildhammer, commissioned by their sons in honor of their fathers after the War of the Three Hammers. The statues stand guard over the pass leading south to the Searing Gorge, which became a volcanic wasteland after the Dark Irons summoned Ragnaros, serving both as a warning to any who would attack the dwarven kingdoms and as a reminder of the price the Dark Irons paid for their crimes. The gate to the gorge is kept locked and guarded by dwarven mountaineers, for the lands beyond are held by the Dark Iron clan.

925.name: Algaz Station
925.description: Algaz Station is a dwarven outpost in northern Loch Modan, just east of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, from which it takes its name. Many dwarven mountaineers are stationed here, guarding the road between Thelsamar, the passes to Dun Morogh, and the tunnels leading north to the Wetlands. The station is a sturdy, practical place of stone walls and watchtowers, and its soldiers keep a close eye on the troggs, kobolds, and wild beasts that threaten the region, as well as the Dragonmaw orcs who have taken over the old fortress in the pass beyond.

936.name: Grizzlepaw Ridge
936.description: Grizzlepaw Ridge is a mountainous ridge south of Thelsamar and east of Stonesplinter Valley in Loch Modan, named for the large population of bears that make their dens among its rocks and pines. The bears roam the slopes and occasionally wander down to the valleys below, and among them is said to be a particularly ferocious old bear that the locals speak of with respect and fear. The ridge offers sweeping views of the loch and the surrounding hills, but few dwarves venture onto its slopes without a rifle at hand.

2101.name: Stoutlager Inn
2101.description: The Stoutlager Inn is the heart of Thelsamar, a cozy dwarven tavern where travelers, miners, and mountaineers gather to share stories, warm themselves by the fire, and enjoy a hearty meal and a mug of ale. Its sturdy stone walls and timber beams keep out the damp chill of Loch Modan, and its common room is rarely quiet, filled with laughter, song, and the clatter of tankards. The inn is one of the most popular places in the region, and many a journey through Khaz Modan begins or ends at its hearth.

38.description: Loch Modan is a land of rugged hills and green valleys in eastern Khaz Modan, lying in the foothills of Ironforge Mountain east of Dun Morogh. At its heart is the great loch from which it takes its name, one of the largest bodies of fresh water in the world, held in place by the massive Stonewrought Dam along its northern shore, a marvel of dwarven engineering. Grey mountains rise on all sides, and the hills are lightly wooded with pine and birch. Unlike the frozen highlands of Dun Morogh, Loch Modan has a cool, damp climate: mists often roll over the water, rain keeps the land lush, and bitter chills claim the mornings and evenings, though the loch itself rarely freezes. The region is rich in fish, timber, and ore, and the dwarves of Ironforge fish its waters, mine its cliffs, and cut its forests. Its main settlement is the town of Thelsamar on the western shore. During the Second War, the orcish Horde overran the region, but the dwarves reclaimed it after the war; broken siege engines still lie on the islands and the lake bed as reminders of that bloody time. Today the land is far from peaceful: troggs unearthed by dwarven digs infest the valleys and caves, kobolds have seized a silver mine, ogres hold a stronghold in the northeast, and Dark Iron dwarves threaten the dam. Dwarven mountaineers guard the passes to Dun Morogh, the Wetlands, the Badlands, and the sealed road to the Searing Gorge.

40.name: Westfall

2.name: Longshore
2.description: Longshore is the long stretch of sandy coastline along the western edge of Westfall, where the dry fields give way to beaches and the endless waters of the Great Sea. The wind blows constantly off the water, and the shore is littered with driftwood, shells, and the wreckage of ships, including a beached elven vessel bearing the symbol of a unicorn. Swarms of murlocs roam the beaches unchecked, building crude huts along the shoreline and attacking those who wander too close. The sound of crashing waves and the gurgling cries of murlocs are constant companions to anyone traveling along the coast.

20.name: Moonbrook
20.description: Moonbrook is a ghost town in southern Westfall, once the thriving center of the region's farmlands and a sister town to Goldshire. During the First War, it was one of the last towns to fall to the Horde before the sacking of Stormwind, and it was rebuilt after the Alliance's victory in the Second War. When the Defias Brotherhood seized control of Westfall, the townsfolk abandoned Moonbrook, and today it is held by the bandits, who use it as a front for their main base of operations, said to lie in an old mine nearby. Its houses, inn, schoolhouse, and smithy stand empty and decaying, haunted by memories of better times, and Defias sentries keep watch over the streets. An unlikely merchant in the old inn trades with anyone willing to pay, regardless of their loyalties.

26.name: Lighthouse
26.description: Along the southern coast of Westfall stands a solitary lighthouse, its tall white tower rising from a rocky outcrop above the crashing waves of the Great Sea. Built by the Kingdom of Stormwind to warn ships away from the treacherous rocks and shoals, its light still burns, guiding vessels along the coast toward Stormwind and the southern seas. The lighthouse is a lonely place, battered by salt winds and surrounded by the cries of seabirds, and murlocs prowl the nearby beaches. Sailors speak of the spirit of a sea captain said to haunt its shores.

107.name: Saldean's Farm
107.description: Saldean's Farm is a small farmstead in northern Westfall, unique in the region as one of the few farms that has not been completely overrun by the Defias Brotherhood. Though the bandits' mechanical harvesters roam the surrounding fields, the farmer and his wife have stubbornly refused to leave their home, determined to hold on to the land that has been in their family for generations. They scrape a living from what remains of their fields and offer basic supplies to travelers. Their farm has become a symbol of the stubborn resilience of the people of Westfall.

108.name: Sentinel Hill
108.description: Sentinel Hill is the last stronghold of the People's Militia in Westfall, a fortified hilltop crowned by a tall stone watchtower in the center of the region. It is here that the men and women of the militia, mostly farmers and patriots who refused to abandon their homes, make their stand against the Defias Brotherhood and the gnolls that plague the land. The hill is home to around three hundred people, with a barracks, an inn, a smithy, and a lumber mill, and gryphon riders connect it with Stormwind and other Alliance holdings. The militia relies on volunteers and adventurers to aid its cause, for help from the crown is scarce. Despite the hardships, the defenders of Sentinel Hill remain determined to one day reclaim Westfall for its rightful people.

109.name: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm
109.description: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm is a farmstead in northern Westfall that has been taken over by the Defias Brotherhood. Its fields, once full of pumpkins and crops, are now patrolled by the bandits' rogue mechanical harvest watchers, and Defias agents have taken up residence in the farm buildings. The farm's owners fled and now live by the road near the Jansen Stead, having lost almost everything. The abandoned fields are overgrown with weeds, and the scarecrow-like harvesters lumber menacingly among the rotting pumpkins.

111.name: Jangolode Mine
111.description: Jangolode Mine is a mine in northern Westfall, once one of the key sources of minerals and ore for Stormwind City. It has been seized by the Defias Brotherhood, and since the soldiers of Stormwind are busy fighting on distant fronts, there are not enough troops available to dislodge them. The mine's entrance is guarded by bandits, and kobolds are said to toil in its tunnels, possibly in league with the Defias. Abandoned mine carts and tools lie scattered around the entrance, relics of the days when honest miners worked here.

113.name: Gold Coast Quarry
113.description: Gold Coast Quarry is a large stone and gold quarry in northwestern Westfall, near the coast. It was once a valuable source of minerals and gold for the Kingdom of Stormwind, but it has fallen into the hands of the Defias Brotherhood, whose agents now patrol the area and work the quarry for their own profit. Murlocs from the nearby coast also wander into the area. The quarry is a stark, rocky pit carved into the hills, its scaffolding and equipment now used by the bandits.

115.name: Westfall Lighthouse
115.description: The Westfall Lighthouse stands on a rocky islet just off the coast at the far southern edge of Westfall, its tall white tower guiding ships along the treacherous shoreline toward Stormwind and the southern seas. The lighthouse is a lonely sentinel, battered by the winds and waves of the Great Sea, and the surrounding beaches are prowled by murlocs. The keepers who once tended its light are long gone, and the locals whisper that the ghost of a sea captain still watches over the coast from its shores. On clear nights, the light can be seen for miles out at sea.

219.name: Alexston Farmstead
219.description: Alexston Farmstead is one of the many farms in central Westfall that have been taken over by the Defias Brotherhood. Its fields are now roamed by the bandits' deadly mechanical harvest watchers, and Defias agents have claimed the farmhouse and barns. The family that once lived here produced a notable architect in the service of Stormwind, but those days of prosperity are long gone. The farm stands as a sad reminder of how far Westfall has fallen.

916.name: The Jansen Stead
916.description: The Jansen Stead is the northernmost farm in Westfall, located near the bridge leading to Elwynn Forest. Like most of the farms in the region, its owners have been driven off by the Defias Brotherhood, and now the bandits and their mechanical harvest watchers control the farm. Nearby, along the road, a displaced farming couple has set up a meager camp after fleeing their own farm, and they are often the first Westfall folk travelers meet when entering the region. The farm's fields are overgrown and its buildings decaying.

917.name: The Dead Acre
917.description: The Dead Acre is the blackened ruin of a farm in southeastern Westfall, close to the bridge leading into Duskwood. When the Defias Brotherhood began taking control of Westfall, they burned the farm and its fields to the ground, and now only smoking ruins and scorched earth remain. The mechanical harvest watchers that roam the smoldering fields are said to be the strongest in Westfall, and the area is avoided by sensible travelers. The Dead Acre is a grim symbol of the cruelty of the bandits and the suffering of Westfall's people.

918.name: The Molsen Farm
918.description: The Molsen Farm is a farmstead in central Westfall that has been taken over by the Defias Brotherhood. The bandits' mechanical harvest watchers terrorize the fields, and Defias agents have claimed the farmhouse as their own. The farm's former owners have fled or been driven away, and the once-fertile fields now lie fallow and overgrown. Like so many farms in Westfall, it serves as a hideout and staging ground for the bandits' raids on the surrounding lands.

919.name: Stendel's Pond
919.description: Stendel's Pond is a small pond southwest of Sentinel Hill in Westfall, one of the few sources of fresh water in the dry, windswept region. Its waters are surrounded by reeds and a few scraggly trees, but the area has been claimed by Riverpaw gnolls, who have set up camps nearby. While water is scarce in Westfall, the presence of the gnolls has kept the local farmers from making use of the pond.

920.name: The Dagger Hills
920.description: The Dagger Hills are a rugged ridge of rocky hills rising behind Moonbrook in southern Westfall, overlooking the ghost town and the sea beyond. The hills are home to some of the strongest and most dangerous members of the Defias Brotherhood outside their hidden underground base, and their camps dot the slopes. The Dagger Hills offer the bandits a commanding view of the surrounding lands, and few who are not Defias venture here. The wind howls through the rocks, and the hills are sparse and barren.

921.name: Demont's Place
921.description: Demont's Place is the burned-out ruin of a farmstead just west of Moonbrook in southern Westfall. Like the Dead Acre, little remains of the original farm but charred timbers and scorched earth, and the area has an eerie, desolate feel. Although no mechanical harvesters patrol the area, it is crawling with powerful agents of the Defias Brotherhood. The locals avoid the place, and some say it is haunted by the spirits of those who once lived there.

922.name: The Dust Plains
922.description: The Dust Plains are the southernmost region of Westfall, a stretch of dry, windswept grassland near the border with Duskwood and the coast. The plains are home to Riverpaw gnolls, who threaten travelers from their camps scattered across the area. An old guard tower, overrun by Defias agents, stands in the plains, a reminder of the days when Stormwind's soldiers kept order here. The wind blows constantly across the plains, raising clouds of dust and making travel unpleasant.

2364.name: The Great Sea
2364.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the western coast of Westfall, stretching out to the horizon beyond the long beaches of Longshore. The sea is often rough, driven by strong westerly winds that sweep inland across the dry farmlands, and its waves break against the sandy shores and rocky outcrops of the coast. Ships sail these waters on their way to and from Stormwind and the southern ports, guided by the lighthouse on the southern shore. Murlocs dwell in the shallows and along the beaches, and the wrecks of old ships lie scattered along the coast.

4668.name: The Cooper Residence
4668.description: The Cooper Residence is an abandoned house in the western part of Moonbrook in Westfall, once the home of the Cooper family, one of the town's more prominent households. When the Defias Brotherhood seized Moonbrook, the family was forced to flee or worse, and their home now stands empty and dusty, its furniture overturned and its belongings scattered. Old journals and newspapers still lie on the floor, telling of the town's better days and its sudden fall. The house is a quiet, melancholy place, a small but poignant reminder of the families whose lives were shattered by the bandits.

40.description: Westfall is a region of rolling hills, pastures, and farmland on the western coast of the Kingdom of Stormwind, lying west of Elwynn Forest and bordered by the sea. Once the breadbasket of the kingdom, it has fallen into ruin after years of war, neglect, and lawlessness. Its fields lie fallow and dry, the grass is yellowed, and strong winds blowing from the sea and from Duskwood sweep across the bare farmland, carrying dust and the cries of carrion birds. After the Second War, the Defias Brotherhood, a band of outlaws formed from the stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind and were never paid for their labor, chose Westfall as their refuge. With Stormwind's armies occupied by distant wars, the bandits drove off many of the farmers, burned fields, seized farmsteads and mines, and set rogue mechanical harvest watchers loose in the fields. The ghost town of Moonbrook is their stronghold, and it is rumored that their leaders hide deep underground in an old mine nearby. Gnolls of the Riverpaw tribe raid from the south, and murlocs prowl the long coast. The People's Militia, a volunteer force of farmers and patriots, holds out at Sentinel Hill and struggles to protect the few farmers who stubbornly cling to their land. The people of Westfall live in fear and resentment, feeling abandoned by a crown that seems to have forgotten them.

41.name: Deadwind Pass

2558.name: Deadwind Ravine
2558.description: Deadwind Ravine is a craggy cleft running through the mountains southward toward Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. The western road winds through the ravine along its upper level, and at its end lies the southern bridge near the ominous tower. The ravine is barren and windswept, its walls of grey stone rising steeply on either side, and the petrified trees cling to the rocks like skeletal hands. The foul wind of Deadwind whistles through the ravine, carrying strange whispers.

2560.name: Ariden's Camp
2560.description: Ariden's Camp is a deserted campsite just north of the main road passing through Deadwind Pass from Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows. Its tents and supplies lie abandoned, and no one knows who, or what, Ariden was, or what became of those who camped here. The site is eerily silent, and the abandoned belongings suggest a hasty departure, or something worse. Travelers rarely linger here.

2561.name: The Vice
2561.description: The Vice is a rugged area in the southern part of Deadwind Pass, scattered along the road leading to Karazhan, and home to the Deadwind ogres. The ogres have built several camps among the rocks and in the nearby caves, and they attack any travelers who wander into their territory. It is said that they serve a mysterious master, perhaps the dark power that dwells in the tower. Nobody knows why the ogres chose to settle in this desolate area, with nothing but restless spirits and vultures for company.

2562.name: Karazhan
2562.description: Karazhan is the ancient ivory tower that dominates the southern part of Deadwind Pass, built on a nexus of powerful ley lines. It was the seat of Medivh, the last Guardian of Tirisfal, whose corruption by the demon Sargeras led him to open the Dark Portal and bring the orcish Horde to Azeroth. After Medivh was slain by his apprentice Khadgar and the hero Anduin Lothar, the tower sealed itself off from the world, and a terrible curse pervaded both Karazhan and the surrounding lands. Many nobles of Darkshire who ventured into the tower to investigate the blight never emerged. Recently, an evil presence has taken the tower as its own, and its halls are said to crawl with spirits, demons, and the echoes of Medivh's power. The Violet Eye, a secret sect of the Kirin Tor, watches the tower closely. Karazhan is a place of great power and great danger, holding some of the most dangerous artifacts and secrets in the world.

2563.name: Morgan's Plot
2563.description: Morgan's Plot is a small, abandoned church with a graveyard and crypt located behind Karazhan in southern Deadwind Pass. It once served the village that flourished at the base of the tower, but now its tombstones lean crookedly in the dead earth, and restless spirits wander among the graves. The church is cold and silent, its windows broken and its walls stained by time. It is a melancholy place, a reminder of the people who once lived in the shadow of the tower.

2697.name: Deadman's Crossing
2697.description: Deadman's Crossing is the eastern crossroads of Deadwind Pass, where the roads lead west to Duskwood, east toward the Swamp of Sorrows, and south toward Karazhan. It is marked by a hangman's tree still bearing a pair of corpses, as well as a signpost warning travelers to turn back and abandon all hope. Despite the grim warnings, the main road through the crossing is relatively safe for those who keep to it, and most travelers pass through quickly without straying. The wind howls through the crossing, and the creaking of the hanging bodies adds to its grim atmosphere.

2837.name: The Master's Cellar
2837.description: The Master's Cellar lies beneath the ruins of a small village in the southernmost part of Deadwind Pass, just south of Karazhan, where the servants of the tower once lived. Its cellars and the caverns beneath them are filled with restless spirits and wailing shades, the tormented souls of those who once served the master of the tower. One entrance leads into a vast wine cellar, while another opens into a collapsed floor descending into a cave system deep underground. The cellars are dark, cold, and filled with eerie whispers.

2937.name: Grosh'gok Compound
2937.description: The Grosh'gok Compound is the largest and southernmost of the caves in the Vice in Deadwind Pass, inhabited by brutish Deadwind ogres and their magi. The cave is dark and foul-smelling, littered with bones and crude weapons, and the ogres within are among the most dangerous in the pass. It is said that the ogres serve a mysterious master, and that those they capture are taken to the tower of Karazhan.

2938.name: Sleeping Gorge
2938.description: Sleeping Gorge is a small chasm in eastern Deadwind Pass, through which one of the paths leading south toward Karazhan runs before turning into the Vice. The gorge is narrow and shadowy, its walls rising high above the path, and an unnatural stillness hangs over it, as if the land itself were holding its breath. The petrified trees and barren rocks give it a desolate, lifeless air.

41.description: Deadwind Pass is a desolate, cursed canyon lying in the heart of the southern Eastern Kingdoms, connecting Duskwood to the west with the Swamp of Sorrows to the east. Once considered part of the Redridge Mountains, it is now a dead land: the trees are leafless and petrified, the grass is grey and lifeless, and a foul, keening wind constantly blows through the canyon, giving it its name. The weather is perpetually stormy or threatening to storm, and lightning often strikes the barren rocks. In the south of the pass stands Karazhan, the ivory tower that was once the seat of Medivh, the last Guardian of Tirisfal, whose corruption by the demon Sargeras led him to open the Dark Portal and bring the orcish Horde to Azeroth. After Medivh was slain by his apprentice Khadgar and the hero Anduin Lothar, a terrible curse pervaded the tower and the lands around it, and evil magic still leaks from Karazhan, draining the life from the region. The pass is inhabited by brutish Deadwind ogres, restless spirits, carrion birds, and strange wisps, and the ruins of a village at the base of the tower are haunted by the undead. It is whispered that a new dark presence has claimed the tower, and that the ogres serve it. Most travelers move through the pass as quickly as possible, keeping to the main road.

44.name: Redridge Mountains

68.name: Lake Everstill
68.description: Lake Everstill is a large, serene lake in the center of the Redridge Mountains, its crystal-clear azure waters reflecting the red peaks and tall elms that surround it. The town of Lakeshire rests on its northern bank, and its eastern river flows past the dark walls of Stonewatch Keep before tumbling over Stonewatch Falls. The lake was once famous for its fishing, but it has recently been overrun by tribes of murlocs that dwell along its shores and beneath its waves. Rumors persist of a great lake beast patrolling its depths, and fishermen speak of it with fear and fascination.

69.name: Lakeshire
69.description: Lakeshire is an ancient human town on the northern banks of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains, home to about fifteen hundred citizens, mostly farmers, fishermen, and travelers. It is a serene and quiet place of timber houses, a town hall, and a cozy inn, a living example of how peaceful these lands were before the coming of the Horde. The town is governed by an elected magistrate and defended by a small guard, for Stormwind's army has largely left Redridge to fend for itself. The great bridge leading across the water to the town lies broken, and Lakeshire lives under the constant threat of the Blackrock orcs who have seized Stonewatch Keep, as well as gnolls and murlocs. Despite its troubles, the townsfolk remain proud and resilient, and gryphon riders connect Lakeshire with Stormwind and the other Alliance holdings.

70.name: Stonewatch
70.description: Stonewatch is the common name of the great human stronghold in the eastern Redridge Mountains, comprising the defensible Stonewatch Keep and the armored Stonewatch Tower, with Stonewatch Falls cascading down the cliff below. Built to guard the eastern approaches to Lakeshire, the fortress has fallen into the hands of the Blackrock clan of orcs, led by a ruthless warlord. The orcs now use Stonewatch as their main base in Redridge, launching raids against the surrounding lands. The loss of the stronghold is a bitter blow to the people of Lakeshire, who once relied on it for their protection.

71.name: Stonewatch Falls
71.description: Stonewatch Falls is a waterfall in the eastern Redridge Mountains, where the river draining Lake Everstill cascades down the cliffs below Stonewatch Keep into a deep pool nestled among the hills. A small tribe of murlocs makes its home here, catching fish and building crude huts along the water's edge. The falls are a beautiful sight, their mist catching the light in shimmering rainbows, but the presence of the murlocs and the orcs in the keep above makes the area dangerous. From here, the river continues on its long journey toward the coast.

95.name: Redridge Canyons
95.description: The Redridge Canyons form a labyrinthine network of narrow passages and rocky gorges in the northwestern part of the Redridge Mountains. Once a favored hunting ground for deer and mountain boar among the people of Lakeshire, the canyons have been claimed by a tribe of gnolls led by a ferocious chieftain, and they are no longer safe to enter. The red rock walls rise steeply on either side, and the winding paths make it easy to become lost or ambushed. The howls and barks of gnolls echo through the canyons, a warning to those who venture too close.

96.name: Tower of Ilgalar
96.description: The Tower of Ilgalar is a dark mage tower in the eastern Redridge Mountains, rising above Galardell Valley. It is the lair of a powerful sorcerer who was exiled from the Mage Quarter of Stormwind for his study of the dark arts, and who now commands the Shadowhide gnolls that infest the valley around it. Dragon bones hang on display throughout the tower, and strange relics fill its chambers, though no one knows what interest the sorcerer has in them. The tower is locked in a long-standing rivalry with the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest, and the two are said to spy on each other through magical means.

97.name: Alther's Mill
97.description: Alther's Mill is an abandoned lumber mill northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains, once a busy place where timber from the surrounding forests was cut and sent downriver. Now its buildings stand empty and decaying, overrun by spiders, buzzards, and the occasional stray orc. Most travelers pass through on their way to Stonewatch Keep, and the mill's locked chests and abandoned storerooms have made it a favorite haunt of those with nimble fingers. The creaking of the old waterwheel and the rustling of the forest are the only sounds that disturb the silence.

98.name: Rethban Caverns
98.description: The Rethban Caverns are an extensive series of caverns stretching deep into the northwestern Redridge Mountains. They are rich in a rare type of ore, which draws miners and prospectors, but the caves have been claimed by a tribe of gnolls led by a cunning chieftain, who guard the ore jealously. The caverns are dark and winding, their walls glittering with mineral veins, and the gnolls' crude camps and torches can be found throughout. Few miners dare to enter without an armed escort.

996.name: Render's Camp
996.description: Render's Camp is an orcish outpost in the northwestern Redridge Mountains, near the pass leading into the Burning Steppes. Like Render's Valley and Render's Rock, it is named after Rend Blackhand, the self-proclaimed warchief of the Dark Horde who commands the Blackrock clan from Blackrock Spire. The camp is held by powerful Blackrock orcs, who use it as a staging ground for their raids into Redridge and keep watch over the road to the north. Its crude palisades, war banners, and burning braziers make it a fearsome sight.

997.name: Render's Valley
997.description: Render's Valley is an orcish outpost in the southeastern Redridge Mountains, named, like Render's Camp and Render's Rock, after the Blackrock warchief Rend Blackhand. The valley is held by Blackrock orcs, though they are not as powerful as their kin in the northwest, and their camps are scattered across the valley floor. The orcs hold prisoners in their camps and use the valley as a base for raiding the surrounding lands. Rumors speak of a hidden mountain pass in the mountains south of the valley that leads to the Swamp of Sorrows.

998.name: Render's Rock
998.description: Render's Rock is a large cave in the northwestern Redridge Mountains, near the entrance to the Burning Steppes, named after the Blackrock warchief Rend Blackhand. It is occupied by powerful Blackrock orcs, who use it as a stronghold and a prison for their captives. The cave is dark and foreboding, its entrance guarded by orc warriors, and the surrounding area is one of the most dangerous in Redridge. The sounds of orcish war drums and the cries of captives sometimes echo from its depths.

999.name: Stonewatch Tower
999.description: Stonewatch Tower is the armored watchtower of the human stronghold of Stonewatch in the eastern Redridge Mountains, standing near Stonewatch Keep. Built by the people of Lakeshire to guard the eastern approaches to their lands, it was seized by the orcs of the Blackrock clan, who now garrison it with their own warriors. From its heights, the orcs keep watch over Lake Everstill and the surrounding hills, and their banners fly where those of Lakeshire once did.

1000.name: Galardell Valley
1000.description: Galardell Valley is a valley in the northeastern Redridge Mountains, home to the dark Tower of Ilgalar, where an exiled sorcerer dwells. The valley is crawling with Shadowhide gnolls, who serve the sorcerer and attack anyone who ventures into their territory. Their strongest warriors can call upon the whole pack for aid, making the valley a dangerous place for the unwary. The valley's forests and meadows have been trampled and despoiled by the gnolls, and an air of menace hangs over the land.

1001.name: Lakeridge Highway
1001.description: The Lakeridge Highway is an old road running along the southern edge of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains, connecting the Three Corners crossroads with the eastern lands and Stonewatch Keep. In the days before the First War, the highway was well traveled, but since the orcs seized Stonewatch it has fallen into disuse. Gnolls now patrol most of the road, and murlocs, black dragon whelps, and wild animals also roam the area, making travel along it dangerous. The highway offers beautiful views of the lake and mountains, but few dare to linger.

1002.name: Three Corners
1002.description: Three Corners is a crossroads in the southwestern corner of the Redridge Mountains, where the roads from the three shires of the kingdom meet: west to Goldshire in Elwynn Forest, east to Lakeshire, and south to Darkshire in Duskwood. A lone Stormwind guard patrols the crossroads, keeping watch over the travelers who pass through. The area is surrounded by forested hills, and the road signs pointing in three directions have given the place its name. It is a busy junction, and many journeys through the southern lands of the kingdom pass this way.

2099.name: Stonewatch Keep
2099.description: Stonewatch Keep is the main fortress of the human stronghold of Stonewatch in the eastern Redridge Mountains, a massive stone keep built to guard the eastern approaches to Lakeshire. It once belonged to the people of Lakeshire, but it was seized by the orcs of the Blackrock clan, and now it is controlled by a ruthless Blackrock warlord and his lieutenants. The keep's halls are filled with orc warriors, warlocks, and their worgs, and it serves as the main base for the orcish raids into Redridge. The loss of Stonewatch Keep is a deep wound for the people of Lakeshire, who dream of the day it will be reclaimed.

44.description: The Redridge Mountains are a region of rugged, red-hued peaks, towering elms, and rushing rivers lying east of Elwynn Forest, northeast of Duskwood, and south of the Burning Steppes. At their heart lies the serene azure expanse of Lake Everstill, on whose northern shore stands the ancient town of Lakeshire. Redridge is under Stormwind's protection, though it has long governed itself, and its people are content and hardy folk who supply the kingdom with timber, fish, and crops. The range once stretched much farther north, but centuries ago it was shattered by the summoning of Ragnaros, which created the Burning Steppes and Blackrock Mountain.
