In recent times, Redridge has become a frontier. Orcs of the Blackrock clan, savage holdouts of the old Horde from the Burning Steppes, have seized the human stronghold of Stonewatch and set up camps throughout the mountains, named after their leader Rend Blackhand. Gnolls of the Redridge and Shadowhide tribes have claimed the canyons and valleys, murlocs infest the lake, and black dragon whelps roam the hills. An exiled sorcerer has taken up residence in a tower in the eastern valleys. The bridge to Lakeshire lies broken, and with Stormwind's armies far away, the people of Redridge must rely on their own small guard and the help of travelers to keep their homes safe.

45.name: Arathi Highlands

313.name: Northfold Manor
313.description: Northfold Manor is a farmstead on the northwestern outskirts of the Arathi Highlands, once a prosperous manor of the kingdom of Stromgarde. It has been occupied by the forces of the Syndicate, who use it as a base for their operations in the highlands. The manor's buildings and fields are patrolled by Syndicate rogues and thugs, and its rightful owners have long since fled.

314.name: Go'Shek Farm
314.description: Go'Shek Farm is a farmstead in the southeastern Arathi Highlands, near Witherbark Village. Once a human farm, it was taken over by the orcs of Hammerfall after the Third War, and it now provides supplies for the Horde outpost. The Forsaken are also said to use the farm for their own mysterious alchemical experiments. The farm is guarded by Hammerfall grunts.

315.name: Dabyrie's Farmstead
315.description: Dabyrie's Farmstead is a farm in the northern Arathi Highlands, inhabited by the Dabyrie family and other local people of Stromgarde, who remain loyal to the Alliance. The farm is protected by its own militia, who defend it against the ogres, Syndicate, and other threats of the highlands. It is one of the few places in Arathi where the old life of the kingdom endures.

316.name: Boulderfist Hall
316.description: Boulderfist Hall is a fortress of the Boulderfist ogres in the southern Arathi Highlands, near the Thandol Span and Witherbark Village. The ogres have strongly fortified the caves, and their chieftain is said to dwell within the largest of them. Boulderfist Hall is one of the main strongholds of the ogres in the highlands, and they launch raids against the humans, orcs, and Syndicate from here.

317.name: Witherbark Village
317.description: Witherbark Village is a forest troll village built around a small lake in the southeastern Arathi Highlands, belonging to the Witherbark tribe. The village includes a large cave, and the trolls have made a loose alliance with the nearby Boulderfist ogres against the forces of Stromgarde. Together, they have even seized a section of Stromgarde itself. The village is a dangerous place, decorated with skulls and totems.

318.name: Drywhisker Gorge
318.description: Drywhisker Gorge is a gorge cutting through the mountains in the eastern Arathi Highlands, northeast of Hammerfall. At its end lies a cave, the only known source of a rare type of bloodstone ore, inhabited by the Drywhisker kobolds. It is said that a mysterious stone shard lies deep within the cave, holding a fragment of some ancient power. The gorge is narrow and rocky, and the kobolds guard it jealously.

320.name: Refuge Pointe
320.description: Refuge Pointe is all that remains of the once-great kingdom of Stromgarde, a fortified encampment on a rocky rise in the central Arathi Highlands. When Stromgarde fell to the Syndicate and the ogres, most of the populace fled south, but the proud remnants of Stromgarde's army stayed behind, determined to fight on and reclaim their land. Led by Prince Galen Trollbane, they conduct the Alliance's military operations in the region from here, aided by the League of Arathor. The outpost is a practical camp of tents and palisades, with a gryphon roost connecting it to other Alliance holdings.

321.name: Hammerfall
321.description: Hammerfall is a fortified Horde outpost in the eastern Arathi Highlands, built on the site of one of the largest orc internment camps from after the Second War. Thrall and his followers attacked and destroyed the camp to free the orcs held captive there, and it was during this liberation that the great Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer fell, struck down by a human knight. The Horde later reoccupied the ruins and named the outpost Hammerfall in his honor. Today it serves as the Horde's forward base in the highlands, with an inn, wind riders, and the camp of the Defilers, who battle the League of Arathor in Arathi Basin. The outpost is guarded by orc grunts and protected by high palisades.

324.name: Stromgarde Keep
324.description: Stromgarde Keep is the ruined capital of the kingdom of Stromgarde, lying in the southwest of the Arathi Highlands. In ancient times it was Strom, the capital of the Empire of Arathor and the birthplace of human magic, and later the seat of the Trollbane kings. After the Third War, the city was overrun and left in ruins, and now it is divided into three warring sections: the inner keep held by the Syndicate, the former mage district held by the Boulderfist ogres and Witherbark trolls, and a last section held by the soldiers of Stromgarde. The city is a battleground of guerrilla warfare, its walls broken, its streets filled with rubble, and its towers crumbling. The soldiers of Stromgarde dream of the day they will reclaim their capital.

325.name: The Tower of Arathor
325.description: The Tower of Arathor is an ancient wizard's tower within the ruins of Stromgarde Keep, once dedicated to the study of the arcane arts by the mages of Arathor, among the first human magi in history. Since the fall of Stromgarde, it has been taken over by the Boulderfist ogres, and the magical defenses installed by its former masters still linger in its halls. The tower is a reminder of the ancient glory of human magic.

326.name: The Sanctum
326.description: The Sanctum is the inner heart of Stromgarde Keep, the ruined capital of the kingdom of Stromgarde in the southwestern Arathi Highlands. Once the seat of the Trollbane kings and their court, it now lies within the part of the city held by the Syndicate, who have made it one of their strongholds. Its grand halls are cracked and dusty, and the banners of the Trollbanes have been torn down. The soldiers of Stromgarde long to reclaim it.

327.name: Faldir's Cove
327.description: Faldir's Cove is a small natural harbor on the southern shores of the Arathi Highlands, near the Drowned Reef. An expedition of the Blackwater Raiders, the pirates of Booty Bay, came here in search of ancient elven treasure said to be hidden in the reef, but a mysterious tide wrecked two of their three ships, leaving the surviving crew stranded in the cove. The cove is sheltered and beautiful, with clear water and rocky cliffs, but the naga of the reef make it dangerous.

328.name: The Drowned Reef
328.description: The Drowned Reef is a dangerous reef off the southern shores of the Arathi Highlands, where many ships have found their last harbor. Beneath the waters of the bay lie the ruins of an ancient installation of the earthen, now inhabited by the naga of the Daggerspine tribe. The naga seem to be able to control the tides of the bay, dooming many hapless crews who try to find refuge in Faldir's Cove. The reef is beautiful and treacherous, with clear water and sharp rocks.

333.name: Circle of East Binding
333.description: The Circle of East Binding is one of the four ancient stone circles in the Arathi Highlands, lying in the eastern part of the region near Hammerfall. Its tall standing stones are guarded by water elementals, and it is said that the circles together hold some ancient and powerful entity imprisoned. The air around the circle feels strangely heavy, and the elementals attack anyone who approaches.

334.name: Circle of West Binding
334.description: The Circle of West Binding is one of the four ancient stone circles in the Arathi Highlands, lying in the western part of the region near Thoradin's Wall. It is guarded by fire elementals, and like the other circles, it is said to be part of an ancient binding that keeps some powerful entity imprisoned. The stones are scorched and blackened, and the air shimmers with heat.

335.name: Circle of Inner Binding
335.description: The Circle of Inner Binding is one of the four ancient stone circles in the Arathi Highlands, lying in the southern part of the region near Stromgarde. It is guarded by earth elementals, and it is said to be part of an ancient binding that keeps some powerful entity imprisoned. A strange shard within the circle is rumored to whisper to those who come near.

336.name: Circle of Outer Binding
336.description: The Circle of Outer Binding is one of the four ancient stone circles in the Arathi Highlands, lying in the central part of the region near Refuge Pointe. It is guarded by air elementals, and like the other circles, it is said to be part of an ancient binding that keeps some powerful entity imprisoned. The wind howls constantly around its standing stones.

880.name: Thandol Span
880.description: On the Arathi side, the great dwarven Thandol Span stretches south from the highlands across the deep sea channel toward the Wetlands and Khaz Modan. The bridge has been badly damaged, first by the Scourge in the Third War and more recently by the Dark Iron dwarves, and one of its spans lies all but destroyed. The road from the bridge leads north into the highlands, and the roar of the waves crashing far below fills the air.

1857.name: Thoradin's Wall
1857.description: On the Arathi side, Thoradin's Wall marks the western edge of the highlands, a great stone wall built in ancient times by King Thoradin to protect the Empire of Arathor. It once symbolized humanity's strength and defensive might, but now it has fallen to decay and war, collapsed and gaping wide. The main road from the highlands passes through its broken gate into the Hillsbrad Foothills.

1858.name: Boulder'gor
1858.description: Boulder'gor is a hill north of Stromgarde Keep in the Arathi Highlands, where forest trolls and ogres of the Boulderfist tribe gather. The ogres have carved an outpost into the hillside, and the trolls and ogres together threaten the soldiers of Stromgarde. The hill is rocky and barren, and the ogres' crude huts and fires dot its slopes.

2401.name: The Forbidding Sea
2401.description: The waters of the Forbidding Sea lie beyond the eastern mountains of the Arathi Highlands, cold and grey under the overcast sky. The mountains prevent easy access to the coast, and the waters are rough and rarely sailed. Seabirds circle above the waves, and the wind carries the smell of salt over the cliffs.

45.description: The Arathi Highlands are a region of grassy, craggy uplands in southeastern Lordaeron, lying east of the Hillsbrad Foothills, south of the Hinterlands, and north of the great canyon that separates Lordaeron from the Wetlands. It is the cradle of human civilization, for here King Thoradin founded the Empire of Arathor and built its capital, Strom, and here humans and high elves first allied against the Amani trolls, as the elves taught the first human mages the arcane arts. After the empire faded, the stubborn families who remained founded the kingdom of Stromgarde, ruled by the Trollbane family, whose soldiers fought with distinction in the Second War. Stromgarde survived the plague of undeath but was later overrun by the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogres, and its remaining army now holds out at Refuge Pointe under Prince Galen Trollbane, fighting to reclaim their ruined capital. The Horde has taken over the former internment camp of Hammerfall, where Orgrim Doomhammer fell during the liberation of the orcs, and now holds it as a forward base. The highlands are a grey, windswept land of rolling grass, rocky outcrops, and scattered farms, with a cold and bleak western coast. Ogres, forest trolls, kobolds, raptors, and spiders roam the land, and ancient stone circles of binding, guarded by elementals, are said to hold some unknown entity imprisoned. The entrance to Arathi Basin, where the League of Arathor and the Defilers battle for the region's resources, lies in the heart of the highlands.

46.name: Burning Steppes

249.name: Dreadmaul Rock
249.description: Dreadmaul Rock is a massive rocky stronghold in the eastern Burning Steppes, the base of operations for the Fire-Gut ogres. It is a large structure with paths winding to its summit and a complicated cave system within, all crawling with ogre warriors and magi. The ogres seek to claim the Burning Steppes as their own, and they fight against the orcs, dwarves, and dragons who also covet the land. The rock was once known as Fire-Gut Rock, after the tribe that dwells there, and it remains one of the most formidable ogre strongholds in the Eastern Kingdoms.

250.name: Ruins of Thaurissan
250.description: The Ruins of Thaurissan are what remains of the ancient capital of the Dark Iron dwarves, which once stood proudly in a lush expanse of land that is now the Burning Steppes. Named after the sorcerer-thane Thaurissan, the city was destroyed in a gigantic explosion when he attempted to summon the Firelord Ragnaros to aid his people in their war against the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans. The blast reduced the city to rubble and the surrounding lands to an ashy wasteland. The surviving Dark Irons retreated into the newly born Blackrock Mountain, where they rebuilt their city in service to Ragnaros. Today the ruins are a haunted place of broken stone and scorched earth, and it is said that relics found among them carry visions of the city's terrible destruction.

251.name: Flame Crest
251.description: Flame Crest is a small camp on a rocky crest in the northeastern Burning Steppes, overlooking the volcanic wasteland. It is run by enterprising goblins who offer their goods and services to anyone who can pay, though the camp also hosts a Horde wind rider master and serves as a waypoint for Horde travelers in the region. A small cave provides shelter from the heat and the dangers of the steppes, and travelers of many races and loyalties can be found resting here. Despite its proximity to the black dragonflight and the Blackrock orcs, Flame Crest maintains an uneasy neutrality.

252.name: Blackrock Stronghold
252.description: Blackrock Stronghold is a massive fortress in the northern Burning Steppes, just outside Blackrock Spire, controlled by the Blackrock clan of orcs. Its dark walls, spiked palisades, and watchtowers loom over the volcanic landscape, and its warriors are savage holdouts of the old Horde who reject Thrall's leadership and the truce he made. The orcs here serve the black dragon Nefarian, who rules from the heights of the spire, and they mine the surrounding mountains for metals to forge weapons and armor. The stronghold is a constant threat to anyone traveling through the region.

253.name: The Pillar of Ash
253.description: The Pillar of Ash is a group of orcish structures near the middle of the Burning Steppes, dominated by a tall tower filled with hostile Blackrock orcs. Nearby stands a huge statue of a human hero, widely believed to mark the spot where the great Alliance commander Anduin Lothar fell in battle at the end of the Second War. The site is a place of grim history, where the blackened earth seems to remember the bloodshed of that war. The orcs who garrison the tower keep a watchful eye on the road and attack any who approach.

254.name: Blackrock Mountain
254.description: On the northern edge of the Burning Steppes, the land rises toward the immense dark mass of Blackrock Mountain, a volcano born from the summoning of the Firelord Ragnaros. From the steppes, a path climbs toward the mountain's entrance, passing the fortifications of the Blackrock orcs. The mountain looms over the entire region, its peak wreathed in smoke and its slopes glowing with rivers of lava. Within, Ragnaros and his Dark Iron servants war endlessly against the black dragon Nefarian and his minions for control of the mountain.

255.name: Altar of Storms
255.description: The Altar of Storms in the Burning Steppes is one of the few remaining altars from the Second War, when orc warlocks of the Horde created such structures to grant intelligence and magical powers to their ogre allies, turning them into ogre magi. The altars were carved from the corrupted power of the great Runestone at Caer Darrow. This one stands cracked and scarred in the shadow of Blackrock Spire, but its remaining energies still draw elementals and ogre magi to the area. The Blackrock orcs perform strange rituals at the altar, and the air around it crackles with dark magic.

2417.name: Blackrock Pass
2417.description: Blackrock Pass is the narrow passage leading from the Redridge Mountains into the Burning Steppes, guarded by a massive iron gate set into the mountains. Some call it the Gates of Hell, for those who pass through leave behind the green, peaceful lands of the human kingdom and enter the scorched, twisted ruin of the steppes. The air grows hot and acrid as one approaches, and the red glow of the volcanic land beyond can be seen through the gate. The pass is a dangerous place, for the creatures and warriors of the Burning Steppes are among the most formidable in the Eastern Kingdoms.

2418.name: Morgan's Vigil
2418.description: Morgan's Vigil is a small Alliance outpost in the southeastern corner of the Burning Steppes, built among the ruins of a village that was burned to the ground. Its houses and watchtower lie in charred ruins, and its defenders live in tents among the rubble, keeping watch over the steppes and the road to Redridge. Despite its battered state, the outpost is a vital foothold for the Alliance in this hostile land, and gryphons connect it to Stormwind and the other Alliance holdings. Its soldiers and agents keep a close watch on Blackrock Mountain and the threats it harbors.

2419.name: Slither Rock
2419.description: Slither Rock is a small, secluded cave in the far northeastern corner of the Burning Steppes, hidden beyond the dragon-infested Terror Wing Path. It is rumored to shelter a solitary dragonspawn of the black dragonflight, who has chosen to dwell apart from his kin. The cave is dark and warm, its walls blackened by heat, and few have reason or courage to seek it out.

2420.name: Terror Wing Path
2420.description: Terror Wing Path is a long valley in the eastern Burning Steppes, home to many whelps and dragonkin of the black dragonflight. Black drakes patrol the skies above, and magma giants are said to wander through the valley on occasion. The path is one of the most dangerous places in the steppes, and only the mightiest warriors dare to travel through it, and never alone. The valley is a scorched, desolate place, its rocks blackened by dragonfire and its air heavy with smoke.

2421.name: Draco'dar
2421.description: Draco'dar is a region of scorched hills in the southwestern Burning Steppes, crawling with the minions of the black dragonflight. Dragonspawn, whelps, and drakes roam the area, and the land bears the scars of their fiery breath. The hills are barren and blackened, and the air shimmers with heat. Travelers are advised not to enter the area alone, for the black dragonkin attack anyone they encounter.

46.description: The Burning Steppes are a scorched, volcanic land lying south of Blackrock Mountain and north of the Redridge Mountains, the only land passage between the Kingdom of Stormwind and the dwarven lands of Khaz Modan and beyond. Once part of the green Redridge Mountains, the region was devastated centuries ago when the Dark Iron sorcerer-thane Thaurissan summoned the Firelord Ragnaros, an event that destroyed the Dark Iron capital, melted mountains, and raised the volcano of Blackrock Mountain. Today the land is a rugged expanse of charred earth, craggy foothills, scattered boulders, and rivers of lava. The sky glows red from the eruptions of the mountain, ash drifts through the air, and the weather is perpetually hot and dry. Now virtually abandoned by Stormwind, the steppes are controlled by the minions of the black dragonflight and the agents of Ragnaros. The Blackrock orcs, savage holdouts of the old Horde who reject Thrall's leadership, maintain settlements and fortifications around the volcano and mine the mountains for metal. Fire-Gut ogres hold their stronghold in the east, black dragons and their spawn roam the southern and eastern hills, and Dark Iron dwarves guard the ruins of their ancient capital. At the end of the Second War, the great Alliance commander Anduin Lothar fell at the foot of Blackrock Spire, slain by Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. The Alliance maintains a small, embattled outpost at Morgan's Vigil, while a neutral goblin-run camp at Flame Crest serves those of the Horde.

47.name: The Hinterlands

307.name: The Overlook Cliffs
307.description: The Overlook Cliffs are a set of steep, towering cliffs in the eastern Hinterlands, marking a dramatic drop from the mountainous highlands down to the shoreline of the Forbidding Sea. The great river that runs through the Hinterlands ends here, plunging over the edge in a massive waterfall. The cliffs are known for their height, and many travelers who underestimated them have fallen to their deaths. The view from the top is breathtaking, stretching far out over the sea.

348.name: Aerie Peak
348.description: Aerie Peak is the capital of the Wildhammer dwarves, a great city carved into an enormous mountainside in the northwestern Hinterlands, overlooking Darrowmere Lake. The mountain has been sculpted into the likeness of a gargantuan gryphon head, with open spaces at its eyes and nostrils, a work of generations so detailed that even individual feathers can be seen. Wildhammer structures and battlements jut from the cliff's base, and gryphons nest in the carved head and circle around it endlessly. Unlike their Ironforge kin, the Wildhammers build their homes above ground with open ceilings to see the sky, and they practice gryphon riding and hammer throwing on the surrounding cliffs. The city is ruled by High Thane Falstad Wildhammer, and its people are fierce, proud, and loyal to their friends. High elves and other allies also live here.

349.name: Wildhammer Keep
349.description: Wildhammer Keep is the great keep at the heart of Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands, maintained by the Wildhammer dwarves. It serves as the city's inn and gathering hall, where dwarves, high elves, and travelers come to rest, eat, and drink. The keep is built in the open-air style of the Wildhammers, with high ceilings and views of the sky, and its halls are lively with song, laughter, and the cries of gryphons outside.

350.name: Quel'Danil Lodge
350.description: The Quel'Danil Lodge is a high elven hunting lodge in the western Hinterlands, near Aerie Peak, the larger of the two remaining high elf outposts in Lordaeron. The lodge acts as an embassy of sorts, through which the high elves maintain their diplomatic relations with other races, and they have struck an alliance with the Wildhammer dwarves against their common enemies, the forest trolls. Several hundred high elves live in the Hinterlands, some here and others in Aerie Peak. The lodge is built in the graceful style of Quel'Thalas, and its name means High Peak in the Thalassian tongue.

351.name: Skulk Rock
351.description: Skulk Rock is an ancient forest troll ruin in the Hinterlands, now infested with slimes and oozes. A cave lies within, one of the few places where ghost mushrooms grow. During the Second War, the Horde maintained a base here, but it has long since been abandoned, and only a few forgotten casks remain. The ruin is damp and foul-smelling, its stones covered in slime.

352.name: Zun'watha
352.description: Zun'watha is a forest troll ruin in the Hinterlands, inhabited by trolls of the Witherbark tribe. The ancient stone structures, built in the days of the Amani Empire, are overgrown with vines and moss, and the Witherbark trolls guard them fiercely against intruders.

353.name: Shadra'Alor
353.description: Shadra'Alor is an ancient temple built by the Amani trolls and dedicated to the spider goddess Shadra, now the primary settlement of the Witherbark tribe of forest trolls in the Hinterlands. Its stone platforms and altars are overgrown with jungle vines and covered in webs, and the Witherbark trolls perform their rituals here. The temple is a dark and dangerous place, and the trolls attack any outsiders who come near.

354.name: Jintha'Alor
354.description: Jintha'Alor is the great capital city of the Vilebranch tribe of forest trolls in the Hinterlands, a colossal stepped city built by the Amani Empire, second in size only to the legendary Zul'Aman. Its terraces rise up the mountainside in tiers, crowned by an altar at the summit, and its walls are decorated with troll carvings and totems. The Vilebranch, the strongest of the Hinterlands tribes, guard the city fiercely, and rumors speak of an ancient egg of the blood god Hakkar hidden within. The city is a formidable and dangerous place, and few outsiders who enter leave alive.

355.name: The Altar of Zul
355.description: The Altar of Zul is an ancient forest troll altar in the Hinterlands, held by the Vilebranch tribe. Built atop a stone platform in the days of the Amani Empire, it is a sacred site where the trolls perform their rituals and keep their holy relics. The altar is guarded by the tribe's priests and warriors, and the air around it hums with dark power.

356.name: Seradane
356.description: Seradane is an area in the northeastern Hinterlands, home to an ancient, massive tree that serves as one of the great portals to the Emerald Dream. Many green dragons and dragonspawn of the Dreaming Aspect Ysera make their home here, guarding the portal against intruders. Yet whispers speak of a corruption creeping into the Dream, and it is said that even some of Ysera's servants have been touched by it. The area is lush and mystical, bathed in a strange light, and the dragons attack anyone who comes too close.

1880.name: Featherbeard's Hovel
1880.description: Featherbeard's Hovel is a small house next to Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands, the home of a Wildhammer dwarf known for his love of gryphons. The hovel is cozy and cluttered, with a fireplace, books, and gryphon-related trinkets, but its owner is often away, searching the wilds for gryphon eggs.

1881.name: Shindigger's Camp
1881.description: Shindigger's Camp is a small camp in the western Hinterlands, where a jovial dwarf and a high elf companion have set up their tents. The camp is a cheerful, if somewhat disorderly, place, known for the dwarf's fondness for song and drink.

1882.name: Plaguemist Ravine
1882.description: Plaguemist Ravine is a narrow mountain pathway in the northwestern Hinterlands, leading north toward Caer Darrow in the Western Plaguelands. As its name suggests, a plague-tainted mist drifts through the ravine from the north, a stark contrast to the natural freshness of the rest of the Hinterlands. Few use the path, for it leads toward the undead-infested lands of the Plaguelands.

1883.name: Valorwind Lake
1883.description: Valorwind Lake is a small, peaceful lake in the Hinterlands, surrounded by forest and hills. It is known as the only place where a rare and mysterious violet mushroom grows. Its clear waters reflect the sky and the trees, and wildlife often comes to drink along its shores.

1884.name: Agol'watha
1884.description: Agol'watha is an ancient forest troll ruin in the north-central Hinterlands, once a temple of the Amani Empire and later of the Vilebranch tribe. Now it is overrun by foul animated sludges, and the trolls have abandoned it. The ruin's stones are covered in slime, and the air is thick with a putrid stench.

1885.name: Hiri'watha
1885.description: Hiri'watha is a forest troll village in the Hinterlands, due south of the Quel'Danil Lodge, inhabited by the Witherbark tribe. The village is built among ancient Amani ruins, and the Witherbark trolls guard it fiercely. The high elves of the nearby lodge regard it as a constant threat.

1886.name: The Creeping Ruin
1886.description: The Creeping Ruin is an ancient forest troll ruin in the Hinterlands, overrun by hostile slimes and oozes that creep among the fallen stones, giving the ruin its name. The troll carvings and statues are covered in slime, and the ruin has been abandoned by its former inhabitants.

1887.name: Bogen's Ledge
1887.description: Bogen's Ledge is a cave in the southwestern Hinterlands, home to a troll witch doctor and his monstrous pet spider. The cave is dark and filled with strange totems, herbs, and webs, and its inhabitants are hostile to the dwarves and elves of the region.

1917.name: Shaol'watha
1917.description: Shaol'watha is a forest troll ruin in the northeastern Hinterlands, held by the Vilebranch tribe. Its ancient stone structures, built in the days of the Amani Empire, are overgrown with vines, and the Vilebranch trolls guard them fiercely. The ruin overlooks the coast and the sea beyond.

2400.name: The Forbidding Sea
2400.description: The waters of the Forbidding Sea wash the eastern coast of the Hinterlands, where the land drops sharply from the Overlook Cliffs to the narrow shoreline below. The sea is cold and often rough, and the great river of the Hinterlands pours into it in a massive waterfall. The Revantusk trolls have built their village on the shore, and their boats ply the coastal waters. Seabirds nest on the cliffs, and the sound of crashing waves fills the air.

3317.name: Revantusk Village
3317.description: Revantusk Village is a forest troll village on the eastern coast of the Hinterlands, nestled at the foot of the cliffs by the Forbidding Sea. It is the first permanent settlement of the Revantusk tribe, who wandered as nomads for centuries until emissaries of the Horde came seeking allies and helped them build a home. In return, the Revantusk became staunch allies of the Horde, and they remain bitter enemies of the Wildhammer dwarves and the other troll tribes. The village is built of wood and thatch on stilts above the shore, decorated with troll carvings and totems, and wind riders connect it to the Horde's other holdings.

47.description: The Hinterlands are a wild, mountainous region in the northern Eastern Kingdoms, lying east of the Alterac Mountains, north of the Arathi Highlands, and bordered by the sea to the east. It is a land of lush forests, rolling hills, deep valleys, rushing rivers, and steep cliffs, untouched by the plague that ravaged Lordaeron, and its climate is mild and green. The Hinterlands were once the heart of the Amani Empire of the forest trolls, and the colossal ruins of their cities still stand among the trees. After the War of the Three Hammers, the Wildhammer dwarves came here and built the city of Aerie Peak, carved into a mountainside in the shape of a great gryphon head; they live above ground, practice shamanism, and are famed for their bond with the wild gryphons of the region, which they ride into battle. High Thane Falstad Wildhammer rules them. The forest trolls remain, divided into three tribes: the powerful Vilebranch, who hold the great city of Jintha'Alor; the Witherbark, who dwell among the temples of Shadra'Alor; and the Revantusk, who have allied with the Horde and built a village on the eastern coast. A small community of high elves lives at the Quel'Danil Lodge near Aerie Peak. In the north, the ancient tree of Seradane serves as a gateway to the Emerald Dream, guarded by the green dragonflight, though whispers speak of a growing corruption there. Wolves, bears, gryphons, owlbeasts, and oozes roam the land.

51.name: Searing Gorge

246.name: The Cauldron
246.description: The Cauldron is an enormous excavation in the center of the Searing Gorge, a vast rift carved into the blackened earth and rimmed by the giant digging machines of the Dark Iron clan. Within its depths, Dark Iron overseers drive their slaves, captured dwarves, gnolls, and others, to work the pits without rest under the oppressive heat. Many of the laborers have been driven mad by the grueling work and the cruelty of their masters, and they attack anyone who interferes with their toil, even would-be liberators. Fire and magma elementals roam the fiery crevices at the bottom of the pit. What exactly the Dark Irons are digging for remains a mystery, though many suspect they seek ancient artifacts of the titans or something even darker.

247.name: Grimesilt Dig Site
247.description: Grimesilt Dig Site is a mining excavation in the Searing Gorge that was originally worked by a dwarven crew before being commandeered by the Dark Iron dwarves. The Dark Irons now dig through the site for their own purposes, and the remains of the original crew's camp and equipment lie scattered among the ash and rock. The pit is surrounded by smoldering earth, and the Dark Iron guards attack any intruders on sight.

1442.name: Firewatch Ridge
1442.description: Firewatch Ridge is a high ridge in the western Searing Gorge overlooking the great excavation of the Cauldron, where the Dark Iron dwarves have established their main camp in the region. Dark Iron soldiers, sorcerers, and overseers garrison its fortifications, along with mechanical war golems and giant flame spiders that crawl among the rocks. Rumors speak of cultists of the Twilight's Hammer hidden in a cave in the northwestern part of the ridge. The ridge is one of the most dangerous places in the gorge, and its fires burn day and night, visible from across the wasteland.

1443.name: The Slag Pit
1443.description: The Slag Pit lies deep within the Cauldron in the Searing Gorge, an underground mining complex rich in many types of ore. It is run by cruel Dark Iron overseers and worked by their enslaved laborers, who toil in sweltering tunnels lit by the glow of molten rock. In the deepest reaches of the pit dwell ravenous incendosaurs, fiery lizards that thrive in the heat. The Dark Irons are fiercely protective of their mining operations, and few who enter the Slag Pit uninvited ever leave.

1444.name: The Sea of Cinders
1444.description: The Sea of Cinders is a broad, flat stretch of scorched land in the southern Searing Gorge, just north of Blackrock Mountain. Ravaged by fire and wind, it is an uninhabitable wasteland where cinders and ashes from the still-smoldering ground constantly drift through the air, stinging the eyes and choking the lungs. The ground is cracked and blackened, and the heat rising from it is nearly unbearable. Travelers heading to or from Blackrock Mountain must cross this desolate expanse, and few linger longer than necessary.

1445.name: Blackrock Mountain
1445.description: At the southern edge of the Searing Gorge, the land rises toward the immense volcanic mass of Blackrock Mountain, whose dark slopes loom over the Sea of Cinders. A passage leads from the gorge into the mountain itself, where a great chained platform hangs over a vast lake of molten rock. The mountain is the seat of power of both the Firelord Ragnaros and his Dark Iron servants, and the black dragon Nefarian and his orc minions, who wage an endless war for supremacy within. The heat grows ever more intense as one approaches, and the rumble of the volcano can be felt underfoot.

1446.name: Thorium Point
1446.description: Thorium Point is a fortified town on a mesa on the northern edge of the Searing Gorge, the center of operations for the Thorium Brotherhood, a guild of master Dark Iron craftsmen who broke away from their clan and its servitude to Ragnaros. Part fortress and part workshop, it is renowned for the skill of its smiths, who work with the rare metals and fiery materials found in the gorge. Though ample resources lie just outside its gates, the Brotherhood keeps a constant vigil against attacks by Dark Iron dwarves, elementals, and wild beasts. Despite its high security, Thorium Point is neutral and open for business to anyone, Alliance or Horde, who can brave the hostile landscape to reach it, and gryphons and wind riders alike land at its roost.

1957.name: Blackchar Cave
1957.description: Blackchar Cave is a mysterious, sealed-off cave in the southern Searing Gorge, near Blackrock Mountain. Its entrance is blocked, and no one knows for certain what lies within. The cave is surrounded by scorched rock and drifting ash, and some claim that the shape of the surrounding rocks resembles a face when seen from above. Many tales are told of what might be hidden in its depths, but none have been proven.

1958.name: Tanner Camp
1958.description: Tanner Camp is a small, isolated camp in the Searing Gorge, home to a skilled leatherworker who has made a life among the harsh, fiery wastes. The camp consists of a single tent surrounded by drying hides and tanning racks, and it is a rare sight of peaceful industry in the hostile land. Behind the camp, a long, sprawling passageway leads into the mountains, where a fearsome thunder lizard is said to dwell.

1959.name: Dustfire Valley
1959.description: Dustfire Valley is a windswept valley in the northeastern Searing Gorge that leads north to the locked gates of the Stonewrought Pass and the Valley of Kings in Loch Modan beyond. Hot winds carrying ash and dust blow constantly through the valley, and the ground is cracked and scorched. The Dark Iron dwarves keep a watch over the area, and the sealed gates at its northern end are a reminder of the day the dwarves of Ironforge abandoned the gorge to the Dark Irons.

2838.name: Stonewrought Pass
2838.description: The Stonewrought Pass is a tunnel leading from the Searing Gorge northeast to the Valley of Kings in Loch Modan, at the northern end of Dustfire Valley. It was designed by the same master architect responsible for the Stonewrought Dam and other great works of dwarven stonework in the Eastern Kingdoms. When the Dark Iron dwarves overran the Searing Gorge, the dwarves of Ironforge retreated through the pass and sealed it behind them, and today it is closed by locked gates guarded on the Loch Modan side by dwarven mountaineers. The tunnel is dark and stifling, and the heat of the gorge can be felt seeping through its stones.

51.description: The Searing Gorge is a volcanic wasteland in southern Khaz Modan, lying between the Badlands and Loch Modan to the north and east and Blackrock Mountain to the south. It was once part of the green Redridge Mountains, but centuries ago, when the Dark Iron sorcerer-thane Thaurissan summoned the Firelord Ragnaros, the tremendous explosion shattered the land and turned it into a blackened, smoldering ruin. Today the gorge is a place of ash, cinders, and scorched rock, with rivers of lava, choking fumes, and a sky darkened by smoke; the air is hot and dry, and fire and magma elementals roam the land. The region is dominated by the Dark Iron dwarves, who invaded after their capital was destroyed and overran the dwarven garrisons, forcing the dwarves of Ironforge to retreat to Loch Modan and seal the passage behind them. At the heart of the gorge lies the Cauldron, a gigantic excavation worked by enslaved captives under the cruel whips of the Dark Irons, who dig for unknown treasures. Not all Dark Irons serve Ragnaros, however: the Thorium Brotherhood, a guild of master craftsmen who broke away from their clan, has established the neutral town of Thorium Point on the northern edge of the gorge, open to all who can reach it. The gorge is accessible from Loch Modan through the locked Stonewrought Pass, from the Badlands through a narrow pass cut by the Horde, and through Blackrock Mountain to the south.

65.name: Dragonblight

4151.name: Westwind Refugee Camp
4151.description: Westwind Refugee Camp is a small taunka camp in the western Dragonblight, where the villagers of Taunka'le Village in the Borean Tundra gathered after learning that their capital, Icemist Village, had fallen to the Scourge. The few survivors of Icemist found their way here too, and the refugees, weary but unbroken, await the chance to strike back.

4152.name: Moa'ki Harbor
4152.description: Moa'ki Harbor is a tuskarr port in the south-central Dragonblight and the largest settlement left to the tuskarr since they lost their capital, Kaskala, to the kvaldir. The sky above the harbor is always fluttering with brightly colored kites, even in troubled times, and it is a lively place of trade, friendly conversation, and storytelling. Giant sea turtles carry passengers from its docks to Kamagua in the Howling Fjord and Unu'pe in the Borean Tundra.

4153.name: Indu'le Village
4153.description: Indu'le Village was a tuskarr village northwest of Moa'ki Harbor in the Dragonblight, built around Lake Indu'le. It was destroyed by chaotic arcane energies pouring out of the ley lines that the blue dragonflight is manipulating nearby. Many of the Kalu'ak tuskarr who lived here were killed outright and now linger as ghosts, and the survivors have been driven mad.

4154.name: Snowfall Glade
4154.description: Snowfall Glade is a snowy glade bordering Indu'le Village to the east in the southwestern Dragonblight, home to the Snowfall tribe of wolvar.

4155.name: The Half Shell
4155.description: The Half Shell is a giant sea turtle moored in Moa'ki Harbor in the Dragonblight, one of the great living boats the tuskarr use to travel between their villages along Northrend's southern coast.

4156.name: Surge Needle
4156.description: The Surge Needle is a floating arcane construct of the blue dragonflight hovering over Moonrest Gardens in the Dragonblight, one of the colossal machines Malygos has ordered placed over ley line clusters. Blue dragonflight sorcerers on its platform and on the ground below focus its power, and raw arcane beings are born from its energies.

4157.name: Moonrest Gardens
4157.description: Moonrest Gardens are a collection of ancient Highborne ruins southwest of Stars' Rest in the Dragonblight, including what seems to have been a temple of Elune. The blue dragonflight has recently invaded the ruins, attempting to redirect the potent ley lines that lie beneath them, and their destructive methods have awakened long-dormant Highborne spirits. A surge needle floats above the gardens.

4158.name: Stars' Rest
4158.description: Stars' Rest is a small night elf camp of the Alliance built within ancient ruins in the southwestern Dragonblight, south of Icemist Village. A moonwell glows at its heart, and frost nymphs have come from the nearby forest to aid the night elves.

4160.name: Lothalor Woodlands
4160.description: The Lothalor Woodlands are a forest in the southwestern corner of the Dragonblight, just west of Indu'le Village. The arcane energies poured out by the blue dragonflight's ley line focus here have ravaged the land, and the ancients of the forest have been driven insane.

4161.name: Wyrmrest Temple
4161.description: Wyrmrest Temple is an ancient titan structure in the center of the Dragonblight, towering above the Dragon Wastes in tier after tier of white columns and golden domes. Legends say it was built by the titans shortly after Azeroth's creation as a sanctuary where the newly created dragonflights could meet and watch over the world, and a symbol of their unity. The temple is the seat of the Wyrmrest Accord, the alliance of red, bronze, green, and blue dragons that Alexstrasza the Life-Binder has formed to oppose Malygos and his blue flight in the Nexus War and to fight the Scourge.

4163.name: Icemist Village
4163.description: Icemist Village was the capital of the taunka and the greatest of their villages, decorated with the tusks and skulls of mammoths and standing on the edge of Lake Wintergrasp in the western Dragonblight. A fissure into Azjol-Nerub opened nearby, and undead nerubians of the Scourge poured out, razing the village, killing most of its people, and taking their High Chieftain, Roanauk Icemist, captive. Today it lies in ruins.

4164.name: The Pit of Narjun
4164.description: The Pit of Narjun is a large sinkhole in the western Dragonblight, just south of the ruined taunka capital of Icemist Village. It was through this gaping hole that the Scourge's undead nerubians emerged to overrun Icemist, and it is one of several entrances to Azjol-Nerub and the Old Kingdom, a vast network of caverns extending beneath half of Northrend. Pools of strange black blood fill its depths, and the last free nerubians are said to make their stand here.

4165.name: Agmar's Hammer
4165.description: Agmar's Hammer is the main Horde stronghold in the Dragonblight, a well-fortified base of the Kor'kron led by Overlord Agmar, built in the new, more aggressive style of Horde architecture. It stands on the doorstep of Icemist Village, and its barracks serve as the local inn. Taunka refugees and orphans have found shelter within its walls.

4166.name: Lake Indu'le
4166.description: Lake Indu'le is the lake at the center of Indu'le Village in the Dragonblight. Chaotic arcane magic leaked out of it, caused by the blue dragonflight's actions to the west, and killed most of the tuskarr who lived around its shores. Corrupted creatures now swim in its waters.

4167.name: Obsidian Dragonshrine
4167.description: The Obsidian Dragonshrine is the dragonshrine of the black dragonflight at the base of a volcano in the northwestern Dragonblight. It is as barren and blasted as the Ruby Dragonshrine is lush: its skeletal trees burn perpetually and magma surges just beneath the skin of the land. Its place at the foot of a volcano reflects the black flight's ancient duty as wardens of the earth, while its constant smoldering reflects their destructive nature. The Scourge has invaded the shrine.

4168.name: Ruby Dragonshrine
4168.description: The Ruby Dragonshrine is the resting place of the red dragonflight, an island of greenery and life in the snow-blasted wastes of the western Dragonblight, befitting a flight whose domain is the fire that gives both life and death. It is said to have formed when a single drop of Alexstrasza's blood struck the snows, melted through, and grew into the Crimson Oak that stands at its center. The Scourge has attacked the shrine, and red dragons fight to defend it.

4169.name: Fordragon Hold
4169.description: Fordragon Hold is an Alliance fortress at the base of Angrathar the Wrathgate in the northern Dragonblight, built of stone with cannon towers and a guard tower. It was raised as the Alliance's staging point for the assault on the Wrathgate and the Lich King's citadel beyond.

4170.name: Kor'kron Vanguard
4170.description: The Kor'kron Vanguard is a Horde fortress at the base of Angrathar the Wrathgate in the northern Dragonblight, a single tower with a burrow, armed with catapults and blade throwers. It was raised by the Kor'kron, the elite warriors of the Horde, as the Horde's staging point for the assault on the Wrathgate.

4171.name: The Court of Skulls
4171.description: The Court of Skulls is the open ground before Angrathar the Wrathgate in the northern Dragonblight, the killing field where the Lich King's undead armies mass to defend the gate against any army that marches on Icecrown.

4172.name: Angrathar the Wrathgate
4172.description: Angrathar the Wrathgate is the barred entrance to Icecrown in the northwestern Dragonblight, a towering wall of saronite knife-edges guarding the way to the Lich King's citadel. The Alliance and the Horde have each built a fortress at its foot, for any campaign to storm Icecrown from the south must first break this gate.

4173.name: Galakrond's Rest
4173.description: Galakrond's Rest is a massive boneyard in the Dragon Wastes of the Dragonblight, where a skeleton far larger than any dragon to darken Azeroth's skies in living memory lies half-emerged from the ice. These are the bones of Galakrond, the monstrous proto-dragon known as the progenitor of dragonkind, who fell here in ancient times. Nearby, the five proto-dragons who defeated him were made into the Dragon Aspects. The Scourge and the Cult of the Damned seek to dig him up and raise him as a frost wyrm.

4174.name: The Wicked Coil
4174.description: The Wicked Coil is a small pillar of rock just north of Galakrond's Rest in the Dragonblight, shaped like a coil when seen from above. A grand necrolord of the Scourge has made it his perch.

4175.name: Bronze Dragonshrine
4175.description: The Bronze Dragonshrine is the shrine of the bronze dragonflight, a sandy, crater-like area northwest of Wintergarde Keep in the Dragonblight, where Nozdormu the Timeless One himself is said to keep vigil among the dead. It is an impossibly warm oasis of ever-shifting sand amid the chill of the Dragonblight, as if it were a preserved pocket of a time when Northrend's climate was sunny and warm, or a piece of a future yet to come. A time storm shrouds the shrine, and the mysterious infinite dragonflight fights its defenders for control of it.

4176.name: The Mirror of Dawn
4176.description: The Mirror of Dawn is a frozen lake east of Wyrmrest Temple in the Dragonblight, its icy surface haunted by ice revenants.

4177.name: Wintergarde Keep
4177.description: Wintergarde Keep is the main Alliance stronghold in the Dragonblight and the headquarters of the 7th Legion, built on high ground behind strong walls and cannon towers. It was raised after the Alliance arrived in Northrend and was welcomed by the people of the old Wintergarde Village below. The keep proved enough of a thorn in the Lich King's side that he brought his most notorious necropolis, Naxxramas, from Stratholme to hover in the skies outside its walls, and the Scourge has overrun the surrounding village and lays siege to the keep.

4178.name: Wintergarde Mine
4178.description: Wintergarde Mine is a mine next to Wintergarde Keep in the Dragonblight, once worked by the 7th Legion. The Scourge overran it, raising the miners within, shortly after a strange, dark ore was found in its depths.

4179.name: Emerald Dragonshrine
4179.description: The Emerald Dragonshrine is the dragonshrine of the green dragonflight, a green valley west of New Hearthglen along the southern coast of the Dragonblight. It is the only dragonshrine not ravaged by the Scourge, protected by powerful plant guardians grown from enchanted seeds. A transparent image of Ysera, the Dreamer, rests at its center among the bones of the green dragons' ancestors, while its guardians, troubled and confused, attack anyone not of the green flight.

4180.name: New Hearthglen
4180.description: New Hearthglen is the great fortress of the Scarlet Onslaught, the remnant of the Scarlet Crusade that has come to Northrend to wage its campaign against the Scourge and anyone else who opposes it. It stands near where the Scarlet fleet made landfall on the southeastern coast of the Dragonblight and was built in record time despite the Scourge and the bitter cold. Reinforced stone walls with menacing ballistae surround barracks, houses, stables, a lumber mill, an abbey, and several churches, culminating in a massive white cathedral, and the Scarlet fleet lies docked in its harbor.

4181.name: Crusader's Landing
4181.description: Crusader's Landing is the beach just south of New Hearthglen in the Dragonblight, where the Scarlet Onslaught made landfall after fleeing the Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands. The Onslaught's flagship is moored here.

4182.name: Sinner's Folly
4182.description: The Sinner's Folly is a ship moored at Crusader's Landing, south of New Hearthglen in the Dragonblight, the flagship that carried the Scarlet Onslaught's leader to Northrend in its flight from the Scarlet Enclave.

4183.name: Azure Dragonshrine
4183.description: The Azure Dragonshrine is the cavernous dragonshrine of the blue dragonflight, south of Wyrmrest Temple and just west of the Path of the Titans in the Dragonblight. Since the start of the Nexus War, Malygos has been diverting Azeroth's ley lines to the shrine to empower his flight's dragons, tearing at the fabric of reality, while the Scourge seeks to raise the bones of the blue dragons buried here.

4184.name: Path of the Titans
4184.description: The Path of the Titans is a massive, ancient road, now ruined, that runs through the center of the Dragonblight. It is said to stretch from Ulduar in the Storm Peaks across Crystalsong Forest and down through the Dragonblight to Wyrmrest Temple, continuing south into the Frozen Sea, where carved columns rise from the waves. A cursed titanic watcher is said to walk its length.

4185.name: The Forgotten Shore
4185.description: The Forgotten Shore lies on the far southeastern edge of the Dragonblight, between New Hearthglen and the Dragonspine Tributary. The shore is perpetually shrouded in mist, its bay choked with the rotting wrecks of ships and its sands littered with shattered, wind-worn wood. It was here that Prince Arthas made his main encampment when he came to Northrend to hunt the dreadlord Mal'Ganis, and here that he burned his own ships to keep his army from returning home. The ghosts of his soldiers still wander the beach, bound to the place of their betrayal.

4186.name: Venomspite
4186.description: Venomspite is a Forsaken town in the eastern Dragonblight, built in the same dark, gothic style as Vengeance Landing, where the Royal Apothecary Society continues its plague experiments against the Scourge. It lies south of the Carrion Fields and the necropolis of Naxxramas.

4187.name: The Crystal Vice
4187.description: The Crystal Vice is a great rend in the ice and snow of the northern Dragonblight, bordering Crystalsong Forest. Like a canyon, it shows how thick the glacier is, with the skeletons of dragons sticking out of its walls. A road runs through it, as it is less treacherous than the glacier above, but travelers must brave the ice giants and the enormous jormungar worms that war within it.

4188.name: The Carrion Fields
4188.description: The Carrion Fields are the front lines of the siege of Wintergarde Keep in the eastern Dragonblight, where thousands of dead lie in the shadow of the necropolis of Naxxramas. The area was once Wintergarde Village, a large, thriving human settlement whose people welcomed the Alliance when it arrived and built the keep. Shortly after, the village was overrun by the Scourge and left in ruins.

4189.name: Onslaught Base Camp
4189.description: The Onslaught Base Camp is a large camp of the Scarlet Onslaught just north of Naxxramas in the Dragonblight, where a scout tower is under construction.

4190.name: Thorson's Post
4190.description: Thorson's Post is a farm on the northeastern edge of the Carrion Fields in the Dragonblight, a holdout amid the Scourge-ravaged land around Wintergarde.

4191.name: Light's Trust
4191.description: Light's Trust is a base camp of the Argent Crusade in the northeastern corner of the Dragonblight, just outside Jintha'kalar, established in an ancient Drakkari temple captured by the crusaders.

4192.name: Frostmourne Cavern
4192.description: Frostmourne Cavern is a cave at the base of the Icecrown Glacier, in the northern Dragonblight, where, it is said, the cursed runeblade Frostmourne once lay on an altar encased in ice, bearing the inscription: "Whomsoever takes up this blade shall wield power eternal. Just as the blade rends flesh, so must power scar the spirit." It was here that Prince Arthas claimed the blade. The ice-rimmed cavern, full of saronite, was given its name by the Scarlet Onslaught, which guards its entrance.

4193.name: Scarlet Point
4193.description: Scarlet Point is an area in the northern Dragonblight, east of the Crystal Vice and directly in front of Frostmourne Cavern, which the Scarlet Onslaught has fortified heavily with scout towers for reasons of its own.

4194.name: Jintha'kalar
4194.description: Jintha'kalar is an area of ruins in the northeastern Dragonblight, just east of Light's Trust. It was an ancient city of the Drakkari trolls before it was sacked by the Scourge, and its people now walk again as undead. A passage leads through it to Zul'Drak.

4195.name: Ice Heart Cavern
4195.description: Ice Heart Cavern is a cave at the northern end of the Crystal Vice in the Dragonblight, full of jormungar worms and the crystalline remains of dead ice giants.

4198.name: Kili'ua's Atoll
4198.description: Kili'ua's Atoll is an atoll just off the coast of the Dragonblight, west of Moa'ki Harbor, the haunt of a gigantic crab.

4223.name: Maw of Neltharion
4223.description: The Maw of Neltharion is a cavern leading into the volcano at the western end of the Obsidian Dragonshrine in the Dragonblight, named after Neltharion the Earth-Warder.

4224.name: The Briny Pinnacle
4224.description: The Briny Pinnacle is a small rocky island just off the coast of the Dragonblight, west of Moa'ki Harbor.

4225.name: Glittering Strand
4225.description: The Glittering Strand is a beach south of Moonrest Gardens in the southwestern Dragonblight, overrun by forces of the blue dragonflight guarding a ley line focus.

4227.name: Dragon's Fall
4227.description: Dragon's Fall is a small Horde camp just west of Galakrond's Rest in the Dragonblight, where the troll hero Rokhan and his dragon hunters make their base.

4230.name: Coldwind Heights
4230.description: Coldwind Heights is an elevated wooded area in the northern Dragonblight, west of the Crystal Vice and east of Angrathar the Wrathgate, home to the Coldwind harpies.

4232.name: Vengeance Pass
4232.description: Vengeance Pass is a path in the eastern Dragonblight running between Venomspite and the Carrion Fields.

4233.name: Dawn's Reach
4233.description: Dawn's Reach is a small Argent Crusade encampment directly south of Naxxramas in the Dragonblight, where riflemen hold the line against the Scourge.

4234.name: Naxxramas
4234.description: Naxxramas is a Scourge necropolis floating above the Carrion Fields in the eastern Dragonblight, the seat of the archlich Kel'Thuzad and a place of torture, suffering, and horrific experiments. It was once a nerubian ziggurat, overrun by the crypt lord Anub'arak and torn from the earth by dark magic, and from it Kel'Thuzad spread the plague across Lordaeron. Having departed the skies of the Eastern Plaguelands, it has returned to Northrend with renewed fury, brought by the Lich King to besiege Wintergarde Keep, and its dark halls are filled with abominations, plagued horrors, death knights, and the frost wyrm Sapphiron.

4241.name: Eldritch Heights
4241.description: The Eldritch Heights are a wooded area on a cliff in the southeastern corner of the Dragonblight, home to the Bloodpaw wolvar village.

4243.name: Wintergarde Crypt
4243.description: The Wintergarde Crypt is a large crypt next to Wintergarde Keep in the Dragonblight, where the remains of nobles and dignitaries who died in Northrend were laid to rest. The Scourge has broken in and raises the dead to join the assault on the keep.

4246.name: Wintergarde Mausoleum
4246.description: The Wintergarde Mausoleum is a mausoleum east of Wintergarde Keep in the Dragonblight, built by humans long ago beneath the old Wintergarde Village and forgotten by the keep's defenders. It became a target of the necromancers of Naxxramas.

4253.name: 7th Legion Front
4253.description: The 7th Legion Front is a small Alliance camp of the 7th Legion beside the Path of the Titans in the Dragonblight.

4254.name: The Dragon Wastes
4254.description: The Dragon Wastes are the icy plain covering much of the central Dragonblight, the ancient graveyard that gives the region its name. A broad stretch of white glacial snow cradles dead dragons of every flight in all stages from flesh to bone, and magnataur roam the wastes on the hunt.

4256.name: Drak'Mar Lake
4256.description: Drak'Mar Lake is a large lake in the eastern Dragonblight, bordering the Grizzly Hills. A small stone ring rises at its center, and legend tells of a maiden who dwells in its waters.

4257.name: Dragonspine Tributary
4257.description: The Dragonspine Tributary is a river that marks the border between the Dragonblight and the Grizzly Hills. It rises in the Drakkari highlands of Zul'Drak, forms a sizable lake in its northern reaches, and flows swiftly south to the sea; despite its name, it is one of the greatest rivers on the continent.

4396.name: Nozzlerust Post
4396.description: Nozzlerust Post is a goblin trading post north of Galakrond's Rest, near the Crystal Vice in the Dragonblight, where goblins trade with all comers and suffer constant raids by the Coldwind harpies.

4414.name: Scarlet Tower
4414.description: The Scarlet Tower is a fully built but empty scout tower of the Scarlet Onslaught at Scarlet Point in the northern Dragonblight.

4478.name: Coldwind Pass
4478.description: Coldwind Pass is a crossing of two bridges spanning a frozen river that connects the Borean Tundra with the Dragonblight.

65.description: The Dragonblight, also called the Great Dragonblight, is the heart of southern Northrend: a vast arctic wasteland of glaring white glaciers, ringed by dense forests and littered with the massive, gleaming bones of perished dragons. It is the place where dragons nearing the end of their lives come to die, and in ancient times it was here that the titans' keepers blessed the five great proto-dragons who had defeated Galakrond, turning them into the Dragon Aspects; the colossal bones of Galakrond still jut from the ice. At its center rises Wyrmrest Temple, a titan-built tower where the dragonflights gather, surrounded by five dragonshrines of the red, bronze, green, blue, and black flights, some of them strange islands of fire, forest, and sand amid the snow. The Dragonblight has known endless strife. The first humans to fall to the Lich King's plague lived here, and Prince Arthas burned his own ships on its shores. Now the Scourge lays siege to the dragonshrines, raising dragon bones into frost wyrms, while the necropolis of Naxxramas hovers over the plains in the east. The blue dragonflight of Malygos tampers with the ley lines beneath the earth, and the Scarlet Onslaught has built a fortress on the southeastern coast. The Alliance and the Horde have both raised fortresses here, above all before Angrathar the Wrathgate, the barred entrance to Icecrown. The tuskarr, taunka, wolvar, magnataur, and the last free nerubians struggle to survive among the bones.

66.name: Zul'Drak

4275.name: The Argent Stand
4275.description: The Argent Stand is the main base of the Argent Crusade in Zul'Drak, built in a Drakkari structure that may once have been an open-air market, its central area serving as an inn. The crusaders chose it as a defensive position to keep the Scourge from taking the second tier of the city; that effort failed, but the crusade has not given up, and it fights on against both the Scourge and the maddened Drakkari.

4276.name: Altar of Sseratus
4276.description: The Altar of Sseratus is a temple directly north of the Argent Stand in Zul'Drak, dedicated to Sseratus, the serpent god. When the Scourge invaded, it was here that the high prophet Slad'ran slew his own god, taking no pleasure in it but believing it might save his home, and swore vengeance on the Scourge for what they had made him do.

4278.name: Drak'Sotra Fields
4278.description: The Drak'Sotra Fields are Drakkari farmlands southwest of Drak'Sotra and just south of the Argent Stand in Zul'Drak, where the trolls cultivate water poppies used for powerful pain-reducing salves. The surviving trolls of Drak'Sotra have retreated here, and Drakkari water binders have summoned water spirits that have run wild across the fields.

4279.name: Drak'Sotra
4279.description: Drak'Sotra is a district of Zul'Drak east of Drak'Agal and west of Kolramas. It was once held by the Argent Crusade, but it was lost soon after the Scourge arrived.

4280.name: Drak'Agal
4280.description: Drak'Agal is a large district of Zul'Drak south of the Amphitheater of Anguish, flooded with putrid, stagnant water and now host to sewage elementals. This part of the city lies in ruins, a battlefield between the Argent Crusade and the Drakkari. A fungus called muddlecap grows here, said to weaken anyone who drinks a concoction spiked with it.

4294.name: Heb'Valok
4294.description: Heb'Valok is a small area north of the Argent Stand in Zul'Drak, filled with bats and spiders.

4299.name: Kolramas
4299.description: Kolramas is a fallen Scourge necropolis south of the Altar of Har'koa in Zul'Drak. When the Scourge invaded, the Drakkari did not go quietly and brought it crashing down, but the crash did not kill all the undead Hath'ar nerubians inside. They have emerged from the wreck, and their necromagi raise any dead they can find, including fallen crusaders, while blight taints the land all around.

4309.name: Drak'Tharon Keep
4309.description: Drak'Tharon Keep is the ancient Drakkari fortress on the southwestern border of Zul'Drak, an impressive collection of spires and carved walls that once guarded the edge of the troll kingdom. It has fallen to the Scourge, and from it the undead trolls of its former garrison march into the heart of Drakkari territory. Its former leader, the Prophet Tharon'ja, has been transformed into a massive skeletal wind serpent.

4310.name: Zeramas
4310.description: Zeramas is a Scourge necropolis floating above the Reliquary of Agony in western Zul'Drak, its upper halls reachable only through the air.

4311.name: Reliquary of Agony
4311.description: The Reliquary of Agony lies directly below the necropolis of Zeramas in western Zul'Drak, an area infested by the Scourge and filled with pools of blight.

4312.name: Ebon Watch
4312.description: Ebon Watch is a small encampment of the Knights of the Ebon Blade in Zul'Drak, from which the death knights conduct their own operations against the Scourge, some in cooperation with the Argent Crusade.

4313.name: Thrym's End
4313.description: Thrym's End is an area of Zul'Drak where the Scourge's undead vrykul conduct dark experiments. The Argent Crusade seeks to establish a battle front nearby, and it is said that Gymer, the king of the storm giants, is held captive here in a gigantic cage.

4314.name: Voltarus
4314.description: Voltarus is a Scourge necropolis in northwestern Zul'Drak, near the border with the Storm Peaks, hovering above the blighted pools of the Reliquary of Pain. From its halls the Scourge directs its war to conquer Zul'Drak.

4315.name: Reliquary of Pain
4315.description: The Reliquary of Pain lies directly below the necropolis of Voltarus in northwestern Zul'Drak, a platform surrounded by blight pools and crystals that serves as a gateway to the necropolis above.

4316.name: Rageclaw Den
4316.description: Rageclaw Den is the home of the Rageclaw wolvar in Zul'Drak. The Scourge has overrun it, and the den is burning to the ground. Rageclaw Lake lies just to the east.

4317.name: Light's Breach
4317.description: Light's Breach is a small encampment of the Argent Crusade north of Drak'Tharon Keep in southern Zul'Drak, the smaller of the crusade's bases in the region. It occupies an abandoned courtyard surrounded by broken walls and serves as a position to hold back the Scourge pouring out of the keep.

4318.name: Pools of Zha'Jin
4318.description: The Pools of Zha'Jin are three small pools in Zul'Drak, where the ghosts of Drakkari trolls walk the land.

4319.name: Zim'Abwa
4319.description: Zim'Abwa is a small area of Zul'Drak centered on the neglected statue of the troll god Zim'Abwa, which is said to grant its blessing to those who bring Drakkari offerings.

4320.name: Amphitheater of Anguish
4320.description: The Amphitheater of Anguish is a great Drakkari arena northeast of the Argent Stand in Zul'Drak, where a goblin promoter, seeking new fortunes in Northrend, stages brutal gladiatorial fights against monsters and champions from across the continent.

4321.name: Altar of Rhunok
4321.description: The Altar of Rhunok is a temple east of the Altar of Sseratus in Zul'Drak, dedicated to Rhunok, the arctic bear god, and surrounded by fitting expanses of snow. When the Drakkari began sacrificing their gods, Rhunok's twisted followers kept his physical form alive to drain his power, leaving his spirit trapped and tormented.

4322.name: Altar of Har'koa
4322.description: The Altar of Har'koa is a temple northeast of Kolramas in Zul'Drak, dedicated to Har'koa, the leopard goddess. When the prophets of the Drakkari began sacrificing their gods, Har'koa's prophet chose to hold her captive here rather than slay her as the others did.

4323.name: Zim'Torga
4323.description: Zim'Torga is a neutral troll encampment held by the Zandalari between the Argent Stand and Gundrak in Zul'Drak. It sits in a small clearing within a tightly grown stand of thorny trees that form a natural wall, and at its center stands a statue of the goddess Zim'Torga, the Mother of Prosperity. From here, the Zandalari seek to aid the dying gods of the Drakkari.

4324.name: Pools of Jin'Alai
4324.description: The Pools of Jin'Alai are frozen pools south of Zim'Torga in Zul'Drak.

4325.name: Altar of Quetz'lun
4325.description: The Altar of Quetz'lun is a temple in Zul'Drak dedicated to Quetz'lun, the wind serpent goddess, guarded by wind serpents and air spirits. When the Drakkari moved to sacrifice her, it is said that Quetz'lun, in the moment before her physical body was destroyed, created a private underworld nightmare and dragged her former worshipers and high priests into it to suffer for their betrayal.

4326.name: Heb'Drakkar
4326.description: Heb'Drakkar is the bat rookery of Zul'Drak, northeast of Zim'Torga, home to Drakkari bat riders and their mounts, which rest near totems that serve as roosts.

4327.name: Drak'Mabwa
4327.description: Drak'Mabwa is an area south of the Altar of Rhunok in Zul'Drak that has become a water-filled crater, blasted open when the prophet of Rhunok absorbed too much of his god's power too quickly.

4328.name: Zim'Rhuk
4328.description: Zim'Rhuk is a small area in central Zul'Drak, just northeast of the Amphitheater of Anguish, centered on the neglected statue of the troll god Zim'Rhuk, the Wise One. The god is protective of his domain, and his guardians deal harshly with any who lack the wits to slip past them.

4329.name: Altar of Mam'toth
4329.description: The Altar of Mam'toth was a temple southeast of Zol'Maz Stronghold in Zul'Drak, dedicated to Mam'toth, the mammoth god. When Mam'toth learned that his worshipers meant to sacrifice him and steal his power, he destroyed himself, his temple, and all the worshipers present, leaving only a crater. His children still roam the area, trampling his former disciples.

4371.name: Mam'toth Crater
4371.description: Mam'toth Crater is what remains of the Altar of Mam'toth in Zul'Drak, left when the mammoth god destroyed himself rather than let his ice troll followers take his power. All that is left is a crater crawling with blue ooze, the remains of his blood.

4372.name: Zol'Maz Stronghold
4372.description: Zol'Maz Stronghold is a stone fortress in northeastern Zul'Drak, the impressive seat of a Drakkari warlord, patrolled by enchanted tiki warriors that guard its hex-protected treasures.

4373.name: Zol'Heb
4373.description: Zol'Heb is a building southeast of Gundrak in Zul'Drak, a sanctum of the Drakkari prophets.

4374.name: Rageclaw Lake
4374.description: Rageclaw Lake is a large lake just east of Rageclaw Den in Zul'Drak.

4375.name: Gundrak
4375.description: Gundrak is the capital of the Drakkari Empire in northeastern Zul'Drak and its final bastion against the Scourge, a massive place of thick walls, tall guard towers, and heavy gates, its tiered buildings winding about one another like a nest. Its architecture is almost identical to that of Zuldazar in the South Seas. In the depths of the city, the most sacred shrines are said to be steeped in the mojo of slain gods, and the twisted high prophets Slad'ran, Moorabi, and Gal'darah grow in power there, infusing their followers with terrible strength. Before its steps lies the great mosaic circle where the prophets hold the last of their loa, Akali, the rhino god.

4390.name: Frigid Breach
4390.description: The Frigid Breach is an area of Zul'Drak crowded with Drakkari trolls.

4468.name: The Dead Fields
4468.description: The Dead Fields are a vast expanse of dead land on the bottom tier of Zul'Drak, in the shadow of the necropolis of Voltarus.

4469.name: Dargath's Demise
4469.description: Dargath's Demise is an area of the Dead Fields in Zul'Drak, where a lone Argent crusader makes his stand amid the undead.

4481.name: Jintha'kalar Passage
4481.description: The Jintha'kalar Passage is a large passage connecting the ruins of Jintha'kalar in the Dragonblight to Zul'Drak.

4489.name: Crusader Forward Camp
4489.description: The Crusader Forward Camp is a small camp of the Argent Crusade near the Dead Fields in Zul'Drak. Soon after it was established, it fell under Scourge attack and its steam tank was destroyed, and the crusaders struggle to hold out against hordes of zombies.

4579.name: Dubra'Jin
4579.description: Dubra'Jin is a small Zandalari outpost west of Gundrak in Zul'Drak, named for a forgotten god whose statue stands nearby. It is said that in return for offerings, the god protects the few trolls here from being overrun by the Drakkari.

4635.name: Drak'Tharon Keep
4635.description: Drak'Tharon Keep stands on the border of Zul'Drak and the Grizzly Hills, a massive Drakkari fortress that once guarded the southwestern edge of the troll empire. Taken by the Scourge, it has become the staging ground for the invasion of Zul'Drak, its fallen defenders now serving the Lich King. Even the mightiest ice troll warriors have failed to retake it.

66.description: Zul'Drak is the homeland of the Drakkari ice trolls in eastern Northrend, a valley between the Grizzly Hills, Crystalsong Forest, and the Storm Peaks that is itself one vast temple city: plazas and ziggurats, walls and aqueducts stretching as far as the eye can see, raised in tiers upon a colossal base. Thornwood trees, frozen ponds, and snow cover the land between the ruins. The Drakkari are among the oldest races of Northrend, and some say of all Azeroth; they were building in Zul'Drak before the Great Sundering, and their empire grew as one tribe conquered and absorbed the others, ruling from the capital of Gundrak. The tribes still war among themselves, and they welcome no outsiders. Now the empire is collapsing. The Scourge seized the fortress of Drak'Tharon Keep, and its necropolises hover over the lower tiers, raising the fallen trolls to fight against their own people. In desperation, the Drakkari prophets have turned on their own gods, slaying the loa, the animal deities they worshiped for ages, and drinking their blood for the power to repel the undead, a sacrilege that has driven many of them mad. The Argent Crusade has come to fight the Scourge here, caught between two armies, while the Zandalar tribe has arrived to intervene on behalf of the gods and to chronicle the fall of the Drakkari Empire.

67.name: The Storm Peaks

4418.name: K3
4418.description: K3 is a neutral goblin base camp in the southern foothills of the Storm Peaks. The goblins came to loot the titan machines of the mountains, but they have had endless trouble with the local wildlife and their neighbors. When the camp was first set up, the frost vrykul of Sifreldar Village raided it and carried off its men to labor in their mines.

4419.name: Snowblind Hills
4419.description: The Snowblind Hills are the southern foothills of the Storm Peaks, where the goblin camp of K3 stands among the snow.

4420.name: Snowblind Terrace
4420.description: The Snowblind Terrace is a high shelf in the southern foothills of the Storm Peaks, above the Snowblind Hills and below the vrykul villages of Sifreldar and Brunnhildar, inhabited by yeti.

4421.name: Garm
4421.description: Garm is a cave and its surrounding snowy plains in the southern foothills of the Storm Peaks, due east of K3, home to the Garm magnataur and the snobolds of the Snowblind tribe, who attack the goblins in vain. The cave is filled with a red haze, spiked red plants, and magnataur sacrificial sites, and in its depths, behind fallen rocks, lie glimpses of ancient titan machinery.

4422.name: Brunnhildar Village
4422.description: Brunnhildar Village is the stronghold of the frost vrykul known as the Hyldnir in the southern Storm Peaks. Unlike their sisters of Valkyrion, they refused the Lich King's offer and did not join the Scourge. Their society is a strict matriarchy that holds men fit only for slave labor, and the proto-drakes they ride nest in the mountains above the village. At its center lies the Pit of the Fang, where the Hyldnir compete for the honor of ruling at the side of the keeper Thorim.

4423.name: Sifreldar Village
4423.description: Sifreldar Village is a small village of the Hyldnir, the female frost vrykul, in the southern Storm Peaks, just over the mountains from Brunnhildar Village. Its warriors raided the goblin camp of K3 when it was first set up and carried off its men as captives to work their mines.

4424.name: Valkyrion
4424.description: Valkyrion is a frost vrykul settlement in the western Storm Peaks whose leader delivered her village to the Lich King in exchange for being made one of his val'kyr. The Hyldnir of Brunnhildar despise their sisters for becoming his servants. In the Blighted Pool at its heart, the vrykul of Valkyrion infect captured proto-drakes and their eggs with the plague, turning them into plagued beasts for the Scourge.

4425.name: The Forlorn Mine
4425.description: The Forlorn Mine connects Sifreldar Village and Brunnhildar Village in the southern Storm Peaks. The Hyldnir send their menfolk and any men they capture to labor in its tunnels.

4427.name: Argent Vanguard
4427.description: The Argent Vanguard is the main forward base of the Argent Crusade, raised in the Valley of Echoes in eastern Icecrown, near the border of the Storm Peaks. It was the first foothold the crusade established when it breached Icecrown under Highlord Tirion Fordring, and it has withstood waves of undead of every kind, even frost wyrms, as the crusaders fight to push deeper into the Lich King's domain.

4428.name: Frosthold
4428.description: Frosthold is the city of the Frostborn, the frost dwarves, in the southwestern Storm Peaks, south of the Temple of Storms. Built in and around a great pit of ice atop a massive mountain, it is reachable only through the air, and it is home to the entire frost dwarf race, who have allied themselves with the Alliance.

4429.name: Grom'arsh Crash-Site
4429.description: The Grom'arsh Crash-Site is a Horde encampment east of the Temple of Storms in the Storm Peaks, built from the wreck of a goblin zeppelin and serving as a forward camp for the Horde's efforts around Ulduar.

4430.name: Temple of Storms
4430.description: The Temple of Storms is a titan temple atop the highest mountain in the Storm Peaks, and thus in all of Northrend, its columns and the circlet of its open roof rimmed with snow. The crack of lightning fills the air even when the sky is clear and the northern lights dance across the stars. It is the sanctum of the keeper Thorim, the Stormlord, who has sat brooding here for ages since the death of his wife Sif.

4431.name: Engine of the Makers
4431.description: The Engine of the Makers is a deep, tunnel-like shaft in the Foot Steppes of the Storm Peaks, part of the vast titan machinery hidden throughout the mountains. At its bottom, encased in a pillar of ice, stands a mysterious device spouting cold air.

4432.name: The Foot Steppes
