4432.description: The Foot Steppes are an area in the western Storm Peaks, at the center of which lies the mysterious Engine of the Makers.

4433.name: Dragonspine Peaks
4433.description: The Dragonspine Peaks are mountains on the southern border of the Storm Peaks, southeast of Brunnhildar Village, where the blue proto-dragons have built their nests.

4434.name: Nidavelir
4434.description: Nidavelir is an iron dwarf village in the northwestern Storm Peaks, southwest of the Snowdrift Plains, from which the iron dwarves send their mole machines to attack the earthen driven out of Ulduar.

4435.name: Narvir's Cradle
4435.description: Narvir's Cradle is a construction site of the iron dwarves in the Snowdrift Plains of the Storm Peaks, where they are building a colossal war engine of iron to use against the earthen.

4436.name: Snowdrift Plains
4436.description: The Snowdrift Plains lie in the northwestern corner of the Storm Peaks, where dolomite giants battle constantly against the raiders of Loken's iron army. The earthen refuge and the iron dwarves' construction site stand on its eastern side.

4437.name: Valley of Ancient Winters
4437.description: The Valley of Ancient Winters runs through the central Storm Peaks, connecting Brunnhildar Village in the east with Dun Niffelem in the west. Frost giants and their frostworgs, mammoths, and jormungar dwell in the valley, which has seen war between the Hyldnir of Brunnhildar and the frost giants of the Sons of Hodir.

4438.name: Dun Niffelem
4438.description: Dun Niffelem is a fortress of massive spikes of ice and iron chains spreading across a section of the Valley of Ancient Winters in the eastern Storm Peaks. It is the home of the Sons of Hodir, the frost giants who are the children of the keeper Hodir, ruled by their king, Jokkum.

4439.name: Frostfield Lake
4439.description: Frostfield Lake is a frozen lake just east of Dun Niffelem in the eastern Storm Peaks, haunted by seething revenants.

4440.name: Thunderfall
4440.description: Thunderfall is a sobering sight in the eastern Storm Peaks, north of Frostfield Lake: a massive, silent grave where ghosts wander. Ages ago, the keeper Thorim, in a fit of rage, hurled his hammer at King Arngrim of the frost giants, who was battling a clan of frost dwarves here. The blast killed everyone nearby and froze the battle forever, catching the moment the shockwave threw many of the dwarves into the air.

4441.name: Camp Tunka'lo
4441.description: Camp Tunka'lo is a small taunka village high in the mountains of the eastern Storm Peaks, resting above Dun Niffelem on one side and the Plain of Echoes on the other. Its remote location has kept it safe from the Scourge attacks that destroyed so many other taunka villages, and its people are wary of strangers.

4442.name: Brann's Base-Camp
4442.description: Brann's Base-Camp is the camp of the famed dwarven explorer Brann Bronzebeard, just west of Dun Niffelem above the Valley of Ancient Winters in the central Storm Peaks, from which he studies the titan ruins of the mountains. A ravaged part of the camp lies at the base of the valley, where the trail up to the camp proper begins.

4444.name: Plain of Echoes
4444.description: The Plain of Echoes lies in the northeastern Storm Peaks, north of Camp Tunka'lo, with the ruined titan Temple of Life at its center. Taunka legend tells that here their hero Stormhoof fought the North Wind, the elemental lord that once crushed the peaks and their peoples in its grip, and weakened it before he fell.

4445.name: Ulduar
4445.description: Ulduar is the greatest titan complex on Azeroth, hidden in the northern Storm Peaks; from outside it looks much like the surrounding peaks, a jumble of rock and ice. For millennia it remained undisturbed by mortals, and since its recent discovery many have wondered whether it was a city built to herald the glory of its makers or a vault of titan treasures. Its keeper Loken has turned to darkness, seized the city from the earthen, and filled the Forge of Wills with the making of iron dwarves and iron giants, and there are whispers of a great evil at work behind the fall of the titan city.

4446.name: Terrace of the Makers
4446.description: The Terrace of the Makers is a complex of temples and other buildings in the north-central Storm Peaks, across the chasm from Ulduar, where the keepers once made their homes and worked. The terrace shows a great deal of damage, its walkways shattered and columns cracked and missing. Atop it stand the Temples of Invention, Order, and Winter, and earthen warders guard it against attacks by Loken's iron dwarves.

4448.name: Path of the Titans
4448.description: The Path of the Titans is an ancient road, now in ruins, that runs from Ulduar over the Terrace of the Makers and through Stormcrest, then south across Crystalsong Forest and the Dragonblight toward Wyrmrest Temple and the Frozen Sea.

4449.name: Uldis
4449.description: Uldis is a titan facility in the Storm Peaks, far below the Temple of Storms but still high on the mountain, entered through a great aperture partially telescoped open on the mountain's southern face. Its interior is filled with titan machinery, like a giant engine room.

4450.name: Loken's Bargain
4450.description: Loken's Bargain is a titan facility halfway up the northern cliff of the Valley of Ancient Winters in the central Storm Peaks, west of Brann's Base-Camp, filled with machinery like a giant engine room or clockworks.

4451.name: Bor's Fall
4451.description: Bor's Fall is a frozen waterfall at the end of Bor's Breath in the Storm Peaks, descending to a frozen lake in the Snowblind Hills.

4452.name: Bor's Breath
4452.description: Bor's Breath is a frozen river in a canyon in the western-central Storm Peaks, almost directly south of Uldis, surrounded by high mountains and ending at the frozen waterfall of Bor's Fall.

4453.name: Rohemdal Pass
4453.description: Rohemdal Pass is a mountain pass west of Frosthold in the Storm Peaks, home to the Frostfeather harpies.

4455.name: Hibernal Cavern
4455.description: Hibernal Cavern is a cave on the northern wall of the Valley of Ancient Winters in the Storm Peaks, between Brunnhildar Village and Dun Niffelem, infested with ravenous jormungar.

4457.name: Torseg's Rest
4457.description: Torseg's Rest is a small camp northwest of K3 in the Storm Peaks, where an exiled frost giant sits beside a fire and a great pack.

4458.name: Sparksocket Minefield
4458.description: The Sparksocket Minefield lies west of K3 in the southern foothills of the Storm Peaks, a field strewn with goblin land mines and turrets.

4459.name: Ricket's Folly
4459.description: Ricket's Folly is the crash site of a goblin flying machine just west of K3 in the Storm Peaks.

4460.name: Garm's Bane
4460.description: Garm's Bane is a goblin minefield between Garm and the Snowblind Hills in the southern foothills of the Storm Peaks, lined with devices that destroy the magnataur and snobolds who charge out of Garm toward K3.

4461.name: Garm's Rise
4461.description: Garm's Rise is a hill above and east of the cave of Garm in the southern foothills of the Storm Peaks, overlooking the border with Zul'Drak.

4462.name: Crystalweb Cavern
4462.description: Crystalweb Cavern is a cave northeast of K3 in the Snowblind Hills of the Storm Peaks, where goblin miners have run into trouble.

4463.name: Temple of Life
4463.description: The Temple of Life stands at the center of the Plain of Echoes in the northeastern Storm Peaks. It was once the post of the keeper Freya, but she is gone. Signs of a great battle against a foe of her own size and strength mark the temple, its guardians have vanished, and the plants that once grew around it are dead.

4464.name: Temple of Order
4464.description: The Temple of Order stands on the northern part of the Terrace of the Makers in the Storm Peaks, decorated with chains, shields, and weapons. It was the domain of the keeper Tyr, but he is long gone; there is no sign of a struggle and no guardians remain, and what became of him is a mystery.

4465.name: Temple of Winter
4465.description: The Temple of Winter stands on the southern part of the Terrace of the Makers in the Storm Peaks, the temple of the keeper Hodir, father of the frost giants. Its frost giant guardians were slain by fire giants and Hodir is gone, and with him the cold weather once called forth from the temple has vanished.

4466.name: Temple of Invention
4466.description: The Temple of Invention stands on the western part of the Terrace of the Makers in the Storm Peaks, the seat of the keeper Mimiron. Rather than a throne, a great titan machine stands at its center, and its mechagnome guardians have been corrupted by some unknown power.

4472.name: Frostgrip's Hollow
4472.description: Frostgrip's Hollow is a hollow southwest of Valkyrion in the Storm Peaks, home to a lone hermit, recently troubled by unwelcome visitors from Loken's iron army.

4473.name: The Frigid Tomb
4473.description: The Frigid Tomb is an icy tomb hidden among the frozen heights of the Storm Peaks.

4476.name: Abandoned Camp
4476.description: The Abandoned Camp is a deserted camp in the Storm Peaks, its tents and supplies left to the wind and snow.

4484.name: Bouldercrag's Refuge
4484.description: Bouldercrag's Refuge is a neutral outpost of the earthen on a ledge above the Snowdrift Plains in the northwestern Storm Peaks, southwest of the Temple of Wisdom. The earthen have made their home here since Loken's iron army drove them out of Ulduar, and they fight to strike back.

4485.name: The Inventor's Library
4485.description: The Inventor's Library is a titan repository on the Terrace of the Makers in the Storm Peaks, where the keepers stored their knowledge. Rather than books and scrolls, it holds databanks and consoles, guarded by mechagnomes.

4486.name: The Frozen Mine
4486.description: The Frozen Mine is a mine southwest of Narvir's Cradle in the Storm Peaks, where captive mechagnomes labor under the iron dwarves of Loken's army.

4487.name: Frostfloe Deep
4487.description: Frostfloe Deep is a large cave in the northeastern corner of the Storm Peaks, northwest of Camp Tunka'lo. Since ancient times the taunka have used it as a burial place for their warriors and chieftains, and it holds many sacred relics, but a malevolent force has disturbed its peace, filling the once quiet caverns with raging elementals.

4488.name: The Howling Hollow
4488.description: The Howling Hollow lies north of and directly below the Plain of Echoes in the northeastern Storm Peaks, a place filled with storm revenants and howling winds.

4490.name: Stormcrest
4490.description: Stormcrest is a peak directly east of Frosthold in the Storm Peaks, covered with great eagles and their nests, crossed by the ancient Path of the Titans.

4495.name: Fjorn's Anvil
4495.description: Fjorn's Anvil is an area east of Frostfield Lake in the easternmost Storm Peaks, a forge of fire and iron where the fire giant Fjorn works his great anvil, surrounded by fire revenants and iron giants.

4499.name: The Blighted Pool
4499.description: The Blighted Pool is a pool of corrupted water within Valkyrion in the Storm Peaks, where the vrykul who serve the Lich King infect captured proto-drakes and their eggs with the plague.

4502.name: Mimir's Workshop
4502.description: Mimir's Workshop is a small titan workshop west of Ulduar, a cavernous space warmed by ever-burning fires and filled with anvils and stores of metal, its floors littered with the broken bodies of mechagnomes.

4535.name: The Pit of the Fang
4535.description: The Pit of the Fang lies at the center of Brunnhildar Village in the southern Storm Peaks, where the Hyldnir hold the Hyldsmeet, a contest in which they battle on the backs of polar bears to decide who shall rule beside the keeper Thorim. No vrykul woman may enter unless she has won at least one duel to the death.

4536.name: Frosthowl Cavern
4536.description: Frosthowl Cavern is a very small cave in the Storm Peaks, a rare shelter from the howling wind.

4542.name: Hall of the Shaper
4542.description: The Hall of the Shaper is a titan hall on the eastern side of the Terrace of the Makers in the Storm Peaks, guarded by iron sentinels.

4543.name: Temple of Wisdom
4543.description: The Temple of Wisdom is a titan temple southwest of Ulduar's Halls of Stone in the Storm Peaks, its columns entwined with strange twisted growths that look disturbingly like dead tentacles. It is believed to have been the seat of the keeper Loken.

4547.name: Halls of Stone
4547.description: The Halls of Stone are a wing of Ulduar in the southern part of the titan city, home to the Tribunal of Ages and the Forge of Wills. The reasons for Loken's treachery and the fate of the other keepers remain a mystery, and it is said that the truth lies within these ancient halls, now held by his iron dwarves and stone constructs.

4548.name: Halls of Lightning
4548.description: The Halls of Lightning are a wing in the eastern part of Ulduar, where the fallen keeper Loken mass-produces iron vrykul for his sinister plans. He commands his forces from his throne here, guarded by storm and fire elementals and his most powerful servants.

4592.name: Gimorak's Den
4592.description: Gimorak's Den is a large cavern in the Storm Peaks, choked with cave mushrooms and the lair of a great worg.

4631.name: The Broodmother's Nest
4631.description: The Broodmother's Nest is the nest of Veranus, the broodmother of the blue proto-dragons, high in the Storm Peaks. Though she is past her child-bearing years, she keeps the nest for sentimental reasons.

67.description: The Storm Peaks are a towering mountain range in northeastern Northrend, looking out over Icecrown to the west, Crystalsong Forest to the south, Zul'Drak to the southeast, and the ocean to the north. It is a harsh and dangerous land: the wind is fierce and constant and can pluck a grown dwarf off a cliff, avalanches thunder down the slopes, and the sun glaring off the ice can blind the unwary, while storms of freezing rain, hail, and snow make every surface slick. Little grows among the stone and ice. The peaks were the home of the titans' keepers, and nearly every mountain bears their mark: temples, terraces, and vast machines hidden in the rock. Atop the highest peak in all of Northrend stands the Temple of Storms, the sanctum of the keeper Thorim, and to the north lies Ulduar, the greatest titan complex on Azeroth, whose recent discovery has raised whispers of a great evil at work behind its fall. Its keeper Loken has turned to darkness, and his iron dwarves and iron giants pour out of the city to spread destruction, driving the earthen from their ancient home. The frost giants of the Sons of Hodir hold the eastern valleys, the frost vrykul Hyldnir ride proto-drakes in the south, and the frost dwarves keep their remote city of Frosthold. A remote taunka village clings to the eastern heights, goblins have come to loot the titan machines, and magnataur, wendigo, and storm giants roam the peaks.

85.name: Tirisfal Glades

152.name: The Bulwark
152.description: The Bulwark is a fortified line of barricades and watchtowers in southeastern Tirisfal Glades, marking the border with the Western Plaguelands. It is the Forsaken's last bastion of defense against the main forces of the Scourge, and here the Forsaken Deathguard stand side by side with the Argent Dawn, united against the armies of the Lich King to the east. Unlike the rest of Tirisfal, the Bulwark is shrouded in the yellowish plague mist that drifts in from the Plaguelands, and the air is thick with the stench of decay. Its defenders are grim and vigilant, for the undead hordes are never far away.

153.name: Ruins of Lordaeron
153.description: The Ruins of Lordaeron are all that remain of the great capital city of the Kingdom of Lordaeron, which once stood as a monument to humanity's might on the shores of Lordamere Lake. In the Third War, Prince Arthas returned here in triumph, only to slay his father, King Terenas, in the throne room and deliver the city to the Scourge. Today the shattered walls, broken towers, and overgrown courtyards stand as a sad reminder of the kingdom's fall, and the bloodstain where the king died can still be seen. It is said that the ruins are haunted by echoes of that terrible day: whispers in the courtyard, the ringing of bells, and the distant cheers that welcomed the prince home. Beneath the ruins lies the Undercity, the capital of the Forsaken, whose guards patrol the ruined halls above.

154.name: Deathknell
154.description: Deathknell is a small Forsaken village nestled in a well-guarded valley in western Tirisfal Glades, just north of Silverpine Forest. It is here that many newly risen Forsaken first awaken to their unlife, rising from the crypt above the village. The village's church serves as one of the main bases of the Forsaken cult of the Forgotten Shadow. The people of Deathknell struggle daily to obtain the resources they need, for the nearby gold mine has been overrun by spiders, and the northern part of the village is held by the mindless Scourge. A detachment of the Scarlet Crusade also camps nearby, launching frequent attacks against the Forsaken. Despite these dangers, Deathknell endures, guarded by the Deathguard.

155.name: Night Web's Hollow
155.description: Night Web's Hollow is a small valley and gold mine just northwest of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Both the vale and the mine are infested with spiders, which skitter among the shadows and lurk in webbed corners, and a great spider matriarch is said to dwell in the deepest recesses of the mine. The Forsaken of Deathknell would dearly like to reclaim the mine and its precious gold, and young Forsaken often test their mettle against the spiders here. The hollow is dark, damp, and covered in thick webs.

156.name: Solliden Farmstead
156.description: The Solliden Farmstead in western Tirisfal Glades is one of the very few places in northern Lordaeron where the native farmfolk have survived untainted by the plague of undeath. The farmers have united with the zealous Scarlet Crusade for protection against the Forsaken and the Scourge, and they grow large pumpkins and hunt in the woods to sustain themselves. Years of living surrounded by the undead have made them as paranoid and hostile as their Scarlet protectors, and they attack anyone they see, even fellow humans. The farm is a strange island of the living in a land of the dead.

157.name: Agamand Mills
157.description: Agamand Mills is a vast network of windmills and farm buildings in northern Tirisfal Glades, once owned by the wealthy Agamand family. When the Scourge attacked Lordaeron, the Agamands ordered their farmhands to remain and defend the property, but their effort was in vain, and the family and their workers were massacred and raised into undeath. Now the mills stand vacant and decaying, their great sails creaking in the wind, and the ghosts and skeletons of the Agamands and their servants haunt their former home. A few of the family broke free of the Lich King and joined the Forsaken. The mills have a deep, eerie atmosphere, and their silhouettes against the green sky are one of the most haunting sights in Tirisfal.

158.name: Agamand Family Crypt
158.description: The Agamand Family Crypt lies just north of Agamand Mills in northern Tirisfal Glades, the burial vault of the once-wealthy Agamand family. A servant of the Scourge has settled within and awakened the corpses and spirits of the Agamands' dead ancestors, who now attack anyone who enters unbidden. The crypt is dark, dusty, and filled with the stench of decay, its stone sarcophagi broken open and its halls echoing with the shuffling of the dead.

159.name: Brill
159.description: Brill is a small town in the center of Tirisfal Glades, just north of the ruins of the old capital, now controlled by the Forsaken. Once a quaint village of the Kingdom of Lordaeron, it was one of the first towns to be afflicted by the plague of undeath, for it was here that the necromancer Kel'Thuzad began spreading the plague, and the mass graveyard outside town was dug to hold the many who died. After the Lich King's power weakened, the Forsaken claimed the town as their own. Today Brill serves as a gathering place for the Forsaken, with a town hall, an inn, a smithy, and stables, and its people fight daily to preserve their freedom against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. The town retains a grim, gothic charm, with its leaning houses, flickering lanterns, and the gallows near the tavern. Zeppelin towers stand to the south, connecting Tirisfal with Orgrimmar and Stranglethorn Vale.

160.name: Whispering Gardens
160.description: The Whispering Gardens are a hillside area in northeastern Tirisfal Glades, south of the Scarlet Monastery. A great battle was once fought here between the forces that would become the Scarlet Crusade and a host of the Scourge, and the spirits of those who fell can still be heard as faint whispers in the twilight. The gardens are overgrown and neglected, and an eerie stillness hangs over them. The Scarlet Crusade guards the area closely, for it lies near the heart of their power.

161.name: Terrace of Repose
161.description: The Terrace of Repose is a garden on the grounds just north of the Scarlet Monastery in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. It is one of the very few places in northern Lordaeron that the plague of undeath has not reached, and the Scarlet Crusade has been able to maintain green hedges and a fountain of fresh, clean water here. The terrace is a peaceful and well-tended place, a stark contrast to the blighted lands around it, but it is guarded by the Crusade's zealous soldiers, who attack any intruders without mercy.

162.name: Brightwater Lake
162.description: Brightwater Lake is the largest lake in Tirisfal Glades, lying in the heart of the region. Before the plague struck, it was a popular place for bathing and fishing, its clear waters sparkling in the sun. Now it lies dark and silent, with dead trees floating along its edges and rotting on its bottom, and the green-tinted sky is reflected in its still surface. The lake's largest island, Gunther's Retreat, is inhabited by mindless Scourge zombies. Murlocs and other creatures dwell along its shores.

163.name: Gunther's Retreat
163.description: Gunther's Retreat is an island in the middle of Brightwater Lake in central Tirisfal Glades. Most of its inhabitants are mindless Scourge zombies, but it is also the home of a reclusive Forsaken lich who has made the island his retreat and who is said to consider himself the only sane undead in the world. The island is overgrown and gloomy, with a small house surrounded by shambling corpses, and few visit it.

164.name: Garren's Haunt
164.description: Garren's Haunt is a large farmstead in northern Tirisfal Glades, with a farmhouse, a barn, silos, and wide fields. Before the plague, it was a bountiful place, but the family who lived here was brutally murdered by the Scourge during the Third War. Now the farm lies grey and lifeless, and it has become the home of undead gnolls who hungrily attack anyone who comes too close. The fields are barren, and the buildings are decaying.

165.name: Balnir Farmstead
165.description: The Balnir Farmstead is a farm in eastern Tirisfal Glades that once belonged to the Balnir family, renowned horse breeders who provided steeds for the royal House of Menethil; it is said that Prince Arthas's beloved horse, Invincible, was born here. Since the plague of undeath, the farm has fallen into the hands of the Scourge, and spirits and animated corpses wander its fields and inhabit its barn. The farm is a grim and tragic place, a reminder of the prince who brought ruin to his own kingdom.

166.name: Cold Hearth Manor
166.description: Cold Hearth Manor is a farmstead in central Tirisfal Glades along the main road, once known for its warm atmosphere and bountiful crops. After the plague of undeath claimed the lives of everyone who lived and worked here, its fields became barren and infested with mindless Scourge zombies. The Forsaken have since claimed the farmhouse, renaming it with grim humor in memory of its former warmth, and they now offer trade to travelers passing along the road. The fields around it remain dangerous.

167.name: Crusader Outpost
167.description: Crusader Outpost is a guard tower in eastern Tirisfal Glades, held by the Scarlet Crusade. Built on a hill overlooking the main road, it allows the Crusade to keep watch over travelers and provides flanking support against enemies who would assault the Scarlet Monastery. The tower is garrisoned by zealous Scarlet soldiers who attack the undead and anyone else they deem impure. It is one of several such towers the Crusade maintains throughout the glades.

168.name: The North Coast
168.description: The North Coast is a long stretch of stony beach along the northern edge of Tirisfal Glades, bordering the Great Sea. Since the plague of undeath tainted the region, the coast has become dark and cold, and the carcasses of dead sea creatures rot at the water's edge. Ravenous murlocs and various sea creatures inhabit the shore, and the waves crash against the rocks under the gloomy green sky. Despite its bleakness, the coast has a stark, haunting beauty.

169.name: Whispering Shore
169.description: The Whispering Shore is a small stretch of coast in western Tirisfal Glades, just north of the Solliden Farmstead. Once a popular fishing spot, it is now the domain of a band of murlocs who ravenously attack anyone who wanders near. The waters off the coast are cold and dark, and nothing remains of their former bounty. The wind blowing in from the sea carries strange whispers, giving the shore its name.

173.name: Faol's Rest
173.description: Faol's Rest is a small, solemn grave site in eastern Tirisfal Glades, just southwest of the Scarlet Monastery. It is believed to be the final resting place of the revered Archbishop Alonsus Faol, founder of the Order of the Silver Hand, who died some time before the coming of the Scourge. Before the plague, the grave was visited by many mourners, but now it lies untended and forgotten, its stones overgrown with moss. The site retains a quiet dignity amid the blighted lands.

459.name: Scarlet Watch Post
459.description: The Scarlet Watch Post is a guard tower in northeastern Tirisfal Glades, just north of the Scarlet Monastery. The Scarlet Crusade maintains it to prevent enemies from assaulting the monastery from its less defensible northern side. The tower is garrisoned by zealous Scarlet soldiers, who keep a constant watch over the coast and the surrounding lands. It is one of several such towers the Crusade has built throughout the glades.

810.name: Stillwater Pond
810.description: Stillwater Pond is a small lake west of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Before the plague, it was a popular picnic spot for the people of the glades, and children who were too young to swim in the larger Brightwater Lake played in its shallow waters. Now the pond lies grey and forgotten, and only wandering undead and wild beasts look upon its cold, still waters. A fearsome darkhound is said to prowl around the pond, preying on the unwary.

811.name: Nightmare Vale
811.description: Nightmare Vale is a wide valley in southwestern Tirisfal Glades. Once verdant and teeming with forest animals, it has been blighted by the plague: the trees have withered, and the wildlife has been devoured by hungry darkhounds and huge vampire bats. The Scarlet Crusade maintains an outpost in the vale, and its soldiers clash with the Forsaken and the Scourge. The vale lives up to its name, especially at night, when the bats fill the air and the darkhounds howl.

812.name: Venomweb Vale
812.description: Venomweb Vale is a wide valley in eastern Tirisfal Glades, just south of the Scarlet Monastery. It was once a haven for hunting deer and rabbits, its trees green and its grass lush, but now it is a tainted place full of poisonous spiders, which give the vale its name. A Scarlet Crusade encampment stands in the middle of the valley. The webs of the spiders hang thick between the withered trees, and the vale is dangerous for unwary travelers.

2117.name: Shadow Grave
2117.description: Shadow Grave is a crypt at the top of a slope in the mountains of western Tirisfal Glades, just above the Forsaken village of Deathknell. It is here that many newly risen Forsaken first awaken to their unlife, freed from the Lich King's control and welcomed into the ranks of the Banshee Queen's people. The crypt is dark and cold, filled with stone coffins, and a path leads down from it to Deathknell. For many Forsaken, it is the place where their new existence began.

2118.name: Brill Town Hall
2118.description: The Brill Town Hall is the most prominent building in the town of Brill in central Tirisfal Glades, a sturdy stone structure that serves as the seat of the town's Forsaken magistrate. From his podium, the magistrate issues orders and tasks to the Forsaken who serve the Banshee Queen, coordinating the fight against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. The town hall is a grim, functional place, decorated with the banners of the Forsaken.

2119.name: Gallows' End Tavern
2119.description: The Gallows' End Tavern is the inn of Brill in central Tirisfal Glades, one of the few taverns in the world run by the Forsaken. Its dim common room is a gathering place for undead travelers, mages, warriors, and other Forsaken who come to rest, trade news, and share a drink, even if they can no longer truly taste it. Captives are said to be held in its cellars. The tavern has a dark, gothic atmosphere, with flickering candles, creaking floorboards, and eerie music.

2399.name: The Great Sea
2399.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the northern coast of Tirisfal Glades, rolling grey and cold onto the stony beaches of the North Coast and the Whispering Shore. Since the plague tainted the land, the waters have grown dark and lifeless near the shore, and the carcasses of dead sea creatures wash up on the beaches. Murlocs dwell in the shallows, and the gloomy green sky is reflected in the restless waves. Few ships sail near this desolate coast.

85.description: Tirisfal Glades is a region of rolling, wooded hills on the northern coast of Lordaeron, once the green heartland of the human kingdom and the site of its great capital city. Today it is the homeland of the Forsaken, the undead who broke free of the Lich King's control and follow the Banshee Queen, Sylvanas Windrunner. The land is steeped in the curse of the plague of undeath: the sky is eternally gloomy and tinted a sickly green, the trees and grass cling to their last shreds of life, and a cold mist drifts over abandoned farmsteads, silent lakes, and ruined mills. Yet Tirisfal retains a haunting, melancholy beauty, especially along its stony northern coast and in the quiet village of Brill. It was here, in the countryside around Brill, that the necromancer Kel'Thuzad first spread the plague that doomed Lordaeron, and it was in the capital's throne room that Prince Arthas slew his father, King Terenas. Beneath the ruins of the old capital lies the Undercity, the seat of the Forsaken. The Forsaken are far from alone in Tirisfal: the mindless Scourge still haunts the derelict farms and graveyards, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade holds its great monastery in the northeast and keeps outposts throughout the glades, and darkhounds, giant bats, spiders, and murlocs roam the wilds. In the southeast, the Bulwark stands as the Forsaken's bastion against the Scourge armies of the Plaguelands.

130.name: Silverpine Forest

172.name: Fenris Isle
172.description: Fenris Isle is a large island in the center of Lordamere Lake, generally considered part of Silverpine Forest. Together with the nearby Dawning Isles, it forms a broken circle of land that was once the rim of an ancient volcano. The island was home to Fenris Keep, a thriving military outpost of the Kingdom of Lordaeron, but when the Scourge took the land, the island was abandoned and its inhabitants fled or were murdered. Now it is occupied by the Rot Hide gnolls and their master, a traitorous mage who allied himself with the Scourge, and they have taken complete control of the island. The island is dark and gloomy, its keep looming over the misty waters.

204.name: Pyrewood Village
204.description: Pyrewood Village is a small human village in southern Silverpine Forest, north of the road near Shadowfang Keep. Its people survived the coming of the Scourge, but not without paying a terrible price: they bear a curse that transforms them into bloodthirsty worgen every night, returning them to human form at dawn. By day, the villagers go about their lives, trading cloth, leather, and armor with travelers, but when night falls, they become savage beasts who attack anyone they encounter. The curse is believed to be the work of the archmage Arugal, who dwells in nearby Shadowfang Keep. Pyrewood is a sad and haunted place, a village living under the shadow of a curse it cannot escape.

213.name: Deep Elem Mine
213.description: The Deep Elem Mine is a silver mine in Silverpine Forest that was once a bountiful source of ore, worked by the forest's hardy young men to provide Gilneas, Dalaran, and Lordaeron with silver for coins and jewelry. The mine prospered until the worgen arrived and tore through the workers, feasting on their flesh. Now the worgen have made the mine their home, led by a cunning pack leader, and they ferociously attack anyone who comes too close. The mine's entrance is dark and silent, littered with abandoned tools.

226.name: The Skittering Dark
226.description: The Skittering Dark is an abandoned mine and the surrounding forest in northwestern Silverpine Forest, named for the countless spiders that infest the mine and its entrance. A particularly nasty spider matriarch is said to dwell in its depths. The spiders' blood is valued by the Forsaken apothecaries for their alchemical concoctions. The mine is dark and covered in webs, and the skittering of countless legs echoes from within.

227.name: Valgan's Field
227.description: Valgan's Field is one of the many desolate farms of northern Silverpine Forest, lying just west of the Shining Strand and north of a small river. Its owner was killed or forced to flee when the Scourge arrived, and the farm is now occupied by the Moonrage worgen. In its heyday, the farm would have been a lovely place, offering a magnificent view of Lordamere Lake, but now its fields are overgrown and its buildings decaying, and the howls of the worgen echo across the land.

228.name: The Sepulcher
228.description: The Sepulcher is the Forsaken's base of operations in Silverpine Forest, built around an old graveyard and crypt along the road that once led to Lordaeron's capital. Since the end of the Third War, the enterprising Forsaken have converted the crypt into a stronghold, and it is one of the only places of safety for the Horde in the forest, surrounded by worgen to the south, the Scourge to the east, and the forces of Dalaran to the southeast. The Sepulcher is a grim place of tombstones, mausoleums, and expeditionary caravans, nestled among the hills above the coast. Bats carry travelers to and from the Undercity and Tarren Mill.

229.name: Olsen's Farthing
229.description: Olsen's Farthing was once a bustling farmstead along the main trade road through Silverpine Forest, where the Olsen family made a good living. When the Scourge came, crazed ghouls and skeletal warriors stormed the farm one night; the family barricaded themselves in the barn, but the undead broke through and slaughtered them all. The Scourge still haunts the farm, attacking anyone who enters, and the barn bears the marks of that terrible night.

230.name: The Greymane Wall
230.description: The Greymane Wall is an enormous grey wall stretching across the southern edge of Silverpine Forest, built after the Second War by King Genn Greymane to seal the kingdom of Gilneas off from the rest of the world. Gilneas withdrew from the Alliance over disputes about the orc internment camps, and its great gates have remained shut ever since. No guards stand on the battlements, and the wall seems dead and silent. Refugees from the north camp in its shadow, hoping for shelter that never comes, and they are easy prey for the worgen that stray this far south. What lies beyond the wall, and what has become of Gilneas, is a mystery to the outside world.

231.name: Beren's Peril
231.description: Beren's Peril is a cave in southern Silverpine Forest, south of Ambermill, between the main road and the side road leading into the hills. Before the plague, it was home to the creatures of the forest and was sometimes used as a retreat by the wizards of Dalaran. When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the cave's creatures were butchered by ghouls and skeletal warriors, and it has remained in the grip of the undead ever since. It poses a constant threat to the nearby Kirin Tor camps and to travelers on the road below.

232.name: The Dawning Isles
232.description: The Dawning Isles are a group of low islets rising from Lordamere Lake east of Fenris Isle, forming part of the rim of an ancient volcano. Once they were idyllic keys rising from the crystalline surface of the lake, but the plague of undeath has tainted them: their trees have grown sickly, and murlocs and creatures of animated plants now roam the islets. Deep fissures in the lakebed below the surface hint at their volcanic origin.

233.name: Ambermill
233.description: Ambermill is a human town in southern Silverpine Forest, southwest of Lordamere Lake, held by the forces of the Kirin Tor of Dalaran. Home to some two thousand people, including soldiers and wizards, it is the only true human settlement remaining in the forest. Before the Third War, Ambermill was a quiet lumber town, but the wizards of Dalaran discovered that it lies atop a dormant ley line node, and they have since fortified it and seek to reactivate the node for their own purposes. Dalaran's soldiers protect the town from the Forsaken and the forest's other dangers, and the Forsaken watch the wizards' activities with deep suspicion. The town's inn is known for its venison stew.

235.name: Fenris Keep
235.description: Fenris Keep is a gloomy fortress on Fenris Isle in the center of Lordamere Lake, once the seat of Silverpine Forest's lordship and an important military outpost of the Kingdom of Lordaeron, guarding the lake and the approaches to the capital. When the Scourge came, the keep fell through betrayal from within, as an ambitious young mage allied himself with the undead; its inhabitants were murdered or forced to flee. Now the traitor commands a large force of plague-ridden Rot Hide gnolls from the keep, and they hungrily attack anyone who approaches. The keep's halls are dark and cold, and an air of treachery hangs over them.

236.name: Shadowfang Keep
236.description: Shadowfang Keep is a dark, brooding castle on a high bluff in southern Silverpine Forest, overlooking Pyrewood Village near the borders of Gilneas. It was once the home of Baron Silverlaine, but it was seized by the demented archmage Arugal, who summoned savage worgen to aid the Alliance against the Scourge, only for the creatures to turn on their allies. Arugal, driven mad by guilt and dark magic, now calls the worgen his children and rules the keep with them, spreading their curse across the forest. Twisted spirits, undead servants, and worgen fill its halls, and its towers loom ominously over the forest. Few who enter its gates return.

237.name: The Decrepit Ferry
237.description: The Decrepit Ferry is a ruined dock on the shore of Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest, once the site of a bustling ferry service that carried goods and people to and from Fenris Isle. The farmsteads nearby sold their crops to the island's lord, and the ferryman earned a small fee for each crossing. When the Scourge invaded, the ferryman was murdered, the ferry destroyed, and ghouls, skeletons, and Rot Hide gnolls overran the docks. Now the ruined pier creaks in the wind, and the area is hazardous to travelers.

238.name: Malden's Orchard
238.description: Malden's Orchard is a small orchard in northern Silverpine Forest, named for its former owner, who was forced to flee when the Scourge invaded Lordaeron. The trees are dark and evergreen, but their fruit has not been picked in years. Large numbers of black worgs have recently taken up residence around the orchard and its single small cottage, making it a dangerous place for travelers. The orchard is quiet and overgrown, a lonely remnant of happier days.

239.name: The Ivar Patch
239.description: The Ivar Patch is a pumpkin farm in northern Silverpine Forest that was once prosperous and pleasant, employing many farmhands and servants. When the Scourge ravaged Lordaeron, the farmer, his family, and his workers all succumbed to the plague and became rotting ghouls. Now the undead farmer and his ghoulish household stalk the overgrown fields, attacking anyone who comes near. The rotting pumpkins and decaying farmhouse give the place a grim and eerie air.

240.name: The Dead Field
240.description: The Dead Field is a decrepit, abandoned farm in northern Silverpine Forest. Little is known of its former inhabitants, but it has recently become a base for the plague-ridden Rot Hide gnolls, servants of the Scourge, whose increasing numbers suggest that something is being planned. A banshee is said to watch over the gnolls, appearing when they are attacked. The fields are barren and grey, and the air is heavy with the stench of death.

305.name: North Tide's Run
305.description: North Tide's Run is the northwestern shoreline of Silverpine Forest, a stretch of beach and the thin strip of the Great Sea beyond. Its most prominent feature is a broken, partially submerged ship lying at the water's edge. The coast is cold and windswept, and the plague-tainted forest comes down almost to the sand. The site holds special significance for the tauren druids, who make pilgrimages here as part of their sacred rites.

306.name: South Tide's Run
306.description: South Tide's Run is the southwestern coast of Silverpine Forest, bordering the Great Sea. Before the plague and the closing of the Greymane Wall, it was a popular bathing spot for the people of Gilneas and Pyrewood, its sandy beaches and gentle waves offering a pleasant escape. Now it is quiet and deserted, and the waves wash up on an empty shore. The worgen of the southern forest sometimes roam the beaches at night.

927.name: The Shining Strand
927.description: The Shining Strand is the shoreline of Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest, stretching from the ruins of the old capital in the north to the range of rough hills that divides Silverpine from the Alterac Mountains. Once the shore sparkled in the sun, giving it its name, but now the Vile Fin tribe of murlocs has built several settlements along the strand, making it very dangerous for travelers. The lake's waters lap gently against the sand, and the murlocs' gurgling cries echo across the water.

928.name: North Tide's Hollow
928.description: North Tide's Hollow is a wooded area of Silverpine Forest just north of the Sepulcher, one of the many haunts of the Moonrage worgen, servants of the archmage Arugal. The worgen have set up crude encampments here, with only the barest necessities, and they attack any who stray into their territory. The hollow is dark and misty, and the howls of the worgen echo through the trees.

1338.name: Lordamere Lake
1338.description: On the Silverpine side, the cold waters of Lordamere Lake stretch east from the Shining Strand toward the distant shores of the Alterac Mountains. The lake is dotted with islands, the largest of which, Fenris Isle, looms with its dark keep in the center. Vile Fin murlocs dwell along the shores, and the waters are grey and still under the misty sky. Ages ago, an ancient plague killed off all the aquatic life in the lake, and the waters are eerily empty of fish.

2398.name: The Great Sea
2398.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the western coast of Silverpine Forest, rolling in grey and cold onto the beaches of North Tide's Run and South Tide's Run. The sea is often rough, driven by strong winds from the west, and the wrecks of ships lie half-buried in the sand. The plague-tainted forest comes down to the shore, and the mist drifting in from the sea mingles with the ghostly fog among the trees.

130.description: Silverpine Forest is a vast, ancient wood stretching along the rugged western coast of Lordaeron, south of Tirisfal Glades and west of Lordamere Lake. Once a verdant and lively forest protected by the Alliance, it is characterized by tall, silver-barked pines towering over grassy knolls and mossy overhangs. Since the Third War, when the Scourge invaded, burned the crops, and massacred the people, the forest has become haunted and wild: its trees are pale and sickly from the plague, ghostly mists drift between them, and an eerie silence is broken only by unnatural howls. Razed farmsteads and abandoned mines dot the land. The Forsaken control the northern forest from their outpost at the Sepulcher and wage a constant guerrilla war against the plague-ridden Rot Hide gnolls, who serve a traitorous mage from the island of Fenris in Lordamere Lake. The few remaining humans hold the south: the wizards and soldiers of Dalaran guard the town of Ambermill and study the plague, while the people of Pyrewood Village bear a terrible curse that turns them into savage worgen at night. The curse is believed to come from the archmage Arugal, who dwells in the dark towers of Shadowfang Keep with his worgen. At the southern edge of the forest stands the Greymane Wall, behind which the kingdom of Gilneas has sealed itself away from the world.

139.name: Eastern Plaguelands

2258.name: The Fungal Vale
2258.description: The Fungal Vale is one of the most corrupted areas of the Eastern Plaguelands, where the plague of undeath has taken its strongest hold over the land. The ground is a dark purple, giant mushrooms rise from the soil, and a murky haze fills the valley. The vale is infested with the Scourge and the Cult of the Damned, and rich veins of ore can be found among its rocks. It lies north of the Marris Stead and the Crown Guard Tower.

2260.name: The Marris Stead
2260.description: The Marris Stead is a farmstead on a small ridge in the western Eastern Plaguelands, near the border with the Western Plaguelands. It is the long-time family home of Nathanos Marris, known as the Blightcaller, a former ranger lord who was raised as one of the Forsaken and now serves the Banshee Queen as her champion. Despite being hunted by the Alliance, he still makes the stead his home. The farm is grim and desolate, and its master's presence makes it a dangerous place for those he deems his enemies.

2261.name: The Undercroft
2261.description: The Undercroft is a crypt in the southwestern Eastern Plaguelands, home to a band of undead trolls led by a fearsome undead dire troll. The trolls raid the Argent Dawn's grave pit at Light's Hope Chapel to steal bodies. The crypt is dark and foul, and the undead within attack anyone who enters.

2262.name: Darrowshire
2262.description: Darrowshire is a ruined town in the southern Eastern Plaguelands, the site of one of the bloodiest battles of the Third War. A Scourge army led by a ghoul lord and a death knight attacked the town, and although the paladins and militia of Darrowshire fought valiantly, they could not stave off the endless legions of undead, and the defenders and civilians alike were slaughtered. Today Darrowshire is silent, a place where only ghosts and memories remain, and its fallen defenders now wander the Plaguelands as ghouls in the service of the Scourge. On rare nights, it is said, the ghosts of the town reenact the terrible battle.

2263.name: Crown Guard Tower
2263.description: Crown Guard Tower is a ruined watchtower in the southwestern Eastern Plaguelands, overlooking the main road. It is one of the four ruined towers that the Alliance and the Horde fight to control, for whoever holds them gains an advantage in the region. The tower's walls are broken and crumbling, and the surrounding land is blighted and grey.

2264.name: Corin's Crossing
2264.description: Corin's Crossing was once a prosperous trading town at the crossroads connecting Andorhal, Stratholme, and Tyr's Hand, surrounded by the farmlands of Lordaeron. When the Scourge turned the region into the Plaguelands, Corin's Crossing became an outpost of the undead, and now it is crawling with their minions. Invisible servants of the Scourge patrol its streets, watching for intruders. Travelers are advised to give the town a wide berth.

2265.name: Scarlet Base Camp
2265.description: The Scarlet Base Camp is a small barricaded fortification on the eastern banks of Lake Mereldar, not far from the Scarlet Crusade's bastion of Tyr's Hand. The Crusade uses it as an outpost to watch the roads and strike at the Scourge. The camp is guarded by zealous Scarlet soldiers, who attack anyone they deem impure.

2266.name: Tyr's Hand
2266.description: Tyr's Hand is a fortified city in the southeastern Eastern Plaguelands, once a large port and a center of trade with the nearby elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas. Founded by pilgrims and named for a legendary hero, it has a long history of hardship, having been razed by the Horde during the Second War and later rebuilt. During the Third War, the Scourge laid siege to the city but could never breach it, and its garrison declared its loyalty to the Scarlet Crusade. Today Tyr's Hand is the regional headquarters and religious center of the Crusade, home to some nine thousand inhabitants and the great Scarlet Basilica. It is relatively untouched by the plague, the only patch of greenery in the bleak Eastern Plaguelands, and its fanatical defenders trust no outsiders.

2267.name: The Scarlet Basilica
2267.description: The Scarlet Basilica is a great cathedral within the walls of Tyr's Hand in the Eastern Plaguelands, the high seat of religious power for the Scarlet Crusade. Built in the style of Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, it is a grand edifice of white stone and crimson banners, where the Crusade's priests and paladins worship and plan their holy war against the undead. The basilica is heavily guarded, and only the faithful of the Crusade are welcome within.

2268.name: Light's Hope Chapel
2268.description: Light's Hope Chapel is the Argent Dawn's base of operations in the Eastern Plaguelands, standing on a hill in the far east of the region. It is a last bastion of the Light in a land blanketed in darkness, welcoming members of the Alliance and the Horde alike who would lend their strength to the fight against the Scourge. Beneath the chapel lies a catacomb housing the remains of the heroes of Lordaeron, many of whom were exhumed and moved here so they could not be raised by the Lich King. The chapel is said to be protected by a holy power that the undead cannot easily overcome. Gryphons and wind riders connect it with the cities of both factions.

2269.name: Browman Mill
2269.description: Browman Mill is a haunted mill just north of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a working mill serving the surrounding farms, it is now crawling with skeletons, banshees, and abominations. The mill's great wheel creaks in the wind, and the undead around it make it a dangerous place.

2270.name: The Noxious Glade
2270.description: The Noxious Glade is a secluded glade on a hill north of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands, suffering from a blight even worse than that of the surrounding lands. The air is a thick, sickly green, and the ground is a dark purple. A plague cauldron and several ziggurats stand within the glade, guarded by the Scourge. A cave at its southern end leads toward Death's Breach and the ruins of the Scarlet Enclave.

2271.name: Eastwall Tower
2271.description: Eastwall Tower is a ruined watchtower in the eastern Eastern Plaguelands, close to Light's Hope Chapel. It is one of the four ruined towers that the Alliance and the Horde fight to control, and its proximity to the chapel makes it the most hotly contested of all. The tower's walls are broken and its battlements crumbling.

2272.name: Northdale
2272.description: Northdale is a destroyed town in the Eastern Plaguelands, north of Light's Hope Chapel and southeast of the road to Quel'Thalas. Its ruins are inhabited by banshees and invisible watchers of the Scourge, and the nearby lake is populated by corrupted water elementals. It was here that the son of Tirion Fordring renounced the Order of the Silver Hand and joined the Scarlet Crusade.

2273.name: Zul'Mashar
2273.description: Zul'Mashar is a forest troll city in the northeastern Eastern Plaguelands, once the capital of the Mossflayer tribe. Long years of fighting with the humans of Lordaeron and the coming of the plague have reduced it to a shadow of its former glory, and it is now in danger of becoming a bastion of the undead, as its own people are being covertly transformed. At its heart rises the great ziggurat of Mazra'Alor. The city is dark and dangerous, and the Mossflayer trolls who remain are hostile to all outsiders.

2274.name: Mazra'Alor
2274.description: Mazra'Alor is the great ziggurat temple at the heart of Zul'Mashar in the Eastern Plaguelands, built by the forest trolls in ages past. It is populated by shadow hunters of the Mossflayer tribe, who perform their dark rituals atop its stone platforms. The temple is overgrown with vines and fungus, and the air around it is heavy with the taint of the plague.

2275.name: Northpass Tower
2275.description: Northpass Tower is a ruined watchtower in the northern Eastern Plaguelands, lying along the road to the Ghostlands and Quel'Thalas. It is one of the four ruined towers that the Alliance and the Horde fight to control, and an altar within its walls is said to grant strength to those who hold it. The tower overlooks the blighted roads leading north.

2276.name: Quel'Lithien Lodge
2276.description: The Quel'Lithien Lodge is a high elven hunting lodge near the entrance to Quel'Thalas in the northern Eastern Plaguelands, one of the two major concentrations of high elves remaining in Lordaeron. It is home to a band of rangers, pathstriders, and woodsmen who remain loyal to the old ways of the quel'dorei and refuse to join the blood elves. The lodge is built in the graceful style of Quel'Thalas, and its rangers keep a vigilant watch over the surrounding lands.

2277.name: Plaguewood
2277.description: Plaguewood is a large, putrid forest in the northern Eastern Plaguelands, stretching south from the gates of Stratholme to Terrordale. It is heavily occupied by the Scourge, who have built ziggurats and slaughterhouses throughout the area. The blight has dramatically altered the landscape: the soil resembles a sponge, and fungus grows to enormous proportions, giant mushrooms dwarfing the trees and belching dark brown gas. The great necropolis of Naxxramas once floated above Plaguewood, before it departed for Northrend. Scarlet Crusaders still travel the road to and from Stratholme, attacking the undead and anyone else they meet.

2279.name: Stratholme
2279.description: Stratholme was once the northernmost and second most populous city of the Kingdom of Lordaeron, the city where the Order of the Silver Hand was founded. At the start of the Third War, Prince Arthas purged the city to stop the spread of the plague, slaughtering its people before they could rise as undead, and the Scourge soon moved in. Today Stratholme is the Scourge's capital in Lordaeron, and its ruins burn to this day. The city is divided between the undead forces of Baron Rivendare and the Scarlet Crusade, who hold its western districts and battle fiercely to retake the city. Its walls and gates loom over the surrounding Plaguewood, and few who enter return.

2299.name: Darrowmere Lake
2299.description: On the side of the Eastern Plaguelands, Darrowmere Lake lies to the southwest, its polluted waters fed by rivers flowing from the north and east. The lake was the site of many naval battles in the Second War, and it is said that Uther the Lightbringer founded the Order of the Silver Hand on its shores. Now the Scourge's filth pollutes its waters, and dead fish wash up on its banks.

2619.name: Thondroril River
2619.description: On the side of the Eastern Plaguelands, the Thondroril River marks the western border of the region, flowing south from the northern mountains into Darrowmere Lake. Its banks are lined with ruined farmhouses and blighted trees, and maggots, bats, spiders, and plague-ridden beasts roam its shores. Near its northern reaches lies the entrance to the Terrorweb Tunnel.

2621.name: Lake Mereldar
2621.description: Lake Mereldar is a large lake in the Eastern Plaguelands, south of Corin's Crossing and west of Tyr's Hand. Its waters are polluted by the plague and infested with corrupted water elementals. The Scarlet Crusade maintains a base camp on its eastern shore. Once a beautiful lake, it is now dark and still, its shores grey and lifeless.

2622.name: Pestilent Scar
2622.description: The Pestilent Scar is a deep chasm in the blighted earth of the Eastern Plaguelands. Unlike the Infectis Scar, it appears to be a natural gorge, possibly a lake that dried up after the plague struck. Now it is inhabited by oozes, and a wrong step on its crumbling edges could lead to a fatal fall.

2623.name: The Infectis Scar
2623.description: The Infectis Scar is a deep chasm in the blighted earth of the Eastern Plaguelands, created by dark magic. It is said that when the runesword of a Scourge death knight was broken against the shield of a dwarven captain near Corin's Crossing, the cursed blade sank into the earth and tore open this great wound in the land. The chasm is dark and foreboding, and its depths are said to still radiate evil.

2624.name: Blackwood Lake
2624.description: Blackwood Lake is a polluted lake in the Eastern Plaguelands, its dark waters infested by corrupted water elementals. It is said that the head of a fearsome ghoul lord was cast into its depths after the battle of Darrowshire. The lake is surrounded by withered trees and blighted earth.

2625.name: Eastwall Gate
2625.description: Eastwall Gate is the side entrance to the city of Stratholme in the Eastern Plaguelands, leading directly into the city's Elders' Square. The gate is heavily guarded by the Scourge, and the walls around it are scarred and blackened by fire. Beyond the gate lie the burning ruins of the undead capital.

2626.name: Terrorweb Tunnel
2626.description: The Terrorweb Tunnel is a long, winding tunnel through the mountains northwest of Terrordale in the Eastern Plaguelands, stretching from Terrordale in the north to the banks of the Thondroril River in the south. It is full of crypt fiends, the undead nerubians of the Scourge, and their webs cover its walls. A powerful nerubian overseer is said to stalk the tunnel, preying on the unwary.

2627.name: Terrordale
2627.description: Terrordale is a ghost town in the northwestern corner of the Eastern Plaguelands, one of the first human settlements to be overrun by the Scourge. Its former name has been forgotten, and now it is known only by the terror that consumed it. The town lies west of Plaguewood and Stratholme, near the entrance to the Terrorweb Tunnel, and its ruins are haunted by crypt fiends and undead. A single delusional merchant is said to remain among the ruins.

4067.name: Plaguewood Tower
4067.description: Plaguewood Tower is a ruined watchtower deep within Plaguewood, the putrid fungal forest outside the gates of Stratholme. It is one of the four ruined towers that the Alliance and the Horde fight to control, and whoever holds it can call upon spectral gryphons to carry them swiftly to the other towers. The tower is surrounded by giant mushrooms and the noxious gases of the forest.

4281.name: Acherus: The Ebon Hold
4281.description: Acherus, the Ebon Hold, is a massive dark necropolis floating in the sky above the far eastern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, casting a long shadow over the lands of the Scarlet Enclave below. Raised by the Scourge and said to be so powerful that even the great necropolis of Naxxramas could not withstand it, it is the home of the death knights, fearsome warriors raised from the corpses of fallen heroes and bound to the power of the runeblade and unholy magic. Within its cold, grim halls, new death knights are forged: they train in the arts of frost, blood, and unholy power, inscribe their weapons at glowing runeforges, and learn to command the dead. Bones, chains, and dark banners fill its chambers, the air is cold as the grave, and the moans of the damned echo through its corridors. From below, the necropolis is a silent, ominous shadow in the orange skies above the Plaguelands, and few among the living have ever set foot inside.

4544.name: Death's Breach
4544.description: Death's Breach is a high plateau in the far east of the Eastern Plaguelands, lying directly beneath the floating necropolis of Acherus and overlooking the lands of the Scarlet Enclave to the east. It serves as the landing ground and staging area for the death knights of Acherus, and a portal of dark magic connects it with the necropolis above. From its edge, the farms of Havenshire, the town of New Avalon, and the distant sea can be seen. A cave leads from the plateau west to the Noxious Glade. The plateau is barren and windswept, and an unholy chill hangs over it.

4545.name: Abandoned Mine
4545.description: This old mine lies in the hills of the Scarlet Enclave in the far east of the Eastern Plaguelands, carved into the rock near the towns of New Avalon and Havenshire. Its ore once supplied the forges of the Scarlet Crusade's last refuge in the east, and its tunnels are lined with mine carts, rails, timber supports, and tools. Deep in the shadow of the necropolis Acherus, it is a dark and dangerous place, and the war that rages over the enclave has not spared it.

4546.name: Ruins of the Scarlet Enclave
4546.description: The Scarlet Enclave is the name given to the far eastern lands of the Eastern Plaguelands around the town of New Avalon and the farmlands of Havenshire, which became the last refuge of the Scarlet Crusade in this part of Lordaeron. Lying on the coast beyond Tyr's Hand, the region was long spared the worst of the plague: its fields of pumpkins and grain, its orchards, its chapel, and the harbor of King's Harbor sustained the Crusade's soldiers and the civilians who sheltered under their protection. Yet the enclave lies in the shadow of the necropolis Acherus, which hangs in the sky to the west, and it has borne the full fury of the war against the Scourge. Its towns, fields, and harbor have known terrible bloodshed, and the land bears the scars of fire, plague, and battle.

139.description: The Eastern Plaguelands are the more heavily devastated half of the Plaguelands, the remnants of the northern Kingdom of Lordaeron, lying east of the Western Plaguelands and north of the Hinterlands. Once beautiful and brimming with farms and villages, the region was governed from Stratholme, Lordaeron's second greatest city, where the Order of the Silver Hand was founded. At the start of the Third War, Prince Arthas purged Stratholme to stop the plague, breaking with Uther and the Silver Hand, and after he returned as a death knight, the Scourge swept over the land. Today the Scourge's rule here is nearly absolute: the ground is brown and sick, the trees have been twisted into giant mushrooms, and the air is choked with orange and sickly green mist. The burning ruins of Stratholme are the Scourge's capital in Lordaeron, Plaguewood is filled with ziggurats and slaughterhouses, and undead, necromancers, and cultists prowl the land. The Scarlet Crusade still holds the fortified city of Tyr's Hand in the southeast and fights a bitter, fanatical war against the undead. At Light's Hope Chapel, the Argent Dawn maintains a last bastion of the Light, welcoming all who would fight the Scourge, and above the far eastern lands hovers Acherus, the Ebon Hold, a vast dark necropolis and the home of the death knights. Amani forest trolls strike from the north, and four ruined towers across the land are contested by the Alliance and the Horde.

141.name: Teldrassil

186.name: Dolanaar
186.description: Dolanaar is a night elf village in the heart of Teldrassil, east of Darnassus and southwest of Shadowglen. Its graceful wooden buildings rest among the great trees, and it is a proving ground for young druids and the first true village that many young night elves visit after leaving Shadowglen. The village has an inn, and teachers and Sentinels guide newcomers in their training. From here, the Sentinels and druids watch over the surrounding forest, which has grown troubled by the corruption creeping through Teldrassil.

188.name: Shadowglen
188.description: Shadowglen is a small, twilit glade in the northeastern part of Teldrassil, bathed in a quiet, eternal dusk and ringed by mountains, with only a single path leading south toward Dolanaar. At its center rises the great tree Aldrassil, a haven for young druids and the place where many night elves begin their training. Wisps drift through the air, nightsabers and young grells roam the clearings, and a spider-infested cave lies in the far northwest. Shadowglen is one of the most secure places in the night elf lands, protected by watchful Sentinels.

256.name: Aldrassil
256.description: Aldrassil is a giant tree at the center of Shadowglen in Teldrassil, within whose hollowed trunk and branches a small village has been built. It is a haven for young druids, priestesses, Sentinels, and other night elves beginning their training, and its leader dwells at the very top of the tree. Spiraling ramps wind around the trunk, connecting its levels, and moonlight filters through its leaves. Aldrassil is the heart of Shadowglen, a place of learning and peace.

257.name: Shadowthread Cave
257.description: Shadowthread Cave is a cave in the northwestern corner of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. It has always been home to the great spiders of Teldrassil, but recently the spiders have become increasingly hostile, and the cave has grown much more dangerous. A particularly large and vicious spider is said to lurk in its depths. The cave is dark and covered in thick webs.

258.name: Fel Rock
258.description: Fel Rock is a cave just north of Dolanaar in Teldrassil, once a beautiful grotto but now corrupted by demonic influence. It is infested with grells, the small imp-like creatures of the forest, and it is said that a vicious satyr dwells within. The cave's corruption is a disturbing sign of the darkness creeping into Teldrassil.

259.name: Lake Al'Ameth
259.description: Lake Al'Ameth is the largest body of water on Teldrassil aside from the great pools of Darnassus, lying south of Dolanaar. Its clear waters reflect the violet twilight of the forest, and its shores are lined with tall trees and flowers. Lately, many enraged timberlings, small living trees, have been seen along its shores, and the lake is no longer as safe as it once was.

260.name: Starbreeze Village
260.description: Starbreeze Village is a small night elf village south of Shadowglen and east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. It was once a peaceful settlement of a few graceful houses, but it has been overrun by corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe, an alarming sign of the darkness that bleeds into Teldrassil. The village's former inhabitants have fled, and the furbolgs' crude totems now stand among the elven buildings.

261.name: Gnarlpine Hold
261.description: Gnarlpine Hold is a furbolg settlement in the far southwestern corner of Teldrassil, the home of the Gnarlpine tribe. Once friendly to the night elves, the Gnarlpine furbolgs have been driven to madness and savagery by the corruption spreading through the great tree, and they now attack anyone who comes near. Their hold is a crude collection of huts and totems among the trees.

262.name: Ban'ethil Barrow Den
262.description: The Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a small barrow den in Teldrassil, built by the night elves as a sacred resting place for the druids of the talon, who slumber within while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. The den has recently been taken over by the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs, and it has become a dangerous place for a lone night elf. Its chambers are carved into the living wood of the tree.

263.name: The Cleft
263.description: The Cleft is a mysterious cave in Teldrassil, lying northeast of Ban'ethil Hollow and northwest of Dolanaar. A hidden yet clear path leads up to it, but the cave itself is empty and silent, devoid of any sign of life or purpose. Its significance, if any, remains a mystery.

264.name: The Oracle Glade
264.description: The Oracle Glade is a sacred shrine in the northwestern part of Teldrassil, home to one of the island's moonwells and to the magical Oracle Tree, an ancient and mysterious tree shaped like a bear with an eagle rising from its back. The tree emerged without warning, and the Cenarion Circle studies it closely, believing that it may one day reveal secrets about the origins of the World Tree. Harpies have recently moved into the glade, and a corrupted spider matriarch is said to lurk in its corners.

265.name: Wellspring River
265.description: The Wellspring River flows from a natural spring deep within the great tree Teldrassil, running north from Wellspring Lake before cascading over the edge of the tree in a great waterfall to the sea far below. Its clear waters wind through the twilit forest, but crazed timberlings now patrol its banks, attacking anyone who wanders near.

266.name: Wellspring Lake
266.description: Wellspring Lake is a small lake northeast of Darnassus and southeast of the Oracle Glade in Teldrassil, fed by a natural spring deep within the World Tree and drained by the Wellspring River. Once a favorite spot for night elven fishermen, it is now home to corrupted timberlings, and nightsabers and spiders prowl the surrounding woods.

478.name: Pools of Arlithrien
478.description: The Pools of Arlithrien are a collection of small, peaceful pools in western Teldrassil, south of the entrance to Darnassus. A lone moonwell stands here, abandoned by the night elves due to the threat of the Gnarlpine furbolgs. Once a tranquil retreat, the pools are now home to hostile wildlife, though their silvery waters still shimmer beautifully in the twilight.

702.name: Rut'theran Village
702.description: Rut'theran Village is a small night elf harbor at the very foot of the great tree Teldrassil, nestled among its enormous roots where they meet the sea. It is the island's gateway to the outside world: ships sail from its pier to Auberdine in Darkshore, hippogryphs fly from its roost, and a shimmering portal carries travelers up to Darnassus, far above in the branches. The village is also one of the main breeding grounds for hippogryphs, and eggs from across Kalimdor are brought here for care. It is a humble but friendly place, a taste of the majestic land above.

736.name: Ban'ethil Hollow
736.description: Ban'ethil Hollow is a small ravine in Teldrassil, south of the road leading from Dolanaar to Darnassus. It is filled with hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs, who occasionally ambush travelers on the road, and the Ban'ethil Barrow Den lies at its far end. The hollow is shadowy and overgrown, and travelers are wise to exercise caution.

2322.name: The Veiled Sea
2322.description: The waters of the Veiled Sea surround the great tree Teldrassil, stretching away in every direction from its colossal trunk and roots. The sea is deep and often misty, and the tree's waterfalls cascade into it from the heights above. Ships sail between Rut'theran Village and Auberdine in Darkshore across these waters, and the coast of Kalimdor can be seen on clear days to the east.

141.description: Teldrassil is a colossal tree rising from the Veiled Sea off the northwestern coast of Kalimdor, so vast that a forested land of hills, lakes, and rivers has grown upon its mighty boughs, high above the clouds. After the Third War, when the night elves lost their immortality with the sacrifice of the World Tree Nordrassil, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm convinced the druids of the Cenarion Circle to grow a new World Tree, and they named it Teldrassil, meaning crown of the earth. The night elves built their new capital, Darnassus, among its western branches, and the land atop the tree became their new homeland, bathed in an eternal, gentle twilight of violet and silver. Yet the tree was not blessed by the Dragon Aspects as Nordrassil had been, and its growth has proven flawed. A creeping corruption has begun to spread through the forest: furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe have turned savage, timberlings have grown enraged, harpies nest in the north, and satyrs and grells lurk in its caves. The vigilant Sentinels and the druids work tirelessly to protect their new home, while young night elves begin their training in the sheltered vale of Shadowglen. The forest is peaceful and beautiful, filled with ancient trees, moonwells, glowing wisps, nightsabers, and owls, and at the foot of the great trunk lies the harbor of Rut'theran Village, the island's link to the wider world.

148.name: Darkshore

442.name: Auberdine
442.description: Auberdine is a night elf port town on the western coast of Darkshore, the main center of civilization in the region. Damaged during the Sundering and later wars, it was rebuilt after the Third War, and it has grown from a small outpost of two hundred souls into a thriving town of several thousand. Its buildings are made mostly of wood rather than stone, and the town is often cloaked in a dark, mysterious mist. Ships sail from its docks to Rut'theran Village in Teldrassil, to the Azuremyst Isles, and to Stormwind, making it a vital crossroads. Its residents are friendly and outgoing for night elves, but beneath their warm demeanor lies a grim determination to protect their home.

443.name: Ruins of Mathystra
443.description: The Ruins of Mathystra are the remains of an ancient night elven city in northern Darkshore, just past the Tower of Althalaxx. Mathystra was devastated by the destruction of the Well of Eternity and has long since been abandoned by the night elves. Its broken pillars and crumbling walls are now inhabited by the Stormscale naga, who aggressively guard against intruders. The ruins still hold scattered relics of the ancient Highborne.

444.name: Tower of Althalaxx
444.description: The Tower of Althalaxx is an ancient tower in northern Darkshore, standing apart from the ruined twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran. In the days before the Sundering, it was the residence of the Highborne governor appointed by Queen Azshara to rule those towns. Ten thousand years later, a cult of warlocks known as the Dark Strand has gathered at the tower, and a foul satyr is said to be among them. Why they have assembled here remains a dark mystery.

445.name: Cliffspring Falls
445.description: Cliffspring Falls is a waterfall in northern Darkshore, the source of the Cliffspring River. Once a pure waterfall, the cave behind it has become corrupted like much of the surrounding land; some believe the corruption seeps from nearby Felwood, while others blame the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who have been found deep within. Naga also crawl through the caves. The falls are beautiful, but the water is no longer pure.

446.name: Bashal'Aran
446.description: Bashal'Aran is an ancient night elven ruin northeast of Auberdine in Darkshore, one of the twin towns founded by Queen Azshara for her favored Highborne servants before the Sundering. The ruins are now overrun by demonic minions, sprites and satyrs, which feed upon the magical energies left among the ancient stones and grow ever stronger. The broken columns and overgrown courtyards still hint at the town's former grandeur.

447.name: Ameth'Aran
447.description: Ameth'Aran is an ancient night elven ruin southeast of Auberdine in Darkshore, one of the twin towns where Queen Azshara's Highborne freely practiced their powerful magics before the Sundering. It is now haunted by the restless spirits of the Highborne who once dwelt within its walls. Among the ruins lie great stone tablets inscribed with the story of the town and its fall, one of the few records of that ancient time.

448.name: Grove of the Ancients
448.description: The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred ruin of an ancient night elven temple in southeastern Darkshore, nestled near the mountains and built around the rushing Wildbend River. It is the meeting place of the Circle of Ancients, and an Ancient of Lore dwells here, together with a few night elves and a sleeping druid. The grove is a place of quiet wisdom, though the river that flows through it carries the taint of Felwood.

449.name: The Master's Glaive
449.description: The Master's Glaive is a mysterious monument in southwestern Darkshore: a massive adamantine glaive embedded in an enormous, shell-like skull surrounded by a small lake. The night elves consider it a sacred place, believing that only the titans could have wielded such a weapon, and many think that a titan slew one of the Old Gods or their minions here. The cultists of the Twilight's Hammer have claimed the site, believing the skull to be the remains of a divine being, and they have raised a dark altar nearby. An ancient one of the region speaks of an old lord of the earth who fell here.

450.name: Remtravel's Excavation
450.description: Remtravel's Excavation is a dig site in southern Darkshore, named after the famous dwarven archaeologist who discovered a most unusual fossil here. The site has since been invaded by troggs and huge stone golems unearthed during the dig, and entering it without proper care can be very hazardous. Scaffolds, tents, and digging tools are scattered among the excavations.

452.name: Mist's Edge
452.description: Mist's Edge is by far the longest stretch of coast in Darkshore, reaching from Auberdine in the south to the region's northern tip. It is dominated by gloomy bays and grey beaches, often littered with the huge carcasses of sea creatures and dotted with the wrecks of sunken ships. Murlocs are an ever-present threat, and crabs scuttle along the entire shore. The mist that rolls in from the sea gives the coast its name.

453.name: The Long Wash
453.description: The Long Wash is a desolate stretch of sand running south from Auberdine along the coast of Darkshore. The shore is gloomy and dark under the perpetual overcast skies, and the beach is littered with debris and the carcasses of dead sea creatures. Murlocs have recently been showing up along the coastline with greater frequency.

454.name: Wildbend River
454.description: The Wildbend River is a tainted river in southern Darkshore, flowing past the Grove of the Ancients. Its source lies in the corrupted lands of Felwood, and the taint carried downstream has spread to the surrounding landscape, wildlife, and furbolg tribes of Darkshore. Its waters are murky and foul, and swimming in it is not recommended.

455.name: Blackwood Den
455.description: Blackwood Den is an area in the far south of Darkshore, near the border with Ashenvale, made up of several camps of corrupted furbolgs of the Blackwood tribe and a small cave.
