The furbolgs, once friendly to the night elves, have been driven mad by the corruption of Felwood and attack anyone who comes near.

456.name: Cliffspring River
456.description: The Cliffspring River is a river in northern Darkshore, flowing from Cliffspring Falls out to the sea. Like so much of Darkshore, it has become tainted, and the wildlife that drinks from it often falls sick. Naga dwell along its course.

2077.name: Twilight Vale
2077.description: Twilight Vale is the name of the southern forests of Darkshore, a shadowy woodland of tall trees and dense undergrowth. Like the rest of the region, its woods are crawling with corrupted furbolgs, feral nightsabers, and rabid bears, and travelers are advised to stick to the roads. The forest grows thicker as it stretches south toward Ashenvale.

2078.name: Twilight Shore
2078.description: The Twilight Shore is the most rugged stretch of coast in southern Darkshore, running south from the Long Wash toward Ashenvale. Its grey beaches are broken up by jutting cliffs and small islands, murlocs are abundant along the shore, and aggressive threshadons lurk in the waters. The coast is wild and beautiful, especially at dusk.

2326.name: The Veiled Sea
2326.description: The waters of the Veiled Sea wash the western coast of Darkshore, rolling in grey and cold onto its rocky beaches. The sea is often stormy, with strong winds and frequent fog, and the wrecks of ships litter the shallow waters near the shore. Ships sail from Auberdine across these waters to Teldrassil, the Azuremyst Isles, and the Eastern Kingdoms, and the great tree of Teldrassil can be seen rising from the sea to the west.

148.description: Darkshore is a long strip of rocky coast in northwestern Kalimdor, stretching south from the northern cliffs to the forests of Ashenvale, with the mountains of Felwood rising to the east. It is a land of shadowed woods, misty beaches, and crumbling ruins, where the weather is cold and stormy much of the time, rain and fog are common, and a wicked wind stirs up the grey waves. Once one of the most prosperous regions of the ancient Kaldorei empire, home to great cities such as Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, Darkshore was ravaged by the Great Sundering, and its ruins have stood empty for thousands of years. The night elves returned to rebuild the port of Auberdine, which now serves as the main link between the night elf lands, the Azuremyst Isles, and the Eastern Kingdoms. Beyond the village, the land is dangerous: the ruins are infested with naga, satyrs, grells, and the restless ghosts of the Highborne; cultists of the Dark Strand and the Twilight's Hammer lurk in hidden places; and the furbolgs of the region have been driven mad by the corruption flowing down the rivers from Felwood. Murlocs, crabs, and threshadons haunt the coast, and the wrecks of ships litter the shallow waters. Sentinels patrol the road from Auberdine south toward Ashenvale.

170.name: Lordamere Lake
170.description: Lordamere Lake is one of the largest lakes in the Eastern Kingdoms, a vast expanse of cold, grey water lying at the heart of the former Kingdom of Lordaeron. Its name means the Lake of Lordaeron, for the kingdom's capital city once stood proudly on its northern shore. Around its shores lay many of the greatest human realms of the age of the Alliance of Lordaeron: Lordaeron itself, the magical city of Dalaran, and the mountain kingdom of Alterac. Today the lake serves as a natural barrier between the Forsaken lands of Tirisfal Glades and Silverpine Forest to the west and the contested Alterac Mountains to the east. At its center lies Fenris Isle, with its dark keep now held by plague-ridden gnolls in league with the Scourge, while the Dawning Isles to the east form the broken rim of an ancient volcano. Ages ago, an ancient plague killed off all the aquatic life in the lake, and its waters are eerily empty. Vile Fin murlocs have built encampments along its shores and islands, and creatures of animated plants roam the isles. Mist often hangs over the water, and the ruins of the capital and the great crater where Dalaran once stood can be seen from its surface.

210.name: Icecrown

4417.name: Onslaught Harbor
4417.description: Onslaught Harbor is the base of the Scarlet Onslaught in Icecrown, a complex of islands off the western coast of the glacier. The harbor is built on a small island connected by a bridge to a larger one crowned by the Crimson Cathedral. Only the most battle-hardened Scarlet crusaders reside here, and with the gryphons they have taken, the base is very hard to conquer.

4467.name: Death's Rise
4467.description: Death's Rise is an outpost of the Knights of the Ebon Blade, a platform carved into the mountainside of western Icecrown, southwest of Jotunheim and east of Onslaught Harbor, reachable only through the air. It was once part of the vrykul's Balargarde Fortress, and the bodies of its former occupants still litter the ground. From here the death knights strike at the Scarlet Onslaught and the vrykul.

4470.name: The Hidden Hollow
4470.description: The Hidden Hollow is a heavily guarded cave on the shore of Onslaught Harbor in Icecrown, behind the Crimson Cathedral. It is said that the Grand Admiral of the Scarlet Onslaught resides within, and the rest of the Onslaught are forbidden from entering.

4477.name: The Shadow Vault
4477.description: The Shadow Vault is a Scourge fortress in northern Icecrown near Aldur'thar: The Desolation Gate, overlooking the North Sea, as if a part of Icecrown Citadel had wandered off to brood over the water, its bladed crown jutting from the mountains. It is a strong strategic position against the vrykul of Jotunheim, and the Knights of the Ebon Blade have fought the Scourge for control of it.

4492.name: Ufrang's Hall
4492.description: Ufrang's Hall is the great hall of the vrykul thane Ufrang the Mighty, west of the Shadow Vault in northern Icecrown, overlooking the Savage Ledge and guarded by the warriors of Jotunheim.

4496.name: Jotunheim
4496.description: Jotunheim is the largest vrykul village in Northrend, a string of buildings winding along the northwestern cliffs of Icecrown above the North Sea. It is where the vrykul were first awakened from their ages-long sleep, and it is second in importance to them only to Ymirheim. It culminates in Balargarde Fortress, which tries to put Utgarde Keep to shame in size and number of decorative skulls, and in the battle pit of Valhalas, vrykul fight to be raised among the Ymirjar, the elite warriors of King Ymiron's army in service of the Lich King.

4497.name: Savage Ledge
4497.description: The Savage Ledge is a ledge just west of the Shadow Vault in northern Icecrown, part of Jotunheim, where vrykul combatants test their might beside Ufrang's Hall.

4498.name: Halls of the Ancestors
4498.description: The Halls of the Ancestors are a mountain pass between Njorndar Village and the southern reaches of Jotunheim in Icecrown, where it is said ancient vrykul heroes lie slumbering.

4501.name: The Argent Vanguard
4501.description: The Argent Vanguard is the main forward base of the Argent Crusade in the Valley of Echoes of southeastern Icecrown, the first foothold the crusade established when it breached Icecrown under Highlord Tirion Fordring. It faces the Scourge fortress of Scourgeholme, and its battlements have withstood waves of undead of every kind, even frost wyrms.

4503.name: Ironwall Dam
4503.description: The Ironwall Dam is a massive dam of saronite separating Icecrown from Crystalsong Forest, holding back the waters of the Decrepit Flow, its openings and ramparts guarded by bloated undead horrors.

4504.name: Valley of Echoes
4504.description: The Valley of Echoes is the southeasternmost valley of Icecrown, entered by a natural ramp from Crystalsong Forest. Here the Argent Crusade built the Argent Vanguard, its first foothold in Icecrown, and crusaders battle the nerubian undead that lurk in webs among the ice.

4505.name: The Breach
4505.description: The Breach is a passage at the northern end of the Valley of Echoes in Icecrown, the opening the Argent Crusade forced through the Scourge's defenses toward Scourgeholme, held by crusaders against the undead beyond.

4506.name: Scourgeholme
4506.description: Scourgeholme is a Scourge fortress in eastern Icecrown, with a slaughterhouse and three ziggurats, among them a newer model. It faces the Argent Vanguard across the valley, and from it the Scourge sends waves of undead and frost wyrms against the crusaders.

4507.name: The Broken Front
4507.description: The Broken Front is the battlefield just south of Mord'rethar: The Death Gate in Icecrown. An Alliance offensive against the gate, launched under the cover of a blizzard, collided here with a Horde force, and Alliance, Horde, and Scourge all but annihilated one another. The Argent Crusade arrived too late to save more than a few; many of the dead and wounded still lie where they fell, and the Scourge holds the gate.

4508.name: Mord'rethar: The Death Gate
4508.description: Mord'rethar: The Death Gate is the first of the three great gates guarding Icecrown, its walls and gate built almost entirely of near-indestructible saronite and manned by massive Scourge constructs. Behind it lies the Valley of Lost Hope, and any army marching on Icecrown Citadel must break it first.

4509.name: The Bombardment
4509.description: The Bombardment is a battlefield southeast of Aldur'thar: The Desolation Gate in Icecrown, where Alliance and Horde bombers rain fire on the Scourge, its ground scarred and littered with crashed plague-spreading machines.

4510.name: Aldur'thar: The Desolation Gate
4510.description: Aldur'thar: The Desolation Gate is the second of the three great gates guarding Icecrown, its walls of near-indestructible saronite manned by massive Scourge constructs, with the Valley of Fallen Heroes behind it. The Alliance and the Horde have each built a small air base atop it, hidden from sight by strange infra-green energy, from which they launch bombing runs against the Scourge.

4511.name: The Skybreaker
4511.description: The Skybreaker is the Alliance gunship patrolling the skies above Icecrown, a marvel of gnomish and dwarven engineering driven by powerful propeller engines and armed with more than twenty broadside cannons, with a steel eagle head on its bow and a massive bomb in its lowest deck. Serving as the mobile base of the Alliance war effort against the Lich King, it often squares off against the Horde's Orgrim's Hammer.

4512.name: Orgrim's Hammer
4512.description: Orgrim's Hammer is the Horde gunship patrolling the skies above Icecrown, named in honor of Orgrim Doomhammer, the latest in goblin zeppelin engineering. It is held aloft by two great steel-armored balloons linked by a metal catwalk, and an enormous cannon juts from the mouth of a stone wolf head at its bow. Serving as the mobile base of the Horde in Icecrown, it often clashes with the Alliance's Skybreaker.

4513.name: Ymirheim
4513.description: Ymirheim is a village of the Ymirjar, the elite vrykul warriors of King Ymiron sworn to the Lich King, in the center of the rift valley of Icecrown. A ramshackle wooden vrykul town wrapping around a high mountain valley, it sits above most of the buildings of Icecrown and guards the saronite mines at its center. It is the most important place in Northrend to the vrykul.

4514.name: Saronite Mines
4514.description: The Saronite Mines lie at the heart of Ymirheim in Icecrown, where the vrykul force captured crusaders to dig saronite for the Scourge. Val'kyr cruelly drive the enslaved miners, who slowly lose their sanity in the depths.

4515.name: The Conflagration
4515.description: The Conflagration is the ground before Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate in Icecrown, named for the great blue flames burning in front of the gate, where the Lich King's elite soldiers have formed up to defend his citadel.

4516.name: Ironwall Rampart
4516.description: The Ironwall Rampart is a great saronite rampart south of the Shadow Vault in Icecrown, overlooking and dominating the Valley of Fallen Heroes below, a position any army must take before it can advance on Icecrown Citadel.

4517.name: Weeping Quarry
4517.description: The Weeping Quarry is a Scourge saronite mine south of the Shadow Vault in northwestern Icecrown, where undead laborers tear the ore from the earth and send it to feed the Lich King's forges.

4518.name: Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate
4518.description: Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate is the last of the three great gates guarding Icecrown, its walls of near-indestructible saronite manned by massive Scourge constructs. Behind it lies Icecrown Citadel, the seat of the Lich King's power.

4519.name: The Court of Bones
4519.description: The Court of Bones is the bleak expanse before Icecrown Citadel, between Malykriss, Corp'rethar, and the Cathedral of Darkness, guarded by the Lich King's Boneguard. It was here that Arthas Menethil fought and defeated Illidan Stormrage before entering the citadel to claim the Frozen Throne.

4520.name: Malykriss: The Vile Hold
4520.description: Malykriss: The Vile Hold is an unfinished Scourge necropolis in Icecrown, the cutting edge of Scourge construction, built entirely of saronite; if completed, it would be indestructible. It is the seat of the Lich King's metalworking, meant as a replacement for the lost necropolis of Acherus, and in the quarry below, new death knights are trained for his armies.

4521.name: Cathedral of Darkness
4521.description: The Cathedral of Darkness is a cathedral of saronite in southwestern Icecrown, near the citadel, where the zealots of the Cult of the Damned gather to worship the Lich King.

4522.name: Icecrown Citadel
4522.description: Icecrown Citadel is the greatest fortress of the Scourge and the last bastion of the Lich King, rising from the Icecrown Glacier as a cathedral of blades and claws made entirely of saronite. A fortress as large as a city, it is layer upon layer of cursed metal wrapped around the Frozen Throne, its towering spires visible from nearly anywhere in Northrend, and its halls crawl with the most vile and loyal of the Scourge. Within dwells the Lich King, a tyrant with nearly godlike power over his tireless legions, who means to bring all Azeroth to its knees.

4523.name: Icecrown Glacier
4523.description: Icecrown Glacier is the great glacier at the heart of Icecrown, split by a vast fissure within and around which Icecrown Citadel was built. In the War of the Ancients, many blue dragons fell on the ground that the glacier later covered, and it was here that the Frozen Throne crashed down. Thousands of undead swarm across its black ice.

4524.name: Valhalas
4524.description: Valhalas is a battle pit at the northern end of Jotunheim in northwestern Icecrown, decorated with wooden dragon heads and overseen by a val'kyr. Here the vrykul fight their most honorable battles: the victors are raised among the Ymirjar, the elite warrior caste of King Ymiron, while the losers become vargul, undead vrykul.

4525.name: The Underhalls
4525.description: The Underhalls are a dank vrykul hall cut into the mountain opposite Valhalas in Jotunheim, filled with bones, rotting flesh, and vargul, the undead vrykul who failed in the battle pit and were exiled here, where dark experiments are conducted on their bodies.

4526.name: Njorndar Village
4526.description: Njorndar Village is the main residential area of Jotunheim, west of the Weeping Quarry in Icecrown, a vrykul village of wooden longhouses and war banners.

4527.name: Balargarde Fortress
4527.description: Balargarde Fortress is a great stone vrykul castle on the cliffs above Onslaught Harbor in western Icecrown, the seat of the overthane who rules Jotunheim. It tries to put Utgarde Keep to shame in size and number of decorative skulls, and it can be seen from the coasts of Sholazar Basin and even the Borean Tundra.

4528.name: Kul'galar Keep
4528.description: Kul'galar Keep is a vrykul keep built into the mountains near Balargarde Fortress in western Icecrown, where the oracles of Jotunheim receive orders from their master and scry upon others through the Eye of the Lich King.

4529.name: The Crimson Cathedral
4529.description: The Crimson Cathedral is the spiritual center of the Scarlet Onslaught, standing on a hill on one of the islands of Onslaught Harbor in Icecrown, where the Onslaught's archbishop tends to his Scarlet flock.

4530.name: Sanctum of Reanimation
4530.description: The Sanctum of Reanimation is the flesh giant laboratory at the top of the Fleshwerks in Icecrown, where the Scourge stitches together undead giants from the bodies of Northrend's giants.

4531.name: The Fleshwerks
4531.description: The Fleshwerks is a great Scourge facility in Icecrown, high above the Avalanche that rumbled down into Sholazar Basin, dedicated to the creation of abominations and flesh giants. Even for a place of the Scourge it is disgusting, full of bubbling poison and plague, with undead birds circling overhead. The Knights of the Ebon Blade and the Argent Crusade fight to shut it down from their camp at the Blackwatch.

4533.name: Sindragosa's Fall
4533.description: Sindragosa's Fall is a boneyard in Icecrown where, in the War of the Ancients, Sindragosa, consort of the blue Aspect Malygos, fell as she desperately sought to reach the Dragonblight to die. Thousands of years later, the Lich King came here and raised her bones as a mighty frost wyrm to lead his Frostbrood, and the Cult of the Damned now raises more frost wyrms from the ice.

4537.name: The Valley of Lost Hope
4537.description: The Valley of Lost Hope lies behind Mord'rethar: The Death Gate in Icecrown, filled with legions of Scourge, a valley of great strategic importance to any assault on Icecrown Citadel.

4540.name: The Valley of Fallen Heroes
4540.description: The Valley of Fallen Heroes lies between Aldur'thar: The Desolation Gate and Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate in Icecrown, where fallen champions of the Alliance and Horde are raised as champions of the Scourge under the command of necromancers and val'kyr. Frost wyrms, flesh giants, and armored skeletons fill the valley.

4541.name: Vanguard Infirmary
4541.description: The Vanguard Infirmary is the infirmary of the Argent Vanguard in Icecrown, where wounded crusaders are tended between battles.

4580.name: Crusaders' Pinnacle
4580.description: Crusaders' Pinnacle is a mountain plateau northwest of the Argent Vanguard and north of Dalaran in Icecrown. The Argent Crusade has fought to wrest it from the Scourge, sanctify its blighted ground, and raise Justice Keep upon it as a fortress in defiance of the Lich King.

4588.name: Blackwatch
4588.description: Blackwatch is a small camp overlooking the Fleshwerks in Icecrown, from which the Knights of the Ebon Blade and the Argent Crusade work to shut down the Scourge's abomination laboratory.

4591.name: Silent Vigil
4591.description: The Silent Vigil is a graveyard in the northeastern corner of Icecrown, a quiet resting place amid the black ice.

4593.name: The Pit of Fiends
4593.description: The Pit of Fiends is a pit in Icecrown south of the Silent Vigil, filled to the brim with skeletons, with a nerubian statue rising from its center; now and then a skeletal arm flails up from the bones.

4594.name: Battlescar Spire
4594.description: Battlescar Spire is a ledge in the mountains south of Jotunheim in Icecrown, a place of reverence for the vrykul, second only to Valhalas as a site of honorable combat.

4595.name: Hall of Horrors
4595.description: The Hall of Horrors is a chamber within the Underhalls of Jotunheim in Icecrown, where the bodies of exiled vargul are stitched together into monstrous creations.

4596.name: The Circle of Suffering
4596.description: The Circle of Suffering is a chamber within the Underhalls of Jotunheim in Icecrown, held by a cruel vrykul thane and his followers.

4597.name: Rise of Suffering
4597.description: The Rise of Suffering is a ledge at the eastern end of Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate in Icecrown, overlooking the last defenses before the citadel.

4615.name: Naz'anak: The Forgotten Depths
4615.description: Naz'anak: The Forgotten Depths is a cave far beneath Icecrown Citadel, two chambers with small lakes joined by an ancient nerubian hallway. A rich growth of fungi lights its darkness, and faceless ones lurk in its depths.

4622.name: First Legion Forward Camp
4622.description: The First Legion Forward Camp is a small camp south of the Bombardment in Icecrown, a former base of Prince Arthas's 1st Legion from his expedition to Northrend, where Lordaeron footsoldiers and their ballistae can still be found.

4658.name: Argent Tournament Grounds
4658.description: The Argent Tournament Grounds are the base of the Argent Crusade's tournament in northeastern Icecrown, north of Sindragosa's Fall, with a great stone coliseum and tilting grounds. The crusade holds the tournament to find the finest champions of the Alliance and the Horde to lead the charge into Icecrown Citadel, for throwing a whole army against the undead would only swell the Lich King's ranks. The Silver Covenant and the Sunreavers represent the two factions, and Argent peacekeepers keep the peace between them.

4666.name: Sunreaver Pavilion
4666.description: The Sunreaver Pavilion is the Horde's base at the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, in the southeast of the grounds, staffed by the Sunreavers and champions of the Horde's peoples.

4667.name: Silver Covenant Pavilion
4667.description: The Silver Covenant Pavilion is the Alliance's base at the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, in the northeast of the grounds, staffed by the Silver Covenant and champions of the Alliance's peoples.

4669.name: The Ring of Champions
4669.description: The Ring of Champions is a great ring of combat in the southern part of the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, where the champions of the tournament face each other in mounted jousting.

4670.name: The Aspirants' Ring
4670.description: The Aspirants' Ring is a jousting ring in the northwest of the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, where aspiring riders prove themselves to rise to the rank of valiant.

4671.name: The Argent Valiants' Ring
4671.description: The Argent Valiants' Ring is a jousting ring in the northwest corner of the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, where valiants face the Argent Crusade's riders to earn the title of champion.

4672.name: The Alliance Valiants' Ring
4672.description: The Alliance Valiants' Ring is an octagonal jousting ring outside the Silver Covenant Pavilion at the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, where Alliance valiants duel the champions of the Alliance's cities.

4673.name: The Horde Valiants' Ring
4673.description: The Horde Valiants' Ring is an octagonal jousting ring outside the Sunreaver Pavilion at the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, where Horde valiants duel the champions of the Horde's cities.

4674.name: Argent Pavilion
4674.description: The Argent Pavilion is the Argent Crusade's headquarters at the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, west of the coliseum, staffed by the crusade's leaders and serving also as a chapel of the Light for all races.

4676.name: Sunreaver Pavilion
4676.description: The Sunreaver Pavilion stands in the southeastern part of the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, the Horde's base of operations for the tournament, where the blood elf Sunreavers host champions of the orcs, trolls, tauren, Forsaken, and blood elves.

4677.name: Silver Covenant Pavilion
4677.description: The Silver Covenant Pavilion stands in the northeastern part of the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, the Alliance's base of operations for the tournament, where the high elves of the Silver Covenant host champions of the humans, dwarves, gnomes, night elves, and draenei.

4692.name: Quel'Delar's Rest
4692.description: Quel'Delar's Rest is a site in Icecrown north of the Silent Vigil, ringed by small lanterns, where an elven sword is lodged in the ice above what seems to be a dragon's skull.

4743.name: Deathspeaker's Watch
4743.description: Deathspeaker's Watch is a camp of the Cult of the Damned on a plateau northwest of the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown, a threat lurking at the tournament's doorstep.

4862.name: The Frozen Halls
4862.description: The Frozen Halls are the entrance chambers on the upper parapet of Icecrown Citadel, leading into the Forge of Souls, where soul grinders serve the Lich King's dark purpose; the Pit of Saron, where captured champions of the Alliance and Horde are forced to labor; and the Halls of Reflection, near the Lich King's own chambers.

210.description: Icecrown is the dark heart of Northrend and the seat of the Lich King, a land of mountains and glacier so hardened and desecrated that the ice has gone black with corruption. It has been a place of evil since the Burning Legion hurled the spirit of Ner'zhul into the glacier in a prison of ice, the Frozen Throne, from which nearly all blight and undeath ultimately flows; from here the Lich King enslaved the peoples of Northrend, crushed the nerubian kingdom, and raised the Scourge. Arthas Menethil defeated Illidan Stormrage at the foot of the throne and merged with the Lich King, and his servants raised Icecrown Citadel around it, a cathedral of blades and claws wrought from saronite, visible from almost anywhere in Northrend. Walls, gates, and massive walkways of saronite lace the glacier, connecting Scourge fortresses, necropolises, and mines, and the region is sealed by three great gates: Mord'rethar, Aldur'thar, and Corp'rethar. Undead outnumber all else, and the vrykul of Jotunheim and Ymirheim serve the Lich King. Now the war has come to his doorstep. The Argent Crusade under Highlord Tirion Fordring has breached Icecrown from the east and holds its tournament grounds in the north, the death knights of the Knights of the Ebon Blade strike from captured strongholds, and the Alliance and Horde gunships, the Skybreaker and Orgrim's Hammer, patrol the skies, battling the Scourge and often each other. The Scarlet Onslaught holds a harbor on the western coast.

214.name: The Great Sea
214.description: The Great Sea is the vast ocean that fills the space between the continents of Azeroth, created when the Well of Eternity was destroyed and the ancient land of Kalimdor was split asunder during the Great Sundering. Every sea in the world connects to it. Its deep, blue waters stretch beyond the horizon, and sailors tell tales of lost islands, sunken cities, and the great whirlpool of the Maelstrom at its heart, where the Well of Eternity once stood. Storms can rise suddenly over its waters, and sea serpents, giant sharks, and naga are said to lurk in its depths. Ships of the Alliance, the Horde, the goblins, and the pirates of the southern seas cross it constantly, carrying travelers and trade between Kalimdor, the Eastern Kingdoms, and Northrend, though the open ocean is so vast that no swimmer could ever cross it.

215.name: Mulgore

220.name: Red Cloud Mesa
220.description: Red Cloud Mesa is a broad, grassy plateau atop high cliffs in southern Mulgore, where young tauren begin their training among peaceful plains and nearly harmless wildlife. Camp Narache, the training camp of the Hawkwind tribe, stands in its northwest. The mesa is known for its serene beauty, and only in its far northeast, where quilboar dwell in Brambleblade Ravine, is any danger to be found.

221.name: Camp Narache
221.description: Camp Narache is a tauren village at the northern edge of Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore, the main village of the Hawkwind tribe and the place where many young tauren begin their training. Its tents and totems surround the great tent of its chieftain, and teachers of the ways of the warrior, the hunter, the druid, and the shaman guide the young. It is a peaceful, welcoming place under the open sky.

222.name: Bloodhoof Village
222.description: Bloodhoof Village is a tauren village in central Mulgore, named after the great chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, and notable as the first permanent tauren settlement built on flat, open ground rather than atop a mesa, a sign of the security the tauren feel in their homeland. The village is surrounded on three sides by Stonebull Lake, and its tents, longhouses, and windmills are a hub of trade and training. Cairne's son, Baine Bloodhoof, leads the village and oversees its protection.

223.name: Stonebull Lake
223.description: Stonebull Lake is a long, horseshoe-shaped lake that surrounds Bloodhoof Village on three sides in central Mulgore. It is known for its abundant fish, and many hours are spent casting lines into its cool waters. A bridge spans the lake at its narrowest point, carrying the road between Thunder Bluff and Bloodhoof Village. The lake is named after a mighty tauren hero who fell battling the Burning Legion.

224.name: Ravaged Caravan
224.description: The Ravaged Caravan is the smoldering wreck of a Venture Company wagon train in Mulgore, which blew apart for reasons unknown. The caravan still spews black smoke, and the goblins aggressively defend the remains of their precious cargo. The site is an ugly scar on the peaceful plains.

225.name: Red Rocks
225.description: The Red Rocks are a group of towering red stone formations in northeastern Mulgore, ancient ancestral holy grounds of the tauren tribes, holding great spiritual energy. Recently, a band of quilboar has invaded the Red Rocks and defiled the holy place, greatly angering the tauren of Thunder Bluff. On the cliffs above lie a small hut and a cave, known to few.

358.name: Brambleblade Ravine
358.description: Brambleblade Ravine is a ravine on the northeastern edge of Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore, filled with enormous twisting thorned vines and home to the Bristleback quilboar, whose chief dwells in a large tent at its center. The quilboar threaten the young tauren training on the mesa above.

360.name: The Venture Co. Mine
360.description: The Venture Co. Mine is an enormous mine dug into the eastern mountains of Mulgore by the goblins of the Venture Company. The savage defilement of the ancient mountains greatly upsets the tauren of Bloodhoof Village, who seek to drive the goblins from their land. The mine has several exits, one leading to a ledge with a goblin camp and a dig site.

396.name: Winterhoof Water Well
396.description: The Winterhoof Water Well is one of the sacred water wells of the tauren, located at the edge of the Rolling Plains in southern Mulgore. For ages, it has been a source of the mystical well-stones used in tauren vision quests. It has recently been occupied by agents of the Venture Company, much to the ire of the local tauren tribes.

397.name: Thunderhorn Water Well
397.description: The Thunderhorn Water Well is one of the sacred water wells of the tauren, located in the grasslands of Mulgore by the north road between Thunder Bluff and Bloodhoof Village. Like the other wells, it has fallen under the control of the goblins of the Venture Company, angering the tauren.

398.name: Wildmane Water Well
398.description: The Wildmane Water Well is the northernmost of the tauren's sacred water wells, located just north of Thunder Bluff in Mulgore. The area is heavily patrolled by the goblins of the Venture Company, who have seized the well for their own purposes.

404.name: Bael'dun Digsite
404.description: The Bael'dun Digsite is a large quarry dug into the mountainside on the western edge of Mulgore, an outpost of the dwarven expedition based at Bael Modan in the Barrens. The dwarves are searching for traces of their ancient heritage, but their excavation has provoked the local tauren, who see it as an affront to the Earth Mother. The dig site is guarded by dwarven riflemen.

637.name: Kodo Rock
637.description: Kodo Rock is a natural stone monument near Camp Narache in southern Mulgore, sacred to the tauren shamans, who come here to commune with the spirits of the earth. The rock can only be seen from a short distance, hidden among the grasslands of Red Cloud Mesa.

818.name: Palemane Rock
818.description: Palemane Rock is a cave in southern Mulgore inhabited by gnolls of the Palemane tribe. The gnolls live both inside the cave, which stretches deep into the mountainside, and in a camp outside, and they attack anyone who wanders too close.

819.name: Windfury Ridge
819.description: Windfury Ridge is a rugged ridge in the northern reaches of Mulgore, home to the Windfury harpies, who swoop down to capture or kill those who come too near their nests. Wild cougars and wolves also dot the hills. The harpies' brilliant feathers are prized by the tauren of Thunder Bluff for decorating weddings and feasts.

820.name: The Golden Plains
820.description: The Golden Plains are a large basin surrounding Thunder Bluff to the southeast in Mulgore, one of the most treasured parts of the tauren homeland and one of their favorite hunting grounds. Large herds of kodos gather here, and it is said that a legendary beast dwells in the shifting green sea of grass. The plains glow golden in the setting sun.

821.name: The Rolling Plains
821.description: The Rolling Plains cover much of southern Mulgore, stretching from Bloodhoof Village to the border with the Barrens. They are inhabited by wolves, kodos, tallstriders, and cougars, and they are the only part of Mulgore where centaur outriders have been able to penetrate. The grassy hills roll gently toward the mountains on the horizon.

215.description: Mulgore is a land of green, verdant plains and windswept mesas in central Kalimdor, the ancestral homeland of the noble tauren. It is nestled in the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains and protected by a natural wall of mountains on all sides, with only a single pass leading east into the Barrens. Once a hunting ground of the night elves, the land was raised by the Great Sundering, and the tauren made their home in its valleys and on its high plateaus. For centuries the tauren lived as nomads, their tent cities moving with the seasons, while the aggressive centaurs warred against them for control of the grasslands. During the Third War, the tauren allied with Thrall's Horde, who helped them drive out the centaurs, and their great chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof led his people to Mulgore, where they built their capital, Thunder Bluff, atop towering mesas. The land is a sheltered, pastoral paradise of rolling grasslands, clear lakes, and pine-scented breezes, rich with kodos, plainstriders, wolves, cougars, and swoops, and dotted with tauren villages, windmills, and great carved totems. Yet it is not free of trouble: quilboar have overrun the sacred Red Rocks and a ravine in the south, the goblins of the Venture Company have seized the sacred water wells and dug a mine into the mountains, harpies nest in the north, gnolls dwell in the southern caves, and dwarves dig for relics at the edge of the plains.

267.name: Hillsbrad Foothills

271.name: Southshore
271.description: Southshore is a coastal town on the shores of Baradin Bay in the Hillsbrad Foothills, the largest settlement in the region and one of the last human towns of the former Kingdom of Lordaeron still held by the Alliance. The survivors of Stormwind first arrived here after fleeing their destroyed kingdom in the First War, and during the Second War it became a busy seaport, before being burned by the Horde and later rebuilt. Today a small Alliance garrison is stationed here, doing its best to drive away the Syndicate and the Forsaken of nearby Tarren Mill while protecting the southern lands from the Scourge. The town is Hillsbrad's center of trade, known for its sea turtles, a local delicacy, and its people still celebrate the defeat of the Horde in the Second War. Southshore lives under the constant shadow of war, and its proximity to Tarren Mill makes it a frequent target of attack.

272.name: Tarren Mill
272.description: Tarren Mill is a Forsaken town in the northeastern Hillsbrad Foothills, nestled among the hills at the foot of the Alterac Mountains. It was once a thriving human town and the site of a major battle during the Second War, but it was destroyed by the Scourge during the Third War and later claimed by the Forsaken as their southernmost stronghold. Under the command of a ruthless high executor, the Forsaken of Tarren Mill wage a bitter war against the humans of Southshore and Hillsbrad Fields. The town retains its timber houses and mill, but its streets are now walked by the undead, and the Royal Apothecary Society conducts its grim experiments here. Bats carry travelers to and from the Undercity and other Horde holdings.

275.name: Durnholde Keep
275.description: Durnholde Keep is a ruined stronghold east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills, once the command center of the orc internment camps after the Second War. It was here that the future Warchief Thrall was raised as a slave and gladiator by the cruel Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore, until he escaped and freed his people. Thrall later returned with his army, defeated Blackmoore in single combat, and called upon the spirits of the earth to level the fortress. Today the ruins are occupied by the Syndicate, who use them as an outpost for their operations in Hillsbrad, Arathi, and the Alterac Mountains. The broken walls and towers stand as a reminder of a dark chapter in the history of both humans and orcs.

285.name: Southpoint Tower
285.description: Southpoint Tower is a ruined watchtower at the far western end of the Hillsbrad Foothills, just south of the road leading to Silverpine Forest. Once it guarded the western approaches to Hillsbrad, but now it stands crumbling and abandoned. The Forsaken sometimes use it as a hidden post for spying on Alliance activity in the area. The tower offers a commanding view of the coast and the road, and its broken walls are overgrown with ivy.

286.name: Hillsbrad Fields
286.description: Hillsbrad Fields is a large and fertile farming area in the western Hillsbrad Foothills, home to the inland town of Hillsbrad and its surrounding farms, orchards, and pastures. The farms provide food for the people of Southshore and the whole region, and apples, pumpkins, and cattle are common sights. The town is governed by a magistrate and a council, and its people wish to live in peace with their neighbors, but they view the Forsaken of Tarren Mill as a constant threat, and the peasants and farmers are frequently targeted by undead raids. Many of the farmers are capable fighters, ready to defend their land. The fields are a rare glimpse of the pastoral life that once flourished throughout Lordaeron.

287.name: Hillsbrad
287.description: Hillsbrad is the name of the old human township that once served as the capital of the region, as well as the farming town that now stands in Hillsbrad Fields in the western foothills. The town is a large farming community of humans loyal to the Alliance, governed by a magistrate and a council. Its fields and orchards stretch across the rolling hills, providing food for Southshore and the surrounding lands. The townsfolk wish to live in peace, but the Forsaken of Tarren Mill are a constant threat, and the town has seen more than its share of bloodshed.

288.name: Azurelode Mine
288.description: Azurelode Mine is an Alliance-controlled mine in the southwestern Hillsbrad Foothills, south of Hillsbrad Fields and west of Southshore. Guards are stationed outside to protect the miners and foremen who work inside, extracting ore for the Alliance. The mine is a busy, noisy place of carts, tools, and lantern-lit tunnels, and it is a frequent target of the Forsaken, who seek to disrupt the Alliance's supply lines.

289.name: Nethander Stead
289.description: Nethander Stead is an abandoned farm just east of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills, now overrun by the Mudsnout gnolls. Giant white mushrooms known as Mudsnout blossoms grow in its abandoned fields, and they are of particular interest to the Forsaken apothecaries for their deadly brews. The farmhouse is decaying and the fields are overgrown, and the gnolls attack anyone who comes near.

290.name: Dun Garok
290.description: Dun Garok is a dwarven fortress nestled into the southeastern hills of the Hillsbrad Foothills, built into the mountainside with sturdy stone walls and gates. Its garrison of dwarves helps protect the humans of Hillsbrad and the Azurelode Mine from their enemies. The Forsaken loathe the presence of the dwarves and frequently attempt to infiltrate the fortress. Dun Garok is a stout, well-defended stronghold, and its dwarves are fiercely loyal to the Alliance.

294.name: Eastern Strand
294.description: The Eastern Strand is a stretch of coastline in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills, where the green hills meet the waters of Baradin Bay. The beaches and shallow waters are home to many naga, serpentine creatures of the sea who attack anyone who wanders near. The strand is beautiful, with its sandy beaches and crashing waves, but the naga make it dangerous.

295.name: Western Strand
295.description: The Western Strand is a stretch of coastline in the southwestern Hillsbrad Foothills, west of Southshore. Many murlocs have built small camps along the shore, and they attack travelers and fishermen who come too close. The beaches are lined with driftwood and reeds, and the waves of Baradin Bay roll gently onto the sand.

896.name: Purgation Isle
896.description: Purgation Isle is a small island off the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills, its rocky heights rising in the shape of a towering spiral. The island has a mysterious and dark history, and it is haunted by the ghosts of renegade paladins, monks, mages, and priests who are condemned and cannot find peace in death. It is said that a dark power delights in summoning the souls of the banished dead here. Few sailors dare to land on its shores.

1056.name: Darrow Hill
1056.description: Darrow Hill is an area of rolling hills in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, near the Alterac Mountains. Mountain lions and bears roam its fields, and yetis inhabit a cave bordering the mountains. The hills offer beautiful views of the surrounding countryside, but their wild inhabitants make them dangerous. Darrow Hill is also frequently the site of skirmishes between the forces of Southshore and Tarren Mill.

1057.name: Thoradin's Wall
1057.description: On the Hillsbrad side, Thoradin's Wall rises at the eastern edge of the foothills, a great stone wall built in ancient times by King Thoradin of Arathor to protect his realm. Once a symbol of humanity's strength and defensive might, it has fallen to decay and war, and now it stands collapsed and gaping wide, its great gate open to all. The main road from Hillsbrad passes through the broken wall into the Arathi Highlands beyond. The wall is a reminder of the glory of the first human empire.

2397.name: The Great Sea
2397.description: The waters of the Great Sea wash the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills, forming the northern reaches of Baradin Bay. The bay is calm and blue on fair days, grey and rough in storms, and its waters are home to sea turtles, murlocs, and naga. Ships from Southshore sail these waters, and small islands, including the haunted Purgation Isle, dot the coast. The sea breeze carries the smell of salt over the green hills.

267.description: The Hillsbrad Foothills are a land of green, rolling hills, fertile meadows, pine groves, and farmland in southern Lordaeron, lying south of the Alterac Mountains and bordered by the sea to the south. While the rest of Lordaeron was ravaged by the Scourge and twisted into a haunted shadow of its former self, Hillsbrad largely escaped that fate, and it remains the best-preserved region of the fallen kingdom, giving travelers a glimpse of what the land was like before the plague. A river flowing from Darrowmere Lake runs through the hills, and small islands dot the southern coast. Despite its pastoral beauty, Hillsbrad is one of the most blood-soaked battlefields in Azeroth. The first battle between the Alliance and the Horde in the Second War was fought here, and after the war the fortress of Durnholde served as the command center of the orc internment camps, where the young Thrall was held as a slave until his escape. In the Third War, the Scourge destroyed the town of Tarren Mill, which the Forsaken later claimed as their southernmost stronghold. Today the human town of Southshore, a stronghold of the Alliance, and the Forsaken of Tarren Mill wage a bitter, unending struggle for the region. The Syndicate, a band of exiled Alteraci nobles and their criminal followers, holds the ruins of Durnholde, while dwarves guard the fortress of Dun Garok in the southeast. Murlocs and naga prowl the coasts, gnolls infest abandoned farms, and yetis dwell in the caves of the northern hills.

269.name: Dun Algaz
269.description: Dun Algaz is a tunneled mountain pass and ancient dwarven stronghold linking Loch Modan to the Wetlands, cut through the rugged mountains that separate the dwarven heartland from the marshes to the north. Its southern end is guarded by the great dwarven Algaz Gate, and the road winds through two long tunnel sections and a small valley between them where an old fortress stands. During the Second War, after the Alliance retook Dun Modr, the retreating orcs fell back to Dun Algaz, which became the Horde's last hold in Khaz Modan. Long ago, the stronghold made the lands to the south among the most peaceful in the Eastern Kingdoms, for few enemies could penetrate the mountains. Today the derelict fortress remains the main thoroughfare between the dwarven lands and the port of Menethil Harbor, but in recent years orcs of the Dragonmaw clan have overrun the outpost in the middle of the pass, forcing dwarven mountaineers to retreat to the upper tunnel. The tunnels are dark, cold, and echoing, and travel through them has become dangerous.

293.name: Thoradin's Wall
293.description: Thoradin's Wall is an immense stone wall stretching across the border between the Hillsbrad Foothills and the Arathi Highlands, built in ancient times by King Thoradin, the founder of the Empire of Arathor, to protect his realm from the Amani trolls and other enemies. For centuries it stood as a symbol of humanity's strength and defensive might, and it later shielded Stromgarde and the Arathi Highlands from the advancing Scourge. Now the wall has fallen to decay and war: it is collapsed and gaping wide, its great gate stands open, and sections of it have crumbled into rubble. The main road between Hillsbrad and Arathi passes through the broken gate, and travelers of all loyalties come and go beneath its shadow. The wall remains an impressive sight, a reminder of the glory of the first human empire and of how far its descendants have fallen.

308.name: The Forbidding Sea
308.description: The Forbidding Sea is a vast, largely unexplored and uncharted sea stretching along the eastern coast of the Eastern Kingdoms, washing the shores of the Hinterlands, the Arathi Highlands, the Swamp of Sorrows, the eastern edge of the Plaguelands, and Eversong Woods. As its name suggests, it is a cold, grey, and unwelcoming sea: its waters are rough and often shrouded in fog, strong currents and sudden storms make it dangerous to sail, and much of the eastern coast is guarded by impassable mountains and steep cliffs. Few ships venture far from the shore, and sailors tell tales of the unknown lands and terrible creatures that may lie beyond the horizon. Some scholars believe that the Forbidding Sea stretches far to the east until it meets the Veiled Sea, on the far side of the world. Seabirds, sharks, and sea serpents dwell in its waters, and murlocs and naga lurk along its shores.

330.name: Thandol Span
330.description: The Thandol Span is a massive dwarven bridge crossing the deep sea channel that separates Khaz Modan from Lordaeron, linking the northern Wetlands with the Arathi Highlands. Built on the site of ancient natural land bridges in what was once known as the Thandol Valley, it is one of the greatest engineering projects ever completed by the dwarves, a blocky stone edifice with thick support columns plunging into the churning waters far below. For centuries, its bridges were capable of bearing entire armies and served as the main route of trade between the dwarves and the human kingdoms of the north. The span has suffered greatly in recent years: it was damaged by the Scourge during the Third War, and more recently Dark Iron dwarves launched an attack that all but destroyed one of its bridges. Great sections have broken off and lie beneath the waves, yet the span remains the only land route between Lordaeron and the southern kingdoms. Dwarven forces fight to hold what remains of the bridge, while the Dark Irons occupy the fortified town of Dun Modr at its southern end. Wind and sea spray whip across the span, and the view from its heights over the narrow channel is both breathtaking and perilous.

331.name: Ashenvale

411.name: Bathran's Haunt
411.description: Bathran's Haunt is an ancient night elven ruin in northwestern Ashenvale, north of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, long abandoned by the night elves. It has recently been occupied by agents of the Forsaken, mostly herbalists and their guards, who have set up a makeshift laboratory among the fallen pillars and broken marble. The land around the ruin has been tainted by their presence, the grass turning brown and the flowers withering. A rare and valuable herb is said to grow here.

412.name: The Ruins of Ordil'Aran
412.description: The Ruins of Ordil'Aran are the remains of an ancient night elven city in northwestern Ashenvale, north of Maestra's Post. Little of the city remains, but the site has become a favorite haunt of the Cult of the Dark Strand, warlocks who lurk among the ruins and strike at any who approach. A great and ancient tree, said to hold special significance, stands among the ruins.

413.name: Maestra's Post
413.description: Maestra's Post is a small night elf outpost in western Ashenvale, south of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran and northwest of Astranaar, consisting of a watchtower and a large night elven building. It is home to Sentinels and a few allies of other races, and it serves as a base for efforts to cleanse the surrounding forest of the Dark Strand and other threats. The outpost is surrounded by ancient trees.

414.name: The Zoram Strand
414.description: The Zoram Strand is a stretch of beach in the northwestern corner of Ashenvale, where the forest meets the Veiled Sea. The area has fallen to the naga, who have taken up residence along the shore among shipwrecks and beached sea creatures. Here lie the entrance to Blackfathom Deeps, an ancient night elven temple sunk during the Sundering, and a small Horde outpost. The beach is wild and beautiful, but dangerous.

415.name: Astranaar
415.description: Astranaar is a night elven town on an island in a lake along the road that crosses Ashenvale, the main stronghold of the night elves in the forest. Its graceful buildings of wood and stone stand among ancient trees, and it has an inn, a moonwell, merchants, and a hippogryph roost. The town is guarded by Sentinels, who keep a constant watch for the Horde, whose outposts lie to the east and west. Astranaar is a beautiful and peaceful place, but it lives under the shadow of war.

416.name: The Shrine of Aessina
416.description: The Shrine of Aessina is an ancient shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, built ages ago by the night elves and dedicated to the wilderness spirit Aessina. It lies in the midst of a forest glade in the heart of Ashenvale: a clear pool with a statue of Aessina clothed only in ivy standing beside it. Dryads are known to visit the shrine to venerate the spirit. It is a place of deep peace and natural beauty.

417.name: Fire Scar Shrine
417.description: Fire Scar Shrine is an ancient shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, flanked by red columns, which has been corrupted by demonic influence and is now a place of great evil. Orc warlocks of the Shadow Council and their demons have taken up residence here, and the shrine's halls are filled with fel energy. The surrounding forest bears the scars of fire.

418.name: The Ruins of Stardust
418.description: The Ruins of Stardust are ancient ruins on an island in a lake in southwestern Ashenvale, south of Astranaar. The lake's waters have been tainted by the demonic rot spreading from Felwood, and the area has taken on a sickly yellowish-green hue, with corrupted bog beasts roaming the ruins. Yet the stardust shrubs that grow here remain unmarred by the taint, and they are known to have powerful healing properties.

419.name: The Howling Vale
419.description: The Howling Vale is a cave in north-central Ashenvale, near the border with Felwood, home to a tribe of savage worgen who have overtaken the ancient Shrine of Mel'Thandris within. Their chilling howls echo through the vale, giving it its name. The shrine was once sacred to the night elves, and its fall is a source of sorrow for the Sentinels.

420.name: Silverwind Refuge
420.description: Silverwind Refuge is a night elven settlement in south-central Ashenvale, just north of Mystral Lake. It is a peaceful outpost of Sentinels, hunters, and herbalists, with a beautiful view of the lake, and it is a popular spot for fishing. The refuge's defenders keep watch over the southern forest and the roads.

421.name: Mystral Lake
421.description: Mystral Lake is the largest lake in Ashenvale, lying in the south-central part of the forest, just south of Silverwind Refuge. Its clear waters reflect the towering trees around it, and water elementals dwell within its depths. The lake is often visited by travelers of all kinds, and its shores are a place of great beauty.

422.name: Fallen Sky Lake
422.description: Fallen Sky Lake is a small lake in southeastern Ashenvale, south of Silverwing Outpost and west of the Warsong Labor Camp. An island lies in the center of the lake, and the surrounding area is inhabited by shadethicket treants, corrupted spirits of the forest. The lake is quiet and secluded.

424.name: Iris Lake
424.description: Iris Lake is a lake in north-central Ashenvale, east of Astranaar, which has fallen to the corruption spreading from Felwood. Its water has turned a sickly yellowish green, and twisted bog beasts roam its shores. Night elves sometimes come here in search of the rare tears of Elune said to be found near the lake.

425.name: Moonwell
425.description: The moonwells of Ashenvale are sacred pools of silvery, glowing water scattered throughout the forest, created by the night elves to harness the light of the moon and holding waters drawn from the ancient Well of Eternity. They are shrines of Elune, kept by priestesses and Sentinels, and their waters are said to soothe and restore. Several of the moonwells in Ashenvale have been abandoned or tainted by the corruption creeping through the forest, and their keepers work to cleanse them.

426.name: Raynewood Retreat
426.description: Raynewood Retreat is a druidic outpost in north-central Ashenvale, built around a great tree and led by a keeper of the grove, one of the sons of the demigod Cenarius. The druids and keepers here oppose the corruption that spreads through their beloved forest, and they watch over the path leading north to Felwood. The retreat is inhabited by Cenarion protectors, faerie dragons, and dryads, but its keeper is hunted by dark forces.

427.name: The Shady Nook
427.description: The Shady Nook is a small valley in Ashenvale, south of Raynewood Retreat and east of Greenpaw Village, inhabited by a family of bears who presumably live in the small cave located there. It is a quiet, shadowy corner of the forest.

428.name: Night Run
428.description: Night Run is the smallest of the three satyr settlements in Ashenvale, located on a cliff-bound naze in the east-central forest, northwest of Splintertree Post. The Felmusk satyrs dwell among a few broken pillars and pieces of ruined architecture, and they are allied with the Cult of the Dark Strand. The settlement is difficult to reach, surrounded by unclimbable cliffs.

429.name: Xavian
429.description: Xavian is a satyr settlement in northeastern Ashenvale, living in the ruins of an ancient night elven temple. It is the center of satyr power in the forest, home to a satyr prince and his court, and is named after Xavius, the night elf counselor who became the first satyr during the War of the Ancients. The satyrs perform their foul rituals among the ruins, and dryads who came to stop them have fallen here.

430.name: Satyrnaar
430.description: Satyrnaar is the most intact of the three satyr settlements in Ashenvale, lying in the northeast of the forest just off the main road from Splintertree Post toward Azshara. The Bleakheart satyrs live in tents among ruined night elven buildings, and they are allied with the Cult of the Dark Strand. Its proximity to the road makes it a frequent site of conflict.

431.name: Splintertree Post
431.description: Splintertree Post is a Horde outpost in eastern Ashenvale, lying northwest of Felfire Hill and close to the Warsong Lumber Camp. It is populated mainly by orcs and tauren, scouts and guards who protect the Warsong clan's lumber operations in the forest, and it has an inn, a wind rider master, and merchants. The outpost is surrounded by a sturdy palisade, and it is frequently attacked by the night elves, who resent the Horde's presence in their ancestral forest.

432.name: The Dor'Danil Barrow Den
432.description: The Dor'Danil Barrow Den is an ancient barrow den in southeastern Ashenvale, south of Splintertree Post, traditionally a resting place for sleeping night elf druids whose spirits walk the Emerald Dream. The den now lies behind the Horde's lines, and the Forsaken have conducted experiments here, severing the sleeping druids from their spirits and driving them insane. It is now filled with skulking Forsaken and the enraged souls of the severed druids.

433.name: Falfarren River
433.description: The Falfarren River runs northeast to southwest across Ashenvale, and it is considered by many to be the dividing line between the night elven lands under Astranaar to the west and the Horde-held lands around Splintertree Post to the east. Its waters originate on Mount Hyjal, pass through a series of waterfalls into the lake at Xavian, and flow southwest past Splintertree before slipping underground beneath the mountains of the northern Barrens. Bog beasts lurk beneath its surface.

434.name: Felfire Hill
434.description: Felfire Hill is a hill in eastern Ashenvale, southeast of Splintertree Post, where many infernals fell during the Burning Legion's invasion in the Third War. It is still inhabited by all manner of foul demons, and the land is scorched and blackened. The Horde has fortified the bridges leading to the hill to protect their nearby settlements.

435.name: Demon Fall Canyon
435.description: Demon Fall Canyon is a canyon in southeastern Ashenvale, famous as the site where the orc chieftain Grom Hellscream slew the demonic pit lord Mannoroth during the Third War, freeing the orcs from their blood curse at the cost of his own life. A memorial stone has been raised in Grom's honor, inscribed with words of tribute from Thrall, and it stands to this day in the canyon, surrounded by lesser demons. The canyon is a place of great significance to the orcs.

436.name: Demon Fall Ridge
436.description: Demon Fall Ridge is a ridge in southeastern Ashenvale, just west of and above Demon Fall Canyon, home to many lesser demons. They inhabit both the ridge and the interior of an abandoned barrow den set into its side, where a powerful dreadlord is said to rule over the demons of Ashenvale.

437.name: Warsong Lumber Camp
437.description: The Warsong Lumber Camp is a large lumber camp in eastern Ashenvale, near the Southfury River and the border with Azshara, operated by the Warsong clan of orcs. The orcs harvest timber here for the expansion of the Horde, and the camp is a noisy place of sawmills, shredders, and stacked logs, guarded by Warsong warriors. The night elves view the camp as a desecration of their forest and frequently attack it.

438.name: Bough Shadow
438.description: Bough Shadow is an area in the northeastern corner of Ashenvale, just beyond Forest Song, home to one of the great trees that serve as portals to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons and dragonspawn of the Dreaming Aspect Ysera guard the portal against intruders, though whispers speak of a corruption creeping into the Dream. The area is lush and mystical.

441.name: Lake Falathim
441.description: Lake Falathim is a lake in western Ashenvale, southeast of the Zoram Strand and southwest of Maestra's Post. It was once a popular place for night elves to swim and fish, but it has recently become overrun with ferocious murlocs. The lake is surrounded by ancient trees.

879.name: Southfury River
879.description: On the side of Ashenvale, the Southfury River forms the eastern border of the forest, separating it from the ruined lands of Azshara. The river begins as a small stream in the highlands around Mount Hyjal and grows into a wide, swift-flowing river as it runs south. Its banks are lined with tall trees, and the Warsong orcs harvest timber along its western shore.

1276.name: The Talondeep Path
1276.description: The Talondeep Path is a winding tunnel through the mountains that connects southwestern Ashenvale with the Stonetalon Mountains. Its entrance on the Ashenvale side lies just west of Mystral Lake. The tunnel is riddled with small dead ends and holes in the walls, but it is otherwise empty and quiet, a dark passage between the green forest and the rocky mountains.

2301.name: Thistlefur Village
2301.description: Thistlefur Village is a village of corrupted furbolgs in west-central Ashenvale, north of Astranaar, the homeland of the Thistlefur tribe. Once friendly to the night elves, the Thistlefur have been driven to madness by corruption, and they aggressively attack anyone who wanders too close. Their village is a crude collection of huts and totems.

2325.name: The Veiled Sea
2325.description: The waters of the Veiled Sea wash the western coast of Ashenvale along the Zoram Strand, rolling onto beaches strewn with shipwrecks and the carcasses of great sea creatures. The sea is deep and often shrouded in mist, and beneath its surface lie the sunken remains of ancient night elven structures lost during the Sundering. Naga swim these waters and haunt the shore, and the great forest of Ashenvale comes right down to the edge of the sand.

2357.name: Bloodtooth Camp
2357.description: Bloodtooth Camp is a camp of corrupted furbolgs in Ashenvale, just west of the Falfarren River. The furbolgs here have been driven mad by corruption and are hostile to all outsiders. Their camp is a crude collection of huts among the trees.

2358.name: Forest Song
2358.description: Forest Song is a night elf and draenei outpost in northeastern Ashenvale, built on the site of an ancient night elven ruin. The draenei, newly arrived allies of the night elves, are helping to fortify the outpost to aid the Silverwing Sentinels against the Warsong clan and the demons of the region, and to reclaim the damaged lands nearby. The outpost combines graceful night elven architecture with draenei crystal-work, and a hippogryph roost connects it with other night elf holdings.

2359.name: Greenpaw Village
2359.description: Greenpaw Village is a village of corrupted furbolgs in central Ashenvale, south of Raynewood Retreat, home to the Foulweald tribe and their chief and shaman. The furbolgs here have been driven mad by corruption and attack travelers of all kinds. The village is a crude collection of huts among the trees.

2360.name: Silverwing Outpost
2360.description: Silverwing Outpost is a night elf outpost in south-central Ashenvale, north of the border with the Barrens and southwest of Splintertree Post. It is the eastern bastion of the night elves against the Horde, located on the eastern side of the Falfarren River, and its Sentinels must constantly fight off attacks from the nearby orcs. The outpost is small but fiercely defended.

2457.name: Nightsong Woods
2457.description: Nightsong Woods is the largest part of the Ashenvale forest, stretching from just east of Astranaar all the way east to Azshara. It is the heart of the conflict between the night elves and the Horde, where the Silverwing Sentinels and the Warsong clan have their holdings, and the Falfarren River roughly divides it into a western night elven half and an eastern Horde half. The southern reaches of the woods have been deforested by the Warsong orcs, while the northern woods remain ancient and wild.

2637.name: Kargathia Keep
2637.description: Kargathia Keep is a Horde fortress in eastern Ashenvale, at the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp just west of the Southfury River. It serves as the base of operations for the officers of the Warsong clan, and its strategic position allows it to receive reinforcements from Orgrimmar. The keep is named after the legendary orc chieftain Kargath Bladefist, and its walls are sturdy and well defended.

2797.name: Blackfathom Deeps
2797.description: Blackfathom Deeps is an ancient temple to the moon goddess Elune on the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale, once known as Lathar'Lazal. It was thought to have been destroyed during the Sundering and lost beneath the sea, but it survives as a series of watery caverns and flooded halls. In recent times, cultists of the Twilight's Hammer were drawn to the temple by whispers and foul dreams, and they now share it with the naga. The entrance, a half-sunken ruin of elegant night elven architecture, stands near the shore.

2897.name: Zoram'gar Outpost
2897.description: Zoram'gar Outpost is a small Horde outpost on the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale, built mostly by trolls. It is the Horde's foothold on the western coast of the forest, and it is surrounded by naga, night elves, and the dangers of the beach. The outpost is a modest collection of huts and palisades, and a wind rider master connects it with other Horde holdings.

3177.name: Warsong Labor Camp
3177.description: The Warsong Labor Camp is a small lumber camp in southeastern Ashenvale, east of Fallen Sky Lake. It is believed to be the camp that Grom Hellscream originally established when Thrall sent him to Ashenvale to harvest lumber during the Third War. Today it is a small operation of loggers, harvesters, and orc guards, often targeted by the night elves.

3319.name: Silverwing Grove
3319.description: Silverwing Grove is a night elf camp in south-central Ashenvale, southwest of Silverwing Outpost, where the Silverwing Sentinels gather to wage their war against the Warsong clan in the nearby gulch. Sentinels, officers, and quartermasters prepare for battle here, and the grove is a place of martial resolve amid the ancient trees.

331.description: Ashenvale is a vast, ancient forest in northern Kalimdor, lying south of Darkshore and Felwood, west of Azshara, and north of the Stonetalon Mountains and the Barrens. It is the ancestral homeland of the night elves, a primordial wilderness of towering trees, deep glades, clear lakes, and winding rivers, where the weather is mild and rain is frequent but filtered by the thick canopy. For thousands of years the night elves tended the forest without cutting it, guarded by the Sentinels, the druids, and the ancients, living trees who watch over the woods. During the Third War, the orcs of Grom Hellscream came to Ashenvale to harvest lumber, killing the demigod Cenarius, before Grom slew the pit lord Mannoroth and freed his people from their blood curse. Since then, the forest has become a bitterly contested land. The night elves hold Astranaar, Maestra's Post, and other outposts in the west, while the Horde's Warsong clan harvests timber in the east from Splintertree Post and its lumber camps, and the Silverwing Sentinels and the Warsong Outriders clash constantly. Demons linger in the places where they fell during the Third War, satyrs dwell in ancient ruins, furbolgs have been driven mad by corruption, naga haunt the western coast, and the taint of Felwood seeps into some of the lakes. Bears, great cats, wolves, harpies, and wildkin roam the woods, and the forest remains breathtakingly beautiful.

332.name: The Great Sea
332.description: The Great Sea is the vast ocean between the continents of Azeroth, born when the Well of Eternity imploded and the ancient land was torn apart in the Great Sundering. Here, far from any shore, only endless blue water stretches in every direction, broken by the occasional distant island or passing ship. The swell rises and falls beneath the sky, seabirds circle high above, and in the depths below swim creatures that few have ever seen. Sailors speak with awe of the Maelstrom, the colossal whirlpool at the center of the sea, and of the countless ships lost to storms and the creatures of the deep. It is a place of solitude and danger, where the wind and the waves rule.

357.name: Feralas

489.name: Thalanaar
489.description: Thalanaar is a small night elf outpost on the border of Feralas and Thousand Needles, guarding the eastern approach to the forest. It has a hippogryph roost and offers little in the way of goods and services, but its Sentinels keep a watchful eye over the road. It is a humble but important waypoint for the Alliance.

1099.name: Camp Mojache
1099.description: Camp Mojache is a tauren village in eastern Feralas, overlooking the scenic Wildwind Lake, straddling a swift-flowing stream that feeds the lake. Its tents, longhouses, and totems are home to tauren and their Horde allies, who work to counter the Gordunni ogres and other threats of the forest. The camp has an inn and a wind rider roost, and its location is one of the most beautiful in Kalimdor.

1100.name: Grimtotem Compound
1100.description: The Grimtotem Compound is a large village of the renegade Grimtotem tauren in Feralas. The Grimtotem, who reject the tauren's alliance with the Horde, have captured many faerie dragons and imprisoned them in a large cage. Their warriors attack anyone who comes near.

1101.name: The Writhing Deep
1101.description: The Writhing Deep is the site of a silithid infestation in southeastern Feralas, a minor hive dug into the earth. The silithid have tunneled deep beneath the forest, and their presence is a grave concern to the inhabitants of the region. The hive is dark and filled with the chittering of insects.

1102.name: Wildwind Lake
1102.description: Wildwind Lake is a beautiful lake in eastern Feralas, near Camp Mojache, surrounded by the towering trees of the forest. Its clear waters are fed by streams flowing from the mountains, and its shores are home to many creatures of the wild.

1103.name: Gordunni Outpost
1103.description: The Gordunni Outpost is an area in the mountains of Feralas, north of Lariss Pavilion, held by the Gordunni ogres. Their presence has caused the normally verdant plant life of the forest to wither into a sickly brown. Ogre warriors, magi, and brutes guard the outpost.

1105.name: Feral Scar Vale
1105.description: Feral Scar Vale is a cave in Feralas inhabited by yetis. The cave is cold and damp, and its fierce inhabitants attack anyone who enters their lair.

1106.name: Frayfeather Highlands
1106.description: The Frayfeather Highlands are the territory of the Frayfeather hippogryphs in Feralas, a hilly region of the forest where the hippogryphs build their nests. The highlands are beautiful and wild, and the hippogryphs fiercely defend their eggs.

1108.name: The Forgotten Coast
1108.description: The Forgotten Coast is a stretch of the western coast of Feralas bordering the Veiled Sea. A dock here serves the ferry that carries travelers across the water to Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle. The coast is lush and quiet, with the forest coming right down to the shore.

1109.name: East Pillar
1109.description: The East Pillar is the eastern of the Twin Colossals, a pair of enormous vertical mountains rising on the western side of Feralas. Some believe the pillars are the stumps of ancient trees that have since eroded into stone. Its summit offers a breathtaking view of the forest and the sea, and a small lake lies atop it.

1110.name: West Pillar
1110.description: The West Pillar is the western of the Twin Colossals, a pair of enormous vertical mountains rising on the western side of Feralas, between which the road to Desolace runs. The pillars are among the most striking landmarks of the region, inspiring awe in all who behold them.

1111.name: Dream Bough
1111.description: Dream Bough is an area in northwestern Feralas home to one of the great trees that serve as portals to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons and dragonspawn of the Dreaming Aspect Ysera guard the portal against intruders, though whispers speak of a corruption creeping into the Dream. The area is lush and mystical, bathed in a strange light.

1112.name: Jademir Lake
1112.description: Jademir Lake is a lake close to the portal to the Emerald Dream in northwestern Feralas. The green dragonkin of Ysera's flight prowl its banks, determined to keep outsiders away. The lake is beautiful and serene, its waters reflecting the great tree nearby.

1113.name: Oneiros
1113.description: Oneiros is an area of Feralas adjacent to the portal to the Emerald Dream at Dream Bough, home to a small ruin and many powerful green dragons. Its name evokes dreams, fitting for the realm of Ysera the Dreamer. The area is guarded closely by the dragons.

1114.name: Ruins of Ravenwind
1114.description: The Ruins of Ravenwind are the remains of an ancient Highborne settlement in northern Feralas, now overrun by the Northspring harpies. A great tree stands at the center of the ruins, protected by green dragonkin, and a pond lies nearby. The ruins hold remnants of the ancient night elves' magic.

1115.name: Rage Scar Hold
1115.description: Rage Scar Hold is a cave in northwestern Feralas, home to the most vicious yetis in the region. Books and magical symbols found within the cave suggest that it once belonged to a mage, or that the yetis have somehow taken an interest in magic.

1116.name: Feathermoon Stronghold
1116.description: Feathermoon Stronghold is a night elf fortress on the northern shore of Sardor Isle, off the western coast of Feralas. It is led by General Shandris Feathermoon, the head of the Sentinel army and adopted daughter of Tyrande Whisperwind, and it serves as the main night elf stronghold in southern Kalimdor. Its graceful buildings and walls overlook the sea, and its Sentinels keep a watchful eye on the Isle of Dread to the south. A ferry connects it with the mainland, and hippogryphs fly from its roost.

1117.name: Ruins of Solarsal
1117.description: The Ruins of Solarsal are night elven ruins on Sardor Isle, south of Feathermoon Stronghold, inhabited by the Hatecrest naga. The ruins are overgrown and half-submerged, and the naga guard them fiercely.

1119.name: The Twin Colossals
1119.description: The Twin Colossals are a pair of enormous vertical mountains rising on the western side of Feralas, between which the road from Feralas to Desolace runs. Some believe they are the stumps of ancient trees that have eroded into stone over the ages. They are among the most striking landmarks of Kalimdor, inspiring awe in all who behold them.

1120.name: Sardor Isle
1120.description: Sardor Isle is an island off the western coast of Feralas, home to Feathermoon Stronghold, the night elf fortress led by General Shandris Feathermoon. The island is covered in lush forest and ancient ruins, and the night elves keep watch over the Isle of Dread to the south, where unspeakable things are said to walk.

1121.name: Isle of Dread
1121.description: The Isle of Dread is an island south of Feathermoon Stronghold off the western coast of Feralas. It is home to many powerful chimaeras, and naga dwell in a cave at its northern end, led by a fearsome naga lord. The island's central valley is surrounded by unyielding cliffs, and terrible things are said to walk there.

1136.name: High Wilderness
1136.description: The High Wilderness is the southeastern part of Feralas, a wild region of towering trees inhabited by many beasts, including gorillas, wind serpents, hippogryphs, and bears. It is one of the most untamed parts of the forest.

1137.name: Lower Wilds
1137.description: The Lower Wilds are an eastern part of Feralas, a wild forest infested by fierce bears and wolves. The trees grow thick here, and the forest floor is dense with undergrowth.

2323.name: The Veiled Sea
2323.description: The waters of the Veiled Sea wash the western coast of Feralas, separating the mainland from Sardor Isle and the Isle of Dread. The sea is blue and often calm near the shore, and naga dwell in its waters. A ferry crosses between the Forgotten Coast and Feathermoon Stronghold.

2518.name: Lariss Pavilion
2518.description: Lariss Pavilion is a large, open-air night elven pavilion in Feralas, just north of Camp Mojache. It is home to a mysterious Highborne who fled from Dire Maul, and it is said that a secret passage beneath the pavilion leads into the ancient city. The pavilion is beautiful and serene.

2519.name: Woodpaw Hills
2519.description: Woodpaw Hills is an area in southeastern Feralas densely inhabited by the Woodpaw gnolls, north of the Writhing Deep. The gnolls are hostile and attack anyone who wanders into their territory.

2520.name: Woodpaw Den
2520.description: Woodpaw Den is an area of Feralas heavily populated by the Woodpaw gnolls, the heart of their territory. Their crude camps dot the forest.

2521.name: Verdantis River
2521.description: The Verdantis River is a small river weaving through central Feralas, just southeast of Dire Maul. Its clear waters are home to unique fish found nowhere else in the world.

2522.name: Ruins of Isildien
2522.description: The Ruins of Isildien are large night elven ruins in southeastern Feralas, now inhabited by the Gordunni ogres. The ancient stone structures have been defiled by the ogres, who have made them their home.

2577.name: Dire Maul
2577.description: Dire Maul is a vast ruined city in north-central Feralas, once the proud Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas. Built twelve thousand years ago by a secret sect of night elf sorcerers to protect Queen Azshara's most prized arcane secrets, it was ravaged by the Great Sundering, but much of the city still stands. Today its three districts are overrun by the Gordok ogres, who claim the city as their kingdom, by spectral Highborne and foul satyrs, and by ancient evils locked within its vaults. A remnant of the original Highborne, a secretive sect called the Shen'dralar, still dwells within. The city's ruins are majestic and haunting.

3117.name: Shalzaru's Lair
3117.description: Shalzaru's Lair is a large, twisting naga lair at the northern end of the Isle of Dread, south of Feathermoon Stronghold's island. The master of the Hatecrest naga dwells deep inside, and the cave is filled with naga sorceresses and serpent guards. A secret underwater passage connects its chambers.

357.description: Feralas is a lush, ancient rainforest in southwestern Kalimdor, stretching from the cliffs of Thousand Needles to the western coast, and from the wasteland of Desolace in the north to Un'Goro Crater in the south.
