Unlike its barren neighbors, it is a land of huge, ancient trees, misty valleys, rushing rivers, and clear lakes, protected by high mountains that may have sheltered it from the devastation of the Sundering. Feralas was once part of the great night elven empire, and the forest holds many ancient ruins, including the vast Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Both the Alliance and the Horde lay claim to the area: the night elves hold Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle off the western coast and the outpost of Thalanaar in the east, while the tauren of Camp Mojache watch over the eastern forest. Both must contend with powerful local forces, most notoriously the bloodthirsty Gordunni ogres, who control many of the ancient ruins and have desecrated the land around them. The renegade Grimtotem tauren have a compound here, naga infest the western islands, silithid hives have appeared in the southeast, and the northwestern forest holds one of the great trees that serve as portals to the Emerald Dream, guarded by the green dragonflight. Gorillas, yetis, wind serpents, hippogryphs, bears, and harpies roam the wilds.

361.name: Felwood

1761.name: Deadwood Village
1761.description: Deadwood Village is a village of the Deadwood tribe of corrupted furbolgs in southern Felwood. Driven mad by the taint of the forest, the Deadwood furbolgs are hostile to all, and they are bitter enemies of the uncorrupted Timbermaw tribe in the north. Their village is a crude collection of huts and totems among the twisted trees.

1762.name: Felpaw Village
1762.description: Felpaw Village is a camp of the corrupted Deadwood furbolgs in the very north of Felwood, near the entrance to Timbermaw Hold. The furbolgs here are maddened by corruption and gather around a foul cauldron, and they attack anyone who comes near. The Timbermaw furbolgs regard them with sorrow and hostility.

1763.name: Jaedenar
1763.description: Jaedenar is an enclave of the Shadow Council in western Felwood, built in a series of ancient night elven ruins and named after the eredar lord Kil'jaeden, who founded the Council with the orc warlock Gul'dan. The warlocks murdered the druids who slept in the barrow den here and turned it into their stronghold, from which they seek to spread the corruption of Felwood to the rest of Ashenvale. The enclave is filled with orc warlocks, satyrs, and demons, and a dreadlord is said to oversee it.

1764.name: Bloodvenom River
1764.description: The Bloodvenom River is a corrupted river flowing through central Felwood, its waters thick with poisonous green sludge. The river spreads its taint beyond Felwood, eventually becoming the Wildbend River in Darkshore. Its banks are crawling with noxious oozes and other corrupted creatures, and swimming in it or drinking from it is extremely dangerous.

1765.name: Bloodvenom Falls
1765.description: Bloodvenom Falls is a corrupted waterfall high in eastern Felwood, the source of the Bloodvenom River. Once a shimmering waterfall fed by pure springs, it now spews putrid water that pours over a rocky edge into a pool of sinister jade. Drinking its water is said to be deadly, and being doused by it burns like acid. Oozes and slimes breed endlessly in its pool.

1766.name: Shatter Scar Vale
1766.description: Shatter Scar Vale is a valley north of Bloodvenom Falls in Felwood, where many of the Burning Legion's infernals fell to Azeroth during the Third War. Still-smoldering craters dot the vale, and demons continue to wander the scarred landscape. The air is hot and heavy with the stench of sulfur.

1767.name: Irontree Woods
1767.description: Irontree Woods is a forest in northern Felwood, once a peaceful glade but now corrupted like the rest of the region by the Burning Legion. Three great ancients have been petrified and remain entombed within the woods. Crazed treants, twisted bog beasts, corrupted water elementals, and ferocious wildlife roam among the trees.

1768.name: Irontree Cavern
1768.description: Irontree Cavern is a deep cave in northern Felwood, inhabited by corrupted treants of the Warpwood. Elementals of amber and stone dwell in its depths, and a powerful creature is said to lurk at the bottom. The cave is dark and twisted.

1769.name: Timbermaw Hold
1769.description: Timbermaw Hold is the home of the Timbermaw tribe of furbolgs, a network of tunnels in northeastern Felwood that connects the cursed forest with Moonglade and Winterspring. When the corruption of the Burning Legion crept into the forests of Kalimdor, most furbolgs fell under its influence, but the Timbermaw escaped it, sheltering in their hold while they watched their beloved forest twisted into a festering perversion. The furbolgs are wary of strangers, fearing they may be enemies, but they value their true friends above all else and share their shamanistic wisdom and crafts with them. They seek an end to the suffering of their corrupted brethren.

1770.name: Shadow Hold
1770.description: Shadow Hold is the main stronghold of the Shadow Council in western Felwood, a gigantic subterranean labyrinth beneath Jaedenar, carved from a corrupted barrow den. Its halls are roamed by warlocks and their demonic servants, and prisoners are said to be held within. A satyr prince and a dreadlord are rumored to dwell in its depths.

1771.name: Shrine of the Deceiver
1771.description: The Shrine of the Deceiver is a corrupted barrow den at Jaedenar in Felwood, named for the Burning Legion's lord, Kil'jaeden the Deceiver. It is filled with warlocks of the Shadow Council, and dark rituals are performed within its halls. The shrine is a dangerous place for the unprepared.

1997.name: Bloodvenom Post
1997.description: Bloodvenom Post is a tiny Horde outpost in Felwood near the Bloodvenom River, perched on the high cliffs overlooking Darkshore. It consists of only a single hut, a wind rider master, a few tauren guards, and some travelers, and it appears to have been founded by the tauren. The outpost offers a rare place of rest for the Horde in the cursed forest.

1998.name: Talonbranch Glade
1998.description: Talonbranch Glade is a small night elf homestead in northern Felwood, a bit south of Timbermaw Hold. It amounts to a single house, a hippogryph roost, and a few friendly but edgy night elves, and it is the closest thing to a safe haven for the Alliance in the cursed forest. From here, travelers can make their way to the Timbermaw tunnels.

2478.name: Morlos'Aran
2478.description: Morlos'Aran is the ruin of a great night elf settlement at the southern edge of Felwood, which flourished long before the Great Sundering. Like the ruins of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran in Darkshore, it was once a thriving city, but now it serves only as a reminder of the golden age that was lost long ago. The ruins are overgrown and tainted by the corruption of the forest.

2479.name: Emerald Sanctuary
2479.description: The Emerald Sanctuary is a camp of druids of the Cenarion Circle in southeastern Felwood, where many druids work to investigate and cleanse the demonic corruption of the forest. It is a rare place of life and hope in the blighted land, open to all who would help the druids in their task. Hippogryphs connect it with other night elf holdings.

2480.name: Jadefire Glen
2480.description: Jadefire Glen is an encampment of demonic satyrs of the Jadefire tribe in southern Felwood. The satyrs dwell among corrupted trees and foul altars, spreading the taint of the forest, and they attack anyone who comes near.

2481.name: Ruins of Constellas
2481.description: The Ruins of Constellas are the remains of an ancient night elf settlement in Felwood, one of many near Mount Hyjal, presumably destroyed during the Great Sundering. A moonwell stands among the ruins, but it has been corrupted with fel energy and is tended by satyrs of the Jadefire tribe. The ruins are dark and dangerous.

2618.name: Jadefire Run
2618.description: Jadefire Run is a satyr encampment in northern Felwood, home to the most powerful satyrs of the Jadefire tribe. The satyrs here are numerous and dangerous, and the area is steeped in fel energy. Travelers are advised to exercise great caution.

361.description: Felwood is a corrupted forest in northern Kalimdor, lying north of Ashenvale, east of Darkshore, and west of Winterspring and Mount Hyjal. Once a lush and vibrant land of woods and meadows, tended by the night elves and protected by the demigod Cenarius, it was as close to a paradise as the world had ever known. During the Third War, the Burning Legion befouled the land using the Skull of Gul'dan, and although Illidan Stormrage consumed the Skull and destroyed the demon lord Tichondrius, the taint remained. Today Felwood is an eerie, dark, and haunted region of twisted trees, blighted meadows, and poisoned rivers. Nothing grows in its charred meadows, the mighty ancients that once guarded the land roam blindly with their bark bleeding fel poison, and the streams boil with toxic sludge. Corrupted furbolgs, satyrs, demons, and the warlocks of the Shadow Council infest the land, and the beasts, refusing to eat the cursed vegetation, have turned on each other in a brutal rage. The night elves feel constant shame for having failed to protect this noble land, and the druids of the Cenarion Circle strive to cleanse it from their outposts. The Timbermaw furbolgs, one of the last uncorrupted tribes, hold the tunnels in the north that lead to Moonglade and Winterspring. Travelers are generally safe on the main road by day, but few dare to leave it.

377.name: Southfury River
377.description: The Southfury River is one of the most prominent rivers of Kalimdor, beginning as a small stream in the highlands around Mount Hyjal and growing into a wide, swift-flowing river as it runs south. It forms the boundary between the ancient forest of Ashenvale and the ruined lands of Azshara, and further south the border between the Barrens and the orcish homeland of Durotar, passing near the walls of Orgrimmar. Its waters are swift and cold in the north and warm and murky in the south, where crocolisks patrol the river and lurk among the reeds. The river finally empties into the Great Sea in a cascading waterfall near the goblin port of Ratchet. Bridges cross it at a few points, and travelers of all kinds pass over its waters.

394.name: Grizzly Hills

395.name: Grizzlemaw
395.description: Grizzlemaw is the great furbolg city in the center of the Grizzly Hills, built within the colossal stump of the fallen World Tree Vordrassil. Behind a tall wooden palisade with guard towers stand massive houses of stone and wood, their floors covered in furs, their walls hung with woven tapestries and trophies, with great fire pits at their hearts. It is said the city began as the lodge of the Frostpaw tribe, who invited other tribes to shelter there through the winter, uniting the scattered hunters into a loose nation. Now the Frostpaw and Redfang tribes are locked in constant war, and a dark madness has spread among them from the depths of the old tree.

4159.name: Westfall Brigade Encampment
4159.description: The Westfall Brigade Encampment is an Alliance camp in the eastern Grizzly Hills. At the start of the war against the Lich King, the People's Militia of Westfall joined the Valiance Expedition and came to Northrend as the Westfall Brigade, and under Captain Gryan Stoutmantle they left Sentinel Hill behind to build this encampment and fight the Scourge.

4199.name: Silverbrook
4199.description: Silverbrook is a seemingly ordinary town of human trappers in the northern Grizzly Hills, nestled among the Silverbrook Hills close to Drak'Tharon Keep. A wooden palisade with four large towers encircles its log houses. Its people are wary of outsiders, and whispers say the Wolfcult has won many sympathizers within its walls. The town has clashed with the soldiers of the Horde in the surrounding hills.

4200.name: Vordrassil's Heart
4200.description: Vordrassil's Heart is one of the three great segments of the World Tree Vordrassil that fell to earth when the tree was destroyed by the night elves long ago. It lies southwest of Grizzlemaw in the Grizzly Hills, and the land around it is covered in living ooze, evidence of the corruption that once doomed the tree.

4202.name: Vordrassil's Tears
4202.description: Vordrassil's Tears is one of the three great segments of the World Tree Vordrassil that fell to earth when the tree was destroyed by the night elves long ago. It lies southwest of the Blue Sky Logging Grounds in the Grizzly Hills, and the land around it is covered in living ooze, evidence of the corruption that once doomed the tree.

4203.name: Vordrassil's Limb
4203.description: Vordrassil's Limb is one of the three great segments of the World Tree Vordrassil that fell to earth when the tree was destroyed by the night elves long ago. It lies directly north of Amberpine Lodge in the Grizzly Hills, and the land around it is covered in living ooze, evidence of the corruption that once doomed the tree.

4204.name: Amberpine Lodge
4204.description: Amberpine Lodge is the main Alliance outpost in the western Grizzly Hills. Alliance-affiliated hunters and woodsmen built it long ago as a meeting hall, and with the war against the Lich King, the Valiance Expedition commandeered it for military use.

4205.name: Solstice Village
4205.description: Solstice Village is a trapper village on a hill in the eastern Grizzly Hills, a cluster of small wooden houses and three towers surrounded by a palisade, where wolves roam freely among the houses. The risen archmage Arugal has worked to convert its people to the Wolfcult, building a new army of worgen for the Scourge.

4206.name: Conquest Hold
4206.description: Conquest Hold is the main Horde stronghold in the Grizzly Hills, a fortress whose walls are built around a deep fighting pit. Its orc commanders are aggressive and ill-tempered even for the Horde, and leadership of the hold can be won by challenge in its pit. The barracks serve as the local inn.

4207.name: Voldrune
4207.description: Voldrune is the only vrykul village in the Grizzly Hills, built southeast of Conquest Hold on the highest ground the vrykul could find. It belongs to the Dragonflayer clan.

4208.name: Granite Springs
4208.description: Granite Springs is a small camp beside the springs south of Zeb'Halak in the northern Grizzly Hills, where travelers keep watch on the troll lands to the north.

4209.name: Zeb'Halak
4209.description: Zeb'Halak is a Drakkari village south of Drak'Tharon Keep in the Grizzly Hills, a cluster of small troll huts surrounding a ziggurat topped by a massive stone head known as the Seer of Zeb'Halak. The village fell to the Scourge before the Alliance and Horde ever arrived in Northrend, and its Drakkari were slaughtered.

4210.name: Drak'Tharon Keep
4210.description: Drak'Tharon Keep is a massive Drakkari fortress on the border between the Grizzly Hills and Zul'Drak, an impressive collection of spires and beautifully carved walls that once served the ice trolls as a formidable outpost at the edge of their kingdom. It has been claimed by the Scourge, and its fallen defenders now serve the Lich King, pouring out to assault the furbolgs and the heart of Drakkari territory. Its former leader, the Prophet Tharon'ja, has been transformed into a massive skeletal wind serpent. Not far from here, Prince Arthas is said to have struck down the dreadlord Mal'Ganis with Frostmourne.

4211.name: Camp Oneqwah
4211.description: Camp Oneqwah is a taunka camp in the central-eastern Grizzly Hills, between Grizzlemaw and the coast, where taunka from villages across Northrend plan to gather as they flee the Scourge.

4212.name: Eastwind Shore
4212.description: The Eastwind Shore is a stretch of the eastern coast of the Grizzly Hills near the Drakil'jin Ruins, overlooking Bloodmoon Isle.

4213.name: The Broken Bluffs
4213.description: The Broken Bluffs are a narrow path along the eastern edge of the Grizzly Hills and the Howling Fjord, used by stone giants under the control of the iron dwarves.

4214.name: Boulder Hills
4214.description: The Boulder Hills rise behind Thor Modan along the edge of Zul'Drak in the northeastern Grizzly Hills. Here a great earth giant leads an army of giants against the iron dwarves and their runed giant servants, while iron dwarves erupt from the ground in drilling machines to join the battle.

4215.name: Rage Fang Shrine
4215.description: Rage Fang Shrine is a furbolg shrine south of Grizzlemaw in the Grizzly Hills, held by the shamans and warriors of the Frostpaw tribe. Here dwells Orsonn, an ancient guardian and son of the Wild God Ursoc, kept a prisoner of sorts by the maddened furbolgs; he loves his people too much to hurt them and so remains.

4216.name: Drakil'jin Ruins
4216.description: The Drakil'jin Ruins lie south of Thor Modan in the eastern Grizzly Hills, a burial ground of the Drakkari Empire and its ancient kings. Their partially collapsed walls and the remains of a much larger complex are morbidly decorated with piles of skulls, and beneath them lies an underground burial complex filled with Drakkari mummies, from commoner to king.

4217.name: Blackriver Logging Camp
4217.description: The Blackriver Logging Camp is an island in the middle of the Blackriver in the Grizzly Hills that once belonged to the Venture Company, until the Alliance and the Horde chased the goblins off. The two factions now fight each other for control of the camp.

4218.name: Heart's Blood Shrine
4218.description: Heart's Blood Shrine is a furbolg shrine far east of Conquest Hold in the Grizzly Hills, held by the hunters and elders of the Redfang tribe. Here dwells Kodian, an ancient guardian and daughter of the Wild God Ursoc, kept a prisoner of sorts by the maddened furbolgs; she loves her people too much to hurt them and so remains.

4219.name: Hollowstone Mine
4219.description: Hollowstone Mine is a mine just northwest of the Westfall Brigade Encampment in the Grizzly Hills. Its miners, once friends of the trappers, refused to join the Wolfcult and paid a terrible price: they were transformed into undead, and they go on mining in the dark.

4220.name: Dun Argol
4220.description: Dun Argol is an iron dwarf city in the eastern Grizzly Hills, ruled by an iron thane. It became the capital of the iron dwarves after the fall of Thor Modan and is far more heavily populated than the Explorers' League ever expected.

4221.name: Thor Modan
4221.description: Thor Modan is an ancient dwarven city in the northeastern Grizzly Hills, its architecture much like that of Ironforge, down to a great statue at the end of its entrance hall. The Explorers' League came here seeking the origins of the dwarven race, believing dwarves were the first people in these hills. The iron dwarves claim it as their ancient home, but much of the city lies in ruins, battered by an army of giants that hurls boulders and uprooted trees at its walls, and the bodies of explorers caught in the crossfire lie strewn among the rubble.

4222.name: Blue Sky Logging Grounds
4222.description: The Blue Sky Logging Grounds are a logging camp in the northern Grizzly Hills where the two rivers of the region meet. Logs are floated from here down the river to Venture Bay, and an oil platform stands nearby.

4229.name: Prospector's Point
4229.description: Prospector's Point is a small encampment north of Dun Argol in the Grizzly Hills, where prospectors keep watch over the iron dwarves' lands.

4231.name: Redwood Trading Post
4231.description: Redwood Trading Post is a trapper camp just northeast of Camp Oneqwah in the Grizzly Hills, where a lone trapper lives with a tame bear and sells moonshine and venison to passing travelers.

4235.name: Heartwood Trading Post
4235.description: Heartwood Trading Post is a trapper outpost in the northern Grizzly Hills, now standing all but abandoned.

4236.name: Evergreen Trading Post
4236.description: Evergreen Trading Post is a trapper outpost southwest of Conquest Hold in the Grizzly Hills. Its trappers were slain amid the fighting in the hills, and soldiers now occupy it.

4238.name: White Pine Trading Post
4238.description: White Pine Trading Post is a trapper post just west of Solstice Village in the Grizzly Hills, where the struggle between the Wolfcult and those who resist it has turned bloody.

4239.name: Aspen Grove Post
4239.description: Aspen Grove Post is a trapper outpost just northeast of Amberpine Lodge in the Grizzly Hills, whose trappers have served as a point of contact between Silverbrook and the Alliance.

4240.name: Forest's Edge Post
4240.description: Forest's Edge Post is a small trapper outpost in the Grizzly Hills with a watchtower and a wooden house, where hunters from Silverbrook have taken up residence.

4242.name: Venture Bay
4242.description: Venture Bay is a small harbor on the southwestern coast of the Grizzly Hills, used by the Venture Company for its logging operations, with stables and several lumber mills. It has become a center of conflict between the Alliance and the Horde, whose scouts fight constantly for control of the bay and its lighthouse.

4244.name: Bloodmoon Isle
4244.description: Bloodmoon Isle is an island off the eastern coast of the Grizzly Hills. Standing above the trees at its top is Shadowfang Tower, the new sanctum of the archmage Arugal, who has been raised from the dead to serve the Lich King. The island is inhabited by Arugal's worgen and the human members of his Wolfcult.

4245.name: Shadowfang Tower
4245.description: Shadowfang Tower is the lair of the risen archmage Arugal on Bloodmoon Isle, off the coast of the Grizzly Hills. The Lich King took note of Arugal's work with the worgen of Silverpine Forest and brought him back from death to serve the Scourge. Built much like Shadowfang Keep, the tower is filled with members of the Wolfcult, whom Arugal gradually transforms into worgen, and a giant worg guards its stables.

4247.name: Duskhowl Den
4247.description: Duskhowl Den is a small cave beneath Solstice Village in the eastern Grizzly Hills, home to a pack of wolves.

4248.name: The Conquest Pit
4248.description: The Conquest Pit is the deep fighting pit at the heart of Conquest Hold in the Grizzly Hills, where Horde warriors test their strength in bloody combat and leadership can be won by challenge.

4249.name: The Path of Iron
4249.description: The Path of Iron is a road built by the iron dwarves that runs from Thor Modan through the eastern Grizzly Hills to Dun Argol and the Ruins of Tethys.

4250.name: Ruins of Tethys
4250.description: The Ruins of Tethys lie spread over five small islands off the coast of the Grizzly Hills, southwest of Bloodmoon Isle, reached by the Path of Iron.

4251.name: Silverbrook Hills
4251.description: The Silverbrook Hills are the picturesque hills of the northwestern Grizzly Hills surrounding Silverbrook, the largest human settlement in the region, just southeast of Drak'Tharon Keep. Horde soldiers and the woodsmen of Silverbrook have fought here.

4255.name: Ruins of Drak'Zin
4255.description: The Ruins of Drak'Zin are ancient ice troll ruins in the Grizzly Hills, remnants of the Drakkari who once contested these hills with the furbolgs.

4262.name: Ashwood Post
4262.description: Ashwood Post is a trapper outpost in the south-central Grizzly Hills, west of Ashwood Lake, standing at the crossroads where the road north from the Howling Fjord meets the main east-west road through the hills.

4266.name: Harkor's Camp
4266.description: Harkor's Camp is a small collection of tents on the northeastern coast of the Grizzly Hills, south of the Drakil'jin Ruins.

4267.name: Vordrassil Pass
4267.description: Vordrassil Pass is a passage through a great section of the trunk of the fallen World Tree Vordrassil, directly beside Grizzlemaw, leading north and then northeast toward the Westfall Brigade Encampment and Ursoc's Den.

4268.name: Ruuna's Camp
4268.description: Ruuna's Camp is a small camp near Vordrassil Pass in the central Grizzly Hills, home to a blind human seer who opposes the Wolfcult.

4270.name: Drak'atal Passage
4270.description: Drak'atal Passage is a passage from the northeastern Grizzly Hills into Zul'Drak, between Ursoc's Den and the Blue Sky Logging Grounds.

4366.name: Ursoc's Den
4366.description: Ursoc's Den is the lair of the Wild God Ursoc, who fought the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. It lies northwest of the Westfall Brigade Encampment in the Grizzly Hills: a great bear's head carved from solid rock, whose mouth opens onto a natural canyon. The furbolgs hold it sacred, and with madness spreading among them, it is said that something stirs in the den once more.

4456.name: Voldrune Dwelling
4456.description: Voldrune Dwelling is the great hall at the heart of the vrykul village of Voldrune in the Grizzly Hills.

4475.name: Zim'bo's Hideout
4475.description: Zim'bo's Hideout is the large hut in the village of Zeb'Halak in the Grizzly Hills, where a Drakkari warlord has taken refuge.

4480.name: The Forgotten Overlook
4480.description: The Forgotten Overlook is an icy cliff in the eastern Grizzly Hills overlooking Heart's Blood Shrine.

4482.name: Arriga Footbridge
4482.description: The Arriga Footbridge is a covered bridge over the Dragonspine Tributary, connecting the Grizzly Hills with the Dragonblight.

4491.name: Bonesnap's Camp
4491.description: Bonesnap's Camp is a very small Horde camp west of Silverbrook in the Grizzly Hills.

4646.name: Ashwood Lake
4646.description: Ashwood Lake is a lake in the south-central Grizzly Hills, beside Ashwood Post.

394.description: The Grizzly Hills are a forested region of southeastern Northrend, bordered by the Howling Fjord to the south, the Dragonblight to the west, and Zul'Drak to the north. Low green foothills laced with pine trees rise toward craggy mountains in the north, cut by picturesque rivers; snow lies everywhere, but the thick forest blocks the wind, and the hills seem almost warm after the Dragonblight and the Borean Tundra. Bears, wolves, foxes, deer, and snowy owls fill the woods, while wendigo and sasquatch prowl the hills. This is the homeland of the furbolgs, who gather in the great city of Grizzlemaw, built within the stump of Vordrassil, a World Tree the druids of old planted here and then destroyed when they found it corrupted. In ancient times the twin bears Ursoc and Ursol were born in these hills and made into Wild Gods. Now a creeping madness spreads among the furbolg tribes. Independent human trappers who have lived here apart from the Seven Kingdoms for generations keep trading posts throughout the forest, though many have been drawn into the mysterious Wolfcult, led by the risen archmage Arugal from Bloodmoon Isle. In the north, the Scourge holds the ice troll fortress of Drak'Tharon Keep, and the iron dwarves battle stone giants around the ruins of Thor Modan. The Venture Company has been logging the forests, and the Alliance, from Amberpine Lodge and the Westfall Brigade Encampment, and the Horde, from Conquest Hold, contest its logging camps and harbor.

400.name: Thousand Needles

439.name: The Shimmering Flats
439.description: The Shimmering Flats are a vast, dry salt pan at the southeastern end of Thousand Needles, on the border with Tanaris. Once a lake, it is now an open expanse devoid of vegetation, home to basilisks, scorpids, tortoises, and vultures, and a wrecked sailing ship lies stranded in its northern part. The heat shimmers over the white salt, and many find a strange, lonely beauty in the silence. Goblins and gnomes have set up the Mirage Raceway here, and the area is littered with the wreckage of countless failed machines.

479.name: The Rustmaul Dig Site
479.description: The Rustmaul Dig Site is an abandoned dwarven dig site in the Shimmering Flats. The Explorers' League was uncovering ruins here when a Horde war party attacked them, and the battle stirred up a nest of silithid from a nearby cave, which overran both sides. Today the site is infested with silithid, and the abandoned tents and tools of the dwarves lie scattered in the sand.

480.name: Camp E'thok
480.description: Camp E'thok is a camp of the Galak centaurs in northwestern Thousand Needles. The centaurs here raid caravans traveling through the canyon, and their camp is filled with stolen goods. A ferocious panther, said to belong to a robbed goblin merchant, is kept caged nearby.

481.name: Splithoof Crag
481.description: Splithoof Crag is a village of the Galak centaurs against the northern wall of Thousand Needles, just east of Darkcloud Pinnacle. At its center lies a cavern known as Splithoof Hold, where the centaurs guard an ancient artifact. The village is a crude collection of yurts and war banners.

482.name: Highperch
482.description: Highperch is an elevated area in western Thousand Needles, home to the proud Highperch wyverns and their nests. The tauren of Freewind Post sometimes come here to gather wyvern eggs to be raised as mounts for the Horde. The heights offer a breathtaking view of the canyon.

483.name: The Screeching Canyon
483.description: The Screeching Canyon is a canyon in southern Thousand Needles infested by aggressive Screeching harpies, whose cries echo off the walls. Roguefeather Den, the harpies' lair, lies at the back of the canyon.

484.name: Freewind Post
484.description: Freewind Post is a tauren town built high atop a mesa in Thousand Needles, out of reach of the centaur warbands that roam the canyon floor. It is reached by the tauren's ingenious wooden lifts or by a series of rope bridges spanning the adjacent pinnacles. The tauren here work to stop the Galak centaurs, watch the Grimtotem of Darkcloud Pinnacle with growing wariness, and send young tauren to Highperch to gather wyvern eggs. The town has an inn and a wind rider roost, and the sunrise from its heights is spectacular.

485.name: The Great Lift
485.description: On the side of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift rises from the canyon floor up the sheer cliffs to the Barrens far above. Its platforms carry travelers and goods between the two regions, and guards watch over its base. The lift is the main link between the Barrens and the southern lands.

487.name: Roguefeather Den
487.description: Roguefeather Den is the lair of the Screeching harpies in south-central Thousand Needles, a small cavern at the back of the Screeching Canyon where the harpies guard their gathered foodstuffs and treasures. The harpies are fierce and attack anyone who enters.

488.name: The Weathered Nook
488.description: The Weathered Nook is a small, well-hidden cave on the cliffs of Thousand Needles, north of Freewind Post, home to a pair of tauren who live there in seclusion. Few know of its existence.

1557.name: Splithoof Hold
1557.description: Splithoof Hold is a cave in Splithoof Crag in Thousand Needles that the Galak centaurs have adapted into a stronghold. The entire cave system is populated with centaurs, who guard an ancient artifact within its depths.

2097.name: Darkcloud Pinnacle
2097.description: Darkcloud Pinnacle is a village of the renegade Grimtotem tauren atop three small mesas east of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles, connected by rope bridges and reachable only by two well-guarded paths. The Grimtotem reject the tauren's alliance with the Horde, and it is whispered that their leaders correspond with an unknown dark power. The village is a dangerous place for outsiders.

2237.name: Whitereach Post
2237.description: Whitereach Post is a small Horde camp along the road near Camp E'thok in Thousand Needles, a waypoint for travelers making their way through the canyon. It is a modest camp, guarded against the centaurs who roam nearby.

2240.name: Mirage Raceway
2240.description: The Mirage Raceway is a racetrack deep within the Shimmering Flats, where goblin and gnomish engineers race their rocket-powered vehicles to settle once and for all whose engineering is superior. Twice a month, the raceway hosts events, and while no official prizes are awarded, being the best is reward enough, and plenty of betting goes on behind the scenes. The track is surrounded by the camps of the rival teams and the wreckage of countless failed machines.

2303.name: Windbreak Canyon
2303.description: Windbreak Canyon is a canyon in Thousand Needles, covering much of the area between Freewind Post and the Shimmering Flats, filled with wind serpents and their nests. The serpents soar over the canyon and attack travelers who come too close.

3037.name: Ironstone Camp
3037.description: Ironstone Camp is a small Horde camp at the border of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Its members were sent to drive out the dwarven excavators of the Rustmaul Dig Site, but they got more than they bargained for when the silithid erupted from a nearby cave. The survivors now hold the camp and fight the insects.

3038.name: Weazel's Crater
3038.description: Weazel's Crater is a large, deep crater in the northern part of the Shimmering Flats. Its origins are mysterious, though some suspect it was created by one of the unstable racing machines of the nearby raceway. It is now inhabited by basilisks.

3039.name: Tahonda Ruins
3039.description: The Tahonda Ruins are the ruins of a tauren village in the southern Shimmering Flats, near the path through the mountains to Tanaris. The village was destroyed and abandoned long ago, perhaps in an attack by the basilisks that now inhabit the ruins. Little is known about its history.

400.description: Thousand Needles is a vast, dry canyon in southern Kalimdor, filled with towering spires of sandstone that rise from the canyon floor like a forest of needles, giving the region its name. Before the Great Sundering, it was a river canyon or perhaps an inland sea, and the needles were shaped by rushing water; the Sundering thrust the land above the water table, and the canyon became a sandy gorge. In the east, it opens onto the Shimmering Flats, a vast salt pan where goblin and gnomish engineers race their machines. Despite its barrenness, the land has its own harsh beauty, and the sunrises seen from atop the mesas are spectacular. The canyons have traditionally been the territory of several tauren tribes, who were forced to live precariously atop the high mesas to escape the centaurs, and now, with the help of the Horde, they fight back from Freewind Post. The Galak centaurs patrol the canyon floor, the renegade Grimtotem tauren hold Darkcloud Pinnacle, harpies nest in the southern canyons, and wyverns roost on the western heights. Rope bridges connect the tops of many spires, allowing travelers to cross the canyon above the dangers below. The Great Lift connects the canyon with the Barrens far above, and the road leads west to Feralas and south through the flats to Tanaris.

405.name: Desolace

596.name: Kodo Graveyard
596.description: The Kodo Graveyard is a vast, bone-strewn plain in central Desolace where kodo beasts instinctively come to spend their last days. No one knows why the aging kodo make the long journey here, but the habit is ancient, and the land is filled with bones, as well as the sick and the dying. It is said that the spirits of the dead kodo still linger among the bones. Vultures circle above, and scavengers come to feast on the fallen.

597.name: Ghost Walker Post
597.description: Ghost Walker Post is a small tauren outpost in central Desolace, directly adjacent to the Kodo Graveyard. It is much more exposed to danger than the Horde's coastal village, and from here the Horde wages war on the Burning Blade and their demons, as well as the warring centaur tribes. The post offers only the bare necessities to travelers, but its tauren are steadfast and brave.

598.name: Sar'theris Strand
598.description: Sar'theris Strand is the long western coast of Desolace, a sunny and grassy shore in stark contrast to the grey wasteland of the interior. It is heavily populated by sea giants, naga, and makrura, and the wreck of a ship lies off its northern part. The waves of the Veiled Sea roll onto its beaches, and the winds create waterspouts against the lowland hills.

599.name: Thunder Axe Fortress
599.description: Thunder Axe Fortress is a stronghold in northern Desolace, held by the cultists of the Burning Blade. Within its walls, the cultists store dark artifacts used to open the demon portals at Mannoroc Coven, and it is said that they also keep a powerful relic stolen from the naga. The fortress is heavily guarded by orc warlocks and their demons.

600.name: Bolgan's Hole
600.description: Bolgan's Hole is a large cave in southwestern Desolace that houses the most prominent members of the Gelkis centaur tribe, including their khan. It is reached by crossing a treacherous rope bridge over a ravine, and it is guarded fiercely by the Gelkis warriors.

602.name: Mannoroc Coven
602.description: Mannoroc Coven is a blasted area in central Desolace, south of Ghost Walker Post, among the ruins of an ancient night elven settlement. It is named after the dreaded pit lord Mannoroth, and the already dead earth has been further scorched by the fel magic of the demons who inhabit it. Infernals, felhounds, succubi, felguards, and doomguards stalk the area, summoned by the cultists of the Burning Blade through magical portals. It is the largest demonic coven in central Kalimdor, and a deadly pall hangs over it.

603.name: Sargeron
603.description: Sargeron is a ruined night elven town in northeastern Desolace, destroyed during the War of the Ancients. Its original name has been lost to time, and its ruins are now home to the Hatefury satyrs, who have renamed it after their demonic master, Sargeras. Relics of the moon goddess Elune still lie among the ruins.

604.name: Magram Village
604.description: Magram Village is the home of the Magram centaur tribe in southeastern Desolace, its yurts and pavilions scattered across the shores and islands of a series of polluted yellow pools, connected by crude bridges. The Magram are locked in a bitter war with the Gelkis tribe, and they attack outsiders who enter their territory.

606.name: Gelkis Village
606.description: Gelkis Village is the principal village of the Gelkis centaur tribe in southwestern Desolace, built in a ring around a large ravine. A cluster of cliffs and bluffs in the ravine is connected by bridges leading to a cave where the Gelkis khan resides. The village lies directly beside the main road through Desolace, making it a hazard for travelers.

607.name: Valley of Spears
607.description: The Valley of Spears is a canyon in western Desolace, home to the Maraudine centaur tribe, the guardians of Maraudon. Only the bravest and mightiest of the tribe's warriors are chosen to guard the sacred tomb of their ancestor, and the entrance to the underground caverns of Maraudon lies in the heart of their territory. The valley is filled with centaur yurts and war banners.

608.name: Nijel's Point
608.description: Nijel's Point is an Alliance outpost in the northern mountains of Desolace, home to humans and night elves who keep watch over the wasteland. Built among ancient ruins, it offers shelter and a hippogryph roost to travelers. No one seems to know who Nijel was.

609.name: Kolkar Village
609.description: Kolkar Village is the center of power of the Kolkar centaur tribe in eastern Desolace, between Sargeron and Magram Village. The Kolkar are the most widespread of the centaur tribes, with villages and outposts in the Barrens and Durotar, and their village in Desolace is their stronghold.

2198.name: Shadowbreak Ravine
2198.description: Shadowbreak Ravine is a well-hidden area in the mountains southeast of Magram Village in Desolace, a haven for the cultists of the Burning Blade. Giant mushrooms grow among its rocks, a summoning circle with great chains stands at its heart, and a purplish atmosphere hangs over it. Felhounds and other demons roam the ravine.

2324.name: The Veiled Sea
2324.description: The waters of the Veiled Sea wash the western coast of Desolace, rolling onto the sunny, grassy Sar'theris Strand. The sea is often stormy, and the winds whip up waterspouts near the shore. Naga, sea giants, and makrura dwell in the coastal waters, and the ruins of an ancient night elven city lie beneath the waves to the northwest.

2404.name: Tethris Aran
2404.description: Tethris Aran is a series of night elven ruins in northern Desolace, just north of Thunder Axe Fortress. The settlement was presumably destroyed during the Great Sundering, and its ruins are now inhabited only by the wild creatures of Desolace. Its broken columns stand silently in the grey wasteland.

2405.name: Ethel Rethor
2405.description: Ethel Rethor is a night elven ruin in the far northwest of Desolace, most of which lies underwater, save for a lone tower with a small bridge leading to a closed entrance. The ruins are inhabited by naga, who seem to avoid the tower entirely. The site is eerie and mysterious.

2406.name: Ranazjar Isle
2406.description: Ranazjar Isle is a small, rocky island off the northwestern coast of Desolace, inhabited by naga. Many night elven ruins on the island seem to be part of the same ancient city as those of Ethel Rethor, and a statue that may depict Queen Azshara stands among them.

2407.name: Kormek's Hut
2407.description: Kormek's Hut is a small hovel in north-central Desolace, apparently once the home of a centaur outcast. It is now inhabited by a strange pair of strangers who have made the hut their own, and a small pen stands outside. It is a lonely place amid the wasteland.

2408.name: Shadowprey Village
2408.description: Shadowprey Village is a troll fishing village on the southern coast of Desolace, along the sunny Sar'theris Strand. Its troll fishermen supply food to the Horde's outpost at Ghost Walker Post, and the village is also a travel hub for the Horde, with an inn offering a beautiful view of the sea. A dryad of the Cenarion Circle works nearby, investigating the remains of the centaur's ancestor.

2617.name: Scrabblescrew's Camp
2617.description: Scrabblescrew's Camp is a small goblin camp near the Kodo Graveyard in Desolace, home to an enterprising goblin who runs a kodo caravan. The camp is a modest collection of tents and crates, and its owner is always looking for opportunities to profit in the harsh land.

2657.name: Valley of Bones
2657.description: The Valley of Bones is a crag in southern Desolace, infested by skeletons and centaur necromancers. Collapsed against the cliff wall are several massive skeletons resembling serpentine giants, clad in armor, one of them still holding a trident. Many believe the valley is cursed, and most centaur tribes avoid it. Some say the bones belong to ancient and terrible beings.

405.description: Desolace is a grey, rocky wasteland in western Kalimdor, isolated by the Stonetalon Mountains to the north and the mountains of Feralas to the south, with the grasslands of Mulgore to the east and the storm-tossed coast of the Veiled Sea to the west. It seems to lie under a supernatural curse: its skies are always dark and stormy, lightning and high winds sweep the land, pools of yellow, polluted water dot the landscape, and the husks of long-dead trees jut from the grey ash. The skulls of ancient kodo stare from their graves, half-buried in dust. Desolace is the homeland of the centaur, who, according to legend, were born in the depths of Maraudon from the dark union of a son of the demigod Cenarius and a princess of the earth elementals. Four warring centaur tribes, the Kolkar, the Gelkis, the Magram, and the Maraudine, dominate the region, fighting each other as fiercely as they fight outsiders. Proud but sorrowful ruins of the ancient Highborne night elves stand scattered across the land, and naga haunt the northwestern coast. In recent times, the cultists of the Burning Blade have summoned demons into the land, threatening to turn it into a stronghold of the Burning Legion. The Alliance holds Nijel's Point in the northern mountains, while the Horde maintains Shadowprey Village on the coast and Ghost Walker Post near the center. In sad contrast to the wasteland of the interior, the western coast is sunny and lush.

406.name: Stonetalon Mountains

460.name: Sun Rock Retreat
460.description: Sun Rock Retreat is a tauren settlement in the middle of the Stonetalon Mountains, south of Mirkfallon Lake, run by a tauren druid. It is home to tauren and orc shamans and warriors devoted to repairing the damage done to the mountains by the Venture Company and investigating the elementals rising from the Charred Vale. The retreat is built of tents and totems on a sheltered rock, and a wind rider master connects it with Thunder Bluff.

461.name: Windshear Crag
461.description: Windshear Crag was once a massive old-growth forest in a valley in the Stonetalon Mountains, leading from the southern border of Ashenvale into the stormy canyons of the range. Now it is the site of a massive logging operation by the goblins of the Venture Company, and the once green landscape has become a barren expanse of tree stumps, polluted waters, and creaking machinery. The operation is overseen by a gnome who is now more machine than flesh, and enormous reaping machines reduce the mightiest trees to sawdust.

463.name: Cragpool Lake
463.description: Cragpool Lake is a small lake in Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains, over which the goblins of the Venture Company have built an enormous wooden structure. From its platform, the overseer of the logging operation watches over his workers. The lake's waters are polluted by the goblins' activities.

464.name: Mirkfallon Lake
464.description: Mirkfallon Lake is a lake high in the Stonetalon Mountains, once home to the tallest waterfall in Kalimdor. The legendary hippogryphs migrate here from the cooler north, and wyverns, slimes, and thunder lizards also roam its shores, while the spiders of Stonetalon lay their eggs nearby. The lake is beautiful and wild.

465.name: The Charred Vale
465.description: The Charred Vale lies in the southwest of the Stonetalon Mountains. Once a tranquil vale, nothing remains of its beauty: the earth is blackened by the flames that consumed its trees, and an evil glow lies over the area. It is now infested by harpies, scorched basilisks, fire elementals, charred ancients, and chimaeras. At its southern end lies the passage to Desolace.

466.name: Valley of the Bloodfuries
466.description: The Valley of the Bloodfuries is a canyon stronghold in the Stonetalon Mountains, home to the infamous Bloodfury harpies. The canyon walls are lined with giant harpy nests and guano, and the bones of their victims litter the valley floor along with abundant treasure. Few who enter the valley survive an encounter with its fierce inhabitants.

467.name: Stonetalon Peak
467.description: Stonetalon Peak is the highest mountain in the Stonetalon range, in the far north of the region, a verdant mountain valley that shows what the entire region looked like before the goblins and elementals arrived. It has long been sacred to both the night elves and the tauren, and the night elves maintain an outpost, a moonwell, and a barrow den here, where druids sleep and commune with the Emerald Dream, aided by dryads and keepers of the grove. During the Third War, it was here that the Alliance and the Horde briefly united against the Burning Legion.

468.name: The Talon Den
468.description: The Talon Den is a barrow den on Stonetalon Peak, inhabited by druids, dryads, and keepers of the grove of the Cenarion Circle. Here the druids slumber and walk the Emerald Dream, protected by the guardians of the forest. The den is a sacred and peaceful place.

469.name: Greatwood Vale
469.description: Greatwood Vale is a forested valley in the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains, linking the dry expanse of the Barrens with the mountains proper. For millennia, its fertile recesses have been a hunting and camping ground for the tauren tribes. Recently, the renegade Grimtotem tribe attacked and destroyed the tauren loyal to the Horde here, burning their camp and slaughtering its inhabitants.

636.name: Blackwolf River
636.description: The Blackwolf River is a small river running through Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains, which over the ages has carved the canyons of the range. Its waters are now heavily polluted by the activities of the Venture Company.

1076.name: Webwinder Path
1076.description: Webwinder Path is a narrow path in the Stonetalon Mountains leading to Windshear Crag, filled with giant Deepmoss spiders and their eggs. Webs cover the rocks on either side, and travelers must take care not to become entangled.

1277.name: The Talondeep Path
1277.description: On the side of the Stonetalon Mountains, the Talondeep Path is a winding tunnel through the mountains leading north to Ashenvale, with its entrance in the northwestern part of Windshear Crag. The tunnel is riddled with small dead ends and holes in the walls, but it is otherwise empty and quiet.

2160.name: Windshear Mine
2160.description: Windshear Mine is a mine in the southeastern corner of Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains, filled with aggressive kobold miners working for the Venture Company. The mine is rich in tin, and its tunnels are lit by the kobolds' candles.

2537.name: Grimtotem Post
2537.description: Grimtotem Post is the base of operations of the renegade Grimtotem tauren in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Grimtotem, who reject the tauren's alliance with the Horde, patrol the post and the surrounding areas with brutes, sorcerers, and mercenaries, and they attack any who come near.

2538.name: Camp Aparaje
2538.description: Camp Aparaje is a demolished tauren camp in the eastern Stonetalon Mountains, along the main road. It was burned and destroyed in the conflict between the Grimtotem and the tauren loyal to the Horde, and the Grimtotem now prowl its ruins, attacking anyone who comes near.

2539.name: Malaka'jin
2539.description: Malaka'jin is a small camp of Darkspear trolls in the southern Stonetalon Mountains, just south of Grimtotem Post. It houses a community of troll hunters who make a modest income selling their catches to passing Horde travelers, and it is said that the trolls here are mounting covert attacks against the night elves of Stonetalon Peak. The camp is built of huts and totems.

2540.name: Boulderslide Ravine
2540.description: Boulderslide Ravine is a small ravine in the Stonetalon Mountains that leads into Boulderslide Cavern. Loose rocks and boulders litter the ravine, and the sound of kobold picks echoes from the cavern within.

2541.name: Sishir Canyon
2541.description: Sishir Canyon is a canyon in the Stonetalon Mountains completely taken over by monstrous Deepmoss spiders. Their eggs and webbing densely cover the whole area, and the most powerful of their number is said to lurk deep inside. Few dare to enter.

3157.name: Boulderslide Cavern
3157.description: Boulderslide Cavern is a mine in Boulderslide Ravine in the Stonetalon Mountains, worked by Gogger kobolds who are frantically mining a rare crystal known as resonite, which carries traces of earthen magic. It is said that the kobolds have dug so deep that they have uncovered something ancient slumbering within.

406.description: The Stonetalon Mountains are a rugged range of peaks in central Kalimdor, lying west of the Barrens, south of Ashenvale, and north of Desolace. Once a low set of hills, the land was thrust high into the sky by the Great Sundering, and the Blackwolf River has since carved it into a vast network of canyons and cliffs. The climate is extreme: the lower elevations are windy, hot, and dry, while rain clouds crash against the western peaks, and the constant, often violent winds, known as the Ill Winds, whip through the canyons. The highest peaks are thickly forested with evergreens, and Stonetalon Peak, the tallest mountain, has long been sacred to both the night elves and the tauren; it was once the home of the Oracle, and during the Third War the Alliance and the Horde briefly united there to fight the Burning Legion. The mountains have traditionally formed a border where night elves and tauren coexist. Today the goblins of the Venture Company are ravaging the land, cutting down the ancient forests of Windshear Crag and polluting the waters, the once lush Charred Vale is a burned ruin full of fire elementals, harpies dwell in their canyon strongholds, and the renegade Grimtotem tauren have attacked their own kin. The night elves hold Stonetalon Peak, the tauren Sun Rock Retreat, and the Darkspear trolls a small camp in the south.

408.name: Gillijim's Isle
408.description: Gillijim's Isle is a remote island in the South Seas off the southern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, lying south of the Island of Doctor Lapidis. Old charts mark it as a jungle island once inhabited by trolls, but few living sailors have set foot on its shores, and the waters around it are far from the usual shipping lanes. The surrounding sea is warm, deep, and blue, home to sharks and other creatures of the open ocean, and the currents can carry the unwary far from land. Tales speak of ancient troll ruins hidden in its jungles, but whatever secrets the island holds remain lost to most of the world.

409.name: Island of Doctor Lapidis
409.description: The Island of Doctor Lapidis is a remote island in the South Seas off the southwestern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, lying north of Gillijim's Isle. Old charts mark it as a jungle island holding the crumbling ruins of the ancient jungle trolls, but few have visited it in living memory, and its origins and the meaning of its name are known to few. The waters around it are deep, warm, and empty of ships, far from the usual shipping lanes, home only to sharks and the creatures of the open sea. The island remains a mystery, a dark speck on the horizon that most sailors prefer to avoid.

440.name: Tanaris

976.name: Gadgetzan
976.description: Gadgetzan is a goblin town in northern Tanaris, the headquarters of the Steamwheedle Cartel on Kalimdor and a neutral haven open to all races and factions. Its walls of wood and metal enclose an inn, an auction house, merchants, and a flight master, and its goblin bruisers keep the peace with brutal efficiency, attacking anyone who breaks the town's rules. Water is precious in the desert, and the goblins have built water towers to supply the town. Gadgetzan is a busy, noisy place of trade, gossip, and invention.

977.name: Steamwheedle Port
977.description: Steamwheedle Port is a goblin harbor on the eastern coast of Tanaris, run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Its docks are busy with goblin ships, though the goblins have proved unwilling to share them with other races. The port is neutral and open to all, and its goblins trade goods from across the seas.

978.name: Zul'Farrak
978.description: Zul'Farrak is the city of the Sandfury trolls in northwestern Tanaris, an ancient troll city of sun-baked stone, temples, and ziggurats rising from the desert sands. Believed to have once been an outpost of the Gurubashi Empire, it is now ruled by the Sandfury, who are hostile to all outsiders. Troll legends speak of a powerful sword split in half and hidden within the city's walls, and whispers tell of an ancient creature sleeping within a sacred pool at its heart.

979.name: Sandsorrow Watch
979.description: Sandsorrow Watch is an area of northwestern Tanaris heavily populated by Sandfury trolls, near their city of Zul'Farrak. Their dwellings and warriors dot the landscape, and the trolls attack any who come near.

980.name: Thistleshrub Valley
980.description: Thistleshrub Valley is a valley in southwestern Tanaris, thick with giant cacti, unusually alive for the desert, and desert-dwelling thistleshrubs, living plants that attack intruders. A path between two great stone pillars leads from the valley down into Un'Goro Crater.

981.name: The Gaping Chasm
981.description: The Gaping Chasm is one of the minor silithid hives in southeastern Tanaris, a large hive complex filled with silithid insects. The chasm is dark and dangerous, and the insects swarm out to attack anyone who comes near.

982.name: The Noxious Lair
982.description: The Noxious Lair is one of the minor silithid hives in southwestern Tanaris, overlooking Un'Goro Crater. The land around it is slightly sunken, as if a river or lake once lay there, and great twitching claws of buried silithid jut from the sand, which is drenched with their foul goo.

983.name: Dunemaul Compound
983.description: The Dunemaul Compound is the stronghold of the Dunemaul ogres in southern Tanaris, from which they have spread to occupy the ancient troll ruins of Eastmoon and Southmoon. The compound is a crude collection of huts and caves, and the ogres attack anyone who enters their territory.

984.name: Eastmoon Ruins
984.description: The Eastmoon Ruins are ancient troll ruins in southern Tanaris, now taken over by the Dunemaul ogres from their nearby compound. The crumbling stone structures are half-buried in sand.

985.name: Waterspring Field
985.description: Waterspring Field is an area of Tanaris east of Gadgetzan, so named for the many water towers that pump water from deep underground reserves. The goblins of Gadgetzan built the towers to supply their desert operations, but a band of nomadic bandits known as the Wastewanders has seized the field and the towers for themselves.

986.name: Zalashji's Den
986.description: Zalashji's Den is a small cave on the eastern coast of Tanaris, the home of a solitary naga. It is a quiet, damp place, and little is known of its inhabitant's purpose.

987.name: Land's End Beach
987.description: Land's End Beach is the southernmost point of the Tanaris Desert, at the far southeastern tip of Kalimdor, an abandoned stretch of coastline reachable only by sea. A crashed flying machine and some driftwood lie in the sand. In the distance, a mysterious island can be seen across the water.

988.name: Wavestrider Beach
988.description: Wavestrider Beach is a stretch of beach on the eastern shore of Tanaris, between Steamwheedle Port and Zalashji's Den. Burning ships can be seen far off the coast, and snapping turtles roam the shoreline. The sea breeze offers some relief from the heat of the desert.

989.name: Uldum
989.description: Uldum is an ancient land of the titans hidden in the far south of Tanaris, beyond the Valley of the Watchers. Its great gates, flanked by colossal titan statues, have remained sealed for ages, and scholars of the Explorers' League have long sought a way inside, searching for evidence of the world's origins. Whatever lies beyond the gates remains a mystery.

990.name: Valley of the Watchers
990.description: The Valley of the Watchers is a valley in southern Tanaris leading to the sealed gates of Uldum, guarded by mighty mountain giants. Colossal statues of the titans gaze out over the valley. A small dwarven camp of the Explorers' League has been set up nearby to study the ancient site.

991.name: Gunstan's Post
991.description: Gunstan's Post is a small dwarven camp in southern Tanaris, east of the Valley of the Watchers, set up by explorers of the Explorers' League who are studying the ancient titan gates of Uldum. The camp is a modest collection of tents and digging equipment.

992.name: Southmoon Ruins
992.description: The Southmoon Ruins are ancient troll ruins in southern Tanaris, just northeast of Uldum, now taken over by the Dunemaul ogres. The crumbling stone structures are half-buried in sand.

1336.name: Lost Rigger Cove
1336.description: Lost Rigger Cove is a cove on the eastern coast of Tanaris, protected by mountains on three sides, the hideout of the Southsea pirates. The pirates build ships here, and agents of the Steamwheedle Cartel constantly try to disrupt their operations. The cove is filled with ships, docks, and pirate camps.

1937.name: Noonshade Ruins
1937.description: The Noonshade Ruins are ancient troll ruins east of Gadgetzan in Tanaris, now overrun by the Wastewander bandits. The crumbling stone structures offer the bandits shelter from the desert sun.

1938.name: Broken Pillar
1938.description: The Broken Pillar is a small group of troll ruins south of Gadgetzan in Tanaris, east of the Abyssal Sands, where a goblin scientist has set up camp to study the mysteries of the desert. The broken pillar that gives the area its name rises from the sand.

1939.name: Abyssal Sands
1939.description: The Abyssal Sands are an endless sea of dunes in Tanaris, said to be home to sand-dwelling silithid that live in hive tunnels just beneath the surface, waiting for unwary travelers. The heat is relentless, and the dunes stretch to the horizon.

1940.name: Southbreak Shore
1940.description: Southbreak Shore is an expanse of flat beach in Tanaris, south of Lost Rigger Cove. It is quiet and almost deserted, save for turtles and sea giants roaming the surf. A small island lies just off the coast.

2300.name: Caverns of Time
2300.description: The Caverns of Time are a vast cave system in eastern Tanaris, the home of the bronze dragonflight and their Aspect, Nozdormu the Timeless One. Charged by the titans with guarding the flow of time, the bronze dragons watch over the caverns, which act as a crossroads for the various timelines, with portals leading to key moments in the world's history. Great bronze dragons patrol the entrance, and relics of past ages lie half-buried in the sands nearby. It is said that those who slip into the caverns without permission never return the same.

2317.name: South Seas
2317.description: The South Seas wash the southern coast of Tanaris, warm and blue under the desert sun. Burning ships and distant islands can be seen on the horizon, and pirates, sea giants, and turtles dwell along the coast. The waters stretch south toward the goblin islands and unknown lands beyond.

440.description: Tanaris is a vast desert in southeastern Kalimdor, lying south of Thousand Needles and east of Un'Goro Crater, an endless sea of sand dunes under a cloudless sky, blazing hot by day and frequently swept by dangerous sandstorms. The southern part of the desert is more mountainous, with great cavern networks extending deep beneath the surface, largely unexplored. Tanaris has been a desert for ages, and it is the ancestral home of the bronze dragonflight, the guardians of time, whose Aspect Nozdormu dwells in the Caverns of Time in the east. In the south lies the gateway to Uldum, an ancient city of the titans, sealed for ages. The goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel have made Tanaris their main base on the continent, founding the town of Gadgetzan and the harbor of Steamwheedle Port, both neutral and open to all. The desert is dangerous: the Sandfury trolls rule from their city of Zul'Farrak in the northwest, the Dunemaul ogres hold ancient ruins in the south, the Wastewander bandits have seized the water towers near Gadgetzan, Southsea pirates hide in a cove on the coast, and silithid hives lurk beneath the sands. Hyenas, scorpids, basilisks, and vultures roam the dunes, and drakes soar on the hot winds.

457.name: The Veiled Sea
457.description: The Veiled Sea is the great ocean washing the western coasts of Kalimdor, stretching from the shores of Darkshore, Ashenvale, Desolace, and Feralas far out into the unknown west. It is often shrouded in mist, giving it its name, and its waters are deep, cold in the north and warmer in the south. The great tree of Teldrassil rises from its waters off the northwestern coast, and the Azuremyst Isles, where the draenei vessel crashed, lie within it. Naga, sea giants, and sea serpents dwell in its depths, and the drowned ruins of ancient night elven cities lie beneath its waves. Beyond the known coasts, the sea is largely uncharted, and some scholars believe it eventually meets the Forbidding Sea on the far side of the world.

490.name: Un'Goro Crater

537.name: Fire Plume Ridge
537.description: Fire Plume Ridge is the active volcano at the center of Un'Goro Crater, its slopes streaked with flowing lava. Fire elementals prowl its slopes, and a mighty fire elemental is said to dwell at its peak. The heat is intense, and the air shimmers above the molten rock. Rare herbs and ores can be found on its slopes by those brave enough to climb.

538.name: Lakkari Tar Pits
538.description: The Lakkari Tar Pits are a series of bubbling pools of tar in north-central Un'Goro Crater, south of Marshal's Refuge and north of Fire Plume Ridge. Giant bones of ancient creatures lie half-sunk in the tar, and tar beasts, creatures formed of living pitch, roam the area.

539.name: Terror Run
539.description: Terror Run is the aptly named area in the southwestern part of Un'Goro Crater, infested with giant dinosaurs of every kind, including devilsaurs, pterrordax, and stegodons. It is one of the most dangerous places in the crater, where the ground trembles with the footsteps of great beasts.

540.name: The Slithering Scar
540.description: The Slithering Scar is an area in southern Un'Goro Crater, home to the Gorishi silithid hive. The insects have dug deep into the earth, and their hive is filled with chittering silithid. Strangely, no pylon stands near this part of the crater.

541.name: Marshal's Refuge
541.description: Marshal's Refuge is a small camp on the northern wall of Un'Goro Crater, a gathering place for explorers, scholars, and adventurers of all races who come to study the crater's wonders. Its tents and makeshift shelters are protected by the high rocks, and a flight master connects it with Gadgetzan and Cenarion Hold. The camp is a lively place of research and adventure.

542.name: Fungal Rock
542.description: Fungal Rock is a cave in the northeastern wall of Un'Goro Crater, inhabited by gorillas. Giant mushrooms grow at its entrance, and the gorillas fiercely defend their home.

543.name: Golakka Hot Springs
543.description: The Golakka Hot Springs are a region in western Un'Goro Crater, north of Terror Run, featuring geysers and steaming pools heated by the nearby volcano. A goblin scientist is said to study the springs and their connection to Fire Plume Ridge. The air is thick with steam.

1942.name: The Marshlands
1942.description: The Marshlands are an area in southeastern Un'Goro Crater, a swampy region inhabited by very large raptors. A path leads up the crater wall here toward Tanaris.

1943.name: Ironstone Plateau
1943.description: The Ironstone Plateau is a region in northeastern Un'Goro Crater, home to fledgling pterrordax, with several stretches of bare rock along the crater wall. It is quiet and secluded.

4381.name: Waygate
4381.description: The Waygate in Un'Goro Crater is an ancient titan device on the bluffs above Marshal's Refuge, capable of transporting those who know how to use it to a distant counterpart far to the north, in the Sholazar Basin of Northrend. Its stone framework is covered in titan runes, and it hums with ancient power.

4382.name: The Shaper's Terrace
4382.description: The Shaper's Terrace is an ancient titan structure on the bluffs above Marshal's Refuge in Un'Goro Crater, recently discovered and linked by a waygate to the Sholazar Basin in Northrend. It is related to the titan buildings found in Northrend and elsewhere in southern Kalimdor, and it holds secrets of the titans' work in shaping the world. Agents of dark powers have been seen there.

490.description: Un'Goro Crater is a vast, lush crater in southern Kalimdor, lying between the deserts of Tanaris and Silithus, isolated from the rest of the world by its towering walls. Within, a steaming jungle of exotic plants and enormous creatures thrives: dinosaurs such as devilsaurs, stegodons, and pterrordax roam freely, giant gorillas dwell in the caves, and silithid have dug hives in the south. At the center of the crater rises an active volcano, Fire Plume Ridge, where fire elementals prowl, and hot springs and tar pits bubble across the land. Strange, glowing crystals dot the landscape, and mysterious pylons stand on the ridges of the crater, their purpose unknown. Its name means God Lands in the ancient Qiraji tongue, and legends say that during the War of the Shifting Sands, the Qiraji could not take this land; many scholars believe the crater was a place of the titans, and an ancient titan terrace with a waygate has recently been found on its eastern bluffs. Explorers, scholars, and adventurers of all races gather at Marshal's Refuge on the northern wall, studying the crater's wonders. The air is hot and humid, and the sounds of the jungle never cease.

493.name: Moonglade

656.name: Lake Elune'ara
656.description: Lake Elune'ara is a large lake in the heart of Moonglade, one of the largest on the continent of Kalimdor, its still waters reflecting the eternal moonlit sky. The village of Nighthaven lies on its shores. Legends say that a mad demigod, defeated many centuries ago, still slumbers in its depths, rising once a year when the moon is at its height. The lake is beautiful and serene, and young druids dive into its waters as part of their training.

2361.name: Nighthaven
2361.description: Nighthaven is the only town in Moonglade, a peaceful village on the shores of Lake Elune'ara where night elves and tauren of the Cenarion Circle live together in harmony. It once held the largest concentration of night elves on Kalimdor, and it has survived for centuries despite demon and undead attacks. Its buildings are built to mesh with the surrounding woods, and its way of life is rooted in nature. Druids of all races come here to train and to seek the wisdom of the Circle, and the village is fiercely protected.

2362.name: Shrine of Remulos
2362.description: The Shrine of Remulos is a shrine in western Moonglade, dedicated to Keeper Remulos, son of the demigod Cenarius and one of the greatest protectors of the Moonglade. The shrine is a peaceful glade of great trees and moonlight, and Remulos himself is often found here, watching over the land and offering counsel to druids.

2363.name: Stormrage Barrow Dens
2363.description: The Stormrage Barrow Dens are the sacred barrow dens in the northeastern corner of Moonglade, an ancient underground complex of passages and chambers where many night elf druids slumber while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. They are named for the great druid Malfurion Stormrage, who sleeps deep within, his spirit lost somewhere in the Dream. The dome in the center of the hill once held the lair of the demigod Cenarius and is now a shrine to his memory. Recently, the peace of the dens has been threatened by strange creatures emerging from the Emerald Dream.

493.description: Moonglade is a sacred, sylvan valley on the lower slopes of Mount Hyjal in northern Kalimdor, lying east of Felwood and below Winterspring, surrounded by tall mountains that shelter it from the outside world. It is a magical forest draped in perpetual night, where the moon hangs high in the ebon sky and bathes the land in a silvery glow, and the weather is a warm, endless summer eve. Moonglade is the home of the Cenarion Circle, the order of druids, and a haven where night elves and tauren live peacefully together, united by their reverence for nature; conflict between the races is not tolerated by its protectors. For thousands of years, the night elf druids slumbered in the Barrow Dens here, their spirits walking the Emerald Dream, and the land remained untouched even when the Burning Legion ravaged the world. During the Third War, the druids awoke to fight the demons. Today the great druid Malfurion Stormrage, for whom the Barrow Dens are named, remains lost somewhere within the Emerald Dream. The village of Nighthaven lies on the shores of the great Lake Elune'ara, and the land is watched over by the Keepers of the Grove, sons of the demigod Cenarius, and by ancients and treants. Druids of every race come here to train and commune with the spirits of nature.

495.name: Howling Fjord

3980.name: Daggercap Bay
3980.description: Daggercap Bay is the great bay at the heart of the Howling Fjord, surrounded by Valgarde on its western shore, the vrykul town of Nifflevar on the eastern cliffs, and the mighty Utgarde Keep at its head, where the Falls of Ymiron feed it from Lake Cauldros. Its frozen waters are home to hammerhead sharks, and vrykul harpoon guns menace any ship that sails in.

3981.name: Valgarde
3981.description: Valgarde is the oldest Alliance settlement in Northrend, a fortified port on the western shore of Daggercap Bay in the Howling Fjord and the Alliance's eastern gateway to the continent. Humans and dwarves live behind its walls, and ships from Menethil Harbor arrive at its docks. The town is constantly raided by the vrykul of nearby Utgarde Keep, and its defenders fight to hold the line.

3982.name: Wyrmskull Village
3982.description: Wyrmskull Village is a vrykul village of the Dragonflayer clan in the Howling Fjord, north of Valgarde, lying in front of Utgarde Keep and the Utgarde Catacombs. From here, the vrykul attack ships with their harpoon guns. The village is ancient, and the spirits of the vrykul dead still dwell here, while the sway of the Lich King is strong among the living.

3983.name: Utgarde Keep
3983.description: Utgarde Keep is a mighty vrykul fortress on the shores of Lake Cauldros in the Howling Fjord, built into the fjord itself so that a lake lies at its feet and waterfalls tumble down the cliffs on either side, serving as a dam for the lake. It is the stronghold of the Dragonflayer vrykul and their king, Ymiron, who has pledged himself to the Lich King, and a San'layn prince of the Scourge is said to reside there. The keep's halls and the pinnacle above are filled with vrykul warriors and their undead allies.

3984.name: Nifflevar
3984.description: Nifflevar is a vrykul town of the Dragonflayer clan high atop the cliffs surrounding Daggercap Bay in the Howling Fjord, larger than Wyrmskull Village and lying in the shadow of Utgarde Keep. Many of its wooden houses are built over the edge of the cliff, and harpoon guns of every size are trained on the bay below.

3985.name: Falls of Ymiron
3985.description: The Falls of Ymiron are the great waterfalls running down the dam built into Utgarde Keep in the Howling Fjord, feeding water from Lake Cauldros into Daggercap Bay. Their roar echoes across the fjord.

3987.name: The Isle of Spears
3987.description: The Isle of Spears is an island in the western Howling Fjord, home to the tuskarr villages of Kamagua and Iskaal. It is reached by the ancient vrykul lift that runs down from the cliffs across the water.

3988.name: Kamagua
3988.description: Kamagua is a tuskarr port on the northwestern shore of the Isle of Spears, the largest tuskarr village in the Howling Fjord, run by the Kalu'ak. Its round-backed buildings, shaped like great fish, have lower levels dug into the frozen earth to keep warm. It is a major stopping point in the travels of many tuskarr clans, and a great sea turtle carries passengers from here to Moa'ki Harbor in the Dragonblight.

3989.name: Garvan's Reef
3989.description: Garvan's Reef is a reef near the Isle of Spears in the southwestern Howling Fjord, where the cold sea breaks over the rocks.

3990.name: Scalawag Point
3990.description: Scalawag Point is a fortified pirate port on the southern end of an island south of the Isle of Spears in the Howling Fjord, home to the Northsea Freebooters and their three frigates. The pirates have armed the camp with many defenses, and they are hostile to all.

3991.name: New Agamand
3991.description: New Agamand is a Forsaken town in the Howling Fjord, named after the Agamand family and their mills in Tirisfal Glades. Unlike most Forsaken towns, it was built from the ground up in the dark, gothic, and spindly Forsaken style. The Royal Apothecary Society has been testing its new plague, meant to destroy the Scourge, around the town, and the land around it has turned dead and brown amid the green fjord.

3992.name: The Ancient Lift
3992.description: The Ancient Lift is a vrykul-built gondola that runs from the high cliffs of the southwestern Howling Fjord down and across the water to the Isle of Spears. Its cars are wooden dragon boats running on a long rope, swaying in the cold wind above the choppy waters, and the tuskarr use it freely.

3994.name: Halgrind
3994.description: Halgrind is a vrykul town in the Howling Fjord that was exposed to the new plague of the Forsaken, serving as a testing ground for the Royal Apothecary Society. The Forsaken took control of the town, and the remaining vrykul are trapped and slowly dying, while their chieftain fled.

3996.name: Baelgun's Excavation Site
3996.description: Baelgun's Excavation Site is a massive dig site in the southeastern Howling Fjord, on the cliffs leading down from the Explorers' League Outpost to the sea. The dwarves uncovered a huge, almost intact statue emerging from the cliff, the work of the titans, but the site has been taken over by the iron dwarves, who prevent further excavation.

3997.name: Explorers' League Outpost
3997.description: The Explorers' League Outpost is an Alliance camp in the southeastern Howling Fjord, east of Nifflevar, where dwarven explorers study the titan ruins of the region and contend with the mysterious iron dwarves.

3998.name: Westguard Keep
3998.description: Westguard Keep is an Alliance fortress atop the cliffs on the western side of the Howling Fjord, with a joint human and dwarven population and a dwarven statue at its center. It serves as the Alliance's aerial gateway to Northrend, with flying machines and a commandeered goblin zeppelin, and its soldiers fight the vrykul of the north.

3999.name: Steel Gate
3999.description: Steel Gate is an excavation site of the Explorers' League in the Howling Fjord, east of the Apothecary Camp and north of Westguard Keep. The digging has dammed the river that once ran through it to the sea.

4000.name: Vengeance Landing
4000.description: Vengeance Landing is the military outpost of the Hand of Vengeance in the northeastern Howling Fjord, the Horde's port in the region, built and run entirely by the Forsaken under the direction of Sylvanas Windrunner. Its docks receive ships from Tirisfal Glades, and a zeppelin tower connects it with the Undercity. A sickly yellow pall hangs over the town, and its defenders fight the vrykul and the Alliance.

4001.name: Baleheim
4001.description: Baleheim is a vrykul town of the Winterskorn clan east of Utgarde Keep and north of Nifflevar in the Howling Fjord, loyal to King Ymiron. Its warriors wage war against the Forsaken of Vengeance Landing.

4002.name: Skorn
4002.description: Skorn is a large vrykul fortress in the northern Howling Fjord, the home of the Winterskorn clan, sitting atop a large hill with a commanding view of the surrounding countryside. Its vrykul prefer hurling frost magic from their watchtowers to manning harpoon guns.

4003.name: Fort Wildervar
4003.description: Fort Wildervar is the Alliance's northernmost outpost in the Howling Fjord, at the base of Frostblade Peak, a sturdy fort of timber and stone whose soldiers and settlers mine the mountain and fight the vrykul and wild beasts of the north.

4005.name: Ivald's Ruin
4005.description: Ivald's Ruin is an excavation site northeast of Nifflevar in the Howling Fjord, where a massive statue's hand rises from the rocky soil, holding a torch aloft. The ruins are the work of the titans, but the iron dwarves have taken over the site.

4006.name: Gjalerbron
