4006.description: Gjalerbron is a vrykul fortress in the mountains of the northern Howling Fjord, where the vrykul, aided by the Scourge, conduct rituals to awaken their long-slumbering kin and to raise their dead as undead warriors. Its lower Waking Halls are filled with sleeping vrykul, while its upper terrace is the site of a great ceremony to revive their king.

4018.name: Camp Winterhoof
4018.description: Camp Winterhoof is a taunka village at the northern edge of the Howling Fjord, on the eastern slope of the mountain Gjalerhorn. Its bright totem poles and rounded, snow-shedding houses are built around hot springs bubbling up from the mountain, and its chieftain has allied his people with the Horde.

4048.name: Ember Clutch
4048.description: Ember Clutch is a forest in the west-central Howling Fjord consumed by a perpetual, magically enhanced fire. These woods were once a peaceful place where proto-dragons laid their eggs and raised their young, until the vrykul awoke. Ancients of the forest watch over the burning trees.

4050.name: Derelict Strand
4050.description: The Derelict Strand is a stretch of the eastern coast of the Howling Fjord, south of Vengeance Landing, where several ships of the Alliance's fleet wrecked, and their surviving crews have set up camp.

4051.name: The Frozen Glade
4051.description: The Frozen Glade is a glade of frost nymphs just south of Caldemere Lake in the Howling Fjord, still intact and untainted by the Scourge. Its nymphs have revealed themselves to seek help from those willing to aid them.

4052.name: The Vibrant Glade
4052.description: The Vibrant Glade is a well-lit, lush glade just northeast of Skorn in the Howling Fjord.

4053.name: The Twisted Glade
4053.description: The Twisted Glade was once a frost nymph glade like the Frozen Glade, in the northern Howling Fjord between Camp Winterhoof and Fort Wildervar, but it has since become corrupted, and its keeper has turned dark.

4054.name: Rivenwood
4054.description: Rivenwood is a forest infested with giant spiders south of Gjalerbron in the northwestern Howling Fjord. Web-wrapped soldiers and adventurers hang from the trees as the spiders' food.

4055.name: Caldemere Lake
4055.description: Caldemere Lake is a lake in the northern Howling Fjord, between Fort Wildervar and the Frozen Glade.

4056.name: Utgarde Catacombs
4056.description: The Utgarde Catacombs are a part of the Utgarde Keep complex in the Howling Fjord, entered through a crevice in Wyrmskull Village. A long spiraling path leads to great vrykul halls filled with undead, and it is said the vrykul are using the undead to dig a tunnel to Gjalerbron.

4057.name: Shield Hill
4057.description: Shield Hill is an ancient vrykul burial ground at the southernmost point of the Howling Fjord. Pirates robbed its graves of their artifacts, disturbing the spirits of the dead, and it is said that their crime is what drew the cursed kvaldir to Northrend's shores.

4058.name: Lake Cauldros
4058.description: Lake Cauldros is a lake in the Howling Fjord that feeds into Daggercap Bay through the Falls of Ymiron. Utgarde Keep sits on its shores, acting as a dam, and Cauldros Isle lies at its center.

4059.name: Cauldros Isle
4059.description: Cauldros Isle is an island in Lake Cauldros just north of Utgarde Keep in the Howling Fjord, home to the wolvar of the Howling tribe.

4060.name: Bleeding Vale
4060.description: The Bleeding Vale is a vale on the eastern coast of the Howling Fjord, southwest of Vengeance Landing, at the foot of the cliffs where the Vengeance Lift rises.

4061.name: Giants' Run
4061.description: Giants' Run is a large swath of land in the Howling Fjord between Fort Wildervar and Vengeance Landing, roamed by giant creatures.

4062.name: Apothecary Camp
4062.description: The Apothecary Camp is a camp of the Royal Apothecary Society on a cliff overlooking the Chillmere Coast in the Howling Fjord, where Forsaken apothecaries conduct their work.

4063.name: Ember Spear Tower
4063.description: Ember Spear Tower is a tower southeast of the Ember Clutch in the Howling Fjord, west of Halgrind.

4064.name: Shattered Straits
4064.description: The Shattered Straits are a collection of shipwrecks and icebergs west of Westguard Keep and north of Kamagua in the Howling Fjord, a treacherous stretch of water.

4065.name: Gjalerhorn
4065.description: Gjalerhorn is a treacherous, craggy, snow-covered mountain in the northern Howling Fjord, bordering the Grizzly Hills. The vrykul fortress of Gjalerbron sits on its slopes, the spider-infested Rivenwood at its foot, and the taunka of Camp Winterhoof on its eastern side. It is said that the wreck of a gnomish flying machine lies at its peak.

4066.name: Frostblade Peak
4066.description: Frostblade Peak is a mountain in the northeastern Howling Fjord, the sister of Gjalerhorn but far more welcoming, free of vrykul and undead. Fort Wildervar sits at its base, and a path winds to its summit, where a glowing blue shrine is said to help those who meditate there overcome their inner turmoil.

4068.name: West Spear Tower
4068.description: West Spear Tower is a tower east of Steel Gate and northwest of Skorn in the Howling Fjord.

4069.name: North Spear Tower
4069.description: North Spear Tower is a wooden tower in the north-central Howling Fjord, just north of an east-west trail.

4070.name: Chillmere Coast
4070.description: The Chillmere Coast is a long coastline in the northwestern Howling Fjord, inhabited by murlocs who have been turned into undead by the invading Scourge.

4071.name: Whisper Gulch
4071.description: Whisper Gulch is an eerie gulch north of Westguard Keep in the Howling Fjord, a narrow crack in the land overgrown with tilting trees and crisscrossed by wooden bridges, many broken and hanging. Mine entrances dot its walls, and the wind brings strange whispers to the ear. The explorers who worked here have gone mad.

4073.name: Winter's Terrace
4073.description: Winter's Terrace is the upper part of the vrykul fortress of Gjalerbron in the Howling Fjord, where the vrykul queen leads a ceremony to revive their slumbering king.

4074.name: The Waking Halls
4074.description: The Waking Halls are vast underground halls in the lower section of Gjalerbron in the Howling Fjord, full of slumbering vrykul and the necromancers who are awakening them. The halls extend deep into the earth, large enough to have held an entire race asleep for thousands of years.

4077.name: Sorlof's Strand
4077.description: Sorlof's Strand is a shoreline on the western coast of the Howling Fjord, south of the Ember Clutch, reached by a vrykul lift.

4226.name: Iskaal
4226.description: Iskaal is a ruined tuskarr village east of Kamagua on the Isle of Spears in the Howling Fjord, now controlled by the Northsea Freebooters. The surviving tuskarr fled to Kamagua.

4252.name: The Broken Bluffs
4252.description: The Broken Bluffs are a narrow path along the eastern edge of the Howling Fjord and the Grizzly Hills, used by stone giants under the control of the iron dwarves.

4260.name: Thorvald's Camp
4260.description: Thorvald's Camp is a small vrykul camp in the Howling Fjord, set up by a vrykul chieftain and a few others who escaped from plague-stricken Halgrind.

4261.name: Ghostblade Post
4261.description: Ghostblade Post is a small Forsaken outpost just south of Nifflevar in the Howling Fjord, watching the vrykul of the cliffs.

4263.name: Lydell's Ambush
4263.description: Lydell's Ambush is a small area just up the road from Baleheim in the Howling Fjord, where Forsaken assassins hide behind a large vrykul cart.

4271.name: Utgarde Pinnacle
4271.description: Utgarde Pinnacle is the upper part of Utgarde Keep in the Howling Fjord, the seat of the most powerful vrykul and of their king, Ymiron, who has sworn himself to the Lich King. Its great halls are filled with the mightiest vrykul warriors.

4379.name: Valgarde
4379.description: Valgarde is the oldest Alliance port in Northrend, standing on the western shore of Daggercap Bay in the Howling Fjord. Its docks bustle with ships arriving from Menethil Harbor, carrying soldiers, settlers, and supplies for the war, while its walls face constant raids from the vrykul of Utgarde Keep. Humans and dwarves work side by side to defend it.

4380.name: Westguard Inn
4380.description: The Westguard Inn is the inn of Westguard Keep in the Howling Fjord, run by a human couple, a warm refuge for soldiers and travelers.

4402.name: Vengeance Lift
4402.description: The Vengeance Lift is a vrykul-built elevator rising into the cliffs from the Bleeding Vale, southwest of Vengeance Landing in the Howling Fjord. A massive stone dragon head juts from the cliffs above, with a chain hanging from its mouth that runs two wooden cars up from the vale below. The Forsaken and the vrykul have fought for control of it.

4403.name: Balejar Watch
4403.description: Balejar Watch is a vrykul watch post just east of Baleheim in the Howling Fjord.

4404.name: New Agamand Inn
4404.description: The New Agamand Inn is the inn of the Forsaken town of New Agamand in the Howling Fjord, a gloomy but welcome refuge for Horde travelers.

4474.name: Twin Shores
4474.description: The Twin Shores of the Isle of Spears and Garvan's Reef in the southwestern Howling Fjord are full of reef bulls and cows, great sea creatures that bask on the rocks.

4479.name: Winter's Breath Lake
4479.description: Winter's Breath Lake is a lake north of Skorn and south of Camp Winterhoof in the Howling Fjord. A mysterious maiden is said to appear on an ice patch at its center.

4532.name: Vengeance Landing Inn
4532.description: The Vengeance Landing Inn is the inn of the Forsaken port of Vengeance Landing in the Howling Fjord, a refuge for Horde travelers arriving in Northrend.

4534.name: Wildervar Mine
4534.description: The Wildervar Mine is a mine dug into Frostblade Peak by the humans of Fort Wildervar in the Howling Fjord.

495.description: The Howling Fjord is a rugged region in southeastern Northrend, a land of green meadows cut by bone-chilling rivers, dark pine forests, and towering fjords whose cliffs plunge into the cold sea. Daggercap Bay is ripped into its southern coastline, and at its head the mighty fortress of Utgarde Keep rises above Lake Cauldros, its waterfalls tumbling down the cliffs. The fjord was the ancient seat of power of the vrykul, giant warriors who slept for ages beneath the earth; the Lich King's Scourge has awakened them, and many have pledged themselves to him, returning to reclaim their keeps and villages and raiding all who come near. Long ago, it is said, Prince Arthas landed on these shores in pursuit of the dreadlord Mal'Ganis. Today the fjord is a battleground: the Alliance's Valiance Expedition holds the old port of Valgarde, Westguard Keep, and Fort Wildervar, and the Explorers' League digs for titan ruins in the southeast, where a race of iron dwarves has appeared. The Forsaken of the Hand of Vengeance hold Vengeance Landing and the town of New Agamand, where they test a new plague meant to destroy the Scourge. The tuskarr dwell on the Isle of Spears, the taunka in the north, and wolvar, proto-dragons, frost nymphs, and pirates inhabit the land and coasts.

618.name: Winterspring

2241.name: Frostsaber Rock
2241.description: Frostsaber Rock is a large, jutting tor in the northern part of Winterspring, home to a great pride of wintersaber cats ruled by a gargantuan female. At its summit, night elf tamers work to tame these beautiful, fierce beasts as mounts. The rock is cold and windswept, offering a commanding view of the snowy valley.

2242.name: The Hidden Grove
2242.description: The Hidden Grove is a forested crater in northeastern Winterspring, surrounded on all sides by high cliffs and virtually inaccessible except through a single cave. It is home to many owlkin who are extremely hostile, and most travelers do not attempt to enter. The grove is lush and secluded, a strange pocket of green amid the snow.

2243.name: Timbermaw Post
2243.description: Timbermaw Post is a small furbolg camp in western Winterspring, across the road from the Frostfire Hot Springs. Although its name suggests it was once held by the friendly Timbermaw tribe, it is now controlled by the corrupted Winterfall furbolgs, who attack anyone who comes near.

2244.name: Winterfall Village
2244.description: Winterfall Village is a large village of corrupted furbolgs in the far east of Winterspring, near Everlook. The Winterfall furbolgs are among the strongest of their kind, and their village is ruled by a powerful high chief who dwells in a cave at the top of the settlement. The village is a dangerous place, and the Winterfall attack all outsiders.

2245.name: Mazthoril
2245.description: Mazthoril is a huge and deep icy cavern in Winterspring, the stronghold of the Cobalt Brood of the blue dragonflight. Within its frozen halls, a legion of blue dragonspawn guards the cavern, led by a powerful general, while drakes and whelps watch over its depths and a blue dragon matriarch dwells at its peak. The blue dragons of Mazthoril have long clashed with the night elves and their wintersaber riders, and the cavern is a place of cold beauty and great danger.

2246.name: Frostfire Hot Springs
2246.description: The Frostfire Hot Springs are a series of steaming pools at the far western end of Winterspring, their warm waters strange in the icy land. Some believe they are the result of demonic interference from Darkwhisper Gorge in the south. The springs are home to fish and are a pleasant place to fish, though the corrupted Winterfall furbolgs dwell nearby.

2247.name: Ice Thistle Hills
2247.description: The Ice Thistle Hills are a large area of snowy hills just southeast of Everlook, home to the Ice Thistle yetis, who live in and around a cave high on the hill. Hunters come here for the yetis' thick furs and horns, and rare herbs and ores can be found in the area.

2248.name: Dun Mandarr
2248.description: Dun Mandarr is a small, abandoned dwarven camp near an icy cavern in eastern Winterspring. It was set up by a dwarven explorer, but the camp was overrun by ferocious owlkin, enraged by an amulet the dwarf had discovered, and destroyed. The ruins of the camp lie scattered in the snow.

2249.name: Frostwhisper Gorge
2249.description: Frostwhisper Gorge is a canyon in southern Winterspring, just north of Darkwhisper Gorge. It is scattered with night elven ruins both at the bottom of the gorge and on the ridges above, and a great bridge spans it, connecting the south with the rest of Winterspring. Huge frost giants roam the gorge, making it a dangerous place.

2250.name: Owl Wing Thicket
2250.description: Owl Wing Thicket is a series of caves in southern Winterspring, home to a large number of berserk and crazed owlkin. It is said that the ancient guardians of Elune who dwell nearby know the story of how the owlkin came into the world. The thicket is shadowy and dangerous.

2251.name: Lake Kel'Theril
2251.description: Lake Kel'Theril is a frozen lake in central Winterspring, its icy surface glittering under the sun. Its shores are home to the Ruins of Kel'Theril, and both the lake and the ruins are haunted by the tormented spirits of the Highborne who perished when the ancient city was destroyed. The lake is beautiful and eerie.

2252.name: The Ruins of Kel'Theril
2252.description: The Ruins of Kel'Theril are the remnants of a great night elven city on the shores of Lake Kel'Theril in central Winterspring, destroyed long ago. The ruins are haunted by the tormented spirits of the Highborne who did not survive the disaster, and the broken columns and crumbling walls stand silent in the snow. The ruins hold many secrets of the ancient night elves.

2253.name: Starfall Village
2253.description: Starfall Village is a small night elf outpost in Winterspring, along the main road northwest of Everlook and south of Frostsaber Rock. It contains a night elven lodge, a smaller house, and an empty barrow den, and its inhabitants prefer to stay within the more defensible lodge. The village is a quiet haven for night elves and their allies in the snowy valley.

2254.name: Ban'Thallow Barrow Den
2254.description: The Ban'Thallow Barrow Den is an old barrow den very close to Starfall Village in Winterspring. Originally empty and unused, it is now home to burrowing worms and spiders. The den's tunnels are dark and cold.

2255.name: Everlook
2255.description: Everlook is a trading town in Winterspring run by the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel, lying at the crossroads of the valley's main trade routes. It is officially neutral and open to all races and factions, and it serves as the base for goblin miners, a center of trade between the Alliance and the Horde, and a resupply point for pilgrims traveling to Hyjal's summit. The town is protected by goblin guards, and its sturdy wooden buildings, inn, and shops offer warmth and safety in the cold valley. The Thorium Brotherhood also maintains an outpost here.

2256.name: Darkwhisper Gorge
2256.description: Darkwhisper Gorge is a treacherous network of chasms and tunnels in the far south of Winterspring, along the valley's southern slope. Poisonous green vapors bubble out of acid pools deep within the gorge, and malevolent sounds echo from a cave at its far end. The gorge has become a refuge for demons of the Burning Legion who remained on Azeroth after the Third War, and it is one of the most dangerous places in northern Kalimdor.

3139.name: Moon Horror Den
3139.description: Moon Horror Den is a small cave just northeast of Everlook in Winterspring, inhabited by raging owlkin. The owlkin are hostile and attack anyone who enters their den. The cave is dark and cold, its floor littered with feathers.

618.description: Winterspring is a cold, snowy valley high on the slopes of Mount Hyjal in northeastern Kalimdor, lying east of Felwood and north of Azshara, above the clouds that separate it from Moonglade below. It is a land of near-perpetual winter, where snow blankets the hills and forests, frozen lakes glitter in the sun, and the air is crisp and clean. Thousands of years ago, the night elves came to this valley to start anew after the Great Sundering, and the ruins of their cities still stand among the snow. The trees of Winterspring were bent and twisted during the great Battle of Mount Hyjal, and the massive roots of the World Tree are exposed here, towering overhead like great archways. The valley has long been the scene of a struggle between the blue dragonflight, who dwell in the icy caverns of Mazthoril, and the night elves and their frostsaber cats. Today the goblin trading town of Everlook stands at the crossroads of the valley's trade routes, open to all, and the night elves keep a small village nearby. Corrupted Winterfall furbolgs, yetis, owlkin, frostsabers, bears, and chimaeras roam the land, and the southern reaches of the valley have been taken over by demons in the toxic depths of Darkwhisper Gorge. Pilgrims pass through Winterspring on their way to Hyjal's summit, the last stop before the sacred World Tree.

1377.name: Silithus

2477.name: The Veiled Sea
2477.description: The waters of the Veiled Sea wash the western coast of Silithus, where the desert meets the sea. The shore is barren and rocky, and the silithid hives can be seen rising from the sands inland. Few ships sail near this desolate coast.

2737.name: The Scarab Wall
2737.description: The Scarab Wall is a great wall at the southern edge of Silithus, marking the boundary between the silithid-infested desert and the ancient kingdom of Ahn'Qiraj. Raised by the night elves and the dragonflights at the end of the War of the Shifting Sands, it is an impressive structure protected by a magical shield that prevents even flying creatures from passing over it. Its great gates sealed the Qiraji within for a thousand years.

2738.name: Southwind Village
2738.description: Southwind Village was once a night elf base of operations in Silithus, destroyed by the Qiraji during the War of the Shifting Sands, when the son of Fandral Staghelm led a detachment to defend it and was captured. Today the village has long since been overrun by silithid, and the tortured spirits of fallen druids and Sentinels wander its ruins aimlessly.

2739.name: Twilight Base Camp
2739.description: The Twilight Base Camp is a village of the Twilight's Hammer cult in Silithus, one of their four camps in the region. Made up mostly of trolls, tauren, and orcs, it is a ramshackle cluster of huts and burrows surrounded by a low wall, with a single well at its center. Its residents are warlocks and other arcane practitioners seeking crystals beneath the sands for some obscure purpose.

2740.name: The Crystal Vale
2740.description: The Crystal Vale is a valley in the far northwestern corner of Silithus, populated by earth and air elementals. Great crystals rise from the ground, and the air crackles with elemental energy. The cultists of the Twilight's Hammer have been drawn to the vale.

2741.name: The Scarab Dais
2741.description: The Scarab Dais is a platform northwest of the Scarab Wall outside Ahn'Qiraj, where the great Scarab Gong stands, the instrument whose ringing opened the gates of the ancient city. It is a solemn and ominous place.

2742.name: Hive'Ashi
2742.description: Hive'Ashi is a great silithid hive in northern Silithus, a towering structure of hardened resin and earth swarming with insects. Its silithid have also infested the Swarming Pillar to the south.

2743.name: Hive'Zora
2743.description: Hive'Zora is a great silithid hive in western Silithus, a towering structure swarming with insects of every kind. The hive's tunnels run deep beneath the sands.

2744.name: Hive'Regal
2744.description: Hive'Regal is a great silithid hive in southern Silithus, a towering structure of resin and earth swarming with insects. It lies near the Scarab Wall and the ancient city of Ahn'Qiraj.

3077.name: Valor's Rest
3077.description: Valor's Rest is a camp in northeastern Silithus used by members of both the Alliance and the Horde, the first sight for travelers entering the desert from Un'Goro Crater. It is home to members of the Cenarion Circle and a graveyard for those who fell in the war against the Qiraji.

3097.name: The Swarming Pillar
3097.description: The Swarming Pillar is a large silithid-infested peak in the middle of Silithus, just south of Cenarion Hold, containing one of their hives. A massive swarm of small silithid buzzes around it constantly, giving it its name.

3098.name: Twilight Post
3098.description: Twilight Post is a camp of the Twilight's Hammer cult in northwestern Silithus, far west of Cenarion Hold. The cultists here serve dark masters and attack anyone who comes near.

3099.name: Twilight Outpost
3099.description: Twilight Outpost is a camp of the Twilight's Hammer cult in the far southwestern corner of Silithus, just northwest of the Scarab Wall. The cultists here conduct dark rituals and attack all outsiders.

3100.name: Ravaged Twilight Camp
3100.description: The Ravaged Twilight Camp is a ruined camp in the Crystal Vale in northwestern Silithus, once used by the Twilight's Hammer cult. It is now the home of a mysterious figure who has turned against the cult.

3257.name: Bones of Grakkarond
3257.description: The Bones of Grakkarond are the huge bones of a bronze dragon who fell during the War of the Shifting Sands, lying in central Silithus. The great skeleton is half-buried in the sand, a solemn reminder of the dragons who fought alongside the night elves against the Qiraji.

3425.name: Cenarion Hold
3425.description: Cenarion Hold is a fortified settlement in northern Silithus, held by the Cenarion Circle, who defend this ancient night elven settlement against the increasingly hostile silithid and the other forces that have entered the region. The druids watch the insects and the cultists, and they welcome adventurers of all races who would aid them. Its walls and buildings are built in the night elven style, and a flight master connects it with Gadgetzan and Marshal's Refuge.

3426.name: Staghelm Point
3426.description: Staghelm Point is a tower atop a peak in northeastern Silithus, named either for Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, who led the night elf armies in the War of the Shifting Sands, or for his son, who fell during that war. A bronze dragon of Nozdormu's brood watches from the tower, and a bronze drake circles in the skies above.

3427.name: Bronzebeard Encampment
3427.description: The Bronzebeard Encampment is a dwarven camp in southern Silithus, east of the Scarab Wall, set up by explorers studying the ancient ruins and the Qiraji. The camp is a modest collection of tents and equipment.

3446.name: Twilight's Run
3446.description: Twilight's Run is a cave in northern Silithus, filled with members of the Twilight's Hammer cult, ruled by a vile cultist. The cave is dark and filled with the signs of their foul rituals.

3447.name: Ortell's Hideout
3447.description: Ortell's Hideout is a small cave in southeastern Silithus, the home of a reclusive hermit who has made the desert his home. It is a quiet, secluded place.

3454.name: Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj
3454.description: The Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj are the outer ruins of the ancient Qiraji city in southern Silithus, beyond the Scarab Wall. The crumbling sandstone temples, pyramids, and statues are swarming with silithid and their Qiraji masters, and the ruins are a place of ancient evil. It was here that the Qiraji held the night elves who fell in the War of the Shifting Sands, and the bones of the fallen still lie among the stones.

1377.description: Silithus is a harsh desert in the southwestern corner of Kalimdor, reached through a wide path from the northwestern corner of Un'Goro Crater. It is a land of rock and sand broken only by the massive, towering hives of the silithid, insectoid creatures who swarm across the desert. A thousand years ago, the Qiraji, the masters of the silithid, launched the War of the Shifting Sands against the night elves; the night elves, aided by the bronze, red, green, and blue dragonflights, drove them back and sealed them behind the great Scarab Wall in their ancient city of Ahn'Qiraj. The silithid have since multiplied and spread across southern Kalimdor. In recent times, the gates of Ahn'Qiraj were opened once more, and the armies of the Alliance and the Horde marched against the Qiraji. The Cenarion Circle maintains a constant presence at Cenarion Hold, watching the silithid, and the bronze dragonflight has returned to the desert for the first time in ten thousand years. The cultists of the Twilight's Hammer have established camps across the land, seeking crystals beneath the sands and serving dark masters, and the ruins of the night elves' ancient villages lie scattered and haunted. The heat is relentless, the wind carries stinging sand, and the buzzing of countless insects fills the air.

1497.name: Undercity

4617.name: Elevator
4617.description: The great lifts of the Undercity carry travelers between the Ruins of Lordaeron above and the depths of the Forsaken capital below. These massive platforms descend through deep stone shafts, accompanied by the groaning of chains and the clanking of machinery, and the ride offers a moment of eerie silence before the city's green-lit halls come into view. Forsaken guards keep watch at the top and bottom of each lift, and the platforms are crowded with travelers, merchants, and soldiers coming and going from the city.

1497.description: The Undercity is the capital of the Forsaken, a vast underground city carved beneath the ruins of Lordaeron's royal capital in Tirisfal Glades. Long before the Forsaken came, the Undercity held the crypts and catacombs of Lordaeron's royalty, as well as the city's dungeons and sewers. After Prince Arthas slew his father and the city fell to the Scourge, Arthas ordered his minions to expand the catacombs as his seat of power, but he was summoned to Northrend before the work was finished. When Sylvanas Windrunner broke free of the Lich King's control, she and her followers drove out the dreadlords who held the city and completed the work, making it the heart of their new nation. Today the Undercity is a dark, cold, and labyrinthine place, built in concentric rings around a central chamber, with the Trade Quarter at its center, the Magic Quarter, the Rogues' Quarter, the War Quarter, and the Apothecarium, where the Royal Apothecary Society brews its plagues and poisons. Canals of green sludge flow through the city, and great lifts carry travelers between the ruins above and the depths below. From the Royal Quarter, the Banshee Queen Sylvanas rules her people, and in recent times elite Kor'kron guards of Warchief Thrall have also taken up posts in the city. The air smells of decay and alchemical fumes, and the silence of the dead hangs heavy over the halls. An orb of translocation connects the city with distant Silvermoon, home of the Forsaken's blood elf allies.

1519.name: Stormwind City

1617.name: Valley of Heroes
1617.description: The Valley of Heroes is the grand approach to Stormwind City, a lush natural basin lying before the city's great gates and spanned by a majestic stone bridge. Along the road stand enormous statues of the heroes of the Alliance Expedition who marched through the Dark Portal into Draenor at the end of the Second War to seal the rift from the other side: the Wildhammer gryphon master Kurdran Wildhammer, the Archmage Khadgar, the Stromgarde commander Danath Trollbane, the ranger-captain Alleria Windrunner, and, at the end of the road, the expedition's leader, General Turalyon. For years all were presumed lost beyond the portal, and their monuments both welcome visitors and serve as a reminder of the sacrifices made for the kingdom. Stormwind's officers and mounted guards watch over the valley, and travelers, soldiers, and merchants pass beneath the statues in an endless stream on their way into the city.

4411.name: Stormwind Harbor
4411.description: Stormwind Harbor lies along the northern edge of Stormwind City, where the white walls of the capital meet the waters of the Great Sea. Built to serve the Alliance's growing needs, it is a busy port of long wooden docks, warehouses, and shipyards, guarded by cannons mounted along the city walls. Great ships sail from its piers to the distant shores of Northrend, carrying soldiers and supplies to the war against the Lich King, as well as to the night elven lands in northern Kalimdor. Siege engines and crates of supplies line the docks, and the air is filled with the cries of gulls, the shouts of sailors, and the creaking of masts. A large shipyard at the harbor's northern tip builds and repairs the vessels of the Alliance fleet.

1519.description: Stormwind City is the capital of the Kingdom of Stormwind and the largest and grandest human city in the world, rising from the northwestern coast of the Eastern Kingdoms beyond the forests of Elwynn. Named for the sudden squalls that sweep down from the surrounding mountains, the city was razed by the Horde during the First War, when Anduin Lothar led its survivors north to Lordaeron; after the Second War it was rebuilt on the same site, a marvel of human design and engineering with white stone walls, blue-roofed towers, and districts separated by shimmering canals. King Varian Wrynn rules from Stormwind Keep, having returned after a long and mysterious absence during which his young son Anduin sat on the throne. The city is the jewel of the Alliance and the home of the Cathedral of Light, the spiritual heart of the faith of the Holy Light, and of the Academy of Arcane Sciences in the Mage Quarter. Its districts include the bustling Trade District, the rougher alleys of Old Town, home to the barracks and the spies of SI:7, the Dwarven District with its forges and the gnomish Deeprun Tram to Ironforge, and the Park, where night elves have planted a moonwell. Humans predominate, but dwarves, gnomes, night elves, high elves, and draenei all walk its streets. The climate is warm and temperate, the skies often clear, and every evening the bells of the cathedral ring out across the city. Two grim prisons, the Stockade and the Vault, rise from the canals, holding the kingdom's criminals.

1537.name: Ironforge

4679.name: The Forlorn Cavern
4679.description: The Forlorn Cavern is a long, dimly lit road winding around the underground lake in the northern reaches of Ironforge, between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Far from the bright glow of the Great Forge, its shadowy passages and secluded nooks have made it a gathering place for those who prefer to conduct their affairs away from prying eyes. Practitioners of the darker arts, including warlocks, and those skilled in stealth and subterfuge keep shops and quarters here, and many a quiet, questionable bargain has been struck in its gloom. The still, black waters of the lake reflect the scattered lanterns, and the air is cool and damp compared to the rest of the city. Respectable dwarves tend to give the cavern a wide berth, and visitors are wise to keep an eye on their coin purses.

1537.description: Ironforge is the ancient capital of the dwarves and the ancestral seat of the Bronzebeard clan, a vast city carved into the heart of a mountain in the snowy peaks of Dun Morogh. Behind its great stone gates lies a world of torchlit halls, winding passages, and cavernous chambers, where rivers of molten rock drawn from the depths of the mountain feed the colossal Great Forge at the city's center, providing heat, light, and fire for dwarven smithing. From the High Seat beside the forge, King Magni Bronzebeard rules the kingdom of Khaz Modan. Once the home of all dwarven clans under the High King Modimus Anvilmar, the city was torn by the War of the Three Hammers after his death; the Dark Irons were driven out and the Wildhammers departed, leaving Ironforge to the Bronzebeards. During the Second War the Horde overran much of Khaz Modan, but Ironforge itself was never breached. Since the fall of Gnomeregan, the exiled gnomes under High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque have made their home in the district of Tinker Town, and the two peoples are now so close that the refugees are often called Ironforge gnomes. The city is home to the Commons with its bank and bustling trade, the Military Ward, the Mystic Ward, and the Hall of Explorers, seat of the Explorers' League, whose scholars and adventurers seek the secrets of dwarven origins. The gnome-built Deeprun Tram runs beneath the earth to Stormwind, making Ironforge one of the most diverse and lively cities of the Alliance. Fires roar in its taverns, hammers ring without end, and the air is warm, smoky, and filled with dwarven laughter.

1637.name: Orgrimmar
1637.description: Orgrimmar is the capital of the orcs and the seat of the Horde, a mighty fortress city at the northern edge of Durotar, built into a canyon at the foot of the mountains that separate Durotar from Azshara. It was founded by Warchief Thrall after the Third War, with the help of the tauren, the Darkspear trolls, goblins, and the hero Rexxar, and named after his friend and mentor, the former warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. The city is guarded by stout walls, massive gates, and tall towers, and parts of it are carved into the mountain itself. It is divided into valleys that serve as its districts: the Valley of Strength, the bustling commercial heart with its bank, inn, and auction house; the Valley of Spirits, home to the trolls and shamans; the Valley of Wisdom, where Thrall's fortress of Grommash Hold stands; and the Valley of Honor, home to the warriors and hunters. A dark tunnel called the Drag leads to the shadowy Cleft of Shadow, where warlocks and rogues dwell, and rumors say the Burning Blade infiltrates the city through tunnels beneath it. The city's architecture is simple and rustic, of wood, hide, and stone, decorated with spikes and banners, and it is home to orcs, trolls, tauren, Forsaken, and blood elves. Zeppelins connect it with the Eastern Kingdoms and Northrend. Orgrimmar is a city of warriors, but also a center of trade and the heart of the new Horde's hopes for peace and prosperity.

1638.name: Thunder Bluff

1639.name: Elder Rise
1639.description: Elder Rise is the mesa directly east of the central bluff of Thunder Bluff, the home of the druids of the Cenarion Circle in the tauren capital. Many druids and their teachers reside here among great tents and totems, and both the Archdruid of the tauren and the elder crone of the Grimtotem tribe make their homes on the rise. Rope bridges connect it to the other mesas.

1640.name: Spirit Rise
1640.description: Spirit Rise is the mesa to the northwest of the central bluff of Thunder Bluff, the center of shamanistic study in the tauren capital, where the Skychaser tribe holds great influence. Shamans gather here among the totems to commune with the spirits, and below the surface of the mesa lie the steamy Pools of Vision. A zeppelin tower on the rise connects Thunder Bluff with Orgrimmar.

1641.name: Hunter Rise
1641.description: Hunter Rise is the mesa to the south of the central bluff of Thunder Bluff, the home of the hunters and warriors of the tauren. Within the renowned Hunter's Hall, warriors and hunters from across the land come to sharpen their skills, and emissaries of the Warsong Outriders and the Frostwolf clan seek recruits here. Rope bridges connect it to the other mesas.

2197.name: The Pools of Vision
2197.description: The Pools of Vision are a series of misty, luminous pools within a tunnel system beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. It is said that the pools reveal visions to those who can channel their energies and deliver messages from the dead. The pools serve as the base of the Forsaken in the tauren capital, where they study items of arcane power and practice their alchemy, much to the discomfort of the tauren, who tolerate them only grudgingly.

1638.description: Thunder Bluff is the capital of the tauren, a city built atop four towering mesas in the far north of Mulgore, several hundred feet above the sprawling Golden Plains. It was founded after the Third War, when Thrall's Horde helped the tauren drive the centaurs from their ancestral land, and it is the first permanent city of a people who wandered as nomads for centuries. The tauren are intensely proud of their home: great tents, longhouses, and totem poles crown the mesas, connected by swaying rope bridges, and wooden elevators, a tauren invention, lift visitors from the plains below. The city is ruled by the great High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, who has led his people for many years. The central mesa is the heart of the city, while Elder Rise is home to the druids of the Cenarion Circle, Spirit Rise to the shamans, and Hunter Rise to the hunters and warriors. Beneath Spirit Rise lie the misty Pools of Vision. The weather is almost always warm and sunny, with breezes blowing in from the Barrens, and the view over the plains of Mulgore is breathtaking. All members of the Horde are welcome, though the tauren tolerate the Forsaken only grudgingly, for their unlife is an affront to the tauren's reverence for life.

1657.name: Darnassus

1658.name: Cenarion Enclave
1658.description: The Cenarion Enclave is the home of the druids in Darnassus, a magical place among the northern terraces of the city where great trees and living buildings house the Cenarion Circle. From its boughs, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads his followers, and druids, hunters, and their animal companions train here. It is whispered that a secretive guild of night elf rogues meets beneath the enclave, if one knows where to look. Nightsabers are bred and taught to carry riders at the foot of the enclave's great tree.

1659.name: Craftsmen's Terrace
1659.description: The Craftsmen's Terrace is a district of Darnassus where most of the city's artisans and craftsmen ply their trades, from tailors and leatherworkers to alchemists and herbalists. It is also home to the city's inn and to a contingent of the Argent Dawn. The terrace is a peaceful place of elegant workshops and gardens, where the quiet sounds of craft fill the twilit air.

1660.name: Warrior's Terrace
1660.description: The Warrior's Terrace is the easternmost district of Darnassus, home to the city's warriors and battlemasters, who train the night elves and their allies in the arts of combat. Sentinels drill in its courtyards, and the terrace opens eastward onto the forests of Teldrassil. It is a place of discipline and martial pride.

1661.name: The Temple Gardens
1661.description: The Temple Gardens are the very heart of Darnassus, lying around the central island of the city's great lake. Here stands the portal that is the only link between the city and the wider world, leading down to Rut'theran Village at the foot of Teldrassil, and the city's bank is found on the central island. The gardens are filled with flowers, fountains, and graceful statues, and to the south rises the Temple of the Moon, the seat of the High Priestess and the sisters of Elune.

1662.name: Tradesmen's Terrace
1662.description: The Tradesmen's Terrace is the commercial heart of Darnassus, where most of the city's merchants keep their shops and where the auction house can be found. Elegant stalls and shops line its paths, and night elves and visitors from other lands come to trade goods from across Kalimdor and beyond. It is the busiest district of the otherwise quiet city.

1657.description: Darnassus is the capital of the night elves, a serene and beautiful city built among the western boughs of the great tree Teldrassil, high above the Veiled Sea. Open to the sky and bathed in eternal violet twilight, it is arranged in graceful terraces around a great central lake, its elegant buildings of living wood and white stone set wide apart and connected by arching bridges. The city is home to the leaders of both the druids and the faithful of Elune: the High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, leader of the night elves, resides in the Temple of the Moon, while Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave, often at odds with Tyrande and with the druids of Moonglade. The great druid Malfurion Stormrage, Tyrande's beloved, remains lost in the Emerald Dream. Darnassus is guarded by Sentinels, ancients of war, and protectors, and its atmosphere is quiet and somewhat melancholic, befitting a people who have only recently lost their immortality. The city's population is almost entirely elven, though guests and diplomats from other races, including draenei, reside here as well. The only link to the wider world is a shimmering portal leading down to Rut'theran Village at the foot of the tree.

1941.name: Caverns of Time
1941.description: The Caverns of Time are a vast network of caves in eastern Tanaris, the home of the bronze dragonflight and their Aspect, Nozdormu, the Timeless One. The titans charged the bronze dragons with guarding the flow of time, and they watch over the caverns, which act as a crossroads of the timelines: through portals within, one can travel to key moments in the world's history, such as the opening of the Dark Portal, Thrall's escape from Durnholde, the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and the culling of Stratholme. The caverns are a strange and wondrous place, where sand gives way to lush forests, great hourglasses turn, and colossal statues of bronze dragon watchers wielding axes tower over everything. Echoes of the past linger everywhere, and frozen figures from other ages can be seen within. In recent times, a mysterious force known as the infinite dragonflight has begun to meddle with time, seeking to alter history, and the bronze dragons seek aid in preserving the timeways. Those who enter without permission are said to emerge changed, some aged, others reduced to infancy by the caverns' strange energies.

2159.name: Onyxia's Lair
2159.description: Onyxia's Lair is a volcanic cave in the Wyrmbog of southern Dustwallow Marsh, the lair of Onyxia, the great black dragon and daughter of Deathwing, brood mother of the black dragonflight. The cave winds deep into the earth, its walls warm with volcanic heat, and the main cavern holds the dragon's vast clutch of eggs, guarded by whelps and dragonspawn. The floor of the great chamber is a thin crust over molten rock below, and the air is thick with smoke, brimstone, and the stench of the dragon's victims. Bones and treasure lie scattered among the rocks. Onyxia is said to harbor a deep malevolence toward the mortal races, and travelers tell grim tales of those abducted by her brood. Few who enter her lair return.

2817.name: Crystalsong Forest

4549.name: The Great Tree
4549.description: The Great Tree stands in northwestern Crystalsong Forest, right next to the Violet Stand. It was planted long ago by followers of Fandral Staghelm from a branch of the World Tree Nordrassil to stem the tide of saronite seeping up from the earth. Smaller than Vordrassil in the Grizzly Hills, it is uncorrupted, and strange runes dot its surface.

4550.name: The Mirror of Twilight
4550.description: The Mirror of Twilight is a lake in south-central Crystalsong Forest, surrounded by ancient night elven arches. It is fed by the Twilight Rivulet with waters from the Decrepit Flow coming out of Icecrown, and glassfin minnows swim in its depths.

4551.name: The Twilight Rivulet
4551.description: The Twilight Rivulet is a stream running from the Decrepit Flow to the Mirror of Twilight beneath Dalaran in western Crystalsong Forest.

4552.name: The Decrepit Flow
4552.description: The Decrepit Flow is a river coming out of Icecrown in northwestern Crystalsong Forest, draining through the Twilight Rivulet to the Mirror of Twilight. Its southern beaches and riverbed are littered with skeletons and the wreckage of siege engines, and its waters have been cut off by the Scourge's Ironwall Dam.

4553.name: Forlorn Woods
4553.description: The Forlorn Woods cover the western half of Crystalsong Forest, between Icecrown and the Storm Peaks to the north and the Dragonblight to the south, with the floating city of Dalaran high above. The Twilight Rivulet cuts through the crystal woods on its way to the Mirror of Twilight.

4554.name: Ruins of Shandaral
4554.description: The Ruins of Shandaral are the remnants of an ancient kaldorei city in the center of the Unbound Thicket, in eastern Crystalsong Forest. Shandaral was founded at the height of the Kaldorei Empire as a repository of Highborne arcane relics. After the Great Sundering cut it off, its sorcerers stole secrets and relics from the blue dragons, and when the dragons came for revenge, the elves' desperate spell crystallized the entire forest. Only stone columns and arches survived, nothing whole remains, and the spirits of the Highborne and their twisted survivors, the Unbound, still wander the ruins.

4555.name: The Azure Front
4555.description: The Azure Front is the blue dragonflight's front against Dalaran and the Kirin Tor in southern Crystalsong Forest, southeast of the Violet Stand. Artifacts of the blue flight lie all around, and the dragons draw power from the largest crystal tree through a chain of surge needles.

4556.name: Violet Stand
4556.description: The Violet Stand is a Kirin Tor outpost built within night elven ruins in southwestern Crystalsong Forest, beneath the floating city of Dalaran and near the Great Tree. The magi raised a magical shield dome to protect it from the blue dragonflight, and the bodies of blue dragonspawn and scorched craters from the fighting litter the ruins. A teleportation crystal links it with the city above.

4557.name: The Unbound Thicket
4557.description: The Unbound Thicket dominates the eastern half of Crystalsong Forest, between Sunreaver's Command to the north and Windrunner's Overlook to the south. All its trees are crystal, great fissures leaking magical energy lace the ground, and even the wind sighs as it passes through the crystal leaves. All that remains of the Highborne who once lived here are ghosts and twisted, maddened creatures called the Unbound, who attack anything they see.

4558.name: Sunreaver's Command
4558.description: Sunreaver's Command is an outpost of the Sunreavers, the blood elf magi of the Kirin Tor, built in a ruined Highborne tower north of the Unbound Thicket in northeastern Crystalsong Forest, facing the Silver Covenant's Windrunner's Overlook across the forest.

4559.name: Windrunner's Overlook
4559.description: Windrunner's Overlook is an outpost of the Silver Covenant, the high elves of Dalaran, built in a ruined Highborne tower in southeastern Crystalsong Forest, on the opposite side of the Ruins of Shandaral from the Sunreavers' outpost. Silver Covenant scouts patrol in and around it.

2817.description: Crystalsong Forest is a landlocked region in the middle of Northrend, a strange land where every tree, every blade of grass, and much of the very earth has been turned to glowing living crystal. Crystals rise like trees, some as tall as towers, others wide, flat, or tilted at odd angles; small streams wind between them and fall as waterfalls lit from behind by the crystals' light. The crystals hum and resonate with the wind and the songs of birds, so that the whole forest seems to play a soft, unending music. Once it was a living forest called Moonsong, where the Highborne of the Kaldorei Empire founded the outpost of Shandaral as a repository of arcane relics. Isolated by the Great Sundering, the elves later stole techniques and relics from the blue dragons of the Nexus. When the dragons came for revenge, the Highborne sorcerers tried to turn the power of the forest against them, and their reckless spell set off a torrent of energy that crystallized the entire forest, shattering every living creature within it. Their spirits still wander the land, and the survivors were twisted into maddened half-crystal beings. Now the floating city of Dalaran hovers over the western forest. The Kirin Tor keep an outpost beneath it, the Silver Covenant and the Sunreavers have claimed ruined Highborne towers on opposite sides of the forest, and the blue dragonflight has established a front against Dalaran in the south as part of the Nexus War.

2917.name: Hall of Legends
2917.description: The Hall of Legends is the great officers' hall of the Horde in the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar, a massive building of wood, stone, and hide decorated with banners, trophies, and the weapons of fallen enemies. It serves as the barracks and gathering place for the Horde's most distinguished warriors, and within it lies the secret armory of the Crimson Ring, which holds weapons from every continent of Azeroth and from Draenor, many taken as spoils of war and bearing proud histories of battles won and lost. Quartermasters here provide arms and armor to those who have earned renown in battle against the Alliance. The hall is a place of honor and pride, where tales of glory are told around great fires and the legends of the Horde are remembered.

3430.name: Eversong Woods

3431.name: Sunstrider Isle
3431.description: Sunstrider Isle is a small, sheltered island at the northern tip of Eversong Woods, one of the few parts of Quel'Thalas left untouched by the Scourge. It is a place of eternal spring and vibrancy, with lush grass, flowering trees, and gleaming elven architecture, including the great Sunspire with its floating satellite buildings. Here young blood elves begin their training in magic and combat before venturing into the wider kingdom. The isle is also home to the Shrine of Dath'Remar, honoring the founder of the elven kingdom. Despite its beauty, the isle has its troubles, including runaway arcane creatures and mana wyrms.

3432.name: Shrine of Dath'Remar
3432.description: The Shrine of Dath'Remar is a monument on the western side of Sunstrider Isle in Eversong Woods, erected to honor Dath'Remar Sunstrider, the founder of the Sunstrider dynasty and first king of Quel'Thalas, who led the high elves from Kalimdor to these lands thousands of years ago. The shrine is a place of reverence and remembrance, and a bronze plaque reminds all who gaze upon it that those who prosper in Quel'Thalas do so thanks to his sacrifice. A strange power seems to linger near the shrine.

3460.name: Golden Strand
3460.description: The Golden Strand is a stretch of sandy beach on the western coast of Eversong Woods, just south of the Tranquil Shore. Its golden sands sparkle in the sun, and the waves of the sea roll gently onto the shore. The Grimscale murlocs have built crude huts near the waterline, and they attack anyone who wanders too close.

3461.name: Sunsail Anchorage
3461.description: Sunsail Anchorage is a port on the western coast of Eversong Woods, once a busy harbor where elven ships came and went. It has been completely taken over by the Wretched, elves who have succumbed to their addiction to magic, and the sunken wrecks of ships, including an elven destroyer, lie in its waters. A single tall building with a great golden crane stands on the shore. The anchorage is a sad reminder of the kingdom's former glory.

3462.name: Fairbreeze Village
3462.description: Fairbreeze Village is a small, picturesque town in southern Eversong Woods, just west of the Dead Scar. Its elegant buildings and gardens are a haven for young blood elves learning their trades before venturing south into the Ghostlands. The village has an inn and various merchants, and its guards keep watch against the Wretched, the arcane creatures, and the blight that threatens from the Dead Scar. The air is fragrant with flowers, and the golden leaves of the forest drift through its streets.

3463.name: Magisters Gate
3463.description: The Magisters Gate marks the grand approach to Silvermoon City on the side of Eversong Woods, where the road from the south climbs toward the great Shepherd's Gate and the shining spires of the capital beyond. Elegant arches, gardens, and magical lights line the way, and the city's guardians and arcane constructs keep watch over all who come and go. The gate is a symbol of the blood elves' restored glory, though the scar of blighted earth left by the Scourge still runs past it into the city.

3464.name: Farstrider Retreat
3464.description: Farstrider Retreat is an outpost of the Farstriders, the elite rangers of Quel'Thalas, in eastern Eversong Woods near Lake Elrendar. The rangers here keep watch over the eastern woods, hunting the trolls, wild beasts, and undead that threaten the kingdom. The building is guarded by Silvermoon's guardians, and the rangers are always ready to welcome those who would aid them in their duty.

3465.name: North Sanctum
3465.description: The North Sanctum is an arcane sanctum in Eversong Woods, southwest of Falconwing Square, one of the magical structures that channel ley energies across the kingdom. A ley-keeper stands watch outside, and the sanctum hums with arcane power. The blood elves rely on these sanctums to maintain the magical defenses and wonders of their land.

3466.name: West Sanctum
3466.description: The West Sanctum is an arcane sanctum on the western isle of Eversong Woods. It suffered a magical malfunction that destroyed its power converter, and it has since been overrun by manawraiths and mana stalkers drawn to the escaping energy. Night elf scouts have been seen observing the sanctum from the shadows. The ruined sanctum crackles with uncontrolled arcane power.

3467.name: East Sanctum
3467.description: The East Sanctum is a ruined arcane sanctum in Eversong Woods, standing at the edge of the Dead Scar, the path of blight left by Arthas and the Scourge. The blood elves study the tainted soil of the scar here, seeking a way to reverse its corruption, but their findings suggest that the damage may be irreversible. The sanctum is crumbling, and the dead earth of the scar stretches away beside it.

3468.name: Saltheril's Haven
3468.description: Saltheril's Haven is a small, elegant estate in western Eversong Woods, owned by a lord who is famous for throwing lavish parties despite the dangers that threaten the kingdom. His guests include magisters, botanists, and artisans, and the estate is filled with music, fine food, and wine. To many, the haven embodies the blood elves' love of luxury and their refusal to let hardship diminish their pleasures.

3469.name: Thuron's Livery
3469.description: Thuron's Livery is a stable just east of the entrance to Silvermoon City in Eversong Woods, where blood elves breed and sell hawkstriders, the swift, long-legged birds that serve as their mounts. The livery is a busy place, with hawkstriders of many colors pacing in their pens and handlers tending to them.

3470.name: Stillwhisper Pond
3470.description: Stillwhisper Pond is a quiet pond just south of Silvermoon City in Eversong Woods, surrounded by trees and gardens. An instructor and his apprentices use the peaceful spot for their studies, and the still waters reflect the golden leaves of the forest above. The pond is a tranquil retreat from the bustle of the capital.

3471.name: The Living Wood
3471.description: The Living Wood is a forested area just east of the Dead Scar in Eversong Woods, where the trees grow especially thick and lush. The contrast with the black line of decay beside it is striking. The wood is populated by treants that have gone mad, perhaps driven to rage by the blight that scarred the land, and they attack anyone who enters their domain.

3472.name: Azurebreeze Coast
3472.description: The Azurebreeze Coast is a stretch of coastline in northeastern Eversong Woods, where the forest meets the waters of the North Sea. Dragonhawks soar above the cliffs, and lynxes prowl the woods near the shore. The coast is beautiful and wild, with clear blue water and golden trees, and the Isle of Quel'Danas can be seen across the channel to the north.

3473.name: Lake Elrendar
3473.description: On the side of Eversong Woods, Lake Elrendar lies in the southeast, stretching across the border into the Ghostlands. Its clear waters reflect the golden forest, and the great Elrendar River flows from it. In its southern reaches, many drowned during the Scourge's invasion, and the lake is now haunted by wraiths of the past. A small island with a cave lies in its waters.

3474.name: The Scorched Grove
3474.description: The Scorched Grove is an area of southwestern Eversong Woods that the blood elves deliberately burned to the ground in an attempt to halt the spread of the Scourge's blight, after the runestones protecting the woods were mostly destroyed. The grove is now a blackened wasteland of ash and charred stumps, populated by aggressive treants who defiantly try to nurture life back into the burned soil.

3475.name: Zeb'Watha
3475.description: Zeb'Watha is a forest troll camp in southeastern Eversong Woods, one of two troll settlements in the area. Although much smaller than nearby Tor'Watha, it is said to house the chieftain of the local Amani trolls, who have long been the enemies of the elves. The camp is a crude collection of huts and totems.

3476.name: Tor'Watha
3476.description: Tor'Watha is the larger of the two forest troll settlements in southeastern Eversong Woods. On its eastern ridge stands a colossal fortress of the Amani with a massive set of gates, empty and silent, while the trolls themselves dwell in the camps below. The trolls are hostile to the elves and attack any who enter their territory.

3480.name: Duskwither Grounds
3480.description: The Duskwither Grounds are an area in northeastern Eversong Woods surrounding the floating Duskwither Spire. Once a place of magical study, the grounds have recently been overrun by arcane creatures and Wretched, drawn by the spire's magical energies. The grounds are eerie and dangerous, filled with the crackling of uncontrolled magic.

3481.name: Duskwither Spire
3481.description: Duskwither Spire is a floating tower in northeastern Eversong Woods, suspended above the ground by powerful arcane magic. It has been overtaken by arcane creatures and Wretched, and its power sources continue to channel energy, drawing ever more magical beings to the area. The spire is a striking sight, hovering above the golden forest.

3482.name: The Dead Scar
3482.description: The Dead Scar is a path of blighted, lifeless earth that runs through the Kingdom of Quel'Thalas, marking the route taken by the death knight Arthas and the Scourge during the Third War on their march from Lordaeron to the Sunwell. Everything in their path was killed and destroyed, and the very soil was corrupted. In Eversong Woods, the scar cuts through the golden forest and the shattered gates of Silvermoon itself, a black wound that remains as a constant reminder of the horrors the blood elves endured. Undead still wander along its length, and nothing grows upon it.

3484.name: The Sunspire
3484.description: The Sunspire is a great blood elf tower on Sunstrider Isle, surrounded by floating satellite buildings held aloft by arcane magic. It is the heart of the isle, where young blood elves come to learn the ways of magic, war, and faith before venturing into the kingdom. The tower's elegant architecture and gleaming crystals embody the restored glory of the sin'dorei.

3485.name: Falthrien Academy
3485.description: Falthrien Academy is a magical academy in the southwestern part of Sunstrider Isle, once a place of learning for young elven magi. It is now crawling with arcane wraiths, and a banished Wretched is said to lurk at its top. The academy's halls are filled with the remnants of uncontrolled magic.

3531.name: Skulking Row
3531.description: Skulking Row is the westernmost path through the Ruins of Silvermoon in Eversong Woods, winding between ruined houses and overgrown gardens. The Wretched lurk in the shadows of the crumbling buildings, and the path lives up to its name.

3532.name: Dawning Lane
3532.description: Dawning Lane is a guarded pathway that cuts diagonally through the Ruins of Silvermoon in Eversong Woods, running from the northwest of the ruins to Falconwing Square. It is a raised, tree-lined walkway with two bridges, patrolled by blood elf guards to keep the Wretched at bay. The lane offers a view of the ruined western half of the capital.

3533.name: Ruins of Silvermoon
3533.description: The Ruins of Silvermoon make up the western half of the ancient capital of Quel'Thalas, separated from the rebuilt eastern districts by the Dead Scar. When Arthas and the Scourge marched through the city on their way to the Sunwell, they devastated this part of Silvermoon, and it has never been rebuilt. Its elegant houses, plazas, and monuments lie in ruins, haunted by the Wretched, elves consumed by their addiction to magic, and by malfunctioning arcane guardians. Falconwing Square, at the southeastern edge of the ruins, is the only part still held by the blood elves.

3534.name: Feth's Way
3534.description: Feth's Way is the easternmost path running through the Ruins of Silvermoon in Eversong Woods, passing between ruined houses and overgrown gardens. The Wretched lurk among the crumbling buildings, and the path is dangerous for the unwary.

3558.name: Elrendar Falls
3558.description: Elrendar Falls is a waterfall just south of Farstrider Retreat in Eversong Woods, where the waters of Lake Elrendar pour over the rocks into one of the rivers flowing northwest toward the North Sea. The falls are a beautiful sight, surrounded by golden trees and mist, and their roar can be heard from afar.

3662.name: Commons Hall
3662.description: The Commons Hall is a structure in the Ruins of Silvermoon, built around a great bonfire. Its name suggests it was once a gathering place or council hall of the city's people. Now it is a lair of the Wretched, led by a particularly hungry and dangerous one, and the fire burns amid the ruins.

3664.name: Huntress of the Sun
3664.description: The Huntress of the Sun is a golden monument in the Ruins of Silvermoon, depicting a female elf archer firing her bow into the sky while standing atop a great medallion. The statue has survived the destruction of the city, and it stands as a proud reminder of the kingdom's rangers and their glory.

3665.name: Falconwing Square
3665.description: Falconwing Square is a small, guarded plaza in the southeastern corner of the Ruins of Silvermoon in Eversong Woods, at the end of Dawning Lane. It is the only part of the ruined western city still held by the blood elves, and it serves as a waypoint for young sin'dorei traveling between Sunstrider Isle and the capital. The square has an inn, teachers of many crafts and arts, and merchants, and its guards keep the Wretched at bay.

3911.name: Tranquil Shore
3911.description: The Tranquil Shore is a quiet beach on the western coast of Eversong Woods, across a mountain ridge west of the West Sanctum. Its peaceful waves and golden sands give it its name, but murlocs inhabit the shore and attack those who come near.

3912.name: Goldenbough Pass
3912.description: Goldenbough Pass is a mountain pass in southwestern Eversong Woods, with a single tower overlooking the Scorched Grove. The pass connects the western coast with the inner woods, and its guards keep watch over the burned lands and the creatures that roam them.

3913.name: Runestone Falithas
3913.description: Runestone Falithas is one of the four remaining runestones on the southern edge of Eversong Woods that protect the forest from the spread of the Scourge's blight. Of the four, it is the only one that remains completely intact and functional, and it is tended by a runewarden who keeps its magic strong. The runestone glows with arcane power, a fragile barrier between the golden woods and the darkness to the south.

3914.name: Runestone Shan'dor
3914.description: Runestone Shan'dor is one of the four remaining runestones on the southern edge of Eversong Woods that protect the forest from the spread of the Scourge's blight. It has become deactivated, and the blight threatens to creep through the gap it leaves. The blood elves are working to restore its power and seal the breach.

3430.description: Eversong Woods is the enchanted forest at the heart of Quel'Thalas, the ancient kingdom of the high elves in the far north of the Eastern Kingdoms. The woods stand in perpetual autumn, their trees crowned with golden and crimson leaves, and the land is dotted with graceful elven spires, floating towers, and shimmering arcane crystals. For millennia, Eversong was the heart of the elven realm, defended by magical runestones and the Sunwell's power, and it saw its share of battles against the Amani forest trolls. During the Third War, the death knight Arthas led the Scourge through the kingdom on his way to the Sunwell, slaughtering countless elves, including the ranger-general Sylvanas Windrunner, and leaving behind the Dead Scar, a path of blighted, lifeless earth that cuts through the forest and even through Silvermoon itself. The survivors rallied under Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider and took the name blood elves, and they have since rebuilt the eastern half of their capital and reclaimed much of the woods. Today the blood elves, led by Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron, are members of the Horde. Yet Eversong is not entirely at peace: the western half of Silvermoon lies in ruins, haunted by the Wretched, elves consumed by their addiction to magic; arcane constructs and mana wyrms run wild; forest trolls lurk in the southeastern hills; murlocs dwell along the coasts; and the runestones that hold back the blight from the south are weakening. The blood elves' struggle with their hunger for magic is reflected in their land: magnificent on the surface, but with lingering darkness beneath.

3433.name: Ghostlands

3488.name: Tranquillien
3488.description: Tranquillien is a town on the western slope of Sungraze Peak in the Ghostlands, overlooking the Dead Scar. Abandoned during the Third War as the Scourge advanced, it fell into disrepair, but it was recently retaken by a coalition of blood elves and Forsaken, who now use it as their base for reclaiming the Ghostlands. The town is surrounded by hostile forces, most notably the Scourge of Deatholme, and resources are perennially scarce, with communications from Silvermoon infrequent. Its elegant elven buildings now house both blood elves and undead, an unusual sight that reflects the alliance between the two peoples.

3489.name: Suncrown Village
3489.description: Suncrown Village is a ruined elven village in the Ghostlands, overrun by the Scourge. Crypt fiends, the undead nerubians of the Lich King, have made their home among its broken buildings, and a powerful one is said to lead them. The village's elegant architecture lies in ruins, a sad reminder of the life that once flourished here.

3490.name: Goldenmist Village
3490.description: Goldenmist Village is a ruined elven village in the northwestern Ghostlands. Its inhabitants were slain when the Scourge came, and now they haunt the ruins as aggressive ghosts, unable to find peace. The village is shrouded in a ghostly mist, and the wails of the dead echo through its empty streets.

3491.name: Windrunner Village
3491.description: Windrunner Village is a ruined elven village in the western Ghostlands, lying in the shadow of the great Windrunner Spire to the south. It is named after the famous ranger family of Alleria, Sylvanas, and Vereesa Windrunner. The village is now haunted by gargoyles and the restless shades of the high elves who once lived here, and its buildings are crumbling.

3492.name: Windrunner Spire
3492.description: Windrunner Spire is the former home of the Windrunner family, standing on the western coast of the Ghostlands. It was the ancestral seat of the famous family of rangers, including Alleria, the hero of the Second War, Sylvanas, the ranger-general who fell defending Quel'Thalas and became the Banshee Queen, and Vereesa. Today the spire is overrun by banshees and cultists of the Scourge, but remnants and relics of the Windrunners still lie within its halls. The tower's tragic history makes it a place of deep sorrow.

3493.name: Sanctum of the Sun
3493.description: The Sanctum of the Sun is an arcane sanctum southeast of Tranquillien in the Ghostlands, still in working order and tended by blood elf magisters. The magisters here coordinate efforts to save the Ghostlands from the Scourge and other invaders, including the night elf spies. The building is guarded by blood elf guardians, and a secret passage through the mountains connects it with Tranquillien.

3494.name: Sanctum of the Moon
3494.description: The Sanctum of the Moon is an arcane sanctum just west of Tranquillien in the Ghostlands. It has been partially destroyed and overrun by arcane elementals and mana wyrms, drawn by its uncontrolled energies. The ruined sanctum crackles with magic, and its broken walls stand amid the withered forest.

3495.name: Dawnstar Spire
3495.description: Dawnstar Spire is a tower in the eastern Ghostlands, believed to have been the home of the prominent Dawnstar family and the former residence of Dar'Khan Drathir before he betrayed his people and joined the Scourge. It is now guarded by his arcane servants. The spire is dark and foreboding, a monument to treachery.

3496.name: Farstrider Enclave
3496.description: The Farstrider Enclave is an outpost of the Farstrider rangers on the southern shore of Lake Elrendar in the Ghostlands, isolated from the rest of the friendly population of the region. The rangers here face apparitions from the lake, trolls of the Shadowpine tribe to the east and south, and lynxes in the woods. They are hardened and vigilant, and they welcome those who would aid them.

3497.name: An'daroth
3497.description: An'daroth is a hidden camp in the northwestern Ghostlands, east of Goldenmist Village, used by the night elf Sentinel spies who watch the blood elves. In ancient times, it was one of three heavily guarded locations in Quel'Thalas that held a piece of the Key of the Three Moons, which protected the kingdom's moongates. The night elves now use its moon crystals to spy on the sin'dorei.

3498.name: An'telas
3498.description: An'telas is a camp east of the Sanctum of the Sun in the central Ghostlands. It was originally used by night elf spies, but they were ambushed and killed by blood elf forces from Tranquillien. In ancient times, An'telas was one of three hidden locations in Quel'Thalas that held a piece of the Key of the Three Moons.

3499.name: An'owyn
3499.description: An'owyn is a camp of the night elf Sentinel spies in the southeastern Ghostlands, where the night elves use moonstones and ley lines to spy on the activities of the blood elves in Silvermoon. In ancient times, it was one of three hidden locations in Quel'Thalas that held a piece of the Key of the Three Moons. The camp is hidden among the trees, and the spies attack any blood elves who discover them.

3500.name: Deatholme
3500.description: Deatholme is a great Scourge citadel in the southwestern Ghostlands, where the Dead Scar begins. It is the headquarters of the Scourge in Quel'Thalas, lying on the other side of the hills from Stratholme, and it is filled with temples, ziggurats, and slaughterhouses. At its center rises the Tower of the Damned, where the traitor Dar'Khan Drathir, the elf who helped Arthas breach the kingdom's defenses, rules with his undead lieutenants. Undead nerubians, banshees, wraiths, and necromancers fill its grounds, and the sky above it has the same reddish-brown tint as the Plaguelands.

3501.name: Bleeding Ziggurat
3501.description: The Bleeding Ziggurat is a Scourge ziggurat near the Dead Scar in the central Ghostlands. It is said to hold an ancient artifact of great power, one that could be turned into a weapon against the Scourge. The ziggurat is guarded by the undead, and its dark stone pulses with necromantic energy.

3502.name: Howling Ziggurat
3502.description: The Howling Ziggurat is a Scourge ziggurat just east of the Dead Scar in the central Ghostlands. Like the Bleeding Ziggurat, it is said to contain an ancient artifact that could serve as a weapon against the Scourge. The wind howls around its dark spires, giving it its name.

3503.name: Shalandis Isle
3503.description: Shalandis Isle is a small island off the coast of the Ghostlands, the base of the night elf expedition known as the Sentinel Spies. A night elf ship is docked offshore, and from here the spies plan their missions to watch the blood elves through the ancient moon crystals of the region. The isle has a distinctly night elven atmosphere, a strange sight in the heart of Quel'Thalas.

3505.name: Underlight Mines
3505.description: The Underlight Mines are a dig site and mine in the Ghostlands, west of the Bleeding Ziggurat and north of the road between Tranquillien and Windrunner Village. They have been taken over by gnolls, who now dig through the tunnels for their own purposes. The mine's entrance is dark and littered with abandoned tools.

3506.name: Andilien Estate
3506.description: The Andilien Estate is an abandoned elven manor in the central Ghostlands. Its owners fled or perished when the Scourge came, and the estate now stands empty and decaying, its gardens withered and its halls silent. The estate is a melancholy reminder of the elven nobility who once lived in this land.

3507.name: Hatchet Hills
3507.description: The Hatchet Hills are a range of hills in the southeastern Ghostlands, southwest of the entrance to Zul'Aman, full of roaming forest trolls. A small camp of adventurers and envoys has been established here to watch the troll city and support those who dare to enter it, and a neutral flight master serves all who come. The hills are rugged and wild, and the war drums of the Amani can be heard in the distance.

3508.name: Amani Pass
3508.description: The Amani Pass is a rugged pass in the southeastern Ghostlands, leading up toward the ancient troll city of Zul'Aman, capital of the Amani Empire. The pass is guarded by forest trolls, and the war drums of the Amani echo through the hills. The ancient stonework of the trolls lines the path, and few outsiders venture this way.

3509.name: Sungraze Peak
3509.description: Sungraze Peak is a mountain in the central Ghostlands, at whose base lie the town of Tranquillien and the camp of An'telas. The mountain holds the Amani Catacombs, ancient troll crypts carved into its slopes. From its heights, the withered forests of the Ghostlands stretch out in every direction.

3510.name: Amani Catacombs
3510.description: The Amani Catacombs are a series of ancient forest troll crypts carved into Sungraze Peak in the Ghostlands, northeast of Tranquillien. They are infested with troll mummies and the Shadowpine trolls who guard their ancestors' tombs. The catacombs are dark and dusty, filled with burial chambers, treasures, and traps.

3511.name: Tower of the Damned
3511.description: The Tower of the Damned is the dark tower at the center of Deatholme in the Ghostlands, the headquarters of the traitor Dar'Khan Drathir, master of the Scourge in Quel'Thalas. Its every entrance is guarded by his dreaded floating eyes, and its halls are inhabited by necromancers and their skeletal minions. The tower radiates dark power, and few who enter its halls leave alive.

3512.name: Zeb'Sora
3512.description: Zeb'Sora is a small forest troll village in the northeastern Ghostlands, inhabited by the Amani trolls. Its crude huts and totems stand among the withered trees, and the trolls attack any elves who come near.

3513.name: Lake Elrendar
3513.description: On the side of the Ghostlands, Lake Elrendar stretches north into Eversong Woods. Its southern reaches are haunted by the wraiths of those who drowned during the Scourge's invasion, and the Farstrider Enclave stands on its southern shore. The lake's waters are dark and still, and an island in its midst is infested with crypt fiends.

3514.name: The Dead Scar
3514.description: In the Ghostlands, the Dead Scar begins at the Scourge citadel of Deatholme in the southwest and runs north through the withered forest, past Tranquillien, and across the Elrendar River into Eversong Woods. It marks the path of Arthas and the Scourge during their march to the Sunwell, and the land along it is dead and blighted. Undead still wander along its length.

3515.name: Elrendar River
3515.description: The Elrendar River is the largest river in Quel'Thalas, flowing out of Lake Elrendar and forming the border between Eversong Woods and the Ghostlands. Its clear waters contrast with the withered forest of the Ghostlands, and the Elrendar Crossing bridges it on the road between the two regions.

3516.name: Zeb'Tela
3516.description: Zeb'Tela is a medium-sized forest troll village in the eastern Ghostlands, inhabited by the Amani trolls. Its huts and totems stand among the withered trees, and the trolls guard their territory fiercely.

3517.name: Zeb'Nowa
3517.description: Zeb'Nowa is a wide-stretched forest troll village in the southeastern Ghostlands, near the Amani Pass leading to Zul'Aman. The Amani trolls who dwell here are numerous and hostile, and their village is decorated with skulls and totems.

3823.name: Isle of Tribulations
3823.description: The Isle of Tribulations is an island in Lake Elrendar in the Ghostlands, northeast of Suncrown Village, inhabited by crypt fiends of the Scourge. Young blood knights are sometimes sent here to test their abilities against the undead. The island is dark and overgrown, its shores lapped by the haunted waters of the lake.

3856.name: Elrendar Crossing
