3856.description: Elrendar Crossing is the bridge spanning the Elrendar River at the border between Eversong Woods and the Ghostlands. It marks the transition from the golden forest of the north to the withered, haunted lands of the south. Blood elf guards watch over the bridge, and travelers pass across it on the road to Tranquillien.

3861.name: Thalassian Pass
3861.description: The Thalassian Pass is a mountain pass in the far southern Ghostlands, leading south through the mountains to the Eastern Plaguelands. It is marked by a great gatehouse, believed to be one of the ancient Elfgates that once sealed Quel'Thalas from Lordaeron, which the Scourge breached with the help of the traitor Dar'Khan Drathir. Scourge banners still flank the gates, and the pass is a grim reminder of the kingdom's fall.

3433.description: The Ghostlands are the southern part of Quel'Thalas, a shadowy region of the elven kingdom lying south of Eversong Woods and north of the Eastern Plaguelands. Once part of the same golden forest, the land was devastated during the Third War, when the Scourge marched through on their way to the Sunwell, and it never recovered. Today the Ghostlands are a dark, cursed land: the trees are withered and black, the sky is gloomy, and a deathly chill hangs in the air. The Dead Scar cuts through the region, beginning at Deatholme, the Scourge's great citadel in the southwest, where the traitor Dar'Khan Drathir, the elf who betrayed his people and helped Arthas breach the kingdom's defenses, rules over the undead. Ruined villages are haunted by the ghosts of the elves who died there, and undead roam the forests. The blood elves and their Forsaken allies hold the town of Tranquillien, from which they strive to reclaim the land. The Amani forest trolls lurk in the eastern hills near their ancient city of Zul'Aman, night elf spies of the Sentinels watch the blood elves from hidden camps, and gnolls, spiders, and wild beasts roam the land. To the south, the Thalassian Pass leads through the mountains to the Plaguelands, guarded by one of the ancient Elfgates.

3455.name: The North Sea
3455.description: The North Sea washes the northern shores of Quel'Thalas, stretching from the coasts of Eversong Woods north toward Northrend. The Isle of Quel'Danas rises from these waters off the northern coast, and the elven ships that sail them have long linked the high elves' homeland with the wider world. The waters are cold and gray, and the winds that blow across them carry the chill of the frozen north.

3477.name: Azjol-Nerub
3477.description: Azjol-Nerub is a vast underground kingdom stretching beneath half the breadth of Northrend, the ancient realm of the arachnid nerubians. Built by aqir who fled north long ago, it became a center of nerubian civilization: a culture almost as old as that of the dwarves, devoted more to scholarship, art, and philosophy than to smithing, with huge libraries of literature and arcane lore. Its corridors are planed and polished, its vaulted halls carved with murals, frescoes, and columns, and phosphorescent fungi the nerubians once cultivated for light now grow unchecked. When the Lich King came to Northrend, he saw the nerubians as the greatest threat to his power and swarmed their kingdom in the War of the Spider. The nerubians nearly won, but every one of them who fell rose again to fight for the Scourge, and in the end the kingdom was overrun and its people slaughtered or raised into undeath; its own king, Anub'arak, now serves the Lich King. Today the Upper Kingdom is patrolled by undead nerubians guarding clutches of eggs that will bring forth new Scourge warriors, while scattered pockets of living nerubians wage a desperate hidden war. Deeper still, in the Old Kingdom of Ahn'kahet, mysterious faceless ones stir, said to answer to an evil power lurking beneath Northrend. Many of the kingdom's treasures, tomes, and tapestries still remain, untouched by the Scourge.

3478.name: Gates of Ahn'Qiraj
3478.description: The Gates of Ahn'Qiraj are the great gates in the Scarab Wall at the southern edge of Silithus, guarding the ancient city of Ahn'Qiraj, the stronghold of the Qiraji and their silithid servants. At the end of the War of the Shifting Sands a thousand years ago, the night elves and the dragonflights sealed the Qiraji behind the wall and its enchanted gates. In recent times, the gates were opened once more with the ancient Scepter of the Shifting Sands, and the combined armies of the Alliance and the Horde marched against the Qiraji legions. Beyond the gates lie the Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj and the great Temple of Ahn'Qiraj, where it is said the true masters of the Qiraji dwell. The area before the gates is a vast field of sand, scarred by battle and littered with the remains of silithid and soldiers, and the great Scarab Gong stands nearby. An ominous silence hangs over the gates, broken only by the distant buzzing of insects.

3479.name: The Veiled Sea
3479.description: These waters of the Veiled Sea surround the Azuremyst Isles off the northwestern coast of Kalimdor, where the draenei vessel known as the Exodar crashed. The sea here is deep and often veiled in mist, and the debris and crystals of the fallen ship have tainted some of the coastal waters with a strange glow, particularly around Bloodmyst Isle, whose shores run red. Murlocs and naga dwell along the coasts, and the drowned ruins of ancient night elven settlements lie beneath the waves. Ships sail across these waters between the Exodar and the night elf lands, and the great tree of Teldrassil can be seen rising from the sea to the east.

3483.name: Hellfire Peninsula

3536.name: Thrallmar
3536.description: Thrallmar is a Horde fortress on a plateau in northern Hellfire Peninsula, founded by Nazgrel, the commander of Thrall's personal security, after the reopening of the Dark Portal, to gain a foothold and keep watch over this demon-infested land. Its orc warriors, shamans, and allies wage war against the fel orcs of Hellfire Citadel and the Burning Legion. Its spiked walls, barracks, kennels, and great hall are built in the rugged style of the orcs, and wind riders connect it with the other Horde holdings in Outland. Demonic forge camps loom on the mountains to the north.

3538.name: Honor Hold
3538.description: Honor Hold is a fortified Alliance stronghold in southern Hellfire Peninsula, the first major settlement Alliance travelers encounter in Outland. It was founded as the main base of the Alliance Expedition, the Sons of Lothar, under General Turalyon; it took months to lay its foundations and finish its walls while the expedition fought off repeated Horde attacks and received only erratic supplies from Azeroth. From here the expedition stormed Hellfire Citadel, and after the Dark Portal was destroyed and Draenor torn apart, its survivors held on to the outpost for many years. Now led by Danath Trollbane, the aging veterans have been joined by the armies of Stormwind, Ironforge, and Nethergarde Keep. Its stone walls, keep, and mage tower are a symbol of the Alliance's enduring presence on this shattered world.

3539.name: The Stair of Destiny
3539.description: The Stair of Destiny is the massive foundation of the Dark Portal on the Outland side, rising at the eastern edge of Hellfire Peninsula where the land drops away into the Twisting Nether. The portal here is much larger and more elaborately decorated than its counterpart in Azeroth. The stair is heavily fortified by both the Alliance and the Horde, who have set aside their differences to hold it, for it is constantly assaulted by the demons of the Burning Legion: felguards, wrathguards, infernals raining from the sky, and a gigantic pit commander. Portals here lead back to Stormwind and Orgrimmar.

3541.name: Forge Camp: Mageddon
3541.description: Forge Camp: Mageddon is the easternmost of the Burning Legion's forge camps in Hellfire Peninsula, a fortress of green fel fire, spiked iron, and smoking forges where gan'arg and other demons craft the Legion's weapons and war machines. Succubi and other demons patrol its grounds, and the camp is a constant threat to the surrounding lands.

3542.name: The Path of Glory
3542.description: The Path of Glory is the great road leading from the foot of the Stair of Destiny to Hellfire Citadel, dividing the eastern half of Hellfire Peninsula. Upon closer inspection, the road is paved entirely with trampled bones, the remains of the draenei slaughtered by the demon-crazed Horde shortly before the first opening of the Dark Portal; the orcs killed the great majority of the draenei race, and of all the ruins they left across Outland, this road is the starkest reminder of that slaughter. The ruined cannons of the Alliance and blade throwers of the Horde from the Second War still line it. Thrallmar lies to the north and Honor Hold to the south, and even many orcs regard the road as one of the Horde's greatest shames.

3543.name: The Great Fissure
3543.description: The Great Fissure is a deep crack in the earth west of Honor Hold in Hellfire Peninsula, crawling with rock flayers and burrowing creatures. A small cave filled with rock flayers and mushrooms lies within the fissure. The chasm is a stark reminder of the forces that tore Draenor apart.

3545.name: Hellfire Citadel
3545.description: Hellfire Citadel is a massive, nearly impenetrable fortress at the heart of Hellfire Peninsula. It was built as the fortress of Blackhand, the first Warchief of the Horde, where the clans were ordered to gather, abandoning their ancestral homelands to form a standing army; Durotan of the Frostwolves called it a blight upon the land. From here the Horde planned the final assault on the draenei city of Shattrath and marched up the Path of Glory to the Dark Portal. When the land withered under the orcs' warlock magic, the fortress took the name Hellfire. Today the citadel is the stronghold of the fel orcs, savage, demon-blooded warriors led by Kargath Bladefist, and in its depths the pit lord Magtheridon is said to be imprisoned, his blood used to breed new fel orcs.

3546.name: Expedition Armory
3546.description: The Expedition Armory is the crumbled ruins of the Alliance Expedition's first base in Hellfire Peninsula. During the Alliance's campaign on Draenor, the human lines crumbled here, and the armory was destroyed by the orcs. Death knights raised the fallen soldiers as ghosts, and the Unyielding still haunt the ruins of their former outpost, endlessly reliving their last battle.

3547.name: Throne of Kil'jaeden
3547.description: The Throne of Kil'jaeden is a massive mountain northeast of Thrallmar in northern Hellfire Peninsula, named by the warlock Gul'dan. It was here, shortly before the first opening of the Dark Portal, that Gul'dan called the orc clans to drink the blood of the pit lord Mannoroth, binding them to the will of the Burning Legion. It is said that a great flaw in the fabric of the universe lies at the mountain, once linked to the lair of Kil'jaeden himself. Today it is a stronghold of the Legion, ruled by Doom Lord Kazzak, who reopened the Dark Portal, and of blood elves who drink the energies of captive demons. It is reachable only from the air, and its peak is wreathed in fel energy.

3548.name: Forge Camp: Rage
3548.description: Forge Camp: Rage is the middle of the Burning Legion's three forge camps in Hellfire Peninsula, directly overlooking the Horde fortress of Thrallmar. Its fel cannons are trained on the outpost below, and gan'arg and other demons work its forges. The camp is a constant threat to Thrallmar.

3549.name: Invasion Point: Annihilator
3549.description: Invasion Point: Annihilator is a Burning Legion stronghold north of Thrallmar in Hellfire Peninsula, where a great fel portal brings demonic reinforcements into Outland. The invasion point is guarded by powerful demons and their overlord, and fel energy crackles in the air around it.

3551.name: Ruins of Sha'naar
3551.description: The Ruins of Sha'naar are the remains of an ancient draenei temple in western Hellfire Peninsula, south of the Cenarion Post. They are now occupied by Illidari fiends and their unwilling servants, the Broken draenei of the Dreghood. The broken walls and shattered statues of the temple are a sad reminder of the draenei civilization destroyed by the orcs.

3552.name: Temple of Telhamat
3552.description: The Temple of Telhamat is a draenei stronghold and religious site on the northwestern frontier of Hellfire Peninsula, one of the few draenei holy places to have survived the orcish onslaught. Its elegant domes and spires rise above the red wasteland, and it serves as a refuge for the draenei and their Alliance allies, with a gryphon roost connecting it to Honor Hold and the lands beyond. From here, travelers set out toward the marshes of Zangarmarsh.

3553.name: Pools of Aggonar
3553.description: The Pools of Aggonar are a series of pools in northern Hellfire Peninsula, once sacred springs of the draenei, corrupted by the blood of the dying pit lord Aggonar; how he died no one knows, but his demonic aura fouled the holy waters, and only his bones remain. On the mountain above, the eredar warlock Arazzius the Cruel, a lieutenant of Doom Lord Kazzak and the Burning Legion's overlord of Hellfire Peninsula, sits on his throne surrounded by demons. The draenei seek to cleanse the pools and restore them to their former purity.

3554.name: Falcon Watch
3554.description: Falcon Watch is a blood elf settlement in western Hellfire Peninsula, allied with the Horde. Its graceful towers and buildings, built in the style of Silvermoon, stand in stark contrast to the red wasteland around them, and its rangers keep watch over the surrounding lands. The outpost has an inn and a dragonhawk roost, and it is a gateway for Horde travelers heading toward Zangarmarsh.

3555.name: Mag'har Post
3555.description: Mag'har Post is a fortress outpost of the Mag'har orcs in northwestern Hellfire Peninsula, east of the Temple of Telhamat. The Mag'har are the orcs of Draenor who never drank the blood of Mannoroth and remained free of demonic corruption. Few know of this post's existence, and it is filled with wounded orcs who have fought against the fel orcs and the Legion.

3556.name: Den of Haal'esh
3556.description: The Den of Haal'esh is a deep chasm in southwestern Hellfire Peninsula, beyond Dustquill Ravine, heavily populated by aggressive arakkoa, the bird-like people of Outland, and their kaliri birds. The arakkoa here practice dark magic and attack anyone who comes near.

3582.name: Zeth'Gor
3582.description: Zeth'Gor is a former Horde city in the mountains of southeastern Hellfire Peninsula, now overrun with fel orcs of the Bleeding Hollow clan. Its crude orcish buildings and fortifications are decorated with skulls and spikes, and the fel orcs here are savage and bloodthirsty. The city is a grim reminder of the Horde's past.

3669.name: The Stadium
3669.description: The Stadium is a ruined fortification west of Hellfire Citadel in Hellfire Peninsula, one of three ancient structures that the Alliance and the Horde fight to control. Whoever holds the Stadium, the Overlook, and Broken Hill gains an advantage in the battle for the peninsula.

3670.name: The Overlook
3670.description: The Overlook is a ruined fortification west of Hellfire Citadel in Hellfire Peninsula, one of three ancient structures that the Alliance and the Horde fight to control. From its heights, the citadel and the surrounding wasteland can be seen.

3671.name: Broken Hill
3671.description: Broken Hill is a ruined fortification west of Hellfire Citadel in Hellfire Peninsula, one of three ancient structures that the Alliance and the Horde fight to control. Its broken walls stand atop a rocky hill overlooking the wasteland.

3765.name: Razorthorn Trail
3765.description: The Razorthorn Trail is the pathway leading from southern Hellfire Peninsula to Terokkar Forest, a hillside covered with enormous brambles and inhabited by vicious Razorthorn ravagers. Travelers must be wary of the beasts lurking among the thorns.

3793.name: Felspark Ravine
3793.description: Felspark Ravine is a demon-infested scar running east to west north of the Legion Front in Hellfire Peninsula. It is inhabited by imps, infernals, and other demons, and the ground glows with fel energy.

3794.name: Valley of Bones
3794.description: The Valley of Bones is a shallow crevasse in Hellfire Peninsula littered with the bones of fallen beasts, just down the hill from the road east of Honor Hold. Two-headed carrion birds circle above, and fire geysers burst through the crust of the ground.

3795.name: Sha'naari Wastes
3795.description: The Sha'naari Wastes are wide plains in western Hellfire Peninsula, south of Fallen Sky Ridge. The Ruins of Sha'naar lie in their southern reaches, and the Cenarion Post stands near the road in the north. The wastes are barren and windswept.

3796.name: The Warp Fields
3796.description: The Warp Fields are an area on the southern edge of Hellfire Peninsula, near the Razorthorn Trail, littered with rogue voidwalkers and swept by violent warp storms. The air crackles with strange energies from the Twisting Nether.

3797.name: Fallen Sky Ridge
3797.description: Fallen Sky Ridge is a wide area of northwestern Hellfire Peninsula populated by dangerous stone colossi. Its most prominent feature is an enormous red crystal that seemingly fell from the sky, and it is whispered that the crystal was deliberately planted to corrupt and awaken the colossi. The ridge is barren and ominous.

3798.name: Haal'eshi Gorge
3798.description: Haal'eshi Gorge is a mountain ridge in southwestern Hellfire Peninsula crawling with arakkoa, who have built their nests and shrines among the rocks. The arakkoa are hostile to outsiders.

3799.name: Stonewall Canyon
3799.description: Stonewall Canyon is a wide gorge running along the western side of the Thrallmar plateau in Hellfire Peninsula. Its red rock walls rise steeply on either side, and wild beasts roam its floor.

3800.name: Thornfang Hill
3800.description: Thornfang Hill is a nesting ground for ravagers in western Hellfire Peninsula, on the path leading to Zangarmarsh. The Cenarion Refuge lies just beyond, at the edge of the marsh. The hill is covered with brambles.

3801.name: Mag'har Grounds
3801.description: The Mag'har Grounds are a cresting plateau in northwestern Hellfire Peninsula, home to a simple Mag'har orc village. The Mag'har Post looms in a nearby pass. The orcs here live a traditional life, free of demonic corruption.

3802.name: Void Ridge
3802.description: Void Ridge is an area in southeastern Hellfire Peninsula, south of the Legion Front and east of Zeth'Gor, full of voidwalkers that enter through shadowy, crackling storm portals. The air is filled with strange energies.

3803.name: The Abyssal Shelf
3803.description: The Abyssal Shelf is a tilted stretch of land at the northeastern edge of Hellfire Peninsula, heavily populated by the Burning Legion's fel reavers, gan'arg, and mo'arg. The Alliance and the Horde launch aerial bombing runs against the Legion forces stationed here. The shelf hangs at the very edge of the world, overlooking the Twisting Nether.

3804.name: The Legion Front
3804.description: The Legion Front is the area along the Path of Glory in Hellfire Peninsula, between Hellfire Citadel and the Dark Portal, where the Burning Legion's forces are most heavily concentrated. Demons of every kind gather here to assault the Stair of Destiny, and the land is scorched and littered with the remains of battle.

3806.name: Supply Caravan
3806.description: The Supply Caravan is a Horde caravan on the road just east of Thrallmar in Hellfire Peninsula. It is frequently attacked by infernals raining from the sky, but blood elf magisters guard it and bring the demons down.

3807.name: Reaver's Fall
3807.description: Reaver's Fall is a small Horde camp between the Legion Front and Thrallmar in Hellfire Peninsula, built around the remains of a destroyed fel reaver, a massive demonic war machine. From here, Horde riders launch aerial bombing runs against the Burning Legion's forces.

3808.name: Cenarion Post
3808.description: The Cenarion Post is a small camp of the Cenarion Expedition in the northern Sha'naari Wastes of western Hellfire Peninsula. The druids here study the ravaged land and seek ways to heal it, and they welcome all who would aid them.

3809.name: Southern Rampart
3809.description: The Southern Rampart is part of the outer walls of Hellfire Citadel in central Hellfire Peninsula, a massive fortification of stone and iron guarded by fel orcs. It grants access to the citadel's Blood Furnace, where it is said the fel orcs are bred.

3810.name: Northern Rampart
3810.description: The Northern Rampart is part of the outer walls of Hellfire Citadel in central Hellfire Peninsula, mostly ruined and inaccessible. Its broken towers and walls loom over the surrounding wasteland.

3811.name: Gor'gaz Outpost
3811.description: Gor'gaz Outpost is a fel orc camp along the Southern Rampart of Hellfire Citadel in Hellfire Peninsula. The fel orcs here guard the approaches to the citadel and attack anyone who comes near.

3812.name: Spinebreaker Post
3812.description: Spinebreaker Post is a small Horde outpost in southern Hellfire Peninsula, east of the Expedition Armory and southwest of Zeth'Gor. It serves as a forward base for the Horde's operations against the fel orcs of Zeth'Gor, and a wind rider master connects it with Thrallmar.

3813.name: The Path of Anguish
3813.description: The Path of Anguish is a jagged canyon in Hellfire Peninsula, south of the Path of Glory and west of the Legion Front, full of infernals, imps, and other demons. Its name, like that of the great road, suggests a long history of defeat and suffering.

3814.name: East Supply Caravan
3814.description: The East Supply Caravan is an Alliance caravan on the road just east of Honor Hold in Hellfire Peninsula, carrying supplies to the Alliance forces fighting at the Legion Front. Soldiers guard it against demons and fel orcs.

3815.name: Expedition Point
3815.description: Expedition Point is an outpost of Honor Hold in eastern Hellfire Peninsula, strategically placed near both Zeth'Gor and the Legion Front. It is built around the remains of a destroyed fel reaver, whose metal the Alliance soldiers mine for their own use. The outpost's defenders fight both fel orcs and demons.

3816.name: Zeppelin Crash
3816.description: The Zeppelin Crash is the wreck of a goblin zeppelin in southern Hellfire Peninsula, between Honor Hold and the Expedition Armory. Its eccentric goblin pilot survived and has set up camp beside the wreckage.

3835.name: Dustquill Ravine
3835.description: Dustquill Ravine is a hillside pass covered with enormous brambles and inhabited by vicious ravagers, just southwest of Falcon Watch in Hellfire Peninsula. An abandoned camp lies in the ravine.

3838.name: Spinebreaker Mountains
3838.description: The Spinebreaker Mountains are a range in southeastern Hellfire Peninsula, nestling Expedition Point and Zeth'Gor among their jagged peaks. Spinebreaker Pass cuts through them. The mountains are red and barren.

3884.name: Spinebreaker Pass
3884.description: Spinebreaker Pass is a straight but narrow chasm in the far southeastern Hellfire Peninsula, connecting Zeth'Gor with Void Ridge and the Legion Front. Its steep walls offer a hidden route through the mountains.

3920.name: Shatter Point
3920.description: Shatter Point is a small Wildhammer dwarf outpost in Hellfire Peninsula, built on a floating fragment of land drifting near the edge of the world. Its gryphon riders launch bombing runs against the Burning Legion's forces on the Abyssal Shelf and fly soldiers to a beachhead near the demons' lines, and the dwarves warn visitors not to come if they have just eaten. A ruined guard tower is its only building, with its top floating just above the rest.

3955.name: Hellfire Basin
3955.description: Hellfire Basin is the wide, sloping area behind Hellfire Citadel in Hellfire Peninsula, descending from the three ruined fortifications toward the citadel. There lies the ominous entrance to Magtheridon's Lair, where the pit lord is said to be held captive in the depths of the citadel.

3483.description: Hellfire Peninsula is a barren, blood-red wasteland in eastern Outland, the shattered remains of the orcish homeworld of Draenor, and the first land travelers see when they step through the Dark Portal from Azeroth. Once lush and verdant, it was rendered dry and lifeless by the dark practices of orc warlocks, and the ground is hard, cracked, and red, with fire geysers bursting through its crust. In places, the bones of the countless draenei slaughtered by the demon-crazed orcs before their invasion of Azeroth still crunch underfoot. When the shaman Ner'zhul opened his portals to other worlds, Draenor was torn apart, and fragments of the peninsula can be seen floating at its edges against the swirling, alien sky of the Twisting Nether. It was here that the heroes of the Alliance Expedition fought the Horde of Draenor, and here that they sealed the Dark Portal from the other side. Today the peninsula is a battleground once more: the great fortress of Hellfire Citadel, once the base of the orcish Horde, is now the stronghold of the savage fel orcs, while the Burning Legion has established forge camps and invasion points, and its armies assault the Stair of Destiny where the Dark Portal stands. The Alliance holds Honor Hold, founded by the veterans of the Alliance Expedition known as the Sons of Lothar, and the Horde holds Thrallmar. The draenei maintain the Temple of Telhamat, the blood elves Falcon Watch, and the Mag'har orcs a hidden post in the northwest, while arakkoa, ravagers, and wild beasts roam the wastes.

3487.name: Silvermoon City

3704.name: The Shepherd's Gate
3704.description: The Shepherd's Gate is the main entrance to Silvermoon City from Eversong Woods, a grand gateway of golden stone and graceful arches leading into the heart of the blood elf capital. Arcane guardians and city guards watch over the gate, and travelers, merchants, and soldiers pass through it in a steady stream. Beyond the gate, the shining spires and floating platforms of the rebuilt city rise in splendor, while the blighted path of the Dead Scar runs past it, a reminder of the day the Scourge broke through.

3487.description: Silvermoon City is the capital of the blood elves, rising in the northeastern part of Eversong Woods within the kingdom of Quel'Thalas, at the northernmost tip of the Eastern Kingdoms. Founded thousands of years ago by the high elves after their arrival from Kalimdor, it may rival Ironforge as the oldest capital still standing in the world. The city was built of white stone and living plants, interwoven with the land, and was home to the famous Academies of Silvermoon, the royal Sunstrider Spire, and the Convocation of Silvermoon. During the Second War, the magisters used the Sunwell's power to shield the city from the Horde's dragonfire, but in the Third War the death knight Arthas led the Scourge through its gates, slaying the king and most of the population. The blood elves have since rebuilt the eastern half of the city, restoring much of its former glory with the new magics brought back from Outland, while the western half still lies in ruins beyond the Dead Scar. Today the city is ruled by Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron, and it is a place of breathtaking beauty: golden spires, floating platforms, chained crystals brimming with harnessed magic, lush gardens, and arcane guardians patrol its streets. Its districts include the Bazaar, the Court of the Sun, the Royal Exchange, Murder Row, and the Farstriders' Square, and an orb of translocation connects it to the Undercity. Beneath its magnificent surface, however, lies the darkness of the blood elves' hunger for magic.

3518.name: Nagrand

3610.name: Burning Blade Ruins
3610.description: The Burning Blade Ruins are the ruins of the ancestral stronghold of the Burning Blade clan in southeastern Nagrand, northeast of Kil'sorrow Fortress. They are now inhabited by the Boulderfist ogres, who have made the ruins their own.

3611.name: Clan Watch
3611.description: Clan Watch is an empty village in southeastern Nagrand, of orcish origin and dating back to the days before the First War. Its abandoned huts and watchtowers stand silent on the plains.

3613.name: Garadar
3613.description: Garadar is the home of the Mag'har orcs in northern Nagrand, named after Garad, the father of Durotan and grandfather of Thrall. The Mag'har are the orcs of Draenor who never drank the blood of Mannoroth and remained free of demonic corruption. Their spiritual leader is Greatmother Geyah, Durotan's mother and Thrall's grandmother, who resides in the great circular hospice at the heart of the town. Garadar is built of wood and hide in the traditional orcish style, and wind riders connect it with the other Horde holdings in Outland.

3614.name: Skysong Lake
3614.description: Skysong Lake is a lake in northern Nagrand, between Garadar and the Throne of the Elements, populated by water elementals. Its clear waters reflect the pink sky and the floating islands above.

3615.name: Throne of the Elements
3615.description: The Throne of the Elements is a sacred site in northeastern Nagrand, the home of the four great elemental furies of Draenor, the mightiest spirits of earth, fire, air, and water. Orcish legend holds that it was here, long ago, that the first orc shamans learned to commune with the elements, and for generations young shamans of every clan made pilgrimages to the Throne to seek the spirits' blessing. Massive standing stones ring the site. Members of the Earthen Ring and other shamans now gather here to seek the elements' wisdom, and the furies tolerate no violence on their sacred ground.

3616.name: Laughing Skull Ruins
3616.description: The Laughing Skull Ruins are the remains of a Mag'har town in northern Nagrand that has been overrun by the Warmaul ogres. Its crumbling buildings and broken barrels, jars, and furniture lie scattered across the ground, and the ogres have raised a mound among the ruins and made them their home. Within them stands the Ring of Blood, a great fighting ring run by a goblin promoter, where warriors test their bravery and strength against ever deadlier foes.

3617.name: Warmaul Hill
3617.description: Warmaul Hill is a large mountaintop in northwestern Nagrand, home to the Warmaul ogres. The ogres of Nagrand were once ruled by the gronn from a massive cavern on this hill, until the ogre lord Cho'war the Pillager led a rebellion and drove the gronn out, uniting the fractured ogre clans under the Warmaul banner. Only the Boulderfist clan refuses to join them, and the two fight constantly over territory. The hill is a stronghold of the ogres, and they fiercely defend it.

3621.name: Lake Sunspring
3621.description: Lake Sunspring is a large lake in western Nagrand, inhabited by water elementals. Its shores were once home to a Mag'har village.

3622.name: Sunspring Post
3622.description: Sunspring Post is a former Mag'har village on the shores of Lake Sunspring in western Nagrand, destroyed by the Murkblood Broken, who slaughtered everyone they could find. The surviving refugees, including many orphans, fled to Garadar, leaving the ruined village in the hands of the Murkblood scavengers. The village is a scene of tragedy.

3623.name: Aeris Landing
3623.description: Aeris Landing is a small outpost of the Consortium, a band of ethereal traders who care little for political power and much for profit, in southern Nagrand near Oshu'gun. The ethereals built it close to the great crystal mountain to mine it, but they halted their work upon learning of its connection to the naaru, and they now trade with travelers for other goods instead. Being so close to Oshu'gun, they are threatened by the voidspawn and rogue ethereals that gather around it. The outpost has typical ethereal structures and a transportation portal.

3624.name: Forge Camp: Fear
3624.description: Forge Camp: Fear is the southernmost of the two Burning Legion forge camps in western Nagrand, a fortress of fel fire and spiked iron where demons forge weapons and war machines. It is led by a demonic overseer.

3625.name: Forge Camp: Hate
3625.description: Forge Camp: Hate is the northernmost of the two Burning Legion forge camps in western Nagrand, watched over by a demonic overseer. Its forges burn with green fel fire, and demons patrol its grounds.

3626.name: Telaar
3626.description: Telaar is the town of the Kurenai in southern Nagrand, allied with the Alliance, home to both draenei and Broken. It is one of the few intact examples of undamaged draenei architecture remaining on what is left of Draenor, with elegant domed buildings and crystal ornaments. The town has an inn, a gryphon roost, and merchants, and its people are proud and hopeful.

3627.name: Northwind Cleft
3627.description: Northwind Cleft is the gorge leading north from the Halaani Basin in central Nagrand, populated by ogres. Its rocky walls are steep and windswept.

3628.name: Halaa
3628.description: Halaa is a town on a plateau at the center of Nagrand. It was once the foremost draenei research site for the study of naaru crystals, but it is now fiercely contested by the Alliance and the Horde. Whichever side controls Halaa gains access to its merchants and supplies, and the other side lays siege to it constantly. The town has changed hands many times, and the scars of battle mark its walls.

3629.name: Southwind Cleft
3629.description: Southwind Cleft is the gorge leading south from the Halaani Basin in central Nagrand, populated by ogres. Its rocky walls are steep and windswept.

3630.name: Oshu'gun
3630.description: Oshu'gun, orcish for Mountain of Spirits, is a great white crystal monolith in southwestern Nagrand. Instead of being jagged like other mountains, it is smooth and triangular, and it is said to be the largest diamond in the known universe. For generations the orcs revered it as a sacred place: every spring and autumn the clans gathered in the river valley at its foot for the Kosh'harg festival, where shamans communed with their ancestors, and the ground was so holy that any fight that broke out had to end in peace or departure. In truth, it is the wreck of the vessel that carried the draenei to Draenor, and deep within it dwells an ailing naaru, surrounded by the spirits of orc ancestors. Rogue ethereals now harvest its crystal, and dark creatures of the void gather around it.

3631.name: Spirit Fields
3631.description: The Spirit Fields are an area of southwestern Nagrand centered around the holy mountain of Oshu'gun. The fields are inscribed with mystic symbols of unknown origin, and they are inhabited by wild elekks, herds of clefthooves, and earth elementals. A son of the gronn overlord Gruul is said to wander the fields.

3633.name: Ancestral Grounds
3633.description: The Ancestral Grounds are a series of small shrines and stones raised to honor the fallen ancestors of the orcs, on the western edge of Nagrand, northwest of Oshu'gun. Something has disturbed the grounds, and the ancestors now roam the site as restless ghosts.

3634.name: Windyreed Village
3634.description: Windyreed Village is a fishing village of the Lost Ones in eastern Nagrand, lying just below the High Path that leads up to Shattrath City. Its huts stand on the shore of a lake.

3636.name: Elemental Plateau
3636.description: The Elemental Plateau is a floating plateau north of the Throne of the Elements in Nagrand, reachable only from the air. Elementals of fire, water, earth, and air dwell here in great numbers, and the plateau is charged with elemental energy.

3637.name: Kil'sorrow Fortress
3637.description: Kil'sorrow Fortress is a large fort in southeastern Nagrand near the border with Terokkar Forest, inhabited by agents of the Shadow Council. It is named after the demon lord Kil'jaeden, and its warlocks plot the corruption of Nagrand.

3638.name: The Ring of Trials
3638.description: The Ring of Trials is an ancient orcish proving ground southeast of Garadar in Nagrand, where warriors have tested their strength for generations. Today, gladiators of all races come to battle within its walls before cheering crowds.

3666.name: Halaani Basin
3666.description: The Halaani Basin is a deep cleft below Halaa in central Nagrand, populated by water elementals. It leads north into Northwind Cleft and south into Southwind Cleft, both full of ogres.

3672.name: Mag'hari Procession
3672.description: The Mag'hari Procession is a small camp near Sunspring Post in western Nagrand, where a Mag'har procession carrying a dead farseer to the Ancestral Grounds was ambushed by the Murkblood Broken. The survivors, including a young warrior of a famous orcish family, now hold the camp.

3673.name: Nesingwary Safari
3673.description: The Nesingwary Safari is a small hunting camp in northeastern Nagrand, where the renowned dwarven big-game hunter Hemet Nesingwary has relocated with his companions, drawn by the excellent hunting of the plains. The camp is filled with trophies and tents.

3699.name: Laughing Skull Courtyard
3699.description: The Laughing Skull Courtyard is the eastern part of the Laughing Skull Ruins in northern Nagrand, a broken courtyard of the former Mag'har town now held by the Warmaul ogres.

3700.name: The Ring of Blood
3700.description: The Ring of Blood is a great fighting ring within the Laughing Skull Ruins in northern Nagrand, where warriors test their bravery and strength against powerful opponents for the entertainment of the crowd. A goblin promoter organizes the fights.

3701.name: Arena Floor
3701.description: The Arena Floor is the fighting ground at the center of the Ring of Trials in Nagrand, where gladiators battle before the crowds.

3705.name: Telaari Basin
3705.description: The Telaari Basin is a deep cleft north of Telaar in south-central Nagrand, populated by earth elementals and the occasional windroc.

3760.name: The Barrier Hills
3760.description: On the side of Nagrand, the Barrier Hills form the northeastern corner of the land, bordering Zangarmarsh to the north and Shattrath City to the southeast. Ogres roam the hills.

3761.name: The High Path
3761.description: The High Path is the rise leading up from Windyreed Village in eastern Nagrand to Shattrath City above, a winding road between the grasslands and the City of Light.

3762.name: Windyreed Pass
3762.description: Windyreed Pass is the path leading north to Zangarmarsh in northeastern Nagrand, named for nearby Windyreed Village.

3763.name: Zangar Ridge
3763.description: Zangar Ridge is the northwestern edge of Nagrand, below which lies the gloomy, luminous Zangarmarsh. The ridge offers a striking view of the giant mushrooms below.

3764.name: The Twilight Ridge
3764.description: The Twilight Ridge is an area in western Nagrand, the site of one of the dimensional gateways that the Burning Legion once used to bring demons from the Twisting Nether into Outland. Illidan's forces shut down the gateways, and the portal is no longer functional, but cultists of the Shadow Council, overseen by an eredar, are channeling magic into its frame in an attempt to reopen it. Floating rock fragments nearby bear four great statues like those that flank the Dark Portal, robed and hooded figures holding swords, whose origin no one knows.

3788.name: The Low Path
3788.description: The Low Path is the road leading down from southeastern Nagrand toward Terokkar Forest, winding between the grasslands and the forest.

3839.name: Abandoned Armory
3839.description: The Abandoned Armory is a lone draenei building just north of Telaar, on the edge of Southwind Cleft in central Nagrand. It contains weapons and supplies, suggesting it was abandoned recently, and a single draenei scholar now dwells there.

3518.description: Nagrand is the last unscarred region of Outland, a land of rolling green and golden grasslands, sparkling lakes, and floating islands drifting beneath a pink-tinged sky, lying south of Zangarmarsh and west of Terokkar Forest. Its name means Land of Winds in the orcish tongue, and it was the homeland of the Frostwolf clan and the meeting ground of the orcish people, who gathered twice each year at the base of the sacred mountain Oshu'gun to give thanks to the spirits. Nagrand is the ancestral home of the orcs and the heart of early orcish shamanism, and it was here that Gul'dan first introduced the orcs to warlock magic. Today it is a fertile retreat where elementals commune with mortals at the Throne of the Elements. It is home to the Mag'har, the uncorrupted orcs who never drank the blood of Mannoroth, whose city of Garadar stands in the north under the guidance of Greatmother Geyah, Thrall's grandmother, and to the Kurenai, Broken draenei who have found new hope, whose town of Telaar stands in the south. The greatest threat to this unspoiled land comes from the ogres of the Warmaul and Boulderfist clans, while the Burning Legion has established forge camps in the west and the Shadow Council holds a fortress in the southeast. Clefthooves, elekk, talbuks, windrocs, and wolves roam the plains, and the town of Halaa at the center of the land is fought over by the Alliance and the Horde.

3519.name: Terokkar Forest

3674.name: Cenarion Thicket
3674.description: The Cenarion Thicket is an encampment of the Cenarion Expedition in northern Terokkar Forest that has been devastated. A terrible blast swept through the camp, killing most of its druids and leaving it overrun by mutated moths and noxious gases. Only a handful of druids survived, one of them driven mad by what he witnessed. The thicket is a grim and eerie place.

3675.name: Tuurem
3675.description: Tuurem is a ruined draenei city in the northern reaches of Terokkar Forest, one of the first draenei cities overrun by the orcs before the first opening of the Dark Portal. Its broken buildings and crumbling walls are now home to mutated draenei, Broken and Lost Ones who have allied themselves with the blood elves of Firewing Point; it is said that the bomb that destroyed the nearby Cenarion Thicket was assembled here.

3676.name: Veil Shienor
3676.description: Veil Shienor is a colony of the arakkoa in northeastern Terokkar Forest, east of the road between Terokkar and Hellfire Peninsula. The arakkoa here serve Skettis and their dark god Terokk, and their nests and shrines stand high among the trees.

3677.name: Veil Skith
3677.description: Veil Skith is a colony of the arakkoa in Terokkar Forest, directly south of Shattrath City, bordering the Bone Wastes. The arakkoa here practice dark magic in the service of Terokk, and they are hostile to all outsiders.

3678.name: Veil Shalas
3678.description: Veil Shalas is the strongest of the arakkoa colonies in Terokkar Forest, located at the base of the mountains below Skettis itself, along the eastern edge of the Bone Wastes. It is here that the sages of Terokk conduct their war against the Light.

3679.name: Skettis
3679.description: Skettis is the hidden capital of the arakkoa, nestled in Blackwind Valley high in the mountains of southeastern Terokkar Forest, reachable only from the air. It was built long ago by the legendary arakkoa king Terokk as a refuge for those outcast and unwanted in arakkoa society. The city is made up of four veils, settlements built in the boughs of the trees and on the forest floor around Blackwind Lake, at whose center lies Terokk's Rest. Arakkoa of every kind and their great kaliri birds inhabit it, guarded by talonsworn forest-ragers. The Sethekk cult and the Skettis outcasts have both broken away from it, and the Sha'tari Skyguard keeps watch over it from a nearby landing.

3680.name: Blackwind Valley
3680.description: Blackwind Valley is a large mountain valley in southeastern Terokkar Forest, home to the arakkoa capital of Skettis and Blackwind Lake. It is accessible only from the air, and its tall trees and misty slopes hide the secrets of the arakkoa.

3681.name: Firewing Point
3681.description: Firewing Point is an outpost of blood elves loyal to Kael'thas Sunstrider in northeastern Terokkar Forest. Its tall tower and courtyard house a dangerous mana bomb, similar to the one that destroyed a village in Netherstorm. The blood elves here are hostile to most outsiders, and the Scryers of Shattrath regard them as enemies.

3682.name: Grangol'var Village
3682.description: Grangol'var Village is a ruined village just north of the Bone Wastes in Terokkar Forest, occupied by warlocks of the Shadow Council who conceal their true purpose. The village is dark and ominous, and those who enter it uninvited rarely return.

3683.name: Stonebreaker Hold
3683.description: Stonebreaker Hold is a Horde town in central Terokkar Forest, built of wood and stone among the trees and guarded by orc and troll warriors. It has an inn and a wind rider master, and its defenders keep watch over the forest and the Bone Wastes to the south.

3684.name: Allerian Stronghold
3684.description: Allerian Stronghold is an Alliance town in southeastern Terokkar Forest, named in honor of the ranger Alleria Windrunner. Its site was chosen long ago, during the Alliance Expedition, when the company of Danath Trollbane camped here while hunting Ner'zhul; its elven and human founders declared that, since the orcs had destroyed so much of Quel'Thalas, the Alliance would claim this, the one green region left on the shattered world, as a symbol of the alliance of elves, men, and dwarves. Home to many high elves, its mage tower, town hall, and graceful buildings are among the few high elven structures in Outland, and its rangers and soldiers watch over the forest.

3685.name: Bonechewer Ruins
3685.description: The Bonechewer Ruins are the remains of a village of the Bonechewer clan of orcs, northeast of Allerian Stronghold in Terokkar Forest. The ruins are brimming with aggressive fel orcs.

3686.name: Veil Lithic
3686.description: Veil Lithic is a colony of the arakkoa along the border between the Bone Wastes and the forest in Terokkar, southwest of the Sha'tari Base Camp. It is here that the minions of Terokk corrupt the birds of the forest for their use.

3688.name: Auchindoun
3688.description: Auchindoun is the ruined city of the dead of the draenei, standing at the heart of the Bone Wastes in southern Terokkar Forest. Far from the other cities of Draenor, the draenei raised a vast mausoleum here and laid their dead to rest within it, watched over by the Auchenai, an order of priests who communed with the souls of the departed. During the Horde's war against the draenei, warlocks of the Shadow Council reached beyond the veil of reality and brought forth an entity of immense evil, an elemental of sound, whose arrival blew the temple apart, reduced the surrounding forest to a charred wasteland, and tore a rift in the Nether. The interred draenei walk the ruins as restless spirits, and ethereals, demons, arakkoa, and the Shadow Council now vie for its four great halls: the Mana-Tombs, the Auchenai Crypts, the Sethekk Halls, and the Shadow Labyrinth.

3689.name: Veil Reskk
3689.description: Veil Reskk is a former draenei shrine in northern Terokkar Forest that has been taken over by the arakkoa and made into a settlement. The arakkoa here serve Skettis and are hostile to outsiders.

3690.name: Blackwind Lake
3690.description: Blackwind Lake is a lake in Blackwind Valley in southeastern Terokkar Forest, in the heart of the arakkoa capital of Skettis. It is accessible only from the air, and its waters are guarded by water elementals. At its center lies Terokk's Rest.

3691.name: Lake Ere'Noru
3691.description: Lake Ere'Noru is a lake in southeastern Terokkar Forest, in a nook in the mountains above Allerian Stronghold, accessible only from the air. Its waters are calm and clear.

3692.name: Lake Jorune
3692.description: Lake Jorune is a lake in central Terokkar Forest, in a nook in the mountains above Stonebreaker Hold, accessible only from the air. An arakkoa settlement stands on its shores, and the arakkoa who dwell there are friendly to outsiders.

3693.name: Skethyl Mountains
3693.description: The Skethyl Mountains are a range in southeastern Terokkar Forest, containing Blackwind Valley, Blackwind Lake, and the arakkoa capital of Skettis. The mountains are tall and rugged, traversable only from the air.

3696.name: The Barrier Hills
3696.description: The Barrier Hills are a range of hills in northwestern Terokkar Forest, forming the border with Zangarmarsh to the north and rising to the very edge of Shattrath City. An extensive ogre settlement stretches across the Terokkar side of the hills, accessible mainly from the air.

3697.name: The Bone Wastes
3697.description: The Bone Wastes are a desolate, charred expanse in southern Terokkar Forest. Before Draenor was destroyed, the land here was forested like the rest of Terokkar, until warlocks of the Shadow Council, assaulting the draenei who defended Auchindoun, summoned an otherworldly being whose arrival ripped the earth asunder and sent waves of destructive energy rolling out to level the forest. The ground is now grey and lifeless, littered with bones and the remains of the trees, and the ruins of Auchindoun stand at its heart. Restless spirits, carrion birds, and undead roam the wastes, and the Alliance and the Horde fight for control of ancient spirit towers scattered across it.

3719.name: Bleeding Hollow Ruins
3719.description: The Bleeding Hollow Ruins are the remains of a village of the Bleeding Hollow clan of orcs, west of the Bone Wastes on the border between Terokkar Forest and Nagrand. The former village has been overrun by Boulderfist ogres seeking new lands.

3858.name: Razorthorn Shelf
3858.description: The Razorthorn Shelf is a passage between southwestern Hellfire Peninsula and northeastern Terokkar Forest, inhabited by ravagers. It is the shortest route between Hellfire Peninsula and Shattrath City.

3859.name: Silmyr Lake
3859.description: Silmyr Lake is a lake near the border with Zangarmarsh in northwestern Terokkar Forest, filled with hostile eels. The lake is surrounded by tall pines.

3860.name: Raastok Glade
3860.description: Raastok Glade is a wooded vale in central Terokkar Forest, east of Stonebreaker Hold, crawling with basilisks, wolves, and warp stalkers.

3885.name: Netherweb Ridge
3885.description: Netherweb Ridge is a spider-infested area of trees southeast of the Bone Wastes in Terokkar Forest. Great webs hang between the trees, and the spiders prey on anything that strays too close.

3886.name: Derelict Caravan
3886.description: The Derelict Caravan is a ravaged caravan in the Bone Wastes, southeast of Auchindoun in Terokkar Forest, now full of shambling zombies and invisible shades. Its wagons lie broken and abandoned.

3887.name: Refugee Caravan
3887.description: The Refugee Caravan is a small makeshift camp in the northern Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest, populated by refugees of many races from Shattrath City. The caravan was attacked by Shadow Council raiders, and its defenders and vindicators of the Sha'tar now protect the refugees while they repair their wagons.

3888.name: Shadow Tomb
3888.description: The Shadow Tomb is a crypt northwest of Auchindoun in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest, occupied by cultists of the Shadow Council known as the Cabal, led by a demonic shivarra. Her harsh voice echoes through the halls.

3889.name: Veil Rhaze
3889.description: Veil Rhaze is a colony of the arakkoa along the border between the Bone Wastes and the forest, west of the Refugee Caravan. It was destroyed when Auchindoun exploded, but the malevolent god Terokk has raised the spirits of its dead to do his bidding.

3890.name: Tomb of Lights
3890.description: The Tomb of Lights is a crypt northeast of Auchindoun in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest, populated by aggressive ethereals drawn into Outland by the rift torn in the Nether.

3891.name: Carrion Hill
3891.description: Carrion Hill is a skeleton-riddled mound northeast of Auchindoun in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest, the feeding ground of carrion birds, including a huge white one.

3892.name: Writhing Mound
3892.description: The Writhing Mound is a bone-riddled hill east of Auchindoun in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest, populated by Auchenai necromancers, draenei who have turned to the dark arts of death.

3893.name: Ring of Observance
3893.description: The Ring of Observance is the inner cloister of the ruined necropolis of Auchindoun, at the heart of the Bone Wastes. It is the central courtyard from which the four great halls of the temple can be reached, each now held by a different power. The ring is surrounded by shattered walls and haunted by the echoes of the explosion that destroyed the temple.

3894.name: Auchenai Grounds
3894.description: The Auchenai Grounds are a ruined temple off the southwestern corner of Auchindoun, roamed by Auchenai initiates and doomsayers, as well as the ghosts of the dead.

3901.name: Allerian Post
3901.description: Allerian Post is a small Alliance camp in eastern Terokkar Forest, just south of Firewing Point, named in honor of Alleria Windrunner. Its soldiers watch the blood elves of Firewing Point.

3902.name: Stonebreaker Camp
3902.description: Stonebreaker Camp is a small Horde camp in eastern Terokkar Forest, close to Stonebreaker Hold. Its scouts investigate the activities of the blood elves of Firewing Point.

3946.name: Wayne's Refuge
3946.description: Wayne's Refuge is an isolated cliff in eastern Terokkar Forest, just southeast of Firewing Point, home to a reclusive veteran of the Sons of Lothar who lives there alone.

3956.name: The Shadow Stair
3956.description: The Shadow Stair is the looming set of steps carved into the northern part of Auchindoun's Ring of Observance, densely populated by cultists of the Shadow Council. It leads toward the depths where the Council holds the terrible entity it summoned.

3958.name: Sha'tari Base Camp
3958.description: The Sha'tari Base Camp is an encampment defended by Sha'tar vindicators southwest of Auchindoun in the Bone Wastes of Terokkar Forest. It serves as a base for those who would enter the ruined necropolis.

3961.name: Sorrow Wing Point
3961.description: Sorrow Wing Point is an isolated mesa south of the Bone Wastes in Terokkar Forest, reachable only from the air. It is a quiet, desolate place.

3973.name: Blackwind Landing
3973.description: Blackwind Landing is a small outpost of the Sha'tari Skyguard just north of Skettis in southeastern Terokkar Forest. The Skyguard, riders of nether rays in the service of the Sha'tar, watch over the arakkoa capital and strike against its dark sages.

3974.name: Veil Harr'ik
3974.description: Veil Harr'ik is one of the four veils that make up the arakkoa capital of Skettis in southeastern Terokkar Forest, a settlement of nests and huts built among the trees.

3975.name: Terokk's Rest
3975.description: Terokk's Rest is an island in Blackwind Lake at the heart of Skettis in southeastern Terokkar Forest. It is said that the arakkoa god-king Terokk can be summoned back into the world here.

3976.name: Veil Ala'rak
3976.description: Veil Ala'rak is one of the four veils that make up the arakkoa capital of Skettis in southeastern Terokkar Forest, a settlement of nests and huts built among the trees.

3977.name: Upper Veil Shil'ak
3977.description: Upper Veil Shil'ak is one of the four veils that make up the arakkoa capital of Skettis in southeastern Terokkar Forest, built high among the boughs of the trees.

3978.name: Lower Veil Shil'ak
3978.description: Lower Veil Shil'ak is one of the four veils that make up the arakkoa capital of Skettis in southeastern Terokkar Forest, built on the forest floor beneath the upper veil.

4078.name: Razorthorn Rise
4078.description: Razorthorn Rise is an area in the mountains at the northern edge of Terokkar Forest, bordering Hellfire Peninsula, accessible only from the air. Razorthorn flayers and ravagers roam its rocky slopes.

3519.description: Terokkar Forest is a dark, ancient forest in southern Outland, lying east of Nagrand, west of Shadowmoon Valley, and southwest of Hellfire Peninsula. Its tall crystal pines, known as olemba trees, form a deep green canopy, and its misty glades are home to wolves, basilisks, warp stalkers, and the bird-like arakkoa, whose hidden capital, Skettis, lies in the mountains of the southeast and who take their name for the forest from their malevolent god-king Terokk. In the northwest stands Shattrath City, the ancient draenei capital, rebuilt with the aid of the naaru and now a sanctuary for refugees of every race. The southern half of the forest is the Bone Wastes, a charred and desolate expanse created when agents of the Shadow Council summoned a terrible entity in the draenei necropolis of Auchindoun, whose blast shattered the temple, laid waste to the land, and tore a rift that drew the ethereals into Outland. The ruins of Auchindoun now stand at the heart of the wastes, haunted by restless draenei spirits and contested by ethereals, demons, arakkoa, and the Shadow Council. The Alliance holds Allerian Stronghold, built by high elves and named in honor of Alleria Windrunner, while the Horde holds Stonebreaker Hold. Fel orcs, blood elves loyal to Kael'thas, and Shadow Council warlocks also lurk in the forest.

3520.name: Shadowmoon Valley

3743.name: Legion Hold
3743.description: Legion Hold is the main stronghold of the Burning Legion in Outland, a giant factory in western Shadowmoon Valley where fel reavers and infernals are built to swell the Legion's ranks. It is ruled by a powerful eredar who receives orders from a superior commander through a magical device, and it is filled with doomguards, mo'arg engineers, shivarra, pit lords, and fel orcs loyal to the Legion. The hold's spiked towers and fel fires make it one of the most dangerous places in Outland.

3744.name: Shadowmoon Village
3744.description: Shadowmoon Village is a Horde settlement in northwestern Shadowmoon Valley, defended by Kor'kron guards, the elite guards of the Warchief himself. It is a relatively recent settlement: the Shadowmoon clan once dwelt elsewhere, and in the days of the war against the draenei this was a simple grove marked by a few Shadowmoon pillars. It was here, after the Second War, that the death knight Teron Gorefiend came to see the elder shaman Ner'zhul. It has an inn and a wind rider master, and its warriors fight the infernals that regularly crash against its walls; the orcs here may be among the last uncorrupted members of the Shadowmoon clan.

3745.name: Wildhammer Stronghold
3745.description: Wildhammer Stronghold is an Alliance keep in western Shadowmoon Valley, founded shortly before Draenor's destruction by Kurdran Wildhammer, one of the heroes of the Alliance Expedition who sealed the Dark Portal from Draenor. The dwarven keep was built over ancestral burial grounds sacred to the orcish Shadowmoon clan, and the spirits of departed Shadowmoon orcs still haunt the land around it. Its sturdy walls and gryphon roosts stand defiant amid the blasted land, and its gryphon riders strike against the Legion and Illidan's forces.

3746.name: The Hand of Gul'dan
3746.description: The Hand of Gul'dan is a massive volcano at the center of Shadowmoon Valley, west of the Black Temple, spewing molten green fel lava. It is named after the warlock Gul'dan, who aided Medivh in opening the Dark Portal, and according to the shamans of the Earthen Ring, it was raised by Gul'dan himself when he severed the bond between the orcish people and the elemental spirits of Draenor. The volcano dominates the landscape, and its elementals rage with pain.

3747.name: The Fel Pits
3747.description: The Fel Pits are a series of fetid and scalding pools lining the western base of the Hand of Gul'dan in central Shadowmoon Valley. Tainted and enraged earth and fire elementals roam the area, and the pools bubble with molten fel lava.

3748.name: The Deathforge
3748.description: The Deathforge is a mine shaft and infernal production site in central Shadowmoon Valley, run by the Shadow Council. Infernals are forged here for the Burning Legion, and the air is thick with smoke and fel energy.

3749.name: Coilskar Cistern
3749.description: Coilskar Cistern is a water-lined cave system in northern Shadowmoon Valley, controlled by the naga of Illidan. Its waters are home to elementals, and its walls are rich in ore.

3750.name: Coilskar Point
3750.description: Coilskar Point is a draenei ruin in northern Shadowmoon Valley, infested by the Coilskar naga and ruled by a naga sorceress. The naga serve Illidan.

3752.name: Illidari Point
3752.description: Illidari Point is a staging ground for Illidan's loyal demons in western Shadowmoon Valley, built among draenei ruins whose original name has been lost to time.

3753.name: Ruins of Baa'ri
3753.description: The Ruins of Baa'ri are draenei ruins just northeast of the Hand of Gul'dan in central Shadowmoon Valley, once the home of a sect of draenei priests closely tied to the Temple of Karabor. They are now populated by Broken and elekks in service to Illidan.

3754.name: Altar of Sha'tar
3754.description: The Altar of Sha'tar is a temple in northern Shadowmoon Valley controlled by the Aldor, the draenei priesthood of Shattrath, who use it as a staging ground for their war against Illidan. The tolerance shown in Shattrath does not extend here, and the Aldor attack those who favor the Scryers on sight. The temple has an inn, merchants, and a flight master.

3756.name: Ruins of Karabor
3756.description: The Ruins of Karabor are the southern part of the ancient temple complex of Karabor, lying outside the massive gates of the Black Temple in eastern Shadowmoon Valley. They are filled with blood elves and doomguards in service to Illidan, and it is here that blood elves are trained as demon hunters.

3757.name: Ata'mal Terrace
3757.description: Ata'mal Terrace is the northern of the two sections of the Black Temple that lie outside its massive gates in eastern Shadowmoon Valley. It is filled with fel orcs and drakonid in service to Illidan.

3758.name: Netherwing Fields
3758.description: The Netherwing Fields are crystal-studded plains in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley, just southwest of the Black Temple, home to many nether drakes and nether dragons of the Netherwing. Great crystals rise from the ground, glowing with otherworldly light.

3759.name: Netherwing Ledge
3759.description: Netherwing Ledge is a huge floating island in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley, populated by Dragonmaw fel orcs and the nether drakes they have enslaved. Mines dot its western tip, and the orcs have built fortified camps.

3821.name: Warden's Cage
3821.description: The Warden's Cage is a prison west of the Black Temple in Shadowmoon Valley, run by Illidan's Broken servitors. It is said that the warden Maiev Shadowsong, who long held Illidan prisoner and pursued him across the world, is now held captive here.

3822.name: Eclipse Point
3822.description: Eclipse Point is a draenei ruin in southern Shadowmoon Valley controlled by the Eclipsion, blood elves loyal to Illidan, who are hostile to everyone. The ruins are filled with a deep blood-red haze, in sharp contrast to the black and green elsewhere in the valley.

3840.name: The Black Temple
3840.description: The Black Temple is the fortress-citadel of Illidan Stormrage, the self-proclaimed Lord of Outland, in eastern Shadowmoon Valley. It was once the Temple of Karabor, the most sacred site of the draenei and the refuge of the Prophet Velen, until the Horde stormed it during its war against the draenei and the temple became the seat of Gul'dan's Shadow Council, while Hellfire Citadel served as the Horde's military capital. After Draenor was torn apart, the Burning Legion held it under the pit lord Magtheridon, until Illidan ousted him and claimed his throne. Its massive walls, towering spires, and great gates loom over the blasted land, guarded by Illidan's most loyal servants: blood elves, naga, Broken, demons, and fel orcs. It is one of the most formidable fortresses in Outland.

3926.name: Shattered Plains
3926.description: The Shattered Plains are a ravager-infested ledge in northern Shadowmoon Valley, a broken expanse of black rock overlooking the valley.

3927.name: Oronok's Farm
3927.description: Oronok's Farm is a simple boar farm atop a mountain northeast of Coilskar Point in northern Shadowmoon Valley, home to an old orc who lives apart from the conflicts of the valley. Domesticated felboars root around the farm.

3928.name: The Altar of Damnation
3928.description: The Altar of Damnation is a site near the Fel Pits on the southwestern side of the Hand of Gul'dan in Shadowmoon Valley, where a vision repeatedly appears depicting Gul'dan severing the orcs' connection to the elemental spirits of Draenor, shattering the land and tearing from it by force the raw energy the elements would not give willingly, to use in the war against the draenei. The remnants of his malice, hate, greed, pride, and corruption are said to linger around the altar.

3929.name: The Path of Conquest
3929.description: The Path of Conquest is a long road that switchbacks through the mountains of southern Shadowmoon Valley, heavily entrenched by blood elves and colossi in service to Illidan.

3930.name: Eclipsion Fields
3930.description: The Eclipsion Fields are a colossus-infested ledge in southern Shadowmoon Valley, near Eclipse Point.

3932.name: Sketh'lon Base Camp
3932.description: The Sketh'lon Base Camp is a camp southeast of the Wildhammer Stronghold in southwestern Shadowmoon Valley, filled with the roaming ghosts of the arakkoa of the Dark Conclave who once lived there.

3933.name: Sketh'lon Wreckage
3933.description: The Sketh'lon Wreckage is an area southeast of Shadowmoon Village in northwestern Shadowmoon Valley, filled with the roaming ghosts of the arakkoa of the Dark Conclave who once lived there.

3936.name: Deathforge Tower
3936.description: Deathforge Tower is a small spire overlooking the Deathforge in central Shadowmoon Valley, held by Wildhammer dwarves who watch the Shadow Council's infernal production below.

3937.name: Slag Watch
3937.description: Slag Watch is a small spire overlooking the Deathforge in central Shadowmoon Valley, held by orcs of the Horde who watch the Shadow Council's infernal production below.

3938.name: Sanctum of the Stars
3938.description: The Sanctum of the Stars is a base of the Scryers in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley, the blood elves of Shattrath who serve the naaru and wage war against Illidan. Those who favor the Aldor are not welcome here. It has an inn, merchants, and a flight master.

3939.name: Dragonmaw Fortress
3939.description: Dragonmaw Fortress is a large fort in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley, full of Dragonmaw fel orcs who have enslaved the nether drakes of the nearby Netherwing Fields as mounts. The fortress is a brutal and dangerous place.

3940.name: The Fetid Pool
3940.description: The Fetid Pool is a sickly green lake in the hills near Legion Hold in western Shadowmoon Valley, populated by fleshbeasts and the site of a sunken fel reaver.

3943.name: Invasion Point: Cataclysm
3943.description: Invasion Point: Cataclysm is a staging ground of the Burning Legion in the mountains of northwestern Shadowmoon Valley, where demons arrive to reinforce the Legion's armies.

3944.name: The Altar of Shadows
3944.description: The Altar of Shadows is a dark altar on the southern edge of Shadowmoon Valley, opposite Netherwing Ledge, said to be the prison of the infamous death knight Teron Gorefiend. Shadowy energy gathers around it.

3945.name: Netherwing Pass
3945.description: The Netherwing Pass is a cut through the mountains south of the Sanctum of the Stars in Shadowmoon Valley, leading to the Altar of Shadows.

3947.name: The Scalding Pools
3947.description: The Scalding Pools are steaming pools in Shadowmoon Valley, heated by the fel-tainted fires beneath the earth. Their waters bubble and hiss, and the air around them is thick with acrid vapor.

3949.name: Magma Fields
3949.description: The Magma Fields are plains filled with green-glowing lava pools in western Shadowmoon Valley, populated by felfire diemetradons.

3950.name: Crimson Watch
3950.description: Crimson Watch is a small blood elf base overseeing the Path of Conquest in southern Shadowmoon Valley, held by the Crimson Sigil, the elite blood elf guards of Illidan. It is said that a high general of the Sha'tar is held prisoner here.

3965.name: Netherwing Mines
3965.description: The Netherwing Mines are a vast dig site on the western tip of Netherwing Ledge in Shadowmoon Valley, worked by Dragonmaw fel orc miners, but recently overrun by rock flayers and oozes.

3966.name: Dragonmaw Base Camp
3966.description: The Dragonmaw Base Camp is a fortified area on the southwestern part of Netherwing Ledge in Shadowmoon Valley, densely populated by Dragonmaw fel orcs.

3967.name: Dragonmaw Skyway
3967.description: The Dragonmaw Skyway is the gap between Dragonmaw Fortress and Netherwing Ledge in Shadowmoon Valley, through which Dragonmaw riders fly on their enslaved nether drakes.

3520.description: Shadowmoon Valley is a grim, blasted land in southeastern Outland, lying east of Terokkar Forest, a spectacle of demonic magic run amok. Day and night, molten fel energy erupts from the land and lights the sky with bilious green flame; the ground is black rock and ash with little vegetation, and the great volcano known as the Hand of Gul'dan, raised when the warlock Gul'dan severed the orcs' bond with the elements, dominates its center, spewing green lava. The valley gave its name to Ner'zhul's Shadowmoon clan, and its northern shore was once called the Skeletal Coast. In the east stands the Black Temple, once the draenei Temple of Karabor, now the fortress-citadel of Illidan Stormrage, the self-proclaimed Lord of Outland, and his Illidari: blood elves, naga, Broken, demons, and fel orcs. Illidan and his allies struggle to hold off the reinforcements of the Burning Legion, which has built the great factory of Legion Hold in the west. The Dragonmaw fel orcs hold a fortress in the southeast, where they enslave the nether drakes of the Netherwing. Yet the forces of light have followed: the Wildhammer dwarves of Kurdran Wildhammer, a hero of the Alliance Expedition, hold the Wildhammer Stronghold, the Horde holds Shadowmoon Village, and the Aldor and the Scryers maintain bases from which they wage war on Illidan in the name of the naaru. Somewhere near the temple, Illidan's former jailor is said to be held captive.

3521.name: Zangarmarsh

3565.name: Cenarion Refuge
3565.description: Cenarion Refuge is a settlement of the Cenarion Expedition on the eastern edge of Zangarmarsh, near the border with Hellfire Peninsula. It was originally founded by druids of the Cenarion Circle who came to Outland to study the local flora and fauna, and their presence grew so large that they formed the Cenarion Expedition. The refuge is neutral and welcomes travelers of all races, and its druids work to protect the marsh from those who would drain or destroy it.

3640.name: Daggerfen Village
3640.description: Daggerfen Village is a village of the Lost Ones, draenei who have degenerated into a primitive state, in northwestern Zangarmarsh. Its crude huts stand on stilts above the swamp, and its inhabitants are hostile to outsiders.

3641.name: Umbrafen Village
3641.description: Umbrafen Village is a village of the Lost Ones in southeastern Zangarmarsh, a cluster of crude dwellings built among the giant mushrooms. The Lost Ones here are hostile and attack those who come near.

3642.name: Feralfen Village
3642.description: Feralfen Village is a village of the Lost Ones in southern Zangarmarsh, built around the ancient Boha'mu Ruins. The Lost Ones here have turned to the worship of animal spirits, and they are hostile to most outsiders, though the draenei hope to bring them back to the Light. Despite their primitive ways, they are not easily fooled.

3643.name: Bloodscale Enclave
3643.description: The Bloodscale Enclave is a region by Marshlight Lake in northwestern Zangarmarsh, infested by the naga of Illidan's armies. A great steam pump stands nearby, draining the waters of the marsh. The naga guard the enclave fiercely.

3644.name: Telredor
3644.description: Telredor is a draenei fortress built atop a giant mushroom on an island of the Zangar Sea in eastern Zangarmarsh, reached by a long floating elevator. For centuries it was a quiet monastery, a retreat for draenei anchorites and spiritualists who tended shrines throughout the marsh, but when the orcs marched on Shattrath, civilians fled here, and the retreat became a refuge for many of their people and proved an impregnable fortress. The draenei here followed Velen in joining the Alliance, and members of other Alliance races have come to study the marsh. Food is scarce, and the draenei share what they have among their own people.

3645.name: Zabra'jin
3645.description: Zabra'jin is a large troll town in western Zangarmarsh, allied with the Horde, its huts connected to giant mushrooms and wooden platforms holding buildings above the swamp. The trolls here have adapted well to the marsh, and a wind rider master connects the town with the other Horde holdings in Outland.

3646.name: Quagg Ridge
3646.description: Quagg Ridge is a ridge in southwestern Zangarmarsh, the home of numerous fungal giants, enormous creatures of living fungus. The giants are territorial and attack anyone who comes near.

3647.name: The Spawning Glen
3647.description: The Spawning Glen is a glen in deep southwestern Zangarmarsh where the sporelings have reared their young for millennia. Recently, the starving fungal giants have begun attacking and consuming the helpless young sporelings, and the peaceful mushroom people are desperate for help.

3648.name: The Dead Mire
3648.description: The Dead Mire is a large dead area in northeastern Zangarmarsh, once a lake that served as a spawning ground for the fungal giants. It has been almost completely drained by the naga of Coilfang Reservoir using a huge pump, and the remaining wildlife has become twisted and withered, crazed for lack of sustenance. The cracked mud and dying mushrooms are a grim sign of the marsh's fate if the draining continues.

3649.name: Sporeggar
3649.description: Sporeggar is a town along the western edge of Zangarmarsh populated by the sporelings, a mostly peaceful race of sapient mushroom people native to Outland. Their homes are built among the giant mushrooms, and they live in harmony with the marsh. The changing climate of the marsh has put them in danger, and they welcome those who would help them survive.

3650.name: Ango'rosh Grounds
3650.description: The Ango'rosh Grounds are an area of northwestern Zangarmarsh infested by the Ango'rosh ogres, who are cutting down the giant mushrooms for their own needs. The ogres are brutal and hostile to all.

3651.name: Ango'rosh Stronghold
3651.description: The Ango'rosh Stronghold is a floating island fortress in northwestern Zangarmarsh, held by the Ango'rosh ogres. It can be reached on land by crossing a huge mushroom that has fallen onto the island, forming a bridge. The ogres guard it fiercely.

3652.name: Funggor Cavern
3652.description: Funggor Cavern is a large cavern in southeastern Zangarmarsh, home to the sporeloks. The cavern is being invaded by marsh beasts led by a powerful creature, and the sporeloks appear to be losing the fight.

3653.name: Serpent Lake
3653.description: Serpent Lake is a large lake in northern Zangarmarsh, the largest in Outland. At its center lies Coilfang Reservoir, the great pumping station of the naga, whose machinery is draining the waters of the marsh. The lake is beautiful but ominous.

3654.name: The Drain
3654.description: The Drain is the great pumping works of the naga in northern Zangarmarsh, where the waters of the marsh are sucked away by the machinery of Coilfang Reservoir. The surrounding lakes and pools are shrinking, and the land around the pumps is drying and dying.

3655.name: Umbrafen Lake
3655.description: Umbrafen Lake is a large lake in southeastern Zangarmarsh, its waters glowing faintly with the light of the marsh's luminous creatures. Giant mushrooms rise around its shores.

3656.name: Marshlight Lake
3656.description: Marshlight Lake is a vast lake in western Zangarmarsh, its waters shimmering with the soft light of the marsh. A ruined demonic portal stands on its western bank, and the naga have built a pump nearby.

3657.name: Portal Clearing
3657.description: The Portal Clearing is a clearing on the western bank of Marshlight Lake in Zangarmarsh, the site of one of the dimensional gateways that the pit lord Magtheridon once used to bring demons from the Twisting Nether into Outland. Illidan shut down the gateways, cutting off the flow of demons, and the portal now stands inactive.

3658.name: Sporewind Lake
3658.description: Sporewind Lake is a large lake in southwestern Zangarmarsh, surrounded by giant mushrooms and drifting spores. Its waters glow faintly in the twilight.

3659.name: The Lagoon
3659.description: The Lagoon is a large lake in south-central Zangarmarsh, its waters calm and luminous. Naga lurk along its shores.

3660.name: Blades' Run
3660.description: Blades' Run is a sloping ridge leading down from a cave in the southern Blade's Edge Mountains to northeastern Zangarmarsh, a path between the jagged mountains and the luminous marsh.

3661.name: Blade Tooth Canyon
3661.description: Blade Tooth Canyon is a sloping ridge leading down from a cave in the southwestern Blade's Edge Mountains to Orebor Harborage in Zangarmarsh. The path winds between steep rocks.

3667.name: Hewn Bog
3667.description: Hewn Bog is a region in western Zangarmarsh northwest of Zabra'jin, infested by ogres. It is so named because the ogres have chopped down all the great mushrooms, leaving behind only hewn stumps. The destruction has deprived the fungal giants of their food, driving them to madness.

3668.name: Boha'mu Ruins
3668.description: The Boha'mu Ruins are an abandoned draenei temple in southern Zangarmarsh, near Feralfen Village, now inhabited by Lost Ones. The temple's crumbling walls are overgrown with fungi.

3718.name: Swamprat Post
3718.description: Swamprat Post is a troll fishing village in northeastern Zangarmarsh, allied with the Horde. Its huts stand on stilts above the water, and a wind rider master connects it with the other Horde holdings.

3720.name: Twin Spire Ruins
3720.description: The Twin Spire Ruins are the remains of a holy draenei site in central Zangarmarsh, a burial ground flanked by two small ruined buildings, with a single broken tower at its center. The Alliance and the Horde fight for control of the two outer structures, and whoever holds both can carry their battle standard into the graveyard between them. Despite the battles fought there, the ruins remain a solemn place.

3766.name: Orebor Harborage
3766.description: Orebor Harborage is a village in northern Zangarmarsh populated mostly by the Kurenai, Broken draenei who seek to reestablish their ties with their uncorrupted kin and who have allied themselves with the Alliance. In ages past the village was a center of draenei learning and trade, and it is said that Akama and Maiev Shadowsong once met here to speak of Illidan.
