4149.description: The D.E.H.T.A. Encampment is a camp of the Druids for the Ethical and Humane Treatment of Animals in the central Borean Tundra, southeast of Lake Kum'uya. The druids here oppose overhunting, and a bonfire in the shape of a famous dwarven hunter burns at the center of their camp.

4150.name: Kaw's Roost
4150.description: Kaw's Roost is a small rise in the Borean Tundra where a mighty tuskarr warrior, renowned as a mammoth hunter, keeps watch over the plains.

4269.name: Shrine of Scales
4269.description: The Shrine of Scales is a naga shrine dedicated to Queen Azshara on the Riplash Strand in the southern Borean Tundra. The invading kvaldir have overrun it, killing or enslaving most of the naga within.

4399.name: Farshire Mine
4399.description: The Farshire Mine is a mine near the town hall in the northern part of Farshire in the Borean Tundra, which once supplied ore to Valiance Keep. It has fallen to the Scourge.

4401.name: Saragosa's Landing
4401.description: Saragosa's Landing is a floating platform high in the sky above the Borean Tundra, where a great blue dragon of Malygos's flight is said to have met her end.

4639.name: Band of Variance
4639.description: The Band of Variance is the lowest of the floating rings of the Oculus, the great arcane structure that orbits above the Nexus on Coldarra. It is where visitors arrive and depart, and the blue dragonflight holds captives here.

4640.name: Band of Acceleration
4640.description: The Band of Acceleration is the second of the floating rings of the Oculus above the Nexus, a level of arcane platforms guarded by the servants of the blue dragonflight.

4641.name: Band of Transmutation
4641.description: The Band of Transmutation is the ring just beneath the top of the Oculus above the Nexus, where a powerful mage lord serves the blue dragonflight.

4642.name: Band of Alignment
4642.description: The Band of Alignment is the uppermost ring of the Oculus above the Nexus, where a great guardian of the ley lines patrols the skies on behalf of Malygos.

3537.description: The Borean Tundra is a vast, wind-swept plain on the southwestern edge of Northrend, the flattest part of the continent and, for many, the first land they see when they arrive to wage war against the Lich King. It is a cold, open expanse of red-brown earth, lichen, and ice, where the wind can almost strip the beard from a dwarf's face and few trees survive. In the south, the soil is hard but farmable; steaming geysers and hot springs bubble in the middle; cliffs shear off into the Westrift along the western edge; and the snowy east is the harshest of all. Mammoths, woolly rhinos, and wolves roam the plains, and whales and countless fish fill the coastal waters. The tuskarr, peaceful walrus-folk who live by fishing and whaling, are the region's native people, though their capital of Kaskala and the village of Pal'ea have been ravaged by the kvaldir, cursed vrykul raiders from the sea. Off the western coast rises the island of Coldarra, home of Malygos and the blue dragonflight, whose Nexus War against the mages of the world has spilled into the tundra. The Scourge holds the temple city of En'kilah and its floating necropolis in the northeast, the naga and kvaldir fight over the southern ruins, and magnataur roam the plains. The Alliance's Valiance Expedition holds Valiance Keep in the southwest, and the Horde's Warsong Offensive, led by Garrosh Hellscream, holds the great fortress of Warsong Hold. The taunka, ancient cousins of the tauren, have been found here as well.

3540.name: Twisting Nether
3540.description: The Twisting Nether is the chaotic, astral realm that lies between worlds, an ethereal dimension of wild magic that connects the myriad worlds of the universe and is home to the demons of the Burning Legion. When Ner'zhul's portals tore Draenor apart, the shattered remnants that became Outland were pulled into the Nether, and at the edges of Outland the land simply ends, giving way to an endless void of prismatic clouds, twisting ribbons of colored energy, and drifting fragments of rock. The sky glows with strange greens, purples, and blues, and distant worlds, among them Azeroth and Draenor's lost moon, can be glimpsed in the swirling heavens. Physical laws seem uncertain here, and the mind strains to make sense of what the eye beholds. Few mortals dare venture beyond the edges of Outland, for those who stray too far may never return, and the demons who dwell in the Nether are never far away.

3557.name: The Exodar
3557.description: The Exodar is the capital of the draenei, built within the largest intact section of the dimensional ship of the same name, which crashed on the western coast of Azuremyst Isle. Originally a satellite structure of the naaru fortress Tempest Keep, the ship was seized in Outland by the Prophet Velen and his followers, aided by the naaru and the Broken shaman Nobundo, in a daring escape from the blood elves who had captured the fortress. The blood elves sabotaged its engines, and the ship hurtled uncontrolled through the Twisting Nether until it crashed onto the Azuremyst Isles, scattering its wreckage and crystals across the land. The survivors made the ship their new home, and the Exodar is now a city of wonder, filled with gleaming crystalline halls, glowing conduits that carry holy energy throughout the structure to provide light and warmth, and the advanced technology of the naaru. Its great central chamber, the Crystal Hall, is surrounded by wings including the Seat of the Naaru, where Velen resides alongside a naaru, the Vault of Lights, and the Trader's Tier. The draenei, having joined the Alliance, welcome their new allies, and the city hums with the harmonious song of the naaru and the quiet devotion of a people who have wandered for thousands of years.

3703.name: Shattrath City

3896.name: Aldor Rise
3896.description: Aldor Rise is the terrace of Shattrath City that serves as the seat of the Aldor, the ancient draenei priesthood who served the naaru long before the Scryers came. Its elegant draenei buildings, crowned by the Shrine of Unending Light, house an inn, merchants, and the Aldor's priests and vindicators. The Aldor resent the presence of the Scryers, and those who favor the Scryers are not welcome here. The rise is reached by a long lift from the Terrace of Light.

3897.name: Terrace of Light
3897.description: The Terrace of Light is the heart of Shattrath City, where the naaru A'dal, leader of the Sha'tar, hovers above a great courtyard bathed in radiant light. The Archmage Khadgar also resides here, and portals created by him connect the city with the capitals of Azeroth. The terrace is defended by the Shattered Sun Offensive, and it is the gathering place for pilgrims, soldiers, and travelers of every race. The song of the naaru fills the air with peace.

3898.name: Scryer's Tier
3898.description: Scryer's Tier is the terrace of Shattrath City that serves as the base of the Scryers, the blood elves who broke away from Kael'thas Sunstrider and swore to serve the naaru. At its center stands the Seer's Library, the faction's headquarters, and the tier also has an inn and merchants. The Scryers are bitter rivals of the Aldor, and those who favor the Aldor are not welcome here. The tier's architecture blends draenei stone with blood elven grace.

3899.name: Lower City
3899.description: The Lower City is the sprawling lower district of Shattrath City, where refugees from every conflict in Outland have gathered. Arakkoa, sporelings, Broken draenei, orcs, ogres, ethereals, humans, and many others live here side by side, building shelters among the ancient draenei ruins, a coalition of peoples home to a dozen different faiths. It is a crowded, lively place of markets, workshops, and the World's End Tavern, and those who help the refugees quickly earn their gratitude. Despite its poverty, the Lower City is filled with hope.

3703.description: Shattrath City, the City of Light, is an ancient draenei city in the northwestern part of Terokkar Forest, now a great sanctuary for refugees of every race in Outland. Its name means dwelling of light in the draenei tongue, and it was once the draenei capital on Draenor, where the fiercest battle against the demon-corrupted orcs was fought; the city fell and lay in ruins and darkness. Then the Sha'tar, naaru born from light, arrived and joined the remnant of the draenei priesthood, the Aldor, and the city was rebuilt. When Kael'thas Sunstrider sent his blood elves to destroy it, a regiment of them laid down their arms and swore to serve the naaru; they became the Scryers, and though they share the city with the Aldor, the two factions remain bitter rivals. Today Shattrath is ruled by the naaru A'dal from the Terrace of Light, where the Archmage Khadgar, the legendary hero of the Alliance Expedition, also resides. The Lower City is crowded with refugees of every race: draenei, Broken, arakkoa, sporelings, orcs, humans, ogres, ethereals, and more. The city is a sanctuary where violence between the Alliance and the Horde is forbidden, and portals created by Khadgar connect it with the capitals of Azeroth. Its towering walls, golden domes, and the radiant light of the naaru make it a beacon of hope in a shattered world.

3711.name: Sholazar Basin

4282.name: The Avalanche
4282.description: The Avalanche is an area in northeastern Sholazar Basin, formed when the Lifeblood Pillar fell and the snows of Icecrown collapsed down into the basin. It has become the Scourge's pathway into Sholazar, its snows patrolled by flesh giants and abominations descending from the Scourge's works high above in Icecrown.

4283.name: The Lost Lands
4283.description: The Lost Lands are a large blighted area covering much of eastern Sholazar Basin, spreading out from the Avalanche and the fallen Lifeblood Pillar. The land is dying, the air is fouled with a yellow haze, and the ground is thick with undead. The gorloc village that once stood here has been abandoned, its people fled or slain. The Avatar of Freya fights ceaselessly to contain the spread of the blight.

4284.name: Nesingwary Base Camp
4284.description: Nesingwary Base Camp is the camp of the famous hunter Hemet Nesingwary and his safari in western Sholazar Basin, just north of the Seabreach Flow. It stands where his ship ended up after crashing through the river's mouth from the sea; he believed the Seabreach Flow would make a fine route inland and found out too late that he was wrong. Now his hunters use the camp as their base for hunting the basin's great beasts.

4285.name: The Seabreach Flow
4285.description: The Seabreach Flow is a river flowing from the sea in the west through a breach in the mountains to River's Heart at the center of Sholazar Basin. The wreckage of Hemet Nesingwary's ship is strewn along its path, and its waters are full of crocolisks.

4286.name: The Bones of Nozronn
4286.description: The Bones of Nozronn are the remains of an ancient rhino in Sholazar Basin, revered by the gorlocs, who keep a shrine in his honor and believe that, with the right incense, his spirit will still answer the questions of those who seek him.

4287.name: Kartak's Hold
4287.description: Kartak's Hold is an outpost of the Frenzyheart wolvar in the far southwestern corner of Sholazar Basin, where they worship Kartak the Abominable and wage constant war against the gorlocs of Sparktouched Haven.

4288.name: Sparktouched Haven
4288.description: Sparktouched Haven is an outpost of the gorloc Oracles just west of the Mosslight Pillar in southwestern Sholazar Basin, constantly at war with the Frenzyheart wolvar of Kartak's Hold.

4289.name: The Path of the Lifewarden
4289.description: The Path of the Lifewarden is an ancient road that encircles Sholazar Basin and its pillars. It was likely once continuous, but the wear of millennia and the flow of water have broken it in many places.

4290.name: River's Heart
4290.description: River's Heart is a small lake at the center of Sholazar Basin, lying below sea level and surrounded by cliffs, where all four rivers of the basin meet and pour down high waterfalls. Lakeside Landing lies on its northeastern shore. Sea creatures washed in from the rivers infest the lake, and no one knows where all the water flowing into it goes; some say the titans made it so for a reason.

4291.name: Rainspeaker Canopy
4291.description: Rainspeaker Canopy is a gorloc village northeast of River's Heart within the Wildgrowth Mangal of Sholazar Basin, the home of the Oracles. They live in little elevated houses, open-sided to catch the cool breezes and thatched with leaves against the rain, and they hang wind chimes tipped with crystal fragments from the pillars in their trees.

4292.name: Frenzyheart Hill
4292.description: Frenzyheart Hill is the village of the Frenzyheart wolvar in Sholazar Basin, a cluster of their typical low, round dwellings atop the hill named after them. They founded it after the Scourge drove them from their old lands, and they are at war with the gorloc Oracles.

4293.name: Wildgrowth Mangal
4293.description: The Wildgrowth Mangal is the dense jungle spreading across central Sholazar Basin, northwest of River's Heart, between the Suntouched Pillar and Rainspeaker Canopy. Shot through with small streams, its trees heavy with fruit, it is home to many dangerous reptiles, among them emperor cobras and great crocolisks.

4295.name: The Sundered Shard
4295.description: The Sundered Shard is the glowing red crystal top of the Lifeblood Pillar in Sholazar Basin, the pillar's heart, blasted off when the Cult of the Damned blew up the pillar with explosives. It lies amid the Lost Lands, surrounded by crystal elementals and the minions of the Scourge.

4296.name: The Lifeblood Pillar
4296.description: The Lifeblood Pillar was one of the great titan pylons that protected Sholazar Basin, in the east of the basin. The Cult of the Damned sabotaged it, and when it fell, the snows of Icecrown collapsed into the basin and opened a path for the Scourge. Half of the broken pillar lies on its side, the titan machine at its apex in wreckage on the ground, and the Scourge has cut a mine into it to take its red crystal heart.

4297.name: Mosswalker Village
4297.description: Mosswalker Village is the ravaged village of the gorloc Mosswalker tribe in the Lost Lands of Sholazar Basin, south of the Avalanche. When the Lifeblood Pillar fell and the Scourge invaded, all its residents fled or were killed.

4300.name: Waygate
4300.description: The Waygate is an ancient titan device in Sholazar Basin, a gateway made to carry travelers between distant places. It is said to link the basin with another of the titans' cradles of life far to the south, but it has lain dormant for centuries.

4302.name: The Skyreach Pillar
4302.description: The Skyreach Pillar is one of the titan pylons of southeastern Sholazar Basin, a tall, narrow butte rising from the basin floor with a thin, elongated device hovering above it, swirling with magic. Blue crystals grow from its sides, and the Frenzyheart wolvar live in its shadow.

4303.name: Hardknuckle Clearing
4303.description: Hardknuckle Clearing is a flat patch of dirt along the southeastern edge of Sholazar Basin, marked by a great tree stump, where gorillas roam under the watchful eye of a hidden matriarch.

4304.name: Sapphire Hive
4304.description: The Sapphire Hive is a large hive south of Frenzyheart Hill in Sholazar Basin, home to a colony of huge blue-hued wasps and their queen.

4306.name: Mistwhisper Refuge
4306.description: Mistwhisper Refuge is an outpost of the gorloc Oracles on the northern bank of Bittertide Lake in northwestern Sholazar Basin, not far from the Frenzyheart wolvar of the Spearborn Encampment.

4307.name: The Glimmering Pillar
4307.description: The Glimmering Pillar is one of the titan pylons of northern Sholazar Basin, a tall, narrow butte with a hovering device swirling with magic. It is covered with white crystals, and flower-headed servants of Freya sit upon its flat top. The Cult of the Damned has tried to destroy it as it did the Lifeblood Pillar.

4308.name: Spearborn Encampment
4308.description: The Spearborn Encampment is an outpost of the Frenzyheart wolvar in northwestern Sholazar Basin, not far from the gorlocs of Mistwhisper Refuge.

4367.name: The Blight Line
4367.description: The Blight Line is the border running down the eastern third of Sholazar Basin, separating the blighted Lost Lands from the living jungle, where the Avatar of Freya holds back the Scourge.

4368.name: The Bonefields
4368.description: The Bonefields are an area of Sholazar Basin strewn with the bones of dead creatures, the hunting ground of great rocs and their matriarch.

4369.name: Dorian's Outpost
4369.description: Dorian's Outpost is the northern camp of Hemet Nesingwary's safari in Sholazar Basin, just west of the Savage Thicket.

4376.name: The Savage Thicket
4376.description: The Savage Thicket is a section of jungle north of the Glimmering Pillar in Sholazar Basin that burns endlessly with magical fire.

4383.name: Lakeside Landing
4383.description: Lakeside Landing is a small beach and landing area for flying machines on the northeastern shore of River's Heart in central Sholazar Basin, where gnomish pilots keep their gyrocopters.

4385.name: Bittertide Lake
4385.description: Bittertide Lake is a brackish lake in northwestern Sholazar Basin near the Glimmering Pillar, fed by a river flowing in from the sea and inhabited by hydras. When it overfills, its water crashes down the Bittertide Falls toward River's Heart. The gorloc village of Mistwhisper Refuge lies on its northern bank.

4386.name: Rainspeaker Rapids
4386.description: The Rainspeaker Rapids are a series of waterfalls flowing from the Avalanche down to River's Heart in Sholazar Basin, where the Avatar of Freya fights constantly against the invading Scourge.

4387.name: Frenzyheart River
4387.description: The Frenzyheart River flows from Wintergrasp past the fallen Lifeblood Pillar and Frenzyheart Hill, merging with the Rainspeaker Rapids before ending at River's Heart in Sholazar Basin.

4388.name: Wintergrasp River
4388.description: The Wintergrasp River runs from Wintergrasp into southeastern Sholazar Basin, passing south of the Skyreach Pillar to the southern part of River's Heart.

4389.name: The Suntouched Pillar
4389.description: The Suntouched Pillar is one of the titan pylons of northwestern Sholazar Basin, a tall, narrow butte with a hovering device swirling with magic. Yellow crystals grow from it, and a small pond ripples in the breeze on its top. The Venture Company has dug a strip mine around it to tear out its crystals.

4391.name: Swindlegrin's Dig
4391.description: Swindlegrin's Dig is a Venture Company strip mine on the northwestern side of the Suntouched Pillar in Sholazar Basin, where goblins strip the yellow crystals from the pillar with little thought for the harm they may do to the basin.

4392.name: The Stormwright's Shelf
4392.description: The Stormwright's Shelf is a high ledge above and west of the Makers' Perch in Sholazar Basin, where rain falls almost constantly.

4393.name: Death's Hand Encampment
4393.description: Death's Hand Encampment is a small camp of the Cult of the Damned in northeastern Sholazar Basin, east of the Glimmering Pillar and west of the Lost Lands, their base of operations in the basin.

4400.name: The Mosslight Pillar
4400.description: The Mosslight Pillar is one of the titan pylons of Sholazar Basin, a tall, narrow butte with a hovering device swirling with magic, sprouting green crystals and many ferns.

4412.name: The Makers' Overlook
4412.description: The Makers' Overlook is a titan facility high on the mountains of northeastern Sholazar Basin, reachable only through the air. Its grand entrance leads to halls cut deep into the mountain, where rune-inscribed gears the size of a keep turn slowly in a massive machine whose purpose no one knows. The titans built it as a vantage point from which to watch over their creations in the basin below.

4413.name: The Makers' Perch
4413.description: The Makers' Perch is a lesser titan facility in northwestern Sholazar Basin, its entrance cut into the mountain wall at the level of the basin floor. A short hall ends in great arched windows looking out over the sea, and titan constructs still guard its empty halls.

4483.name: The Lost Passage
4483.description: The Lost Passage is a hidden road leading north from the Borean Tundra into southwestern Sholazar Basin, joining the southern circuit of the Path of the Lifewarden.

3711.description: Sholazar Basin is a tropical jungle basin in the midst of Northrend, between the Borean Tundra and Icecrown, ringed by towering mountains. After the bitter cold of the rest of the continent, stepping into it is like stepping onto another world: hot, humid, and teeming with life. When the titans shaped Azeroth, the keeper Freya made Sholazar a cradle of life, a place for experimentation like Un'Goro Crater far to the south, where the power of the Well of Eternity had coalesced. Its warm climate and its protection from foul creatures are maintained by great titan pylons: tall, narrow buttes rising from the basin floor, each crowned with crystals and a hovering device swirling with magic. At the center lies River's Heart, where four rivers meet, surrounded by the dense jungle of the Wildgrowth Mangal, and titan facilities still watch over the basin from the mountainsides. The basin is home to rhinos, gorillas, crocolisks, hydras, and wasps, and to two warring peoples: the Oracles, a gathering of gorloc tribes, and the Frenzyheart wolvar, who came here after the Scourge drove them from their lands. But Sholazar is no longer untouched. The Cult of the Damned sabotaged the Lifeblood Pillar in the east, letting the snows of Icecrown collapse into the basin and the Scourge pour in, and the Avatar of Freya fights ceaselessly to contain the spreading blight. The famous hunter Hemet Nesingwary has made camp here after his ship crashed in, and the Venture Company strips the pillars of their crystals.

3917.name: Auchindoun
3917.description: Auchindoun is the shattered necropolis of the draenei, standing at the heart of the Bone Wastes in southern Terokkar Forest. For thousands of years, it was the most sacred temple of the draenei, the place where they interred their honored dead beneath the earth. During the dark days before the Horde's invasion of Azeroth, the site was also briefly a fortress of the Bleeding Hollow clan. In recent times, agents of the Shadow Council infiltrated the necropolis and summoned an entity of immense evil, an ancient elemental of sound, and the ritual caused a massive explosion that blew the temple apart, laid waste to the surrounding forest, and tore a rift in the Nether itself, drawing the otherworldly ethereals into Outland. The interred draenei now walk the ruins as restless spirits. Its four great halls have been claimed by different powers: ethereals siphon arcane energy from the Mana-Tombs, demons harvest souls in the Auchenai Crypts, arakkoa zealots work dark magic in the Sethekk Halls, and the Shadow Council plots in the Shadow Labyrinth, where it struggles to contain and harness the entity it unleashed. The ruins are haunting and dangerous, their crypts filled with echoes of the dead.

3979.name: The Frozen Sea
3979.description: The Frozen Sea is the great body of water south of Northrend, stretching from its southern coasts toward the Maelstrom; lying between the continents, it is a part of the Great Sea. Its cold, gray waters wash the shores of the Borean Tundra, the Dragonblight, and the Howling Fjord, where pack ice and icebergs drift. Alliance and Horde fleets cross it to reach the continent, tuskarr ride their giant turtles between their coastal villages, and the carved columns of the ancient Path of the Titans rise from its waves. Kvaldir raiders and sea monsters haunt its depths, and its gales are felt as far away as Kul Tiras.

4080.name: Isle of Quel'Danas

4081.name: The Dawnchaser
4081.description: The Dawnchaser is a blood elf destroyer anchored in the waters north of Sun's Reach Harbor on the Isle of Quel'Danas, the northeasternmost of the three warships lying off the coast. Its crimson sails and golden hull, decorated with the graceful ornaments of Quel'Thalas, make it a striking sight on the blue waters of the North Sea. The ship is heavily armed, and the waves slap against its sides as it rides at anchor within sight of the harbor.

4082.name: The Sin'loren
4082.description: The Sin'loren is a blood elf destroyer anchored in the waters north of Sun's Reach Harbor on the Isle of Quel'Danas, the southernmost of the three warships lying off the coast. Built in the elegant style of the elven navy, with crimson sails and golden trim, it is heavily armed with cannons and ballistae. From its decks, the spires of Sun's Reach and the golden forests of the island can be seen across the water.

4083.name: Silvermoon's Pride
4083.description: Silvermoon's Pride is a blood elf destroyer moored at the docks of Sun's Reach Harbor on the Isle of Quel'Danas. It is not yet seaworthy, and its crew works to repair it. The ship's elegant design and golden trim reflect the pride of the blood elf navy.

4084.name: The Bloodoath
4084.description: The Bloodoath is a blood elf destroyer anchored in the waters north of Sun's Reach Harbor on the Isle of Quel'Danas, the northwesternmost of the three warships lying off the coast. Like its sister ships, it bears crimson sails and a golden hull, and it is armed for war. The ship rides at anchor in the cold waters of the North Sea, within sight of the island's harbor.

4085.name: Shattered Sun Staging Area
4085.description: The Shattered Sun Staging Area is a camp just south of Sun's Reach Harbor on the Isle of Quel'Danas, where the Shattered Sun Offensive first landed and began its campaign to retake the island. Recruits train under drill sergeants here, and the Offensive's quartermaster supplies the troops. The camp is a busy place of tents, weapons racks, and soldiers of both the Aldor and the Scryers working side by side.

4086.name: Sun's Reach Sanctum
4086.description: The Sun's Reach Sanctum is an arcane sanctum on the Isle of Quel'Danas, south of Sun's Reach Harbor. Retaken by the Shattered Sun Offensive, it serves as one of the Offensive's main headquarters, and the great astrolabe at its top rotates once more. A portal connects the sanctum with Shattrath City in Outland. Its elegant halls are filled with Aldor and Scryer officers planning the campaign.

4087.name: Sun's Reach Harbor
4087.description: Sun's Reach Harbor is the main harbor of the Isle of Quel'Danas, where ships from the mainland and beyond arrive. It was retaken by the Shattered Sun Offensive from Kael'thas's forces, and its main building now serves as the island's inn. The harbor is busy with soldiers, sailors, and supplies, and blood elf destroyers can be seen in the waters beyond.

4088.name: Sun's Reach Armory
4088.description: The Sun's Reach Armory is a building on the Isle of Quel'Danas, on the east side of the square near the Sun's Reach Sanctum. Retaken by the Shattered Sun Offensive, it now supplies the troops with weapons, armor, and provisions, and smiths repair the equipment of the soldiers who fight on the island.

4089.name: Dawnstar Village
4089.description: Dawnstar Village is a village of elegant elven buildings on the Isle of Quel'Danas, standing amid the island's golden forests. It has been at the heart of the fighting on the island, and the Wretched, demons of the Burning Legion, and blood elf soldiers have all been seen in its streets, while a demonic portal once burned nearby. Its gardens are trampled and some of its buildings scarred by battle, yet the village still shows the grace of Quel'Thalas.

4090.name: The Dawning Square
4090.description: The Dawning Square is the central plaza of Sun's Reach on the Isle of Quel'Danas, lying between the Sun's Reach Sanctum and the Sun's Reach Armory. Retaken by the Shattered Sun Offensive, it is now a bustling place where soldiers gather, merchants sell their wares, and officers coordinate the campaign. Its elegant stonework and golden trees recall the beauty of Quel'Thalas.

4091.name: Greengill Coast
4091.description: The Greengill Coast is the southeastern shoreline of the Isle of Quel'Danas, home to the small Greengill murlocs, who have built a village of huts along the shore. The Darkspine naga have invaded the village and their sirens have enslaved the murlocs through mind control, forcing them to do their bidding. The coast is beautiful, but the naga make it dangerous.

4092.name: The Dead Scar
4092.description: On the Isle of Quel'Danas, the Dead Scar resumes at the southern tip of the island and runs about halfway across it toward the Sunwell Plateau, marking the path Arthas and the Scourge took to reach the Sunwell during the Third War. The earth along it is black and lifeless, and nothing grows upon it. In recent times the scar became a battlefield between the remnants of the Scourge and the demons of the Burning Legion, and the land is littered with the signs of their struggle.

4094.name: Sunwell Plateau
4094.description: The Sunwell Plateau is the sacred heart of the Isle of Quel'Danas, where the Sunwell, the great fountain of arcane power created by the founders of Quel'Thalas from the waters of the Well of Eternity, lies within a grand complex of golden walls, courtyards, and spires. For thousands of years the Sunwell was the source of the high elves' power and the soul of their kingdom, until Arthas defiled it when he used its waters to resurrect Kel'Thuzad. In recent times the plateau became the focus of a desperate struggle, as the fallen prince Kael'thas Sunstrider and the Burning Legion sought to use the Sunwell as a gateway for the eredar lord Kil'jaeden to enter Azeroth. To the blood elves, it remains the most sacred place in the world, and the fate of the Sunwell is bound to the fate of their people.

4095.name: Magisters' Terrace
4095.description: The Magisters' Terrace is an elegant complex of walkways, courtyards, gardens, and halls on the northeastern corner of the Isle of Quel'Danas, built in the grand style of Silvermoon for the magisters of Quel'Thalas, who studied and channeled the Sunwell's power here. In recent times it was seized by the fallen prince Kael'thas Sunstrider and his followers, who made it their stronghold on the island during the struggle for the Sunwell. Its beauty, with floating crystals and arcane lights shimmering above the sea, belies the treachery that has taken place within its walls.

4080.description: The Isle of Quel'Danas, also known as the Sunwell Isle, is an island lying off the northern coast of Eversong Woods, separated from the mainland by a channel of the North Sea. Seven thousand years ago, the founders of Quel'Thalas created the Sunwell here, a mystic fountain of immense power at a convergence of ley lines, using water from the Well of Eternity; its energies sustained the elves and their kingdom for millennia. During the Third War, Arthas created a bridge of ice to reach the island and used the Sunwell's waters to resurrect the lich Kel'Thuzad, defiling the fountain and leaving the island to rot. In recent times, the island became the stage of a desperate struggle, as the fallen prince Kael'thas Sunstrider and the Burning Legion sought to use the Sunwell as a gateway for the eredar lord Kil'jaeden. In response, the Sha'tar of Shattrath united the draenei of the Aldor and the blood elves of the Scryers into the Shattered Sun Offensive, which made the harbor town of Sun's Reach its base. The island bears the scars of these battles, from the blighted path of the Dead Scar to the shattered buildings around Dawnstar Village. Naga lurk along the southern coast, where the small Greengill murlocs live, and the island is also home to the aeries where the blood elves breed their dragonhawks. Despite everything, its golden forests, white beaches, and elegant elven spires remain breathtakingly beautiful, and the Sunwell Plateau rises at its heart as the most sacred place of the elven people.

4197.name: Wintergrasp

4538.name: The Sunken Ring
4538.description: The Sunken Ring is an ancient titan ruin in eastern Wintergrasp, near the fortress, where goblin engineers have set up a workshop that builds siege weapons for whoever holds it.

4539.name: The Broken Temple
4539.description: The Broken Temple is an ancient titan temple in western Wintergrasp, now in ruins, where goblin engineers have set up a workshop that builds siege weapons for whoever holds it.

4575.name: Wintergrasp Fortress
4575.description: Wintergrasp Fortress is the great titan fortress at the heart of Wintergrasp, the prize for which the Alliance and the Horde endlessly fight. It is protected by two rings of walls, an outer wall with great gates and an inner wall around the keep, and it guards the entrance to the Vault of Archavon, where titan relics of untold power lie.

4576.name: Central Bridge
4576.description: The Central Bridge is the middle of the three bridges spanning the river in Wintergrasp, where soldiers of the Alliance and the Horde clash on their way to and from the fortress.

4577.name: Eastern Bridge
4577.description: The Eastern Bridge is the easternmost of the three bridges spanning the river in Wintergrasp, a crossing fought over by the armies battling for the fortress.

4578.name: Western Bridge
4578.description: The Western Bridge is the westernmost of the three bridges spanning the river in Wintergrasp, a crossing fought over by the armies battling for the fortress.

4581.name: Flamewatch Tower
4581.description: Flamewatch Tower is a cannon tower in southeastern Wintergrasp, overlooking the Cauldron of Flames, one of the towers that guard the southern approaches to the fortress.

4582.name: Winter's Edge Tower
4582.description: Winter's Edge Tower is a cannon tower in southern Wintergrasp, one of the towers that guard the southern approaches to the fortress.

4583.name: Shadowsight Tower
4583.description: Shadowsight Tower is a cannon tower in southwestern Wintergrasp, overlooking the Forest of Shadows, one of the towers that guard the southern approaches to the fortress.

4584.name: The Cauldron of Flames
4584.description: The Cauldron of Flames is a volcanic area in southeastern Wintergrasp, a fiery basin of molten rock and smoke amid the frozen valley, inhabited by fire elementals.

4585.name: Glacial Falls
4585.description: Glacial Falls is a large lake on a ridge above the Sunken Ring in Wintergrasp, home to water elementals, whose waters flow down into the lower valley.

4587.name: The Forest of Shadows
4587.description: The Forest of Shadows is a dark forest in southwestern Wintergrasp, haunted by shadowy revenants and wandering shades.

4589.name: The Chilled Quagmire
4589.description: The Chilled Quagmire is a watery, frozen marsh in western Wintergrasp, home to water revenants and glacial spirits.

4590.name: The Steppe of Life
4590.description: The Steppe of Life is a grassy area south of the Forest of Shadows in southwestern Wintergrasp, inhabited by lashers that disguise themselves as large flowers and attack anyone who comes too close.

4611.name: Westspark Workshop
4611.description: The Westspark Workshop is a siege workshop in southwestern Wintergrasp, where goblin engineers build siege weapons for whoever holds it.

4612.name: Eastspark Workshop
4612.description: The Eastspark Workshop is a siege workshop in southeastern Wintergrasp, where goblin engineers build siege weapons for whoever holds it.

4197.description: Wintergrasp is a frozen valley in western-central Northrend, lying between Sholazar Basin, the Borean Tundra, the Dragonblight, and Icecrown, raised above the surrounding lands. It was once the bed of a vast lake, Lake Wintergrasp, which has shrunk and left the basin open, revealing ancient titan ruins, dark forests, frozen marshes, lakes, and a volcanic cauldron of fire. At its heart stands Wintergrasp Fortress, a titan complex with domed watchtowers guarding the entrance to the Vault of Archavon, which holds titan relics of untold power, protected by ancient giants who resent all intruders. The valley also contains rich deposits and elemental energies. Since the start of the war against the Lich King, the Alliance and the Horde have fought endlessly for control of the fortress and the vault, and Wintergrasp has become a battlefield where siege engines built in goblin workshops batter the fortress walls and control changes hands again and again.

4201.name: Vordrassil's Tears
4201.description: Vordrassil's Tears is one of the three great segments of the World Tree Vordrassil, lying southwest of the Blue Sky Logging Grounds in the Grizzly Hills. Long ago, the druid Fandral Staghelm planted branches of Nordrassil across Northrend, and the greatest of them, named Andrassil, the Crown of the Snow, towered over these hills for decades. But its roots reached so deep that they touched the prison of an ancient evil, and madness spread among the creatures of the land. The Cenarion Circle had no choice but to destroy the tree, and renamed it Vordrassil, the Broken Crown. Its fallen pieces still lie in the forest, and the land around this segment is covered in living ooze, evidence of the corruption that doomed it.

4258.name: The North Sea
4258.description: The North Sea stretches along the southeastern coasts of Northrend, beyond the shores of the Grizzly Hills and the Howling Fjord, and extends south toward the northern coasts of Lordaeron. Its cold, gray waters are dotted with islands such as Bloodmoon Isle and the Ruins of Tethys, and they are crossed by Alliance and Forsaken ships bound for the fjord's harbors, while vrykul longships and kvaldir raiders prowl the mists.

4395.name: Dalaran

4560.name: The Underbelly
4560.description: The Underbelly is the sewer system of Dalaran, the city's slum, home to many races but mostly goblins. At its heart lies the Circle of Wills, a great hall with dueling circles and an arena. To the southwest, a quarter called Cantrips & Crows holds a tavern and inn, and in a hidden chamber to the northeast, the city's rogues run a black market. A long pipe leads from it out into the open sky above Crystalsong Forest.

4564.name: Krasus' Landing
4564.description: Krasus' Landing is an area on the eastern edge of Dalaran, named after the Kirin Tor mage Krasus, where flying mounts and their riders arrive and depart.

4567.name: The Violet Hold
4567.description: The Violet Hold is the great prison of the Kirin Tor in Dalaran, its magically shielded cells filled with row upon row of dangerous inmates who have long been held there to protect the city. It was destroyed and rebuilt during the Third War. Now Malygos's blue dragonflight assails it, pouring through portals that open within the prison through a great crack in its roof, threatening to set its inmates free.

4568.name: The Eventide
4568.description: The Eventide is a plaza in southern Dalaran, home to the city's bank and a fountain into which some of Azeroth's most influential figures are said to have tossed lucky coins.

4569.name: Sewer Exit Pipe
4569.description: The Sewer Exit Pipe is a long pipe leading out of the Underbelly, the sewers of Dalaran, and opening into the empty sky high above Crystalsong Forest.

4570.name: Circle of Wills
4570.description: The Circle of Wills is the central hall of the Underbelly beneath Dalaran, where duelists test their skill in dueling circles and arena fighters gather.

4598.name: Krasus' Landing
4598.description: Krasus' Landing lies on the eastern side of Dalaran, named for the Kirin Tor mage Krasus, the place where gryphons, wind riders, and other flying mounts carry travelers to and from the floating city.

4599.name: Sewer Exit Pipe
4599.description: The Sewer Exit Pipe is one of the outflow pipes of Dalaran's sewers, running from the Underbelly to an opening high in the sky above Crystalsong Forest, with nothing but a long fall below.

4601.name: Dalaran Island
4601.description: Dalaran Island is the floating mass of earth upon which the city of Dalaran rests, its edges falling away into open sky high above Crystalsong Forest.

4613.name: Dalaran City
4613.description: Dalaran City is the floating city of the Kirin Tor high above Crystalsong Forest, a place of violet spires, enchanted streets, magical shops, and scholars, open to the Alliance and the Horde alike as a neutral sanctuary in the war against the Lich King and the blue dragonflight.

4614.name: The Violet Citadel Spire
4614.description: The Violet Citadel Spire is the tallest spire crowning the Violet Citadel at the heart of Dalaran, its sharply pointed tip surrounded by a circular array held in place by powerful magic, rising above everything else in the city.

4616.name: Sunreaver's Sanctuary
4616.description: Sunreaver's Sanctuary is the Horde district of Dalaran, named after Archmage Aethas Sunreaver of the Council of Six and kept by the Sunreavers, the blood elf magi under his command. It houses an inn, merchants, and a portal to Orgrimmar.

4618.name: Antonidas Memorial
4618.description: The Antonidas Memorial stands in Dalaran between the Magus Commerce Exchange and Sunreaver's Sanctuary, honoring the archmage Antonidas, the former leader of the Kirin Tor, who was slain by Arthas Menethil when the Scourge destroyed Dalaran. Designed by his student Jaina Proudmoore, the statue hovers above the grass, holding a constantly turning orb in one hand and his greatstaff in the other, and a plaque bears Jaina's words of dedication.

4619.name: The Violet Citadel
4619.description: The Violet Citadel is the great fortress at the heart of Dalaran, a towering spire raised by magic, roofed with slate the color of lapis lazuli. It holds the research laboratories and great spell libraries of the Kirin Tor and the Arcane Vault of their most powerful artifacts. Here the archmage Rhonin and the Council of Six rule the city and lead the Kirin Tor's war against the blue dragonflight and the Scourge.

4620.name: Magus Commerce Exchange
4620.description: The Magus Commerce Exchange is the main trade district of Dalaran, filled with shops selling enchanted goods, craftsmen's wares, and plans, and with masters of nearly every craft teaching their skills.

4632.name: Dalaran Floating Rocks
4632.description: The Dalaran Floating Rocks are chunks of earth drifting in the sky high above the floating city of Dalaran.

4637.name: Vargoth's Retreat
4637.description: Vargoth's Retreat is the chamber of Archmage Vargoth within the Violet Citadel of Dalaran.

4638.name: Violet Citadel Balcony
4638.description: The Violet Citadel Balcony is a balcony outside Archmage Vargoth's chamber in the Violet Citadel of Dalaran, looking out over the city and the crystal forest far below.

4739.name: Runeweaver Square
4739.description: Runeweaver Square is a plaza at the center of Dalaran, set between the Silver Enclave and Sunreaver's Sanctuary, with a fountain at its heart.

4740.name: The Silver Enclave
4740.description: The Silver Enclave is the Alliance district of Dalaran and the headquarters of the Silver Covenant, a group of high elves who oppose the inclusion of the blood elves in the Kirin Tor. Its guards swiftly teleport away any members of the Horde who approach.

4395.description: Dalaran is the city of the magi, capital of the magocratic nation of the same name and home of the Kirin Tor, the order that has led the study of the arcane throughout human history. Its violet spires once rose by the shores of Lordamere Lake, until the city was destroyed by the Scourge in the Third War and later rebuilt behind a magical dome. Now the Kirin Tor have lifted the entire city into the sky and moved it to Northrend, where it floats high above the western reaches of Crystalsong Forest, not far from Icecrown, to oppose both the Lich King and the blue dragon Aspect Malygos, whose war against all mortal spellcasters has made Dalaran a prime target. The city is ruled by the Council of Six from the Violet Citadel, led by the archmage Rhonin. Dalaran has opened its gates to the Alliance and the Horde alike as a neutral sanctuary: the high elves of the Silver Covenant keep the Silver Enclave for the Alliance, while the blood elf Sunreavers keep Sunreaver's Sanctuary for the Horde, and the two factions eye each other warily. Its enchanted streets are full of shops, magical curiosities, and scholars, while the Underbelly, the sewers beneath it, serves as the city's slum.

4630.name: The North Sea
4630.description: The North Sea reaches around the eastern and northern coasts of Northrend, a frigid expanse of gray water and drifting ice beneath bitter winds. Few ships venture far into these waters, where icebergs and fog hide the coasts and the cursed kvaldir and other sea raiders are said to rise from the mists.

4742.name: Hrothgar's Landing

4760.name: The Sea Reaver's Run
4760.description: The Sea Reaver's Run is the strait north of Icecrown, between the continent and the island of Hrothgar's Landing. Ships of the Silver Covenant and the Sunreavers sail its cold waters to fight the kvaldir, whose deepcallers summon kraken from the depths to attack any vessel that tries to pass.

4769.name: Hrothgar's Landing
4769.description: Hrothgar's Landing is the mist-shrouded island at the heart of the kvaldir's domain off the northern coast of Icecrown. It once held a tuskarr village, but the kvaldir slew or drove away its people, and their longships now gather here to raid the ships of the Sea Reaver's Run.

4742.description: Hrothgar's Landing is a small, mist-shrouded island off the northern coast of Icecrown, separated from the continent by the strait known as the Sea Reaver's Run. A tuskarr village once stood here, until the kvaldir, the cursed sea vrykul, came under their chieftain Hrothgar and slew or drove away its people, renaming the island after him. It has become a staging point from which the kvaldir launch raids against the ships sailing the strait, calling up great kraken from the depths, while the fleets of the Silver Covenant and the Sunreavers battle to drive them back from Icecrown's shores.
